13273: Farmhands looking for the door in the barn keep ending up at the wrong end.
13471: A fallen soldier who did many evil deeds returns to earth as punishment in the shape of a large dog with fiery eyes and frightens people. Later smugglers use the story to scare customs officers by dressing up as a dog, but this fails.
35897: The skin of a werewolf was found in a tree and the suspected farmhand was sent far away. When they threw the skin into the oven, he came running up screaming, but when it was burnt, he was glad to be rid of it. They had found out that he was the werewolf by throwing a blue apron to the wolf; the next day the farmhand had blue threads between his teeth.
38979:
A farmer's son returning home from the fair at night is addressed at a haunted spot by a white lady, who asks him to release her and so make his fortune. He agrees, and each time the ghost orders him to do something he says: "Do it yourself!" as the ghost had told him to beforehand. The ghost leads him through passages, doors and halls until they come to 5 chests, on which sits a big black dog that takes his breath away. He can no longer speak, and the ghost takes leave for 100 years; the man is back on the road where he was addressed, drags himself home and is dead 2 days later.
Someone heard of his adventure and also tried his luck, saw a light dancing ahead of him at midnight, took fright and fled.
38980: At fort Ronduute a woman appears every 100 years. She asked a passer-by to come with her to the cellar of the fort. There were 3 chests, with a dog on one and on the 2nd a lion holding the key to the 3rd in its mouth, which the man has to take. He does not dare, and the woman takes leave for 100 years.
38981: On the spot where a convent once stood, the white nun appears every ten years.
38982: At night a lady asks a poacher to release her. She takes him to three chests of treasure and sends him to the big black dog to take the key from its mouth. The man sees that the dog is the devil and has himself brought back up, after which he is cursed. He comes home ill and stays ill for a long time. He remains poor all his life.
38987: A soldier who behaved wretchedly during his life comes haunting without a head after his death, rattling a chain.
38996: At a haunted spot a voice was always heard sighing: "Where shall I put it?" One day a drunkard says: "Put it on the devil's neck." From then on the voice is no longer heard.
39007: When grandfather and his friends were coming back from the fair, there was a white cat sitting on the road, which disappeared when grandfather read the Gospel of Saint John.
39026: If you kick a cat, you can get a beating. Someone kicked at a cat and at once there were a thousand of them.
39038: A farmer's farmhands hear the shutters banging at night, but when they go to look, they are closed; other ghostly noises can be heard too, but nothing can be seen. Sometimes a white horse runs along with the others, but when they try to tie it up, it is gone.
39046: If someone was bewitched, people went to the friars of Gent for Easter nails, which were then laid under the doormat, so that the witch could no longer enter the house.
39110: At the urging of a minister from Goes, the Friars Minor are driven out and move to the monastery in Sas van Gent. But when the minister dies, a black dog with fiery eyes appears, breathing fire, so that everyone flees. The chief minister is fetched in vain, after which help is sought from the Friars Minor. The consignator goes there with two helpers, armed with the Blessed Sacrament, and holds the host up to Satan, who then flies out through the windowpane in flames. And so the Friars Minor got their church back.
49566: One of the best-known haunted houses in the Netherlands, a villa in Sas van Gent, is threatened with demolition. The ghosts of Canadian soldiers and a German soldier are said to roam there. A strong supporter of demolition is a neighbour who is bothered every weekend at night by young people partying in the villa. Many villagers, however, want to preserve the villa, partly because of its reputation as a haunted house. A petition has been started, and it is successful.
127071: A man who curses is given a beating by the devil as punishment.
156129: In the old days a werewolf roamed around Ename. One evening a man was jumped on by the werewolf. He had to carry the animal on his back until he got home. There the werewolf leapt into the field.
156134: Long ago many witches lived in Ouwegem. Those witches stole the thickest straw brooms from the basket maker and flew on them through the air to Cologne.
156139: A little boy always lay sweating and moaning in his bed. His father gave him a thump, but that did not help. When the parents told the curate about the problem, he knew at once what was going on. He sprinkled the child with holy water. After that the boy was no longer ridden by the mare.
156182: A man coming back from Moerbeke with his wife saw a black cat walking in front of him. When the man tried to chase the cat away, the animal grew bigger and bigger. In the end the man no longer dared to chase the cat away, so he had to take a detour.
156241: To avoid being ridden by the mare at night, people placed their clogs with the heels pointing towards the bed.
156242: A woman on her way to Zonnegem suddenly saw a large wheat field there. At a certain moment she saw something in the field that looked like a little rabbit. When she took a step forward, the rabbit had vanished. The woman turned around and saw a man as tall as the church. It was the devil himself.
156266: In a house in Ouwegem knocking was heard on the shutters at night. It sounded as if dogs were scratching at the wood. The next day a fence was put up around the house so that the dogs could no longer reach the shutters. But the following night the knocking was heard again. The woman of the house sought advice from the parish priest, who said: "That is a dead woman who is returning because her brother promised twenty masses but never had them said." The woman then took money to the friars and asked them to begin the masses the very next day. Instead of twenty masses, she even had thirty masses said. Since then those people never heard the knocking at night again.
156296: A man whose first wife had died had promised to have a Mass said, but he had never kept that promise. At night the man saw a black cat sitting under his bed. The man became ill with fear and could no longer sleep. Finally the man told everything to his second wife. After the promised Mass had been said, the cat did not appear again.
156309: On a bewitched farm, one evening a woman saw caterpillars coming out from under the chimney hood. The woman threw the caterpillars into the stove. A sorceress had sent the vermin.
156348: A woman often lay tossing in her bed at night because she was ridden by the mare. To protect yourself against the mare, you had to put your clogs upside down beside the bed.
156364: A little child was often given an apple by a woman and always began to cry after eating the fruit. One day the child's mother cut such an apple in two to give half to her other little daughter. The mother then found a little bundle of straw inside the apple.
156384: A house was built on the spot where the Sint-Jozef chapel used to stand. That house was haunted. Most occupants therefore did not stay long in it.
156404: In the old days, when farmers saw a woman walking back and forth strikingly often, they believed that woman would bring misfortune to the stables or the household.
156405: Some men who went to bring in the harvest in France slept in a barn at night. Every morning the men found that rats had gnawed at their belongings. With them was also a Swiss shepherd who was not bothered by the rats. "They won't touch my things," the Swiss always said. One night the other men decided to play a trick on the Swiss shepherd. They damaged the Swiss man's shoes so it looked as if rats had gnawed them. When the Swiss woke up in the morning, the men said: "Well, look at that, I thought they didn't come to you!" The Swiss shepherd said: "They won't do it again," went outside and made a fire. Then all the rats ran to that fire and burned. After that the Swiss took his belongings and left.
156413: Strange things always happened at night in the small castle. In the morning everything was normal again. When the castle wall was demolished, a pile of leather money and a letter about a thousand years old were found. After that the castle was no longer haunted.
156433: A man went on pilgrimage to Saint Renilde near Halle. Afterwards he went to an inn to eat his sandwiches. When he told the landlady that he came from Erpe, the woman said: "Then you also know where the Oonegemmeers is. Are those tree stumps still there? I spent many nights there and had a lot of fun, but I'm glad I'm rid of it now."
156458: Every night a woman saw a figure approach and sit on her blanket. Then she saw the figure leave by the window. The woman stuck a paasnagel (Easter nail) under her gate.
156492: A man was always ridden by the mare at night if he had forgotten to put his clogs upside down beside his bed.
156540: A farmer had a sow with piglets. Because the farmer had five small children, his brother kept watch over the piglets in the stable at night. At one point a blow sounded on the stable door, though no one could be seen. Some time later burning matches fell down. The man was convinced someone was up in the stable loft, but that turned out not to be the case. The people notified the police, who gave them permission to shoot if they saw anyone. In the end the farmer sought advice from the priests of Oudenaarde. The priests promised to come. When the farmer hurried home at four in the morning, he met a man who said: "You needn't hurry. By the time you get home, your whole farm will have burned down". When he got home, the farmer learned from his brother that his house and stables had all caught fire at once, like a pile of paper doused in petroleum. About four weeks later someone committed suicide in that house. The priests of Oudenaarde came and put an Easter nail under the door.
156599: A farm in Nederbrakel was so badly haunted that people were afraid to go to bed in the evening. Every evening men with chains walked about in the attic there.
156621: In Moerzeke a little boy had been bewitched by a witch. The boy played all kinds of tricks, so his parents had the priests of Dendermonde read prayers over him. After that the boy behaved normally.
156665: People were playing cards in a café in the Melsenstraat when suddenly the mother of one of the players came in to urge her son to come home. When the son refused, the woman came back with a black cat, which she put on the table. The café owner grabbed the black cat and struck the animal against a tree. The next day the woman had two black eyes.
156685: In Zarlardinge lived a witch. When this witch found no victim, she had to work her evil on her own son. The boy often lay there as if half dead. When the parish priest once came to visit, the witch turned out to be convinced that her son would not die.
156718: In Etikhove some people had died who had hidden something somewhere. After their death a stalkeers (will-o'-the-wisp) always flew to the same spot. After money was found at that spot, the stalkeers never appeared again.
156726: One morning on a farm, people found that the ground had been completely churned up by rats. They did not rule out that the rats had been sent by sorcery.
156745: Four men out one evening had a walk of two and a half hours ahead of them. When the men came into the woods, they saw cats everywhere. One of the men said: "If those cats don't go away, I'll give them a whack." But another man replied: "No, don't do that. Leave them alone." As soon as the men came out of the woods, the cats had vanished.
156838: Of people who had got lost, it was said that they had been 'ridden off by the mane'.
156895: There was dancing in the cafés near the Sint-Hermeskerk in Ronse. One day devils with horse's legs were seen dancing along there.
156898: A sorceress had been in a house where there was a small child. After the sorceress's visit, the whole house was full of lice.
156905: A man walking home one evening saw a white cat sitting on the roof of the well in his garden. When the man began talking to the cat, the animal said: "Brother White asked me, beautiful white cat, where do you come from?"
156947: By the Molenbeek in Duitsenbroek (Goeferdinge) stood a watermill that had belonged to an abbey. Under the bridge over the brook, people often saw a white figure floating after sunset. One day the ghost story came to an unexpected end. The daughter of a nearby farm often took her cattle to drink at the brook. When the girl sat there, she always stuck her stick into a hole in a weathered beam. One day, to her great alarm, the girl saw a heap of coins fall out of the beam. The parish priest of Overboelare used the money to have masses said. Since then the white ghost has not been seen again.
156971: Near Sint-Gillis-Dendermonde a werewolf had hidden his skin in a woodpile. Some people had found the skin and thrown it into a hot oven. At that very moment the werewolf came running to save his skin.
156973: Near Sint-Gillis-Dendermonde a werewolf had hidden his skin in a woodpile. Some people had found the skin and thrown it into a hot oven. At that very moment the werewolf came running to save his skin.
157037: There used to be a lot of hunting in the woods of Wortegem. One day someone shot at a hare there. But the animal could not be hit, because the gun always broke or no bullets came out.
157054: On the Billegemsbaantje in Wanzele, will-o'-the-wisps were seen wandering back and forth at night. People believed these lights were the souls of dead Freemasons who came to ask forgiveness for their sins.
157094:
An innkeeper's wife with four children always had disreputable people in her house. The sorceress had driven her own son mad.
In a house where a baby was born, a toad was seen coming in. The father quickly grabbed the animal and threw it into the stove. The next day the man met the innkeeper's wife, who said: "You wanted to kill me, didn't you!" The innkeeper's wife wore a cloth on her head because she had been burned.
157144: If one saw a magpie, one could expect misfortune, people used to believe.
157178: On a farm in Ronse a cow had fallen ill. Someone who claimed the cow was bewitched said: "When the cow urinates, fill a bottle with her urine and put the bottle on the table. The person responsible for the harm will come by and pull the stopper out of the bottle." They did as the man had advised and found that the cow was cured 18 days later.
157203: In Verrebroek a strange fellow sat in a café and said to a man: "Tomorrow you will be plagued by rats." The next morning that man's house was indeed full of rats. The man never saw the strange fellow again.
157207: In Oordegem a big black cat was always prowling around a farmer. When the farmer grew tired of it, he shot at the animal with his gun and hit it in the paw. The next day the farmer heard that a woman from the village had a gunshot wound in her leg.
157229: People who were ridden by the mare could no longer find their way home.
157251: A woman on her way to Linkebeek met a black cat. The woman was afraid of the animal, because she believed it was a witch who had died a few days earlier and had returned.
157257: In one family a sick boy lay in bed. A woman came to visit and stayed sitting by the bed. Because this woman had a bad name, the boy's mother went to the sexton of Sint-Denijs-Boekel to get an Easter nail. When the visitor was again sitting with the boy, the mother stuck the Easter nail under the chair. The visitor then began to sweat and said: "X, release me." Then the visitor left and never came back.
157261: Whenever a man went to church to have his child baptised, he always met a woman. Afterwards the child died. Only three of that man's children survived. When those children were taken to be baptised, they did not meet that woman.
157278: A man coming back from the fields grew frightened when he suddenly saw a big dog running towards him. The man took another road, but five metres further on the dog appeared there again.
157299: In the old days people often met a werewolf in the evening. That was someone who wore a sheepskin, donkey skin or bearskin and had himself carried for a while. Werewolves had sold their souls to the devil.
157350: A pregnant woman who had been ridden by the mare went to confession. The priest said to her: "That will not happen to you again", and he was right.
157359: A man had met a ghost in the middle of the street that would not get out of his way.
157361: A woman coming back from the factory was approached on the way by a werewolf. The woman quickly threw a few rags of cloth on the ground. The werewolf had to unravel the cloth, which gave the woman the chance to get home.
157388: A man who was poaching in Kwaremont shot at a hare. He had hit the animal, but a little later so many hares appeared that the man ran home in fear.
157390: A woman who worked as a maid on her sister's farm did not dare stay on the farm at night because it was haunted. The doors flew open and creaking could be heard everywhere.
157407: A man who worked as a farmhand found a skin with paws while trimming the hedge. Assuming it was the skin of kledde (a shape-shifting bogeyman), they threw it into the burning oven. But the skin would not burn, and only smoke came out of the oven. The skin had turned completely black from the smoke, and its owner had been smoked black as well. Right after that incident he left, and he was never seen again.
157408: One winter evening a woman had invited her brother and sister because she had baked waffles. In the galgestraatje (little gallows street) the brother and sister met a gentleman and said: "Good evening". But the gentleman did not answer. When the two looked back, they no longer saw the gentleman.
157417: On a farm where they had a lot of misfortune with the animals, a little grey cat was always seen walking about. When the people went to the stable, the cat went with them. The animal was the cause of the misfortune.
157430: In Mater lived a woman who was said to be a witch. When the witch's cow had been stolen, the woman walked through the village and heard her cow lowing. "Look, there is my cow," the woman said.
157434: A woman lived in a small house with a little barn next to it that was full of hay. The woman always walked around the barn with burning candles, so people believed the building would burn down one day. When the insurance people came to take a look at the barn, the woman said: "The barn cannot burn down." She laid a bundle of straw outside and put a candle on it. Strangely enough, the hay did not catch fire.
157450: Two witches lived in Ename. A man coming back from Ename station kicked at a black cat that was running in front of his feet. A moment later one of those witches stood before him.
157469: People who had been ridden by the mare had a bad dream and sweated terribly.
157497: The farmer of Hof Ter Kraaien had sold his soul to the devil and brought in his harvest with the help of crows.
157518: A man who had got lost was only ten minutes' walk from his house, yet he could not get there. He lost his clogs and kept ending up at the same spot. People said the man had been ridden by the mare.
157526: A man whose wife had died three days before saw the ghost of his dead wife walking among the runner beans. The man died of fright.
157578: People who were out in the evening and got lost had been ridden by the mare and had to wander about all night.
157601: On a farm in Steenhuize, two cows were found in the morning tied up with the same chain. That farm was haunted.
157603: On a farm worked a farmhand who left every evening at about the same time. The farmhand had hidden a skin in a tree stump. One day the farmer sent his farmhand to Lessen so that he could burn the skin. But the farmhand came running to the oven straight away. He had to be held back. When the skin had burned up, the farmhand was content because he had been freed from the devil.
157631: On a farm the cows were untied every night. Because no one dared to come to that farm any more, the building stood empty for four years. After that someone did go to live there, and no longer experienced anything strange.
157648: On a farm in Doel lived a daughter who could gather as many eggs as she liked. That girl could surely work witchcraft. The girl walked down the street with a basket full of eggs, but never said where she had got those eggs.
157657: A man walking home in the dark was afraid of a black cat, because he believed it was a witch. If you kicked such a cat, the next day you could see an injured woman walking about.
157663: In a house in Ronse knocking was heard every night, and the police were called. The officers heard the knocking too, but there was nothing to be seen. In the end the people had to leave their house. After that the house stood empty.
157669: In Oudenhoven a woman had died at a very great age. One evening the elderly daughter of the dead woman saw a shadowy figure in the kitchen two or three times. "What can that be?" the woman asked. A little later she heard knocking and a voice that said: "Oostakker." The village priest advised the woman to go on pilgrimage to Oostakker. The dead woman had probably promised during her life to make that pilgrimage but never fulfilled the promise.
157670: An old woman had died in Huise. The carpenter had laid the woman's body in the coffin. A few days later, however, people heard scratching in the coffin, so that no one dared to come near it anymore. When the carpenter came to open the coffin, a cat jumped out. People believed that the witch had returned in the shape of a cat. In reality the coffin was probably not properly closed, so that the cat had crept into it.
157716: A farmer whose cow was due to calve was astonished when he saw an animal born with the head of a goat and the hindquarters of a cow. The cow must have fallen victim to a witch.
157727: A woman who was always ridden by the mare (nightmare) had to urinate in a bottle and then seal the bottle tightly. The culprit then had to come and ask the woman for forgiveness, or else he could no longer urinate.
157743: In Neigem lived a witch who sold milk and of whom everyone was afraid. No butter could be made from her milk.
157777: The lord of Neigem castle had promised to give fifty sacks of wheat to the poor. Because he had not kept his promise, he came haunting the castle after his death.
157780: A woman coming home with her sister saw a strange circular light above her house. One of the women had a premonition and said: "I know what that means: we must not go home anymore. Something is surely going to happen to our father." A few days later the woman's father did indeed die.
157806: A woman had put a stove in her washhouse. Every time the woman took her washing off the line, the stove fell over and the cooking pot crashed to the floor. The woman put another stove in her washhouse, but exactly the same thing happened with this one. The woman's mother-in-law had a bad name. One day, when the woman had hurt her foot in the washhouse, she saw her mother-in-law and sister-in-law outside watching her. After the woman had consulted a secular clergyman (?) from Eigenbrakel, she had no more problems. The woman had first gone to a parish priest, but he did not have enough power to undo the evil.
157846: One night a castle is said to have sunk in Gooik. After that, bells were always heard ringing at that spot.
157850: The notary of Asse rode on horseback to Dendermonde. On the way the notary saw two men who wanted to ride along with him. When the notary gave the men a hand to help them onto the cart, he knew instinctively that they were devils and quickly kicked them to the ground. Then the notary smelled sulphur.
157886: A woman from Mater believed she was bewitched and went to the priests of Gent, who said many prayers for her. When the woman asked the priests what was wrong with her, they answered that someone wanted to murder her by witchcraft. Because the woman had a strong heart, the priests believed she would survive. The woman gave alms and the priests promised to pray for her for nine days.
157893: On 11 July the Amelberga procession was held in Mater. One year, however, the weather was so bad that it was decided not to hold the procession. The next morning people were astonished to find Saint Amelberga standing on her throne in the church all covered in dirt. Since that event the procession has been held every year on 11 July, whatever the weather.
157931: A boy always got biscuits from a woman. He had heard from someone that the woman was a witch. He had been advised to place his feet crossed in the witch's footprint. When the boy did so, the woman turned around. After that he never ate her biscuits again.
157971: Witches were people who had special knowledge and special powers. Their hands often tingled and they could, for example, heal illnesses with their hands. Because such special powers were rather controversial, such people often ended up at the stake.
157995: A woman was kneading her bread when a sorcerer passed by with the words: "Your bread will fail." Indeed, the bread would not rise. When the woman cut it, it crumbled completely.
157999: In Mater lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. That woman went to Mass every day. When the woman was old, she had to go to the convent to be cared for there. One morning, after heavy rain showers and gusts of wind during the night, the witch was found on the floor of her room. Everything in the room had been turned upside down. After that people knew for certain that the woman was a witch.
158019: In a café lived a woman who had special powers. In those days people had the habit of going to the café on Sundays. If someone had walked past the café twice without going in, the witch made sure that they did go in the third time.
158071:
A carter came with a horse to plough a farmer's field. The farmer said to the carter: "Well, I've heard that your girlfriend is a witch. Is that true?" The carter knew nothing about it but was determined to find out. When he was visiting his girlfriend, at about half past ten he pretended to have fallen asleep; by then he had already been told several times to go home. He saw his girlfriend take a pot from a cupboard and twice rub her head with a kind of ointment. Then she said "Over hedge and over fence" and left. The carter rubbed himself with the ointment too and said by mistake: "Through hedge and through fence." Because he had got the charm wrong, he of course crashed into everything and arrived at his destination covered in blood.
When the carter came to plough for the farmer again the next day, he said: "Now I know! She's a damned witch and I'm never setting foot in that house again!"
158112:
Kludde (a shape-shifting bogeyman) often sat in a wood and by willow trees. He had sold his soul to the devil and had been given a skin.
On a farm worked someone who played kludde and had hidden his skin in a willow. Someone had found that skin and thrown it into a burning oven. Although kludde was out in the field, a moment later he was standing by the fire to save his skin. As soon as the skin had burned up, kludde was freed.
158116: A man coming home from work at one o'clock at night saw a small white rabbit sitting on the dike. The man took the rabbit home and put it in a little case. The next day, to his great horror, the man found that the rabbit had turned into the skeleton of a child. The man turned deathly pale and went to the priest. The priest told the man it was his own fault; after all, he should leave everything alone at night. Later the man died of that incident.
158151: People who could no longer find their bearings or their way home had been led by the 'dolf' (a spirit that leads people astray).
158176: In Velzeke lived two women who were suspected of being witches. When these witches got up from their chairs in church, their chairs were full of pins, people said.
158253: In the evening people were not allowed to walk past the stone cross by the Paambeek, because someone was once said to have been struck by lightning there. The ghost of that person returned there, people believed.
158265: Two farmers could not get along. When one farmer was on the other's meadow with his sheep, the other tried to catch him. When the angry farmer came closer, he saw dung heaps instead of sheep. The German shepherd had brought this about.
158268: A man from Mere who was a soldier in Leipzig in Napoleon's time was approached one day in an inn by an old woman, who asked him where he came from. When he said he was from Mere, the woman went on: "Then you'll know where the Dikke Linde (Fat Lime Tree) of Aaigem stands," to which the man said: "I should think so. I've often sat on it."
158269: 'Berewulven' (werewolves) were people who had pulled an animal skin over themselves and who roamed about in the evening, jumping onto the backs of passers-by. One day a man from Kruishoutem who was not afraid of werewolves had to carry such a beast all the way to his house. But the man threw the werewolf into the barn and shouted: "If you dare come out, I'll stick you on my dung fork." When the man opened the door a while later to look, he saw that the werewolf was his own neighbour.
158289: On a farm in Oudegem all the animals died through the doing of witches.
158309: In Sint-Denijs-Boekel there was a haunted castle. Chains could be heard rattling there and there was always noise in the stables.
158314: A farm suffered much misfortune. The trouble had begun on the day the farmer saw a crying child. A little boy stood outside crying because there was a bird's nest in the hedge and he could not get it out. So the farmer took the nest out of the hedge himself to give it to the boy. But when the farmer turned around, the child had vanished without a trace.
158349: A man coming back from Zandbergen saw sorcerers and sorceresses sitting at the edge of the wood. In that area lived a sorceress who could make people be ridden by the mare at night if they had seen her during the day.
158351: In a café in Bevere worked a maid who had a bad name. One morning all the curtains in the café had been torn to pieces. A man who sat drinking a glass of beer in the café was startled when the bottom of the glass suddenly fell to the floor. The maid was dismissed and taken to a psychiatric institution.
158392: A woman who was suspected of being a witch came to visit her daughter in Eksaarde. An hour after the woman had arrived, her other daughter also came to visit with her husband. The other daughter found it strange that her mother was there, because she thought she had seen her on the way. A week after the mother had stayed with her daughter, all kinds of things happened in the daughter's house. Two cows miscarried and a horse and two pigs died. A priest from Steenbrugge came to read prayers over the stable. The priest said that a witch had probably been in the stable. After that no stranger was allowed in the stable any more.
158415: A child who had convulsions could not be helped by the doctor. The parents kept watch over the child. At midnight strange things always happened. One night it seemed as if a cat was scratching at the door, another night there were sounds as if barrels of water were being emptied. The neighbours even came outside to see what was going on, but no one saw anything. Because a neighbour woman often came to visit, the grandmother said: "Let's throw a sprig of blessed palm into the stove and then close the lid." When they did that, the woman suddenly leapt outside. She was never seen again after that and the child recovered.
158439: On the edge of the municipality of Hofstade, criminals used to be hanged on the gallows. In the evening no one dared to go to that place anymore.
158480: In the Broekstraat in Hamme lived a man who had remarried after his wife's death. Because a ghost always appeared in the house at night, the man's second wife irritably asked the ghost what it had come for. The ghost replied: "Well, madam, I am your husband's first wife."
158483: On a farm in Denderleeuw a farmhand was ridden by the mare. One day a neighbour came to ask whether he could bake his bread in the farmer's oven. As soon as the fire was lit, the farmhand came running up in tears. He wanted the fire put out at once because they were burning his skin in the oven. That farmhand had sold his soul to the devil.
158511: In Liedekerke lived a witch. If that witch stopped at a house where there was a child, the child would be bewitched the next day.
158589: On a farm in Sint-Antelinks all the animals died and the farmer's wife fell ill. One day a woman had been in the garden there and had said: "You have fine cabbages! We don't have a single blade of green!" After the farmer's wife had given the woman a cabbage, the misfortune began. They sent for the priests, who put an end to the calamity.
158613: A man hacked at a frog that was sitting in a smithy, because he believed the frog was a witch.
158670: A farm on the Kraneveld in Eine was haunted. The shepherd who lived there heard noise at night and could not keep his sheep and cows in the stable. So the man moved away. The haunting went on at that farm for a good two years. The priests then exorcised the farm.
158680: A hundred years ago, in every municipality there was someone who dressed up in the evening in an animal skin as kledde (a shape-shifting bogeyman) to frighten people and make them carry him. On a farm in Aspelare they had found kledde's skin. When they were about to throw the skin into a burning oven, kledde was already standing by the fire to take his skin out.
158703: On a farm where cows often died or animals broke loose, people went to the friars. That helped them.
158728: At a wedding party a drunk man was ridden by the mare, so that he lost his way and ended up at the brewery in Oudenhove.
158742: A farm in Erpe was haunted every night. For two weeks a terrible noise had been heard between a quarter to twelve and twelve. One day the farmer's uncle came to keep watch at the farm. At a quarter to twelve the stable doors began rattling and banging open and shut again. In the drying loft there were sounds as if someone was being murdered. Everyone ran outside, but nothing could be heard there. As soon as they went back in, the noise started again. Because the haunting recurred every day, they went to the white canons of Ghent. A white father came to exorcise the farm until he was drenched in sweat. That same night the father went back to Ghent. After that the ghostly noises were no longer heard.
158765:
A woman had wanted to give marshmallows to some children, but the children had refused to take them. Their mother always said they were not allowed to accept anything from that witch. If they had taken something anyway, they had to throw it away over their heads and make the sign of the cross to protect themselves against evil.
The witch did not leave it at that, however, and said: "You will hear more from witches!" Shortly afterwards a cow of those people was due to calve. The calf that was born was a real monster. It had five legs and its tail was not at the top but at the bottom. The animal lived only a few hours.
Afterwards those people had their stable blessed. The farmer's wife had often asked the priest to come by, but he kept putting it off. So the farmer's wife had fetched holy water at the Sint-Hermeskerk. With a palm sprig she sprinkled every corner of the stable while praying the Gospel of Saint John. After that the farm had no more problems.
158781: The sorceresses could not leave the church as long as the missal remained open.
158785: A family from Belsele was always visited by an old woman who came to fetch milk. When one day the woman had to wait a while for her milk, she cried out: "Damn, it's always the same here. I wish you had no more milk!" Shortly afterwards the farm indeed had no more milk. Some time later the woman came to visit again. This time an Easter nail was put under her chair. The woman began to sweat and was told: "Now you will have to undo what you have done, or else you won't be able to get up". The woman then said: "Go to your stable and you will have milk again". After the woman had gone outside, an Easter nail was put under the threshold. After that the woman could no longer come in.
158811: People who were ridden by the mare had a dream.
158826: A boy from Bevere had a 'pearl' on his eye. No doctor or quack could cure the boy. One day he was advised to go to an old woman in Leupegem. The boy followed the advice and eight days later he was completely cured. That woman was suspected of being a witch.
158849: A witch had visited a farm in Oude Broek. The next day the animals there lay with their necks wrung. The people then bought other animals, but these turned out to give no milk. After the people had consulted the White Fathers, their misfortune came to an end.
158850: A woman was annoyed by a cat that always came and lay on her when she was in bed. At first she thought it was her own cat, but when she called the animal by its name, she was surprised to see the cat run away. The woman also found that her own cat was sleeping peacefully under the stove. One night the woman managed to scratch the cat that was tormenting her. The next day her mother-in-law came in wearing a short-sleeved blouse. The mother-in-law said: "Look how the cat scratched my arms!"
158923: In Mullem a cat always roamed around a house. When someone was out in the evening, the cat would follow that person. People believed the cat was a witch.
158940: The statue of Saint Lambert was taken to the church. But the saint was not content there, for the next day his statue was hanging in the woods again. A little chapel was built on that spot.
158962: People took a child that cried all the time to the friars of Gent. The clergymen read prayers over the child and said: "When you go home, you will meet a woman who asks where you have been. You must not answer and you must just keep walking". The people did as they had been advised. The next day they found that their child was growing like a weed.
158990: A mother from Sint-Maria-Lierde went to the friars in Ghent because her child was ill. The friar read prayers over the child until he was drenched in sweat. He also advised the mother not to talk to anyone at Ghent station. At the station the mother was approached by someone who said: "Your child is ill, isn't it?" When the mother did not answer, the woman went on: "The more I squeeze this little doll, the more your child suffers." When the mother got home, she saw the same woman coming. The woman wanted something to drink, but the mother sent her away. The woman threw a little cap over the hedge and left.
158992: A shepherd had to wander all night around a small field because he could not find a way out. The man had been ridden by the mare.
159071: On a farm, a farmer used to work a little at his loom in the evenings. Every time he sat there, a cat crept through a hole in the door. One evening the farmer struck at the cat, which then ran off. The next day the farmer found that one of his farmhands had a blow to his face. "I fainted," said the farmhand.
159076: On a farm in Sint-Maria-Latem shouting and yelling was heard every evening. The farmer claimed that his cows were lowing and pulling themselves loose, but the people keeping watch on the farm could hear or see nothing. The farmer could not churn butter either. He blamed all his problems on a witch. One night the farmer came to someone for help because his cows were fighting in the meadow. The other people, however, could not see that. After the farmer had gone to the friars of Gent, he no longer experienced such strange things.
159097: A woman from Mater went to help her daughter with the work in Nederename. When the woman left, the daughter asked: "Mother, what should I give you for this?", to which the mother replied: "Nothing, but have a Mass said for me." The daughter, however, forgot her promise. One day the daughter noticed that her baby could not sleep. When she went to look by the oven, she saw a strange beast like a calf crawling upwards. The beast said: "My child, what is held against me?" After the daughter had had the promised Mass said, the strange beast did not appear again.
159119: In a family the mother had suddenly fallen ill. The priest who came to visit the woman every day said: "She is quietly going to heaven". The family, however, found it strange that the sick woman had such a good appetite and believed evil had something to do with it. One of the sick woman's sons told the priest about his suspicion. When the son asked the priest to read prayers over his mother, the clergyman said: "You're mad. That doesn't exist anymore". The man said he would go to the Augustinian friars in Gent if the priest would not read prayers over his mother. The priest replied: "You don't need to go to Gent. I will come tomorrow". After the priest had read prayers over the woman, she recovered. The witch was someone who had come for coffee fourteen days earlier. She had brought cakes herself.
159139: Some girls were on their way to work in Ronse at about five in the morning. On the way the girls met a woman, and one of them said: "There's the witch." The woman heard it and said: "You won't be saying that tonight." At about half past six that evening the girls came back from Ronse. That one girl saw a black ribbon lying in the street, which she could not step over. The girl took another road, but saw the ribbon lying there again. The woman was standing there too and said: "What are you going to say to me?" The girl replied: "Come on, let me through. I won't do it again."
159181: A priest from Mullem could saddle people with lice, rats and mice.
159186: A woman who had sold her soul to the devil used to bake in the evening. When she had said something like "Over everything and over everything", her spirit was gone. One evening she stood at her trough with her hands in the dough, but her spirit was gone. Her husband had seen it. He went for a walk in his garden and heard beautiful music there. He decided to copy his wife, but made a mistake and said: "Over everything and through everything." As a result he ended up in the bramble bushes. When he came home the next morning covered in scratches, his wife said: "You got it wrong. It's 'over everything and over everything'."
159220: Two brothers coming home one evening suddenly saw a strange beast leap out near the Varenberg. The animal rubbed against the legs of one of the brothers. The two then ran home and nearly banged their door in out of fear. They believed it was witchcraft.
159224: Sometimes people were jumped on at night by the 'little man', who tried to strangle them. People to whom this happened had to be shaken awake. To protect themselves against such torment, people had to use Easter nails.
159237: In the past there were women who could bewitch children. They would visit somewhere and take hold of the little child. A few days later the child fell ill and sometimes even died. People then believed the child had been bewitched.
159246: A mother who had had a baby went into a shop with the child. Suddenly an unknown woman came in and said: "Oh madam, you have a lovely baby!" When the woman had touched the child, it began to cry. The child cried for four days and four nights. The mother went to Gent with the child. When she came home, she feared the child would die, but it recovered after all.
159264: A man and his son were cutting bramble branches when a witch from Ooike came by and gave the son a thick slice of bread with a slice of meat. The father then said to the witch: "If you don't clear off quickly, I'll cut off your head with my knife!" After that the witch was quickly gone.
159269: A sick boy was advised by the doctor to have an operation. A woman who came to visit the boy, however, said: "I wouldn't have that boy operated on so quickly. First go to the friars of Gent". When the people were at the friars, these said the boy was suffering from a heart disease. The friars also said: "The person who caused this evil lives near you. When you come home, she will come to ask where you have been with the boy and what was said, but you must not answer". The people were also given a medal and a prayer that they had to say for nine consecutive days. Moreover, they had to put an Easter nail under the door. When the witch then came by to fetch a kilo of salt, they had to say: "Come in". The witch would then not be able to get in, however. When the witch next came by and was invited in, she stood dawdling and said: "I don't have much time". The woman did indeed ask about the boy's health.
159295: In Nederhasselt a large dog with a long chain often roamed about in the evening. People said it was the devil.
159357: A brave man who dared to spend the night in a haunted castle began baking cakes during the night. At midnight the man heard a voice call: "I'm falling, I'm falling!" The next moment a lot of misshapen little men fell out of the chimney and ran to the cellar. The little men asked the brave man to lift a stone and take the money that lay under it. But each time the man said: "Do it yourself." Then the little men said: "We are the counts of the castle and we are damned. That is a purse for him and that one is for him, …"
159358: A man always thought he heard a watch ticking in a wall.
159367: A man saw an old woman coming towards him at night. He was ridden by the mare every night. When four or five men kept watch in the man's room, he began to shout and cry, but the men could not see the mare.
159388: Strange things happened in the house of a seventy-three-year-old woman. The drawers and trunks were always broken open and the farmer's pockets were emptied. That mischief was caused by a man who lived nearby.
159390: A man from Nieuwerkerken worked in France as a seasonal labourer. One day, when he was sitting in the café with his friends, the landlady heard that the group were Flemings. When she learned that the men came from Nieuwerkerken near Aalst, she said: "Oh, is that little lime tree still there? I came to gatherings there on many nights."
159393: In Nederename lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. When one day the witch's cow had been stolen, that woman found her cow and brought the animal back.
159410: A carter out with his cart met a witch in the Koolstraat. The woman who had loaded the cart was still sitting on the wagon. The witch said to that woman: "Mind you don't fall off." A little further on the cart overturned. The woman ended up in the water and drowned.
159439: A rich gentleman who had always paid his farmhands little had died on a farm. After his death the gentleman came haunting at night.
159440: In Ename lived a witch whose cow was stolen during the war. When the witch went looking for the cow, the animal began to low. Because of that the witch got her cow back immediately.
159480: A woman who worked as a maid on a farm met kledde (a werewolf-like goblin that leaps onto people's backs) every evening on her way home, and it made her carry it. One day a farmhand advised the maid to hit kledde on the snout with her apron. That evening the maid followed the advice. The next day she saw the threads of her apron between the teeth of one of the farmhands.
159519: If one saw a spider's web in the morning, it would be a busy day. If one saw the web at noon, one would have luck. If one saw it in the evening, one could expect misfortune.
159531: In Zulzeke a man who had moved a boundary post during his life came haunting. The ghost kept calling: "Where shall I put it?" A passer-by answered: "Put it back where you damn well got it." After that the ghost no longer appeared.
159537: A woman from Elversele ran a café together with her husband. One Sunday a musician from Elversele drove his cart to the fair in Sinaai. Seeing the many people riding along, the café owner, annoyed because she would be unable to serve beer to anyone that day, said: "They won't get far!" Five minutes later the axle of the cartwheel broke, so that all the people had to turn back.
159558: On a farm worked a farmhand who was out every night. One evening the farmer discovered the skin of kledde (a shape-shifting bogeyman) in a woodpile. When the farmer threw the skin into the burning oven, the farmhand was already standing beside him. They had to hold the farmhand back by force, or else he would have jumped into the oven.
159563: Some people were sowing grain in the field. Suddenly a woman came by, put her hand into the sack of grain and said: "You do have fine grain! I won't see such fine grain again in all my life". When the woman had gone and the farmer looked into the sack, he saw that all the grain had gone mouldy.
159565: On his way, a man from Ronse had kicked a cat that ran under his feet. At that the cat screamed. The next moment the man was surrounded by dozens of cats, so that the priest had to be fetched.
159585: On the road to the church of Beveren a devil dressed in black walked about. People going to early mass met the devil and were silently accompanied by him as far as the church. There the devil vanished again.
159591: A man from Denderhoutem going on pilgrimage to Halle stopped at an inn on the way. When he told the landlady he came from Denderhoutem, the woman replied: "Does the chapel of the Seven Sorrows still exist? I often went and sat on it with five others."
159592: In Elversele lived a rag-picker who had special powers. When a farmer drove home with a cart of hay, the witch often asked for some hay. If the farmer refused, the witch said: "You'll give me some hay all right, because you won't get home with it!" A little further on the hay cart overturned.
159613: On a farm, people saw a hand and a little later a leg fall out of the chimney by the open hearth.
159616: On 't Schreiberg (1) near the Duizend Appels neighbourhood, people used to hear the Roeper (the Caller). That was the soul of a French soldier from Napoleon's army. At night the soldier called out to the farmers who had murdered him.
159641: A woman had poured hot water on a black cat. The next day the woman was visited by a neighbour whose arm was completely burned.
159678: In Eksaarde there used to be a haunted castle. The haunting took place in a wing of the castle that had been converted into a farm.
159699: A man went to early Mass in the Zakdam (1) at four in the morning. On the way, at the Hoekput, the man kicked at a pack of cats that were roaming there. One of the cats fell into the water and a little later came out in the form of a human.
159707: A farmer's wife from Orroir could not churn butter. Instead of butter she found a ball of hair in the butter churn. Afterwards the farmer's wife went to the friars to have the evil driven out.
159747: On a farm in Ramscheute a big rat was always running around. No one managed to catch the animal. When two animals had died on the farm, the vets were called. While the vets were in the barn, two more animals died in the stable. The vets advised the farmer to go to the friars in Gent. A friar came to the farm and said that the same thing was happening on three other farms. He also said: "Don't worry. Nothing will go wrong now." After that the rat was never seen again.
159764: In an old tree stump behind a farm, a farmer found a bearskin. After the farmer had thrown the skin into the burning oven, the stable hand came running up. He cried that he was in terrible pain and begged the farmer not to burn the skin. So the farmer gave his farmhand the skin back.
159767: Every Friday evening a woman went to help the priest of Ottergem. When the woman reached Erondegem, she was followed by a black cat. At midnight the woman arrived at the priest's house, where the cat sat down on the doorstep. The moment the priest came to open the door, the cat promptly vanished. The priest said to the woman: "Yes, that is a dead woman who comes back."
159813: In the old days many lights could be seen in Ouwegem. People claimed they were the little souls of dead children who came back.
159906: If a witch could not do harm to other people, she herself became the victim of the evil. In Steenhuize a witch became paralysed in this way.
159931: A giant once lived in Viane. One day the giant decided to leave the region. On the way, both his legs got stuck in the ground. That is how two deep pits came to be on the Herhout in Tollembeek. After much pulling and tugging he freed himself and went past Tollembeek towards Geraardsbergen. On the border of Atembeke and Galmaarden the giant shook the mortar off his right foot. That lump of mortar became the Bosberg. A little further on the giant did the same with his left foot, and there the Oudenberg was formed.
159933: A man from Bachout returning from Sinaai heard rumbling and ringing on the way and felt the werewolf sitting on his back. When he got home the man died of fright.
159935: Will-o'-the-wisps sat on the hedges in the evening. No one could reach those lights. People claimed they were the little souls of unbaptised children.
159966: In a house in Sint-Cornelis-Horebeke a woman had visited and played with the little child. Afterwards the child became completely emaciated and a few days later it was dead. Strangely enough, the child had also suddenly grown a horse's tail fifteen centimetres long. The people had been to the friars and had put an Easter nail under the threshold, so that the witch could no longer get in.
159968: In a house, the children stopped growing after a sorceress had visited. The people went to Affligem, where the monks advised them to examine the cradle. The parents found lice all over the cradle. The sorceress had put them there. After the people had cleaned the cradle, they had no more problems.
159983:
In a room a light could sometimes be seen appearing at night, which said: "I am Oostakker, I am Geeraardsbergen, …" That was the spirit of a returned dead person who had promised to go on pilgrimage but had not fulfilled that promise.
In the same way the French general Geoffrey cried: "debout les morts!" (rise up, ye dead!), and that is how the battle of the Marne turned out the way it did. (?)
160001: A farmer was working in the field together with a friend. When the two men went somewhere for a glass of beer, the farmer forgot to take his hatchet along. When he returned, the hatchet had disappeared. The farmer went home and told his pregnant wife what had happened. During the whole of the woman's pregnancy the hatchet remained invisible. On the day the child was born, a woman threw the hatchet into the farmer's garden. Then the child began to cry. Nine days later the child stopped crying after the friars of Gent had been consulted. A witch had bewitched that hatchet. The people put a little cross above their door, so that the witch no longer came in. When she was once explicitly invited in anyway, she refused.
160010: On a farm no one dared go behind the barn in the evening. A curious woman who wanted to get to the bottom of it went to look behind the barn and saw someone there dressed entirely in black.
160026: If a child had not grown a month after its birth, it was bewitched. One then had to go on pilgrimage to Gent for the child. An Easter nail was then placed on the child's cradle, after which it recovered. A bewitched child could sometimes also get 'the old man'.
160040: A Swiss shepherd who had stayed on in Hofstade after the French Revolution was a werewolf. The shepherd was away every night. When one day his skin was found, the oven was heated and the skin thrown in. At that moment the man was crying and raving with pain.
160064: A woman had to wait in the street for an hour before she could cross, because there were rats running everywhere. Those rats had been sent by someone.
160115: A man visiting his brother one evening saw a beautiful white rabbit with red eyes sitting in the churchyard. The man decided to catch the animal on his way back. But when his brother came along with him, he advised him not to catch the rabbit, because witchcraft was probably involved. The two went home by another road. Neither of them ever saw a white rabbit again.
160162: A mother whose five-year-old child had not been baptised was visited one day by a woman who said: "You must have that child baptised". The mother heard at least twenty cats yowling and kicked at them, but she could not hit a single animal. At night the child began to cry and a quarter of an hour later it was dead. The mother was convinced the visitor had bewitched her child. She went to the visitor's house, but that woman turned out to be gone.
160169: The son of a handloom weaver had to go and buy new bobbins from a woman. On his way home, however, the boy met a 'loetie' (a werewolf), which took his bobbins from him and bit into them. When the boy told at home what had happened to him, he looked at his father and then said: "Now I know who the loetie was. It was you, father, because the yarn is between your teeth."
160194: If one hears a magpie chattering, one can expect news.
160220: In the Zeedijkstraat, which was later renamed 'Veerstraat', a man said to his girlfriend: "Are you afraid of dogs? If you meet one, throw your handkerchief at the animal." The girl did as she had been advised. When the dog was gone and her boyfriend appeared again, the girl saw that he had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
160223: People chased by a 'berewulf' (werewolf) could get rid of the creature by throwing a handkerchief or an apron at it. The werewolf had to tear the cloth into little pieces, which gave the people time to get away.
160248: In Vloesbergen the parish priest preached that there was no more filth in his parish. A boy who had studied for the priesthood put it to the test and stuck an Easter nail under the church door. Because of this, ten women could not leave the church after mass. When the priest asked the boy what he had done, he answered: "I wanted to see whether it was true that there is no more filth in the parish."
160253: A woman claimed that at night she had seen a black hand of her mother's in a sheet. In the morning that hand lay in a sheet beside her.
160325: In Sint-Barbara a nun sat praying beside another nun who could not die. At a certain moment the devil came in and scratched the prayer book. That book was kept for a long time. Later the children who went to school there were very afraid when they had to pass the room where the devil had appeared.
160334: A man coming home by bicycle during the war saw a signpost to Sint-Lievens-Essche by the church of Sint-Antelinckx. The man knew he had to go right, but still lost his way because he had been ridden by the mare.
160360: In a house in Temse where the people were eating, a woman came to ask for a slice of bread. When the farmer's wife sent the woman away, the latter said: "Just wait, you misers, you won't be eating much longer!" When the farmer's wife cut another slice, she found that a rat had been baked into the bread.
160362: A girl had to go and cut clover in very cold weather. A gentleman came by, saw that the girl was crying from the cold, and said: "I will do your work, but you must promise me that the first thing you tie tomorrow morning will be mine." The girl agreed. The gentleman was after the girl herself, for the first thing one tied in the morning was an apron. But the girl knew better and the next morning first tied a bundle of straw. And so the gentleman was tricked.
160387: A witch who could not unload all her magic power on her neighbours bewitched her own children. The children, although they were all big strong fellows, died one by one.
160391: A boy had to clean the stable while his parents were at early Mass. After finishing the job, the boy fell asleep in the hayloft. A while later he woke up and heard his mother's footsteps. But the boy could not move. After that incident the boy never slept in the hay again. Such things could not happen if one had laid one's socks crossed by the bed.
160412: In the evening you had to be home before midnight, or else you would be surrounded by cats. The more you kicked at the cats, the more animals appeared. It was not customary to catch cats to eat them. If someone had done so, a thousand cats would later be seen sitting on that person's grave.
160415: In the past people sometimes put an Easter nail under the door to keep evil out of the stables.
160416: In Liedekerke lived a witch of whom the children were afraid. That witch sometimes made the animals ill.
160442: A man who had gone to collect lacework in the evening and was walking from Lebeke (Denderhoutem) to Kerksken saw that the winnowing mill in the meadow was all lit up. When the man came closer, he saw that the mill sails were full of candles. The man woke the miller. The miller came to look and said: "That must be a witch who did this to me". He set the mill turning, so that the little lights all flew away.
160563: A woman who had gone to cut grass for her rabbits met someone on her way home, who said: "Empty that sack, because that is not grass." The woman emptied the sack and saw rats crawling out of it.
160566: In Moerbeke lived a man whose mother-in-law was suspected of being a witch. After her death the witch came to wake her son-in-law every night at twelve o'clock. One day the man went upstairs and asked: "What do you want? Do you want masses? I will have them said." But there was no answer, and the man never heard anything again.
160589: In an orchard in Vlekkem stood an uninhabited, dilapidated house. One evening a man who lived in the Kattembos went to see his girlfriend together with his stable hand. When the two men were going home late that evening, they saw a light burning in the little house in the orchard. They crept up to it and saw a lavishly laid table at which beautiful young ladies sat eating. Maids in white aprons were walking about. When the stable hand's knee suddenly slipped off the windowsill with a bang, the light in the house went out and the whole scene vanished. The man had recognised several of those present, but he never wanted to name any of them.
160622: In a house in Steenhuize-Wijnhuize, all sorts of paw prints were always seen around the stove in the morning. Because the people found this strange, they decided to keep watch one night. They had loaded a gun with rosary beads. That night, however, they saw nothing unusual.
160674: When someone had died somewhere, people did not dare to walk past the house of the deceased for fear that they would die too. A black cloth was hung on a house of mourning so that people knew they had to start praying. When that cloth had fallen to the ground, no one dared to pick it up.
160707: Three farmhands worked on a farm in Erpe. One evening a strong man was jumped on the back by kledde (a werewolf-like spook). The man managed to strike kledde a blow, and so the next day it was discovered that one of the farmhands was kledde.
160710: A group of women were sitting in a ditch in Voorde. When they saw a woman passing by, they began to laugh loudly. The passer-by hurried away. When she got home, she found that all sorts of things had gone wrong on her farm. A cow had died and some horses and pigs had miscarried. Witches always enjoyed it when they could do people harm.
160728: A girl was taking a walk with her little sister. At the railway she met an old woman who tapped the child on the cheek and said: "Oh, what a lovely child you are!" When the woman was not even fifty metres further on, the child began to cry incessantly. The child's mother sent for the doctor, but he could not find the cause of the problem. A woman advised the mother to go to the friars of Edingen. The friars said prayers until they were drenched in sweat, because they had to strain hard to free the child from the evil.
160736: Three men on their way to Lokeren saw a young kitten walking on the road. One of the men kicked the kitten, knocking it unconscious. The men grew frightened, but left the animal lying there and went on. When they arrived in Lokeren, they saw the same kitten again. The man who had kicked the animal collapsed.
160769: A cow had been stolen from a witch in Ename. When the witch came to Mater, she heard her cow lowing there and went to fetch the animal back.
160790: Witches could fly away at night. They would say: "Over hedge and over verge, to the wine cellar in Brussels." A man got the charm wrong. He said: "Through hedge and through verge, to the wine cellar in Brussels." That man arrived at his destination badly injured.
160797: A farmer who consorted with the devil and owned an animal skin was at work in his field. At a certain moment someone found the farmer's skin and threw it into the oven. The next moment the farmer came running to save his skin. They had to hold him back, or else he would have jumped into the oven.
160817: A man from Bazel whose wife was about to give birth went to Haasdonk to fetch his mother. When the man was in the Schrijnwegen, a tree there suddenly broke in two. The branches were torn from the tree and a hellish noise could be heard. When the man reached his mother, he hardly dared go back home. His mother, however, was not afraid because she always carried a relic with her. The two reached the man's wife without any trouble.
160837: In Grotenberge lived a farmer whose animals were always ill. The animals were sometimes even thrown up against the ceiling. The farmer was advised to put Easter nails under the door of his stable. After that he had no more problems with his animals.
160864: 'Berewulven' (werewolves) were people who had dressed up in a bearskin and who jumped on late passers-by and had themselves carried to their homes. These people hid their skin in a woodpile. They had to stand at a crossroads at midnight with a black hen under their arm and renounce their faith. Then they received a note with instructions on what to do.
160872: A man playing cards in a café saw a woman come in and sit down there. When the man's mother came into the café and asked him to come home, the man refused to go with her. A little later the mother came back with a black cat. She put the cat on the table in front of her son and cried: "Play cards with that!" The café owner grabbed the cat and threw it against a tree. The next day the woman who had been sitting in the café had two black eyes.
160891: In a house in Ronse two cats always came in in the evening to warm themselves. When one evening the cats sang "May we have a little milk?", the woman poured boiling milk over the animals. The next day two old women from the neighbourhood lay in bed with burns on their faces.
160899: A man was bound to a chair. He could only get up after the priest allowed it. That priest could work magic.
160921: A man coming home along the paved road one evening suddenly saw a witch standing beside him, although there had been nobody on the road before. "What are you doing here?" the man asked. The next moment the woman had vanished.
160942: A man coming back from the inn one evening saw as many as three hundred cats running before his feet.
160960: On a farm that was bewitched, many animals died. The friars had to come to that farm.
160962: A witch had given a packet of biscuits to a child. The child's mother took the biscuits away to burn them in the stove. The biscuits would not burn, however, so they had to be thrown away.
160998: In the past people put an Easter nail under the door to make sure no witches could come in. Sometimes Easter nails were also placed under the threshold or under the pillow of a bewitched child.
161020: In Viane there once lived an old woman whom everyone feared because she was believed to be a witch. After that witch had been at the farm, the farmer's wife had said: "Now not a single hen will lay an egg!" That indeed turned out to be the case.
161059: A poacher went every evening with his gun to 't Gootje, where he had often seen three little white rabbits sitting. The poacher had tried several times to shoot at the rabbits, but his gun never worked at that moment.
161064: A man who was baking cakes saw a cat crawl in through the drain hole for the water and said: "Look, pretty pussycat, go and sit under the stove". The cat said of one of the pancakes: "That one is for me". Assuming that the cat had something to do with evil, the man threw a hot pancake at the animal. The cat then cried: "Mie is burnt". The next day four women from the village were walking around with burnt faces.
161084: People who were ridden by the mare felt that something was sitting on them, squeezing their throat shut. To protect themselves against the mare, people placed one clog with the heel and the other with the toe pointing towards the bed.
161091: It was haunted at 't Kort Haagske in the Ysebertstraat. When the gentlemen of Nokere drove past there in their horse-drawn carriages to the station of Olsene, their horses often took fright and bolted. In the evening people heard noises in the air there. Along the side of the road people saw a white disc.
161110: In the old days people always saw lights on the water and above a pit in the field. They believed these lights were lost little souls for whom one had to pray a great deal.
161116: A woman who often believed she was the victim of witchcraft sometimes saw a white powder lying by her door. One day her husband said: "Damn, there's white powder there and two pigeons are dead".
161165: A woman who was kneading bread suddenly stood stock-still with her arms in the trough. Some people went to fetch the priest. When the clergyman arrived, he said the witch had 'left her spirit'. Someone went to warn the woman's mother. That mother remained very calm and said: "It's not serious. I'll come along in a moment". The mother calmly cooked porridge and then went along with the people. She sent those present away with the words: "You have no business here". Then she stood by her daughter and said: "Our little cow has calved". Then the woman regained her spirit and asked: "Is it a heifer?"
161182: On a farm in Zegelsem people saw a candle sitting in a tree. It was a dead person who had come back. The light came from the ghost's mouth. The dead who came back had usually hidden money somewhere.
161256: A man from Idegem went to visit his girlfriend in Sint-Maria-Oudenhove. As he walked home in the evening with a friend, he heard beautiful music near a little wood, which was also lit up. When the two men came closer, one had a violin and the other a barrel organ pressed into his hands. At first the men had great fun, but in the end they grew tired and made the sign of the cross to stop the sorcery. One man was holding a clog and the other was turning the tail of a tomcat.
161273: During High Mass a woman always walked around the stables. People did not want to let that woman near their children because they were afraid she would harm them. That woman had 'the name', that is, a reputation for witchcraft. She was said to have already caused many animals to die in stables elsewhere.
161297: A mother whose daughter had fallen went to Merksem on a friend's advice. A healer lived there who received her clients in a small cellar room. The mother had to go to that healer every month. When she came back, her daughter could walk, but by the end of the month the child could no longer walk again. The mother had to burn a candle in the lid of a shoe polish tin and lay a medal in front of that tin. The candle had to burn down to a certain point. From the soot the healer then read what the child had to do. At eleven o'clock at night the mother heard a sound as if a heavy horse was walking past, but there was nothing to be seen. One morning the daughter woke up around half past five. She sat up and seemed to be looking at something. When her mother asked what she was looking at, the girl answered: "I'm not looking at anything". The priest was called to read prayers over the girl. The clergyman put Easter nails under the threshold and said: "Now she can't get in anymore". The next moment knocking was heard under the cupboard.
161314: If people saw a black crow, they could expect misfortune. When, for example, such a crow was seen while someone in the house was ill, one could be sure that the person's health would worsen.
161317: A woman who had terrible toothache went on a pilgrimage to Mespelare with her husband. When the two stopped at an inn on the way to eat their sandwiches, the landlady asked: "You must come from near Aaigem?", and the man said yes. The landlady went on: "Then you know where the Dikke Linde stands. I went there often and had a lot of fun there. But I am glad that it is over now."
161332: A farmer on whose farm a hare was always running about had two bullets blessed by a priest. When he saw the hare running again, the farmer sat by the window with his gun at the ready. But when he fired, his gun did not go off. The further the hare ran, the bigger it grew.
161387: In the Zuurstraat in Voorde two poachers were waiting for hares. Suddenly a hare on three legs came running up and asked whether the other hares had not passed by yet. The men were so shocked by this that they ran away at once.
161407: One evening, on her way home, a woman saw a fierce wind rise up. Because she was frightened, she ran home quickly. When she reached her house, she saw a man dressed in black with a large umbrella walking there. A moment later the man had vanished without a trace.
161408: A lane in Sint-Denijs-Boekel was haunted. A frightened man who thought he had seen the ghost did not dare go home alone and had someone go with him. When the men came closer, they saw that the 'ghost' was a blown-over tree.
161413: In Voorde there lived a man who could drive away rats. That man had to leave a gap open through which the rats could run away. The last rat that ran away waved its little paw.
161430: A nine-year-old boy who had gone to help his mother pick hops had to go home with a wheelbarrow at about nine in the evening. A man went with him. When the two came to a little bridge, the boy could not get across it with his wheelbarrow. The man tried too, but he could not do it either. The boy's dog was also very restless. When the boy had to cross the bridge with the wheelbarrow the next day, it worked. Later people found out that the man was the son of a witch.
161431: It was said of the daughter of a sorcerer from Bevere that she had special powers. A man who was trying to shoot a hare near this daughter's house had already fired several shots in vain. Then the girl said: "You can shoot another twenty times, you won't hit a single hare." The man fired about three more times, but the daughter was proved right. So people had to believe she had special powers. When the man walked past the daughter's house, he said: "I have to restrain myself, because I'd like to put a bullet in your backside!" To which the daughter replied: "You'll need your bullets on your way home!" The man had set off for home at ten in the evening and only reached his house at half past four in the morning, although he had less than five hundred metres to walk. He had got lost and had to wander about all night.
161465: In houses where fat women lived, tapping on the windows was always heard in the evening. One night the rural policeman kept watch at such a house. At midnight a large figure crawled on four legs to the window. The policeman fired his gun but could not hit the beast.
161468: In Erpe near Zevekote, a white lady was seen flying past every night at twelve o'clock. People believed it was a woman from the neighbourhood who had come back.
161473: A woman had lived her whole life in a quarrel with her neighbours, because they had unjustly taken a piece of her field. After her death her ghost always walked back and forth on that piece of field in the evening. Only after a chapel was built on that spot did the dead woman stop appearing. In 1931 the chapel was demolished because it stood in the middle of the field. The parish priest said the chapel should not be rebuilt in another place.
161494: In the old days a ball about fifty centimetres across could sometimes be seen rolling along the street. The ball rolled through the gate towards a farm's woodpile. It pushed against the wood, so that the whole yard was strewn with wood. When people went outside afterwards, there was nothing unusual to be seen at the woodpile.
161555: A man was coming back in the dark from a visit to his girlfriend, who lived five kilometres away. On the way the man was followed by a rabbit. When he noticed that the rabbit kept following him, the man became afraid. Moreover, the rabbit grew bigger and bigger. When the man looked back and saw that the rabbit had already become as big as a calf, he ran as fast as he could to the farm where he worked as a stable hand. The man quickly climbed the ladder to his sleeping place above the horse stable. He saw the rabbit's head in front of the horse stable. The man then shut the door and did not sleep a wink all night. In the morning the rabbit was gone.
161563: A farm in Volkegem was haunted. But it also often happened that some joker threw stones at the farm door.
161568: A woman who was ridden by the mare was thrown to the ground and seized by the throat, so that she was frozen with fear.
161623: A farmer who had been working in his field all day had hardly anything to show for it in the evening. Suddenly a strange gentleman in fine clothes came along and said: "If you sell me your soul, I will manure your field tonight." The farmer accepted the offer and the next day his field was manured.
161626: A mother went with her child to the fair in Bevere. At the fair an old woman had stroked the child. When the mother came home, her child was completely weakened and cried all the time. The child was bewitched.
161658: If a witch could not get at a certain person, she made sure that person had misfortune with the animals in his stable. People then sent for the friars to pray.
161688: On a farm there was much misfortune. Now something in the house was broken, then cows died. They sent for a friar, who asked for a bucket of water. In that water the people saw the face of the culprit appear; it was the neighbour woman.
161689: In the old days two pedlars with a large basket often came to Vlekkem. Every time those pedlars came to a farm, they dropped something, such as a pin or a needle. Afterwards something always went wrong with the animals. When the five cows became restless, the vet did not know what to do. After the farmer's wife had given the cows blessed bread, the animals calmed down again. When the pedlars came again after that, everything they had dropped on the floor was thrown into the stove. After that people were no longer troubled by the evil hand.
161714: A cowherd who dressed up as kledde (a shape-shifting bogeyman) was always away in the evening. One day the boy's skin was found in a tree stump. When the skin had been thrown into the oven, they had to hold the boy back, or else he would have jumped into the fire to save his skin. The boy cried: "Why did you burn my skin?
