I only had a few more days to go about as kledde! What will become of me now?"
161740: 't Kastanjen hof' was haunted. There were always cats there, which suddenly vanished without a trace. Kledde was there too.
161741:
A brewer always had a great deal of money because he had sold his soul to the devil. Every Friday a black tomcat sat in the brewery cellar, pointing with its right paw at the stone under which the gold coins lay. That cat was the devil. One day the brewer had thrown something at the cat. The next day he found that his wife had lost a hand.
The brewer could also foretell the future. Once he predicted that at half past eight in the evening 101 soldiers would come out of the street next to the brewery, marching in 25 rows of four. The last soldier would be a lame man, who marched alone and would come and ask people what time it was. And so it happened.
161752: A man had to deliver maize to a woman who was suspected of being a sorceress. The man carried a sack of a hundred kilos upstairs. When he was on the ladder, the second-to-last rung broke, so that the man fell. A little later the sorceress came to ask what was the matter, to which the man replied: "You know that very well, because you bewitched me."
161788: A man was always followed by a black cat. He believed the animal had something to do with evil.
161833: If a black crow sat on the roof of a house where a sick person lay, that sick person would die.
161845: In the old days the graveyards were often haunted. A man walking past the beguines heard a whistling there and walked on. At the graveyard the man saw a ghost walking with a burning candle in its backside.
161904: On a farm lived a farmhand who was often away at night. One day the farmer found a skin that belonged to the farmhand. While the farmhand was away, the farmer burned the skin in the oven. A little later the farmhand came running up in tears to save his skin. After the skin had burned up, the farmhand was freed.
161938: In Temse there lived a witch who sometimes went to ask a farmer for something. If the farmer refused, he afterwards had problems in his stable.
161941: A man walking home one Sunday evening walked past his own door. A bit further on he saw four little rabbits sitting by an uninhabited house. The man tried to catch the rabbits but did not succeed, and so he went home.
161946: In the past people believed that a swallow brought luck.
161955: At midnight a priest was out together with the sexton. On the way the two met a man. In Etikhove the priest asked the sexton: "What shall we do with him? Leave him standing or let him go home?" The priest bewitched the man so that he was stuck to the ground.
161981: One evening a man was walking home with his little black dog. The dog kept creeping between the man's legs because it was afraid. A little further on the man saw a sheet in the middle of the street. He did not get home that night.
162000: In Kemzeke there used to be small houses that were haunted. A black dog always appeared there. One day a woman broke her poker on the animal. Strangely enough, the dog was still alive afterwards. The people then went to fetch paasnagels (blessed Easter nails).
162029: A man coming home from work at night saw a bicycle on the road ahead of him. The cyclist said to the man: "I'm going to Hamme, but I'm nearly there." But the cyclist was riding in the wrong direction. The next day the man heard that the cyclist had wandered about all night and only found his house in the morning. The cyclist had probably been ridden by the mare.
162070: A young man had often been invited by an old woman to drink a cup of coffee and eat a piece of gingerbread at her house. Everyone advised the boy against it. But because he would not listen, he was bewitched and died.
162095: A man from Kwaremont was walking home at night with his father. The two men were followed by a cat and the son kicked at the animal. After that, however, he could not move on. Only when his father was a long way ahead did he notice that his son was not following and was still standing in the same spot.
162113: A woman went out with a friend whose mother was suspected of being a witch. The woman fell into the water, but her friend helped her out again.
162142: A man coming back from Kieldrecht was ridden by the mare. He rode around the hedge all night without being able to find his bearings and only got home very late.
162166: If a witch lived in the neighbourhood, she was often blamed when something had gone wrong somewhere. If a cow had died after that woman had visited, people believed she had bewitched the cow.
162226: A man out walking met a small woman with a hat. Because she was a sorceress, the man kicked at the woman. But he missed, and a moment later he no longer saw the figure. The sorceress could not get into a certain house because an Easter nail was stuck under the door.
162244: A man who had hidden money somewhere died before he could tell anyone where his money was. After the man's death a light was seen that pointed out the spot where the money lay. After the money had been found, the dead man was released.
162262: A woman who had always been close to her father constantly felt after his death that he was with her.
162268: In Hamme there once lived a witch who could turn herself into a magpie. Every night the magpie flew about. When people saw a magpie in the evening, they were afraid, because then they knew what was going on.
162283: At Sint-Laries-linde there used to be white rabbits that circled around late walkers.
162290: In a café where there was much dancing and cursing, someone said one evening: "This will go on until the devils themselves come," to which those present replied: "Let them come." Suddenly a gentleman dressed in black came in. He wore a black top hat and had a large black dog with him. Those present went on dancing and cursing until they saw that the gentleman had horse's legs. At that moment everyone fled. The gentleman flew up into the air with his dog, and a whole pack of dogs came to meet them.
162314: In a brewery, as many as twelve cats were seen coming in, crying: "Shall we, shall we". A farmhand poured boiling water over the animals. The next day several women from the village wore a bandage around their arm or foot.
162343: An old woman had died in a fire at a farm on the Pollarekassei. A year later her ghost returned at All Saints to say that people must pray more, or else another house would burn down.
162380: If a sorceress passed a field where a farmer was sowing, the seed did not come up.
162410: In the old days people did not dare to walk past the churchyard in the evening, because they were afraid they would see glowing skulls there. These were said to be the souls of the dead who were not allowed into heaven.
162432: A man who had been stabbed to death came haunting. After a while a cross was placed at the haunted spot. One day a letter hung on the cross bearing the murderer's name. The murderer, however, had also already died.
162441: In a café in Ronse where there was dancing, a gentleman with horse's legs came in.
162466: On the Leeuwarde in Zegelsem the spirit of a man walked about who had moved a boundary post during his life. The ghost kept calling: "Where shall I put it? Where shall I put it?" A drunkard answered: "Put it where you got it." After the ghost had put the post back, it was released.
162472: In Hamme lived a woman who could turn herself into a spider.
162474: A woman coming home from work in the evening was often jumped on along the way by a werewolf that had itself carried. Werewolves had sold their souls to the devil. If their skin was burned, they died. Usually the priests were sent for when such a skin had to be burned.
162497: On a farm, every morning at three o'clock, a horse came and hung its muzzle over the half-door.
162517: On a farm in Woubrechtegem lived a woman suspected of being a sorceress. On another farm the people and animals were victims of witchcraft. One day the farmer's wife cut off a paw of a cat that always came there, using a poker. The next day people said the sorceress had lost a leg.
162518: A house in Welden was haunted. There were always white mice running around in that house. If a sorceress came into a house where there was a little child, the child fell ill.
162557: A woman went to mass in Denderwindeke every day. At the chapel of Our Lady of Seven Sorrows she saw two men carrying a coffin. She also heard a voice say: "Pray more."
162574: A woman had seen a whole brass band playing above the trees in the Kapelledreef.
162575: A farmer's wife had a farmhand who worked well but sometimes also dressed up in bearskins. One day the farmhand was sent away so that the bearskin could be burned in the oven in the meantime. When the skin had caught fire, the farmhand came home sweating to take the skin out of the oven. After the skin had burned up, the farmhand was freed.
162637: Two children had died shortly after birth. Before the birth someone had been asked to be godfather, but of course nobody knew that two children would be born instead of one. When the godfather came to the churchyard, he heard a voice call: "It's my godfather!", to which another voice said: "It's my godfather!" The man went to the parish priest and told him what he had heard. The priest then went to the churchyard and said: "This man is godfather to you both." After that nothing strange was heard again.
162664: A man had gone and stood at a crossroads of six roads with a black hen in order to sell his soul. Then a gentleman in fine clothes and with horse's legs came walking up.
162676: A man who had been playing cards all evening claimed he was not afraid of ghosts. When the man walked home, he was surrounded by as many as a thousand cats, so that he could not get home.
162717: A mother who was about to give birth to her fourth child was visited by a witch from the neighbourhood, who came to ask how things were going. Shortly after the child was born during the night, the witch came again and said: "How is the child? It won't stay good for long." After that the child began to cry ceaselessly. The mother went on pilgrimage to the friars of Ghent. When she came home, her child was dead. Then the witch began to bewitch the mother's six-year-old daughter. At night the daughter saw the dead child in a ball. When she opened her eyes, she saw a black cat sitting on the windowsill, which would not be chased away. The girl then went to stay with her grandmother and was thereby freed from the witchcraft.
162718: A man heard a car drive past but saw nothing. Such things happened quite often. It was a sorceress from the neighbourhood who caused those strange phenomena. If a sorceress had someone's handkerchief, she already had power over that person.
162751: A man wandered around a meadow all night because he could not find the gap in the fence. That man had been ridden by the mare.
162753: In the old days, when people had had a bad dream, they believed they had been ridden by the mare.
162845: A sorceress lived in Nijken (a hamlet of Denderwindeke). A man who wanted to pick the peas in his garden had picked only one pea when he heard a voice call: "Leave those peas alone."
162847: In Mater there lived a woman who was said to be able to work magic. The children were not allowed to accept marshmallows from that woman.
162854: A man from Smeerhebbe saw a white apparition in the churchyard at night that said: "The day is for you and the night is for me". The man was so frightened that he quickly pulled the door of his house shut.
162856: In Overboelare there lived an old widow about whom people whispered that she was a witch. In reality that woman could do no more than anyone else. When a child in a house fell ill after that woman had visited, people believed the woman had bewitched the child. The people then sent for the parish priest.
162909: In Ottergem there lived a man who could do anything. When he stood in the doorway, he could make passers-by stand still. The man owned many books that were kept in a little room no one was allowed to enter.
162910: A werewolf who was possessed by evil and owned a skin had sold his soul to the devil. When his master was about to burn his skin, the farmhand suffered great pain. Afterwards, though, he was freed.
162913: A farm near the castle of Moregem was haunted. The blankets were eaten there, and at night there was so much noise that the occupants went deaf within fourteen days. All night long people heard the plates on the mantelpiece dancing and the butter churn turning. The milk pails made noise too. When people went to look in the morning, there was nothing strange to be seen.
162914: Some people who could not churn butter went to the friars, who came to bless everything. The people also had to make a novena. The friars said that within nine days someone would come to ask for a jug of milk. On the eighth day a neighbour woman did indeed come for milk. That neighbour was suspected of having caused the evil, although in reality it was someone else, who had once passed by there.
162915:
A farmhand working on a farm near the Munkbos owned a wolfskin with which he had to roam about as a werewolf. One day the werewolf had jumped on a man.
When the farmhand's skin was found and thrown into the oven, the farmhand immediately came running to save his skin. But he was too late. Shortly afterwards the farmhand died.
162951: On a farm in Temse lived a woman who could make mice by dipping a cloth in water. Every drop that then fell from the cloth turned into a mouse.
162966: After a dog had been heard howling in Zottegem, a young person in the street died.
162967: A boy who had been out had to pass a crossroads around midnight. He saw a large white sheet lying there. Just as he was about to pick it up, a big rooster jumped up. The boy was startled and went home frightened. The rooster followed him all the way to his door.
162982: A woman going to the fair came close to a house in Kruishoutem where a witch was staying. The woman felt so ill that she had to lie down on the bed. People all claimed she had been bewitched by that witch.
162999: On a farm worked a farmhand who had sold his soul. When the farmer went to fetch his two horses from the meadow in the evening, there were not two but three horses. The farmer believed his farmhand was responsible. Then the farmhand ran away. He was never seen again.
163003: In Lozer wood there stood a mill that was badly haunted.
163005: A carter out late in the evening saw a white ghost in the distance that made the horses restless. The carter walked up to the ghost and stamped on it. At that moment the carter was surrounded by flames.
163010: Some farmhands who went to plough the field always saw a black dog churning up the ploughed furrows. The farmhands tried to shoot the dog dead, but did not succeed. After they had a bullet blessed, they were able to hit the dog. When they got back to the farm, they found the farmer lying dead in his bed.
163072: At a wedding party a drunk man had lost his way. People said that the man had been 'led by the day'.
163102: On a farm in Vlekkem no butter could be made and the calves died. A parish priest who came to look at the farm told the people that the trouble might be caused by someone who was dead. After the friar's visit there was no more misfortune on the farm.
163105: In Doel there once lived a woman who had special powers. When that woman had been in a barn, all the newborn calves there died.
163126: A farmer noticed that his farmhand was never home at night. One day the farmer found under a woodpile the skin with which his farmhand dressed up as kledde (a shape-shifting bogeyman). When the farmer had thrown the skin into the fire, the farmhand was suddenly standing beside him. The young man suffered terrible pain, but when the skin had burned, he was freed.
163129: A clog maker from Sint-Denijs-Boekel was ridden by the mare. The man managed to get home all the same. There he grabbed his hatchet, after which he saw the mare leave through the water drain hole.
163154: A house was so badly haunted every night that the occupants decided to go and live elsewhere. The evil went with them, however, so that the people could not sleep at night in their new home either. They sent for the friars, who put an end to the haunting.
163155: A man whose wife had died remarried a young girl. One evening the man went to fetch his young wife from the school in Waregem. When the man and the girl were nearly in Nokere, they saw ahead of them a fine funeral procession with four horses and a hearse. On either side of the hearse walked a red lady who wore strange clothes and held a lantern. As soon as the couple came closer, the people in the procession immediately stepped aside to let them through. The girl was so sick with fear that she refused to go back to the brothers in Waregem. One of the brothers said to the man: "You must persuade her to come back to school. The next time you go home in the evening, I will go with you." No sooner said than done. When the couple went to Nokere again, the farmer walked a short distance behind them. As soon as the man saw anything, he was to give the brother a sign. The man saw the funeral procession appear again and immediately warned the brother. The clergyman went ahead and a moment later the procession had vanished. Since then the man and the girl never saw the funeral procession again.
163205: A man coming home one night was pestered on the Bosberg by a cat that kept running around him. When the man had kicked the animal, he was suddenly surrounded by as many as a thousand cats.
163226: Some boys who had mocked a witch could not sleep at night and felt as if something was being thrown on them.
163248: A man who was sawing a tree stump suddenly saw a pigeon fall into the water. His friend said: "Come on, let's get that pigeon." The men crept along the bank towards the pigeon with a stick. A moment later, however, the pigeon had vanished without a trace, without anyone seeing it fly away.
163261: A four-year-old boy always saw dogs at night. His parents took the boy to the friars, where he was given a bread roll and a prayer he had to say. The next day no more strange things happened to the boy.
163275: A woman asked a farmer for a piece of field to plant ten rows of potatoes. After the farmer had said he did not rent out potato fields, the woman said to the neighbours: "They won't eat potatoes there this year either." Later the farmer dug up fine fat potatoes. But they could not be eaten, because they all began to rot.
163304: In Wortegem a man had died who had promised during his life to have many Masses said. The man's son always saw a beast sitting in the corner of the hayloft at night, which said: "Whether you sleep or whether you wake, your neck I'll break." One day the son found a pot of money in that corner. At that moment he remembered his father's promise. After the son had had the promised Masses said, the beast did not appear again.
163309: In the old days people were often ridden by the mare. To protect themselves against the mare, they had to place their clogs upside down next to their bed.
163324: One evening a woman was returning from a visit to her sister in town. In the Stuurstraat the woman felt something heavy jump onto her foot. She put her other foot forward and felt the heavy creature settle on her other foot. The woman began to sweat and screamed in despair. In the end she went to the little chapel of Our Lady, where she prayed the Gospel of St John. After that the woman was delivered from the evil.
163373: A man who was friends with a wizard's son went to evening school in winter. Although the man knew the way well, he got lost. The next day the wizard's son asked him, laughing: "You surely didn't get home easily yesterday? That was my father."
163382: A man walking past the churchyard saw a white ghost there letting its hand hang over the wall.
163385: In a village there was a house that was always full of rats. In that house lived a mother whose youngest son fell ill. The father's mother was a sorceress. One day the children's mother lay ill in bed. Before leaving for work, the father said to his children: "If mother comes and gives you something, you must not eat it!" When their grandmother came to visit, the children were sitting around the stove. They each got an apple from their grandmother. The smallest child bit into the apple, although his older brother tried to stop him. After the grandmother left, the youngest son began to pine. They put the boy in his bed. He saw mice crawling all over the ceiling and the churning bench. The parish priest came to bring a relic, but that did not help. Although it was wartime and people were afraid of the Germans, the child's father dared to go on pilgrimage to Edingen. But because the man was a liberal, the friars would not listen to him. The son died after being ill for two years.
163440: A farmer had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a new barn. The barn was finished after just three days. At the end of his life the farmer had to go with the devil.
163462: In Huise there lived an ugly woman who was said to be a witch. Whenever that woman was nearby, people always hid their children. Once, when that woman had visited someone, those people's child had fallen ill.
163467: A girl who was attacked on the way by a devil threw a spool of yarn at the apparition. The devil had to pull all the threads loose, which gave the girl the chance to run away. When she got home, the girl saw her boyfriend standing there. He had the threads of the spool between his teeth. He was the devil.
163530: A mother whose child was ill went to a healer in Merksem. Together with the others present, the woman had to hold a stick in her hand. Whoever could hold the stick longest would be cured. Although the mother held the stick longest, her child died anyway. Moreover, a rattling of pots and pans could be heard in her house.
163531: People who dealt in evil could take on all kinds of shapes. They could, for example, change into animals or monsters. In a house that creaks, many evil spirits are present.
163532: A man from near Aaigem who went to Wallonia to fetch coal went into a café for a glass of beer. After the landlady had asked him where he came from, she went on to ask: "Is the Dikke Linde still standing in Aaigem? I had fun there many nights when we gathered there, but that is over now."
163554: In Erwetegem there lived a woman suspected of being the patroness of the sorceresses. On a road where that woman had relieved herself, a man twice fell with his bicycle into the sorceress's urine. When people could not bake bread or churn butter, they blamed that sorceress.
163565: People who were ridden by the mare had a horrible dream. Many people from Viane went on pilgrimage to the Waterkasteel in Lessenbos to make a novena there so that they would no longer have bad dreams.
163593: A man who went to work on a farm usually came home late in the evening. On Saturdays he always got a small sack of grain from his master. When the man came to the Kistberg in the dark one Saturday evening with his sack on his back, he suddenly saw a large castle standing there, with lights burning inside. Through the windows the man saw people walking to and fro. Footmen stood at the gate. The man was frightened half to death, dropped his sack of grain and ran home to tell what he had seen. When the man went back to that place the next day, his sack of grain was still lying there, although it was worth a lot in those days.
163622: Werewolves were people who went out alone at night. They had to consort with the devil. They had also received a skin from the devil. People coming home from work were sometimes jumped on by a werewolf and had to carry him to their house.
163644: A house on the Capenberg was plagued by rats. A man who could drive away rats walked around the house three times and prayed the Gospel of Saint John. The man had to leave an opening through which the rats could run away. At the place the rats were sent to, they had to have as much food as in the house they came from.
163695: Two men out together saw an old woman coming from behind a house with a stick and two fine pears in her hand. The woman offered the pears to one of the men, but his friend said: "No, you mustn't accept them!" If the man had taken the pears, he would have been bewitched. If you went against a witch's will, she could do you no harm.
163750: 't Spookhol, a house on the heath in Waasmunster, was haunted. On Sundays at twelve o'clock four men always came there to play cards. Although the doors were locked, the men always got in. At a certain moment they were there, although no one had seen them arrive. After a while the men vanished from one moment to the next.
163756: In the past the Black Widow could be seen appearing in some places. She was a woman dressed entirely in black who wore a black hat with a veil. If one had seen the Black Widow somewhere, one could expect misfortune.
163758: In a street in Ronse there was haunting after a small chapel had been demolished. People claimed that the nun who had stood in its porch was coming back.
163759: At the 'kannebank' (dish rack) where people washed their dishes, a toad was seen every day. One day a woman poured boiling water over the animal. The next day a woman with burns was walking around the village.
163796: A witch who was doing the washing suddenly stood stock-still with her hands in the washtub. The people went to the parish priest, who said: "Just leave her. She will revive her life spirit herself." A little later the witch moved again.
163801: A woman always saw candles by a tree next to a fountain. When the tree was removed, hidden money was found there. After the money was found, the candles were no longer seen, since the ghost had been released.
163803: On the Lierenhoek in Sint-Martens-Lierde stood an old farm that was haunted. The friars went there once and banished the evil to the water for a hundred years. After that people were no longer troubled by the evil. In the room, though, there was a tile that could not be fixed in place by any means.
163829: A woman always heard knocking on her window at night and then saw a white shawl. One night she heard a voice call: "If you don't get up, I'll take your child. I am the devil's ghost." The woman saw a sorceress from the neighbourhood in the moonlight. The woman sat crying all night with her child on her lap.
163886: A pregnant woman had been given a little black dog by a wizard. The dog always came into the woman's room. Because her husband was annoyed by the animal, he gave it a kick. When the child was born, it turned out not to be healthy. The priest came to visit and asked the people whether they had been given a little dog. He predicted that the wizard would come to fetch his dog and advised the people to send that man away. The next day the wizard did indeed come by. After he was sent away, he was never seen again.
163907: A man who always encountered a hare was told by a priest: "Shoot at it, or it will be the end of you!" The man did as he was advised. The next day he found that he had shot his neighbour dead.
163917: A black cat often came into a house. One day the woman of the house poured boiling water on the animal. The next day she heard that a neighbour had burns on her face.
163964: When a cow was about to calve on a farm, a certain woman stood at the door listening whether all was going well. When there were problems, people believed that witch had caused them.
163965: A boy was courting a girl whose mother was a witch. His parents had often warned him about sorcery, but he did not want to abandon his girlfriend. One evening the boy had fallen asleep in his girlfriend's house. When he woke up, he heard his girlfriend and her mother say: "What shall we do? We'll let him sleep." Then the two women took something that lay under the chimney and rubbed themselves with it. After that they said: "Over hedges and over gates and back!" When the women had gone, the boy rubbed himself with the same ointment and said: "Through hedges and through gates." He arrived at his destination badly injured. His girlfriend then put the boy on her feet and went back with him over hedges and gates. The boy broke off the relationship immediately.
163968: If you met a cat at midnight, you must not kick the animal. Otherwise ten or twelve cats would come running up.
164021: In Sint-Maria-Horebeke there lived a sorceress who could do anything. A woman from the village went to the parish priest and said she was always tormented at the Zwalmbeek. When the woman had to go to that place again, she sent for the priest. The priest walked behind the woman. At the bridge the priest knocked (?). The sorceress had to run so hard that sparks flew from the stones.
164022: A man from Mere claimed he would never need a car because no one could travel as fast as he could. The man said: "I go to a secret place. I may not tell anyone where that place is. I turn to a corner, where my travelling companion appears. Then I put my toes on his feet and we both fly through the air at full speed." Once the man had been very frightened when he flew over the church, because his feet had nearly caught on the church tower.
164096: In the old days people never ate with their left hand, because they believed it brought the devil into the house. A knife lying on the table must never be spun around. When the knife came to rest, the person its point was aimed at would soon die.
164101: Almost every evening a man saw kledde (a werewolf-like spook) pass by his window. One evening he gathered some young people in his house, so that together they managed to stab kledde with a dung fork. The next day people were saying who kledde was.
164123: On a farm there was a heifer that gave a lot of milk because she had just calved. At some point the heifer gave no more milk, but a little later she gave three buckets again. The next night the people saw rats all over their farm. The farmer went to the friars, who advised him to go to confession and communion the next day with his whole family. A sorceress from the neighbourhood had caused all that trouble.
164150: One evening a man came across a cat and kicked at the animal. A few metres further on, the man was surrounded by cats. When the man came to his senses again, he found that he was sitting on a tree stump, although he had not climbed onto it himself.
164156: At Easter a woman in Ename went to confession. The woman saw that a sorceress was sitting next to her, and felt cold from her back down to her legs.
164157: In a bewitched house people had many problems with their children. One child could not walk and the other had to be tied into its cradle because it was so restless. When those people had moved, they had no more problems. The new occupants of the bewitched house, however, also had misfortune with their children.
164167: In a house in Nederzwalm people were playing cards on New Year's Eve. Downstairs the old mother lay on her bed. It was said of that mother that she could work magic. A card player who had the 'peike zot' (jack of spades) said at one point: "Wait a moment, I'll be right back." When the man returned, his 'peike zot' had vanished. The sorceress had magicked that card away, so that someone else had it.
164196: On a farm all the animals were wasting away. One day an old woman sat in the stable, rubbing a little bone and saying: "Over hedge and over gate to the farmer's wine cellar in Brussels." Then the woman flew away. The farmhand wanted to follow her, but got the charm wrong and said: "Through hedge and over gate to the farmer's wine cellar in Brussels." The farmhand was scratched all over when he arrived at his destination.
164209: A farmhand who worked for a farmer was completely emaciated. At night the farmhand was always away. One night they followed the farmhand and saw him take a skin out of a woodpile. The next day they sent the farmhand on an errand to a faraway place. Meanwhile they threw the skin into the oven. Although the farmhand would have had to walk at least four or five hours to reach the farm, the next moment he was already standing by the oven to save his skin.
164230: A farmhand often told of 'the damned Regina'. She was a damned princess who was the cause of thunder.
164248: A woman suffering from jaundice had been in bed for weeks. Because her health did not improve, the doctor said: "Something else is at play here. There are men who are doing you harm." The people then went to the Poor Clares in Aalst to fetch Easter nails. They put those Easter nails under their door, so that no one could come in any more. At midnight the sick woman woke because someone was rattling the door. But no one managed to get in.
164264: A man who wanted to bake bread found that the dough would not rise and the oven would not get hot. Suddenly the man discovered a bottle of liquor in the oven. After he had removed the bottle, the oven got hot and the dough did rise. It had probably been a magic bottle put there by a witch.
164298: In Sinaai there lived a woman who was said to be a sorceress. A man who suspected that sorceress of bewitching his child went with the child to the friars of Dendermonde. After prayers had been read over the child and its clothes had been burned, it was cured.
164324: In Maarke-Kerkem there lived a witch of whom people were very afraid. When people had met the witch, they no longer dared to go and fetch water afterwards. The neck of the witch's little son was only one or two fingers thick. The witch had bewitched her own child.
164347: In the old days people set their cooking pot on the Leuven stove. The underside of the pot was often covered in soot, and sometimes that soot began to glow. When that happened, people believed something was about to happen.
164350: A farm in Vlierzele was badly haunted. One morning there was a wagon standing in the bakehouse that could not have got in through either the doors or the windows. At night gentlemen were seen there sitting at a table writing. It was said that those gentlemen came there to look for money.
164363: One Saturday an old man came peddling rat poison at a house in Zulzeke. When the people bought nothing, the peddler was very offended. A few days later the people in that house were playing cards when they suddenly heard a noise in the attic. It sounded as if dogs were running around. When they went to look, they found the attic full of rats. The neighbour said he had seen a whole pack of rats climbing up. A few days later the peddler came by again. This time the people did buy a packet of rat poison, whereupon the peddler laughed and said: "I thought you didn't have any rats."
164365: In the past people were very afraid of black cats because they believed they were sorcerers or sorceresses.
164392: A man saw a whole troop of cats dancing in the street. The animals were holding each other's paws.
164437: A farm in the Hoogstraat was haunted. When the people came home one day, the door was open and all the furniture was upstairs (?). The people were so angry that they went somewhere for a drink. When they got home, they found the furniture lying upside down in the cellar. That was witchcraft.
164438: A woman lying in bed felt a heavy weight pressing on her. The woman was being ridden by the mare.
164439: On a farm in Steenhuize-Wijnhuize there was much misfortune in the stable. Although there had never been rats there before, there were now so many that they even jumped into the bed. When the friars came to read prayers over the place, they sweated terribly.
164447: One morning a little woman came to a farm for milk. "Come in," said the farmer's wife, but the woman began to tremble and could not get over the threshold. The farmer's wife wanted to take the woman's jug, but could not because the woman kept her hands clenched. Under the threshold of that farm lay an Easter nail. The people believed that woman had caused misfortune on their farm.
164477: On a farm the animals died and the children would not grow. The friars were sent for. The clergymen predicted that a French speaker would come by, who would be punished. One day a strong wind rose and a French-speaking woman came flying in. Because the gate slammed shut, the French speaker got stuck in it. That place was later called 'de toveressenhoek' (the sorceresses' corner).
164487: A man going to the Pattoterij saw something strange at a crossroads at midnight. Two children appeared, hiding their faces behind an umbrella. The man said to the children: "Children, what are you still doing out on the street so late?" The children did not answer and kept saying: "Hey! Hey!"
164504: On a farm, while churning butter, people found horse chestnuts in the butter churn. This was the work of witchcraft. A certain person who always came to the farm to fetch milk never came again after that.
164519: In Groot-Zottegem there lived people who owned special books. Those people sometimes stuck pins into dolls.
164529: In Matere people always came across a midwife. In one house butter could no longer be churned after that midwife had visited. After that incident the midwife was no longer let into that house.
164560: A baby could not sleep because its cradle kept rocking back and forth. It was a returned soldier who had been killed in the Second World War who made the cradle move.
164564: A woman went to a farmer to ask for milk. Because the woman felt she had not received enough milk, she asked for a little more. The farmer, however, would not give her any more. At that the woman said: "You will regret that!" Shortly afterwards the farmer found that his milk was full of little frogs.
164567: A man who had to manure a farmer's field took a dung fork, went to the field and said: "I mine and each his own." Then the field was manured in no time. Whenever that man went to church, he was dragged from one tree to the next. In the church he was pulled up by his hair by the devils.
164616: On Monday evenings and nights it often happened that people had to carry a werewolf. A man would be jumped on in a deserted street or meadow by someone wearing a dog skin, cowhide or sheepskin. After the man had carried the werewolf a little way, the werewolf urinated on him. Then the man was freed of his burden.
164621: A young man walking home with some friends on a winter evening at about ten or eleven o'clock saw two little lights at eye level in the distance. The man was not afraid and walked towards the lights, finding that they were the eyes of a black cat. The man tried several times to catch the cat, but did not succeed. It must have been a haunting.
164624: The chattering of a magpie was believed to be an omen of misfortune.
164641: In Steenhuize someone had shot at a sorceress. A little later a dead cat lay there.
164658: On a farm in Hofstade worked a farmhand who was a werewolf. One day the werewolf had jumped onto a woman's back. The woman then threw a red handkerchief into the werewolf's mouth. The next day the farmhand was seen to have the red threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
164677: In church, a woman from Orroir fell victim to an old woman who gave her lice. The woman's head was crawling with lice.
164730: One evening a man had taken a white rabbit home with him. The next day, to his great horror, the man found that the rabbit had turned into a skull. The skull said: "Take me back to the place where you got me, or I will break your neck!"
164754: A mother did not like that a certain woman always came near her youngest child. One day the child became so ill that it had to go to hospital. The mother was convinced that this woman had bewitched her child.
164774: At the Steenwerk (1) in Belsele there was a bell pit at the spot where a church is said to have stood in Napoleon's time. Pots of gold are also said to lie hidden in the ground there.
164804: A man who worked on a farm had to light the oven. In the woodpile the man found a skin. He realised it was the skin of someone who had chased him, and threw it into the oven. After that the werewolf never got another skin from the devil. It was the farmer the man worked for who had been playing the werewolf.
164821: If a dog was heard howling when someone in the family was ill, that person would die. In a house where the dog howled all night, the mother died on her sickbed.
164828: An Easter nail had to be fetched from a clergyman. Superstitious people carried an Easter nail on them or stuck one under the threshold so that no sorcerers could come in. If an Easter nail had been stuck under a witch's chair, she would say "I'm leaving" as many as twenty times, but she could not get up as long as the Easter nail was there.
164831: A man went along a little path near the station to fetch milk at a farm. On the way the man saw a big dog standing there, blocking his way. Another man walking on that path went to fetch the fathers. After the clergymen had prayed there for a while, the dog turned into a human.
164873: A man and a woman whose daughter had died went on a caravan holiday to Italy. The man claimed that he had spoken with the ghost of his dead daughter at night.
164957: When a man shot at a will-o'-the-wisp one night, the light flew on. It was said that such lights were the souls of unbaptised children.
164959: Two brothers who had been fishing saw a big black dog lying in the grass on their way home. One of the brothers threw his shoe at the dog, but the animal did not move. When the man threw his second shoe as well, the dog did not move. But the man no longer dared to fetch his shoes, and he and his brother hurried home. On the way, the two were followed the whole time by the black dog at a distance of about ten metres. When they got home, the brothers fled inside and slammed the door. Then the dog struck the door with its paw, so that its claws stuck in it.
164979: In the Kruisstraat a ghost always walked back and forth at night with a post on its shoulders.
165005: When a werewolf roamed about in the evening, he jumped on passers-by and had himself carried.
165007: A man came across three kittens at the churchyard of Zandbergen. The man took the kittens home and put them in a basket under the stove. The next morning, to his great horror, the man found that the kittens had disappeared and that there were three skulls in the basket. The priest advised the man to take the skulls back to the place where he had got them. After the man had done so, the skulls turned back into kittens.
165061: One evening a man had come across a black cat and kicked the animal. The next day the man was visited by a woman who had a black eye.
165064: A woman who always handed out mint sweets to the children went one day to look at a baby lying in a cradle. A short time later the child died. People claimed that this woman had bewitched the child and no longer wanted to let her into their houses.
165091: Near a farm in Ouwegem a werewolf roamed about, who had hidden his bearskin in a hollowed-out tree stump. When the man and the farmer he worked for were taking flax to Desselgem, his skin was found and thrown into the oven. The skin had barely caught fire when the man was standing by the oven to save it. But it was already too late, so the man was freed. He had sold his soul to the devils.
165116: The Rechtstraat in Eksaarde used to be haunted. A carriage with two horses always drove along the ridge of the roof of a house there. The people then sent for the friars, who nailed a horseshoe to the roof. After that nothing strange happened in the house any more.
165126: A man could change his shape. Once the man had leapt at his wife in the shape of a dog. The woman had thrown her apron at the dog. Some time later she saw that her husband had the threads of her apron between his teeth. In the end that man was burned at the pillory in Stekene.
165149: On a farm in Kwaremont people were churning butter. Suddenly they saw that the butter churn was full of black hairs. A witch from the neighbourhood had caused it.
165190: On a farm in Nazareth worked a farmhand who was a 'berewulf' (werewolf). Once, when the farmhand was at work in the field, his skin was found and thrown into the oven. As soon as the skin had caught fire, the farmhand said: "They are doing me harm."
165208: In Oordegem there was a house of pleasure. A man who had gone there against his father's wishes came home terrified because on the way he had been surrounded by some fifty black cats. He was convinced that all those cats were witches. After that the man never went to that house of pleasure again.
165211:
A woman whom some people suspected of being a witch often sat reading a book by candlelight in the evenings until midnight.
On a farm where two cows had died and another cow no longer gave milk, the fathers from Gent were sent for, and they advised the people to keep a close eye on a certain woman. The people had probably put an Easter nail under the door and had begun praying a novena. When the witch came past the gate on the ninth day, she immediately turned back. After that the cow on that farm gave milk again.
165285: In Ename lived a witch who could make people lose their way. A man who fell victim to the witch walked around the meadow for two hours and was drenched in sweat.
165320: A man coming back from Aalst was leapt upon on the way by kledde (a werewolf-like goblin that leaps onto people's backs). The man hit kledde on the snout with the bag in which he kept his food. So the next day people knew who kledde was, because he had the threads of the bag between his teeth.
165328: One evening there was a knock at a house. Two men who had been on pilgrimage came to ask whether they could spend the night there. The people let the men in and offered them a place to sleep. The men told them that a dead relative had once promised a pilgrimage but had not been able to complete it. That is why the dead person appeared every day at those people's bedside after his death. By making the pilgrimage themselves, the men were able to release the dead person.
165346: On a farm in Wijngaard lived a farmhand who consorted with the devil. One day he was in the field with the other farmhands. They had been told to bring a wheelbarrow of manure to the field. When by evening still nothing had been done, the farmer grew angry. The farmhand in charge said: "I'll make up for the delay" and lifted a wheelbarrow full of manure onto his shoulders. In this way he carried off three wheelbarrows of manure on his shoulders.
165353: If you had seen a crow or a magpie, you could expect news. Some people believed that crows and magpies foretold misfortune.
165362: A man who had moved a boundary post during his life walked about with the post near the tunnel in Nukerke after his death, calling: "Where must I put it?" One day a drunkard answered: "By the Lord God, put it where you got it!" After that the dead man no longer appeared.
165381: In the old days every village had only one pump where people could fetch water. One day a woman from Elversele was told by her neighbours that she was no longer allowed to fetch water at the pump. "Just wait, you will regret that!" the woman replied. When the neighbours wanted to pump water the next day, toads and frogs appeared. After that the people let the witch take water from the pump again. They were even so afraid that they carried the water to the witch themselves.
165385: On a farm in Mere worked a farmhand who was away every day. One day when the farmer went to bake bread, he found the skin of kledde (a shape-shifting bogeyman) in a woodpile. While his farmhand was at work in the field, the farmer threw the skin into the glowing oven. The next moment the farmhand was already standing by the fire to save his skin. It took two or three men to hold the farmhand back until the skin had burned up and the farmhand said with relief: "Now I am at ease again."
165406: A woman always saw a big black dog arrive when she had finished churning butter. The dog took a big lump of butter and ran off. People believed that witches came to steal butter in this way.
165412: A man coming home one evening saw a big white cat on a notorious road. The man struck at the animal and the next moment was surrounded by white cats, so that he could go no further.
165413:
A strange man asked for spirits in a café. The landlady explained that she did not serve spirits because she had no licence for them. The man sat down opposite her, and a little later the landlady put a bottle of liquor in front of him. That was witchcraft.
A little later the man began to play cards. When the jack of spades fell on the floor, one of the card players bent down to pick it up. He saw that the stranger had goat's legs. The man asked the stranger for the bottle. When the stranger handed it over, the man pressed the cross of his rosary into his hand. The next moment the stranger had vanished.
165417: In Nederename and in Mater lived women who were suspected of being witches. One of those witches visited a sick child every day who just would not get better. The witch even cut her procession robe into pieces to lay on the child's wounds. Because the child did not recover, the parents put an Easter nail under their threshold. They believed the woman came there to bewitch, but in reality she simply felt pity for the child.
165460: Some people going to the shop one evening met a little old woman, who said: "When I am dead, you must pray for me". A while later the old woman died. The people had forgotten to pray for her. When one day they went to the shop to buy thread, they saw the old woman kneeling in a clover field with her hands raised. The people who saw it were very frightened.
165476: Two men coming back from the procession in Lede at about one o'clock at night saw something that looked like a little dog moving near the Erp chapel. The men tried to chase the little dog away, but it kept running back and forth in front of them. In the end the men grew frightened and hurried home.
165526: In a family a child had died just before it was due to make its first communion. When the curate came to comfort the parents, the people said that their other child had 'the old man'. The priest then asked: "Have you perhaps ever refused someone a slice of bread?" The mother could not remember anything. She was given an Easter nail to put under the threshold, so that the witch could no longer come in.
165527: A mother from Bevere had already lost two babies. Each time the mother had been churched, a woman stood outside the church who wanted to see the child. When the mother was churched after the birth of her third child, she told the priest she suspected that this witch had caused her children to die. The priest advised her to have the child prayed over in the great church in Ronse or by the fathers of Gent. When the woman came home with her child that day, the child did nothing but cry. In the end the mother decided to go to the church in Ronse, where the child was prayed over and given a medal. The child survived.
165539: A woman always saw a black dog when she went to fetch water. When someone had shot at the dog with a blessed bullet, one of the neighbours went missing. In the old days there were people who had dealings with the devil. That dog must have been a devil.
165592: After a theft had been committed somewhere, the ghost of the thief came haunting.
165620: A man was ridden by the mare every night. Once, when two friends stood by his bed, they beat on the man's bed with a stick when he started to shout. The man went to the friars.
165647: A man who had to saw down a tree found that his saw would not work. At that moment a priest came in and said: "That is the evil hand. I will bless your saw." The saw had been bewitched by someone from Meerdonk who had visited the man a few times and had not shown himself since.
165693: On a farm in Schorisse a horse or a cow lay dead every night. Two men who had to keep watch in the stable suddenly saw six white rats. They heard music and saw a woman on horseback. The men told the farmer what they had seen. The next night the farmer also slept in the stable. He did see the woman on horseback, but he could not see the rats. He shot at the apparition. The next morning the maid who worked on the farm lay dead in bed.
165715: A woman churning butter saw a cat approaching and threw a skimmer at the animal. The next day she asked a maid: "Isn't your mother coming today?", to which the maid replied: "She can't, because her back is all burned".
165776: During a thunderstorm a farmer ran to a small cottage for shelter. Through the window he saw an old woman sticking pins into a red heart. When he went in, the woman immediately hid the heart. The farmer said he came from Iddergem and then heard the woman's daughter call from the next room: "From Iddergem! Oh mother, we had so much fun there in the willows!" The mother answered: "Be quiet, silly child."
165797: A woman from Schorisse who had been in labour for days could not give birth. Finally her husband went to an Augustinian father in Gent. The priest came to the house and said: "There is evil at work here. A woman will come by and you must give her what she asks for." That night at twelve o'clock there was a knock at the door. It was a woman asking for a safety pin. The man gave her what she asked. Five minutes later the child was born.
165829: A sorcerer from Waregem sometimes caused people to suffer a plague of rats.
165868: A man from Zonnegem was coming back in the evening from Ottergem, where he had gone to visit his girlfriend. On the way the man was chased all the way to his house by a white horse. That must have been a ghost horse.
165902: Some people returning from a concert in Sint-Antelinks were followed by a cat and kicked at the animal. A few days later one of the men had to drive to Essche. On the way he saw a woman in front of his cart with her arm in a bandage. Afterwards the man blamed himself for not having kicked that woman.
165953: The devil had left his paw print at a place called 't Duvels Voetstap. He had also pressed his paw into an apple tree near 't hof Ten Berge.
165955: White cats were always roaming near a small wood in Asper, so that no young fellow dared to walk around there.
165967: People who had lost their way were said to have been 'led by the dolf'.
165990: People wanted to carry a saint's statue from Appelterre-Eichem to Pollare. On the way they could hardly make any progress. The next day the statue was standing in Eichem again.
165995: An old sorceress had a wax doll into which she stuck pins. When she visited somewhere, she often asked to see the youngest child. The sorceress then made a few signs of the cross and stroked the child. When she got home, she stuck a pin into the wax doll. The child then felt pain in that same spot.
166023: A woman stuck pins into a doll to torment the people she could not stand.
166024: Two men who went to fetch 'stouken' (1) during the First World War lost their way, so that they were still wandering about at two in the morning. The men had been ridden by the mare.
166069: In a house where an old woman had died, a mouse ran around two days after her death. People said that the mouse was the dead woman who had returned.
166102: A farm in Latem was haunted. One winter night the farmer's wife heard a noise that seemed to come from the kitchen. The farmer thought there were animals in the house and went downstairs. But there was nothing to be seen. The farmer had only just got back into bed when the noise began again. The farmer, his wife and the children got up and saw the pots and pans dancing on the sink. In the kitchen they even saw sheep walking in a line. The people were scared to death and the next day told their neighbours what they had experienced. The next evening some men came to keep watch in the farmhouse. At midnight the haunting began again. The next day the friars were consulted. Two clergymen read prayers over the farm until the sweat rolled down their faces. After that nothing strange happened there any more.
166124: On a farm in Ophasselt worked a stable hand who dressed up as kledde (a shape-shifting bogeyman). One day the stable hand was sent away so that his skin could be burned in the meantime. But as soon as the skin had caught fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his skin. After that incident the oven was never used again for baking bread.
166145: A woman brought peelings to a donkey on a farm every day. One day the people saw that the donkey was drenched in sweat. They went to look and found darning needles among the peelings. The people then fetched Easter nails to put under the door. After that the woman never visited again.
166183: On a farm in Lede, every night there was noise in the attic as if a herd of horses was running around. When the people went to look, there was nothing to be seen. One morning the farmer found a horse's hoof in the attic.
166204: A man whose three children had wasted away and who was suffering a plague of mice sent for the curate of Schorisse. The clergyman came with a book and said a number of prayers. After that the problems were over.
166210: People took a small child who was covered in lice because of a witch to the priest. The clergyman predicted that the witch would have to come to the house. And so it happened.
166250: A lord of a castle was married to a beautiful woman. In the woods around the castle a big black dog always roamed at night, and the people were very afraid of it. They tried several times to catch the dog, but did not succeed. When the lord woke up one night, he rushed outside on seeing the dog. The lord cornered the dog, and the animal attacked him. The lord just managed to strike off one of the dog's paws, after which the animal ran off howling. When the lord came home and wanted to tell his wife the whole story, he saw that she was doubled up in pain because her right hand had been cut off.
166285: In Kastel a man had mocked an unknown woman he had met. The woman had said nothing. The next day, however, the man could not get out of bed because he had such terrible back pain. The back pain lasted seven weeks and the doctors could not help.
166294: Strange things happened on a farm in Kruibeke. When the people went to bed at night, the blankets were always pulled off. One day the people asked: "What do you want? A mass?" After a mass had been said, nothing strange happened any more.
166339: In Okegem a woman came round peddling eggs. Wherever that woman had stood at the threshold, the children in that house died. People who had fallen victim to the witchcraft had to go to Affligem.
166348: Rotten eggs had been found at a house in Ename. When the people threw the eggs away, they heard a bang as if the house was exploding.
166407: On a farm in Voorde a woman from the neighbourhood came on a Saturday to ask for a loaf of bread. She was given the bread and left. Two days later the farmer's wife went to the pigsty. Because one of the pigs kept walking around in its pen, she decided to go to the fathers of Affligem. The priest gave her water, wine, bread and salt. The pigs would not eat, had foam on their lips and dug deep holes in their pen. When the father advised her to put something blessed in the pigs' feed, the farmer's wife said: "But the pigs won't eat." The priest replied: "They will eat that." And so it was. After that intervention the pigs behaved normally again. The trouble had probably been caused by the witch who had come for a loaf. On the farm they also had to go to confession and communion every day for nine days. After that they had no more misfortune there.
166428: A farmhand rode along with some men to Zingem to fetch coal from the boat. But the farmhand was someone who owned a skin with which he had to go about as kledde (a shape-shifting bogeyman). While they were away, the oven on the farm was heated to burn the farmhand's skin. The farmhand sensed instinctively what was happening and was at the oven in no time to save his skin.
166477:
In the old days 'berewulven' (werewolves) often roamed about. They were people who had thrown a bearskin over themselves and peered in through the windows of houses. When you went outside, you were jumped on by a werewolf and had to carry the beast. Werewolves only roamed about during Advent.
People who were angry with their neighbours sometimes went about as werewolves to teach them a lesson. Now and then the werewolf himself got a sound thrashing.
166480: A man who went to fetch draught oxen near Diest met an old woman on the way, who asked whether the company came from near Wichelen. When the man said yes, the woman went on: "I had fun there under a linden tree many nights. But I am glad that it is all over now."
166484: Werewolves went about with a sheepskin over themselves and jumped on passers-by to be carried.
166488: On a farm in Impe there was much misfortune. The animals were always falling ill or dying. At night the animals could be heard kicking, but when people went to look, there was nothing to be seen. When the people kept watch one night, they saw the witch sitting in the beet pit.
166506: On a farm that had a lot of misfortune in the stables, the people went to the fathers of Gent for advice. The fathers said: "A good acquaintance regularly comes to visit you. You should keep him out. Tomorrow he will come as far as the farm, but he will not come in." That visitor never set foot on the farm again. Sometimes he stood watching from a distance, but he did not come any closer. He lived with his sister in the woods. His sister knew all the news, although she never went out. People said the magpies came to tell her the news.
166559: A woman who went to the castle of Moregem every day often got lost on her way home in the evening, although she knew the way well. When the woman saw a witch standing with outstretched arms, she cried: "What are you doing here? You'd be better off in your bed. It must be you who is doing this to me!" Although the woman had been on her way since nine o'clock, she was still not home at midnight. The witch had made her lose her way.
166560: A woman who sold herring often had a witch come into her shop. Because the woman's little child was ridden by the mare every night, the woman went to the parish priest, who advised her to put an Easter nail under the threshold. When the woman had done so, the witch could no longer leave the shop by the front door. She had to go out by the back door.
166564: In the old days men often told their wives they had been ridden by the mare. In reality they had simply visited too many inns.
166588: A woman often came to a farm when a cow was due to calve. She would sit hidden behind a door and no one knew how she had got in. As long as the woman was there, the cow could not calve. After she had been chased away, the calf was born.
166612: Some people who had three goats found that blood instead of milk came from the goats' udders. The animals were also covered in flies. The people's little daughter developed a hunchback and became very ill. Another child died. The mother went to the fathers, where she was told that a certain woman who often visited would return within three days. They were not to give that woman anything, however. The woman visited once more, but after that she did not dare come again. The people had no more problems either.
166631: When a small child somewhere was ill, people said it was bewitched. It was believed, for example, that a witch had made the child ill by sticking needles into a pillow.
166636: At night there was knocking and stamping at the door of a little house, although nothing was ever to be seen. That must have been witchcraft.
166661: A clog maker went with some friends to buy trees in the Netherlands. On the way the men laughed at a neatly dressed woman they met. But the men did not know that the woman was a witch. On the way home the cart with the trees would hardly move. The witch was sitting on it.
166669: A woman who often had a strange visitor put an Easter nail under the threshold. When the witch came to visit again after that, she could not get in. One day the woman walked in the witch's footsteps. She wanted to catch up with her, but fell flat on her face.
166694: Some people had put the skin of kludde (a shape-shifting bogeyman) into the oven. Kludde said: "Give me back one little bell or one little hair of my skin." But the people did not do so, because that would give kludde his power back. When the skin had burned, kludde was glad because he had been freed from a hellish torment.
166707: A hunter shot at a hare but could not hit the animal. At that very moment the bells were rung for High Mass. The hare jumped into a hole in a tree stump and the hunter ran after it. He thought: "Now I've got him," but when he reached the tree, the hare said: "The angelus is already ringing, you've missed your High Mass."
166769: A farmer's wife had set out water for the calves. When she went to give the water to the animals, it had strangely disappeared. Two hours later the water was standing there again. The farm had a heavy door with two large bolts, which were often both opened although nobody had been nearby. Many animals died in the stables. One day the friars came to the farm. One of the clergymen sat praying among the bluestone sills because he believed the evil was in them.
166800: A man whose grain had been bewitched could not manage to mow even a single stalk.
166834: If you saw a black hen at a crossroads, you would have bad luck, because that hen had to do with haunting.
166883: A priest who could work magic often went to Heldergem. When on his way home he saw a stable lantern near the mill, he said: "Go home and wash your children so they are clean, because they are full of lice." A moment later the stable lantern had vanished.
166887: When someone had had a child, they were not allowed to lend anything out, for then they could fall victim to witchcraft.
166906: Some pranksters had stuck an Easter nail under the door of the church of Nieuwerkerken. After mass, six or seven sorceresses could not leave the church until the Easter nail had been removed.
166909:
A man did not believe that the woman walking a little way ahead of him was a witch. Still, he followed his friend's advice and placed his feet crossed on the woman's footprint. At that the woman turned around.
That same woman always went to fetch milk at a farm where there was a little girl. Because the child would not grow, the farmer's wife went to the friars, who said: "The evil hand has something to do with it. Here is a little scapular you must hang on the gate." After the farmer's wife had hung up the scapular, the woman who came for milk could no longer get past the gate. The child grew up into a healthy woman.
166924: Werewolves went about in a bearskin and had themselves carried. They held meetings at crossroads.
166933: In the old days a joker would sometimes pull something over his head and walk along a certain path to frighten people. People walking there were sometimes jumped on by the joker and had to carry him. Those people had been ridden by the mare.
167040: A man from Nederbrakel had sold his soul to the devil. One Sunday evening, when the man was sitting in an inn, the innkeeper would not serve him any more drink because his money had run out. The drunkard began to curse and was thrown out by the innkeeper. After asking for beer in vain at several inns, he walked home cursing. On the way he met a gentleman dressed in black, who said: "I will give you as much money as you want, but you must always obey me." The drunkard agreed to the proposal and was given four five-franc coins. When that money was gone, he could take more money from a little box, for the contents of that box would always be replenished as long as the man stayed loyal to the devil. Then the drunkard went back to the inn, where he banged his fist on the bar and demanded beer. When he threw a coin on the bar, they had no choice but to serve him. The next morning the man went to look in the little box and found that there were still four coins in it. From then on the man went to the inn every day and cursed like a heathen. Everyone avoided the man because they were convinced he was possessed by the devil. Since the man had sold his soul to the devil, a werewolf had also been sighted in the municipality. Because the man could no longer find work with the farmers in his area, he went to look for work in another municipality. He was taken on as a farmhand on a farm, but had to promise not to drink or curse any more. For a while that went well, but eventually the man fell back into his old habits. One day the farmhand had loaded a cart full of manure. When the farmer wanted to set off with the cart, he could not, because it was stuck in a hole. However hard the farmer tried, he could not get the cart moving. The farmhand asked whether he could sort it out. After he had cursed at the horses a few times, the cart moved off without any trouble. The fear of the werewolf that roamed the area in the evenings grew even greater, and it became so bad that women and children no longer dared go outside after dark. One day someone on the farm found a bearskin in a woodpile. On the first Monday of March the farmer told the farmhand to manure a piece of field near the woods. If the work was done by noon, the farmhand could go to the fair in Geraardsbergen. When the farmer went to see at about eleven o'clock how the work was going, he found to his great anger that his farmhand was asleep. He kicked the farmhand awake and made it clear that he could not go to the fair until the field had been manured. But the farmhand was not bothered. He got up cursing, stuck the dung fork into one heap of manure and said: "I do mine and each does his own." The next moment all the manure heaps burst open by themselves. A few hours after the farmhand had left for the fair, the farmer heated the oven to burn the skin. But before he could throw the skin into the fire, the farmhand was standing by the oven. The farmer and his wife fled, and the farmhand left the farm cursing, with the skin under his arm. A few years later the man was freed from the devil in the church.
167047: On his way home one evening a man came across a pretty little cat. When the man had kicked at the cat, he was suddenly surrounded by cats, who sang: "Ei bau bei, pretty cat, where do you come from?"
167048:
A man walking home one Sunday evening was jumped on along the way by a prankster dressed up as a bear, who shouted: "The day is for you and the night is for me, and you must carry me to over there." After the man had carried the prankster a little way, he gave him a sound thrashing. So the next day everyone knew who the bear was.
People who owned such a bearskin suffered great pain when someone burned it. The person in question would then immediately appear at the oven to save his skin.
167051: A house in Ronse was haunted every evening. At night people heard noise there, but when they went upstairs to look, there was nothing to be seen. Because the people could not raise any animals there, they were forced by poverty to move.
167055: In a house in Opbrakel where a man had died, someone was heard stamping and banging every night. The occupants of the house could not sleep and fell ill. The doctor advised the people to go and see a clergyman. The village priest came to bless the whole house and thought that would put an end to it. Because the haunting only got worse afterwards, the occupants wrote to the friar of Ghent, who promised to come. The friar of Ghent said to the people: "Come to me for confession and go to communion tomorrow morning. I will give you a white handkerchief. You must say an act of contrition and go into the room as soon as the noise is heard again. Then you must ask: 'What do you want of me?' and throw the white handkerchief into the room." When the people did this, the voice of the returned dead man said: "You promised to put up a cross here and you must do it. Are you going to put up that cross, yes or no?" The people answered: "We promise." After that no more strange noises were heard in the house. The next day they saw that four fingers and a thumb had been burnt into the handkerchief.
167110: A woman who was scutching flax always saw a white dove sitting on the scutching shed around ten or eleven o'clock at night. The woman sought the advice of the priest, who told her to bring nine people into the house and then ask the dove what was expected of her. The dove then said to the woman: "You must go with nine people to the chapel of Gouverland." When the woman set off for that chapel, she said: "Go ahead, we will follow." On the priest's advice the woman also took a white handkerchief, because after the pilgrimage the dove would turn into a person who would shake her hand. And so it happened. A burnt handprint was left on the handkerchief. The handkerchief is still kept in the church of Haasdonk.
167146: A man who had moved the boundary post of his field came haunting after his death with the words: "Put that post back in its place!"
167185: A woman had come to a house to fetch lard. She had gone to the baby's cradle and lifted the child up. Afterwards that child's cradle was full of woolly caterpillars.
167217: In Haaltert there was a bell pit. When the church burned down, an unconsecrated bell fell into that pit. The bell was never found again.
167232: A farmer coming home in the dark saw a man sitting by the roadside, despondent because he had no work. The man asked the farmer whether he had any work for him. But when the man sat up, the farmer saw that he had a goat's foot and said: I'm sorry, friend, but I can't help you. The farmer made the sign of the cross and walked away.
167245: Noise was always heard in a house in Oudenaarde. When the chimney wall was demolished, leather money was found there. After that the haunting was over.
167249: In the old days there were people with special powers that allowed them to travel very quickly. They could do this not only with their mind, but also with their body.
167254: A man coming home one evening heard a loud bang but saw nothing. When the man was in bed, he heard the bang again. He also heard rattling in the washstand. When the man got out of bed, the sound could no longer be heard. As soon as he lay down in bed again, the sound started again. Knocking could be heard in that house all night.
167280: If you heard magpies chattering, you could expect news.
167299: A man coming back in the evening from the field where he had gone to move the threshing machine lost his way and ended up in the same place three times.
167332: In the past many witches lived in Bevere. In Huttegem there were as many as seven women suspected of being sorceresses. The parish priest always said that no witches could enter places where an Easter nail was stuck under the door. Two altar boys had stuck an Easter nail under the church door, so that seven witches remained sitting in the church. During a sermon the priest once said that such practices had to stop, or else he would name the witches by name. After that, witchcraft in Bevere greatly decreased.
167333: A witch who lived in a small house had the power to stop six horses. A little later the witch had vanished without a trace. After the witch's death nobody wanted to buy her house.
167365: A sorcerer could make a whole swarm of mice run out of a heap of earth.
167369: At night a woman heard carts driving and horses stamping, although there was no road in that place.
167383: Kledde (a shape-shifting bogeyman) had hidden his skin in a hollow elm. Passers-by often had to carry kledde. One evening kledde's skin was thrown into the oven. They had to hold kledde back, or else he would have jumped into the oven to save his skin. When the skin had burned up, the young man was glad because he was freed.
167435: In the past everyone was afraid of black cats. After all, they believed they were witches in the shape of a cat.
167446: In a house that was haunted, all sorts of things could always be seen moving in the evening. Now a pot fell off the table, then a chair toppled over. A clergyman had to be sent for.
167500: To avoid being ridden by the mare, one had to urinate into a new bottle and then seal it.
167524: A cloth weaver who had gone to collect money somewhere one evening saw a werewolf jump out of the hedge. Convinced that someone wanted to rob him, the man quickly threw the cloth in which he had wrapped the sheets on the ground and shouted: "Unweave that!" While the werewolf unravelled the cloth, the man was able to go home. The next day the cloth weaver told his neighbours what had happened to him. A farmer who had also heard the story found the cloth weaver's cloth in his oven, half unravelled.
167527: A man came back from work every day together with a friend. One day the friend said he had to go into the woods for a moment to relieve himself. In reality he went to quickly dress up as a werewolf. The werewolf got under the man's feet. When the man threw his handkerchief at the werewolf, he was left alone.
167549: On a farm in Kruibeek all the horses were lying in a tub one day. The farmer sent for the parish priest, who promised to come back in the evening. In the evening the clergyman said to the farmer: "You go to sleep and leave me here alone in the stable." The next day, remarkably enough, the haunting was over.
167555: On a farm lived a farmhand who was away every night. This only came to light when one night a sow was about to farrow and the farmhand was not in his bed. In the orchard behind the farm stood an old tree stump with a hollow in it. One night they saw the farmhand take a skin out of that hollow and go off with it. That is how they knew the farmhand went about as kledde (a shape-shifting bogeyman). The farmer sent the farmhand off with the cart on a trip that would take at least two days. The next morning the farmer lit the oven and threw the skin in. Shortly afterwards the farmhand was standing by the fire to save his skin. They had to hold him back, or else he would have jumped into the fire. As long as the skin was burning, the farmhand suffered terrible pains. Afterwards he was relieved to be freed from his burden.
167572: A man out on the road in Moregem heard the trampling of horses at midnight. A little later the man saw someone coming on horseback who seemed to be wearing a hair cloak. The man saw hair everywhere.
167575: A brewer from Etikhove who could not brew beer always saw a mewing black cat about. Because the animal annoyed him, the brewer shot the cat dead. A little later the brewer found that his own wife was dead.
167628: A woman had struck at two frogs that had come in through the water drain. The next day two neighbours were ill. Those neighbours were suspected of being sorceresses.
167724: In Eilaart a gentleman was walking with his daughter around a meadow. The girl said to her father: "Look, papa, if I want to, I can make the harvest here fail by tomorrow." The next day the crops in that field were mouldy, and the farmer sat crying. The gentleman said to the farmer: "You mustn't cry. Now I know what my child can do. I will pay for all the damage."
167726: Werewolves were pranksters who dressed up and had themselves carried by passers-by.
