167749: A man returning from the fair in Oordegem was followed by a black cat. The man was convinced the cat was a sorceress. When he met a group of boys a little further on, together they threw the cat over the hedge. A little later, however, the cat appeared on the road again. They pelted the animal with stones, but it did no good. The next day a young woman was walking around the village covered in scratches and wounds.
167784: A woman always saw a black cat near her. It was a dead sorceress who had returned. One day an old woman poured hot water over the cat, and the animal died. The next day that old woman herself lay in bed with burns.
167805: A mother who had to run an errand left a woman to look after her baby. When she came home, the mother found that the child had become unmanageable. The mother said to the woman: "You have bewitched my child. You will not leave here until you have undone the spell!" The woman took the baby in her arms and walked around with it, and so the spell was undone.
167810: On her way home, a woman was followed the whole time by a little dog with a bell that would not be chased away. Terrified and sweating, the woman arrived home.
167821: There was always a racket in a café in Schorisse. "The devils may come and dance here," the landlord had once said. One day an unknown couple came in and began to dance. They were two devils with horse's legs. At a certain moment the devils suddenly vanished. No one knew where they had come from or where they went.
167839: In the attic of a farm, people suffered a plague of fleas after a woman had visited. From one day to the next the fleas were gone.
167843: A man who was out one evening with his friends said to them: "If you see a cat, don't kick at it, because then we could experience strange things." A little later, however, one of the men kicked at a cat anyway. The next moment there were a thousand cats.
167869: It was haunted in Sint-Cornelis-Horebeke. Around twelve or one o'clock, a woman whose sister had died always walked across the churchyard with a white sheet over her and a black cat in her arms. A young man coming back from a date with his sweetheart one Sunday saw a large oven standing there, with the ghost underneath it. Terrified, the young man ran away.
167893: On a farm in Sinaai worked a farmhand who dealt with evil. One day the farmhand was sent to Sint-Niklaas so that his animal skin could be burned in the meantime. But as soon as the skin caught fire, the farmhand came in sweating. If they had not held him back, he would have jumped into the fire. After the skin had burned up, the farmhand was freed from evil.
167898: A man from Geraardsbergen went to the fair in Wallonia. In the evening he played 'anchors and sun' there, a forbidden game in which money was staked. The police had caught the players and even taken them to jail. The man was afraid of how his family would react if he only came home the next morning. But one of his friends, who was also in jail, said to him: "Don't worry. At midnight we'll be out of here!" Around half past eleven the prisoners were indeed free. The man did not know how that was possible. Between Lessen and Geraardsbergen the men were followed by a horse at a distance of about ten metres. The animal stopped when the men stopped and went on when the men went on. Near Overboelare the horse suddenly vanished. The man got home around three o'clock in the night.
167926: Sorcerers could not cross a threshold with an Easter nail under it, but this only worked when they were twenty-four hours away from their own parish. Some men had stuck an Easter nail under the door of the church porch and then went to the fair at Erwetegem. They went to watch what happened from a café opposite the church. Two women could only leave the church when the priest led them outside.
167928: During the French Revolution people often hid church bells to keep them out of the hands of the French, who wanted to make money from them. Later those bells could not be found again, and they could be heard ringing at night.
167972: In the past there was a lot of hunting in Heurne. Some hares were real witches. However hard the hunters tried to hit those hares, they never succeeded.
167977: A man was working in a field in France when an old woman passed by and asked: "Are you Belgian?" The man answered: "Yes, I am from Sint-Goriks-Oudenhove." The woman then said: "From Sint-Goriks? We have had a lot of fun there by the big linden tree!" Everyone believed that the old woman was a witch.
167997: On a farm in Sombeek that was troubled by evil, the farmer went to the fathers. The priests foretold that a woman would come begging for nine days in a row. The farmer had to put an Easter nail under the door and send the woman away without giving her anything. Nine days later the beggar woman stopped coming and the farmer was freed of the evil.
168004: One evening around half past nine a boy from Maarke-Kerkem came home. When he got home he saw everyone sitting fearfully around the stove. In the attic and on the stairs there was noise as if everything was being smashed. When the father went upstairs with a lantern, he saw nothing. As soon as he was downstairs, the noises could be heard again. The same phenomena recurred every day for an hour and a half or two hours. At nine o'clock there was knocking at the gate. A while later the noises in the attic began. The mother went to fetch the parish priest to read prayers over the house, but that did not help. The haunting lasted nine or ten days. The people who had lived there before were said to have had much misfortune with their animals.
168014: The miller of Kallo went to set his mill going in bad weather. When the miller saw a spotted little cat creep between his legs, he said: "What are you doing here, sweet spotted cat?", to which the animal replied: "If the miller had not spoken so nicely, this spotted cat would have taught him a lesson".
168067: A man driving to the dairy in the morning saw meowing cats everywhere. The man's aunt went to consult the friars, who told her she was no longer allowed to go to Mass (?).
168117: A man went with his uncle to the market in Geraardsbergen to buy a cow. On the way the men saw a crow flying over their heads. Because they believed this brought bad luck, they did not dare buy anything at the market.
168127: One night a man was chased by a big horse. When the man looked back again a little later, he was being chased by a whole herd of horses. After that incident the man's hair turned grey with fear.
168131: A man went to the priest because his daughter had been bewitched by a witch. The priest came to anoint the girl, but the child snapped at him. Then the curate came, who did manage to anoint the child, but afterwards said: "It has gone too far. The child will die within nine days." At midnight the child began to cry. A little later she was calm. Nine days later the girl died.
168259: In Sint-Cornelis-Horebeke lived an old woman who had three goats. Although the woman had tied her goats up indoors, a man came to tell her that her goats were running about outside. The woman went to tie her goats up again, but a little later the animals were loose again. This little game was repeated several more times.
168327: In a wood in Rijst between Schorisse and Maarke-Kerkem, a man and a woman lived in a little clay hut with their dog 'Duc'. The man was a rag-and-bone man who was afraid of nothing. When his wife died, the man was left alone. One winter the man wanted to bake waffles. He was standing at the trough when he heard a voice say: "I'm going to fall!" The man replied: "Fall then, as long as you don't fall into my trough." Then something fell to the floor. The same thing happened several more times, but the man paid no attention. After three things had fallen down, a ghost stood in the room and said: "I am the child of the devil and I bring the dead food." The man answered: "Then you bring drink too. Sit down, good friend, have a waffle and get out your bottle."
168331: A woman had a ten-year-old daughter who always began crying in her sleep at midnight and moaned: "Oh mother, oh mother, please help me, for I see all sorts of strange things." After the child had been prayed over by a father, the girl stayed calm.
168373: A boy had often heard his mother tell about the 'eleven o'clock wagon'. That was four, five, six, seven or eight cats in a row, heading to town to put on a play.
168389: In Elst a werewolf roamed about and had itself carried by passers-by.
168432: On a farm in Zulte the farmer and his wife slept with their baby's cradle beside their bed. In the morning the parents found that their child's head was stuck through the handle of the cradle, although that handle was normally far too small for it. The next morning the child's head was stuck through the other handle. The parents then put the cradle in the kitchen and kept watch there. At a certain moment they saw a black cat creep through a small hole in the windowpane. The cat sat down under the stove and a little later left the house the way it had come. The next evening the scene repeated itself. But the farmer had put a pot full of animal feed on the stove. He poured the boiling liquid over the cat, which ran off howling. The next day one of the neighbours lay dying with severe burns.
168439: A man who was ridden by the mare felt as if a weight of a hundred kilos was lying on him. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to place one's clogs upside down next to the bed when going to sleep.
168458: In Stekene lived a woman who believed in neither God nor commandment. During a procession a hare ran out of the field through the procession. People said the hare was the notorious woman, who had turned herself into an animal. Afterwards the woman was tortured and burned at the pillory on the corner of the Bormte. That stone can still be seen in the museum of antiquities in Sint-Niklaas.
168478: The Engels Hof was haunted. A man walking past there saw lots of white posts along the road. People walked over money there with their feet, but they could not pick it up.
168518: In the past it often happened that sounds were heard in the chimney of a house. When the walls were then demolished, leather money was found there. After that the haunting stopped.
168520: On a farm where the milk always went bad, the fathers were sent for. The priests came to pray and sweated terribly while doing so. Afterwards one of the fathers said: "Put a chair ready. The witch will come at night and sit on it, but she will not be able to get off the chair. She will cry until there are blisters on her legs."
168525: A man from Erpe went on a pilgrimage to Halle. When he came into an inn there, an old woman asked him where he came from. After the man had answered, the woman said: "Do you know where the Oonegemmeers is, then? Is that old tree stump still there? I went there many nights and had a lot of fun there."
168550: A man who was ridden by the mare heard a woman in clogs approaching. Then the man was seized by the throat. Because the man was afraid to go to sleep, he sat up in bed, said: "Praised be Jesus Christ" and then prayed five Our Fathers. After that the man never heard or felt the mare again.
168551: People who were ridden by the mare were led to a certain place by a strange force.
168597: A farmhand who slept in the horse stable always heard a knocking at night. Then he began to sweat and was ridden by the mare. He could protect himself against the mare by placing his clogs upside down by the door.
168605: One evening a boy went to visit his girlfriend in Bevere. The girl and her mother, however, were both witches. At a quarter to twelve mother and daughter had to leave. The boy jumped on his little donkey and went home. The next evening the boy hid somewhere so that he could watch mother and daughter take a pot of ointment from the chimney. After rubbing themselves with the ointment, they went outside, said "Over hedge and over everything" and flew away. Then the boy also rubbed himself with the ointment and said: "Through hedge and through everything." He arrived at his destination badly injured. There he jumped on his little donkey, which brought him home in three leaps.
168606: A man was followed on his way by a werewolf. The man threw his scarf at the animal, but the werewolf jumped on him. When he got home the man collapsed.
168630: A man could no longer sleep at home because he was ridden by the mare. He would then get up and see all sorts of things. When the mare came, she first stood in her victim's clogs before seizing the person. After his mother had hung a rosary on her son's bed, he could sleep again, even though he did not know the rosary was hanging there.
168636: A farmer told the parish priest that he had found out that his farmhand had to go about as Osschaert (a shape-shifting bogeyman). The priest advised the farmer to go to the friars in Dendermonde. The friars told the farmer to send his farmhand far from home and in the meantime take his animal skin from under the woodpile. The skin then had to be thrown into a burning oven. No sooner said than done. When the skin was in the oven, the farmhand immediately came running home, sweating heavily. If the oven door had not been locked, the farmhand would certainly have jumped in.
168673: A farmhand working on a farm in Mater suddenly got a terrible toothache. On that farm the horses jumped about at night and the window shutters flew open and shut. After the friars had been to the farm, the situation improved.
168706: A woman could not die until she had taken over her mother's magic powers. That woman had once had a relationship with a man who eventually married someone else because he had discovered that she was a witch. That man had no happiness in his marriage.
168715: A man returning from a christening in Bouzelene at which he had been godfather saw an old woman walking ahead of him on his way home. The man was annoyed by the woman and said: "Damn it, I'll throw her in the water!" But the man himself fell into the well.
168736: In Rozebeke lived a woman with her unmarried daughter. People suspected these two women of being able to work witchcraft, because it happened several times that people in a certain street were hindered by masses of frogs and toads.
168742: A maid coming home from work at about midnight saw a dead man standing against the church, who had been buried two weeks before. The girl nearly died of fright and ran home quickly, where she told her mother what she had seen. When her mother went back with her to look, the dead man had vanished. The next evening the girl saw the dead man again. This time her mother said: "If he is standing there again tomorrow, you must ask: 'What do you want of me?'" On the third night the girl asked the ghost what it wanted. The ghost then said something. After the girl had promised to fulfil the promise, she never saw the ghost again.
168799: Two men walking along the canal in Ninove saw a black cat in front of them and shouted: "Go on, puss, get out of here!" A little later the men saw a gentleman dressed in black with a top hat near the town hall. A moment later he had vanished without a trace. In a street a little further on the men saw the cat again. They struck at it but could not hit it. Then the black gentleman appeared again. When the men finally managed to hit the cat with a stick, the animal burst apart into a ball of fire.
168826: A man who was going to Appelterre with his wife suddenly saw at the bridge in Pollare that his wife had disappeared. At the church of Pollare the woman appeared again.
168838: In Ename lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch. A man who claimed that his son had died because of that witch placed an Easter nail under the threshold, after which the witch no longer came in. In the evening black cats roamed the street by the witch's house.
168857: If people saw a black cat or a magpie, they believed they would have bad luck.
168861: During his life a farmer had promised to give two sacks of wheat to the poor when he could afford it. When the man lay on his deathbed many years later, he asked those around him to fulfil the promise in his place. But the people did not do it. About two months after his death, the dead farmer appeared to his brother with the words: "You must give that wheat, or else I may not enter eternity." Only after the farmer had appeared three times did his brother give wheat to the poor. After that the dead farmer did not appear again.
168889: A mother had had a baby. A woman with special powers had wrapped the child in its swaddling clothes. After that the child cried day and night, so the witch had to be called back to undo the harm she had done. The witch pulled as many pins out of the child's swaddling clothes as she had hairs on her head. After that the child stopped crying.
168903: If you heard a magpie chattering, it was believed that disaster was coming. If you saw a magpie walking ahead of you, you would have good luck. If the magpie walked behind a person, that person would have bad luck.
168919: Anyone with small children who hung nappies outside in the evening had to make sure they were brought in before sunrise. Otherwise a witch could stick pins into the nappy and make the child ill.
168951: A woman from Klein-Sinaai always saw yellow lice on her body. She could not get rid of the lice by any means. In the end the woman went to the monks of Dendermonde, who advised her to go on a pilgrimage. After the woman had done so, she was rid of the lice.
168995: A man whose wife had died believed he had seen his dead wife at night. She had spoken with him and then suddenly vanished.
169018: Near a house in Impe a skin was found in the hedge. Because they happened to be making a fire in the oven just then, they threw the skin in. At that moment someone came running up, crying all the while: "It's mine!" After the skin had burned up, the man said: "Now that I am freed from it, it will surely be over."
169038: A man came across a German shepherd in which he believed he recognised a dead person. Shortly afterwards the dog was run over, so that the person supposedly died for the second time.
169040: A man had seen a devil in broad daylight, dressed all in black and wearing iron around himself. He also always had a dung fork with him.
169129: People who were ridden by the mare had a stoppage of the blood. People who knew only a little French and were ridden by the mare in their sleep suddenly spoke French as well as anyone. Victims of the mare saw someone approaching, who jumped on them.
169162: A woman who was making mittens saw a few magpies sitting and said: "I will get a letter from X." A while later that indeed happened.
169166: One night a boy from Rijsel was coming home with his friend. On the way the two saw a beautiful cat. They took the animal with them. A quarter of an hour later they felt the cat growing heavier and heavier. When one of the boys said: "Damn, this cat is heavy!", the animal answered: "You will take me back to the place where you found me." The next day that boy's hair had turned grey with fear.
169183: At night people heard noises in a barn as if someone was threshing there.
169191: On a farm in Zulzeke many piglets had already died. There was a woman who regularly came to look at the piglets. Sometimes she asked for a glass of milk, other times for buttermilk. The farmer sent for the priest, who closed the stable door and prayed over the place. He also gave the people an Agnus Dei to put under their threshold. A short time later the woman came by again, but she was not let in. People did have to be careful, though, for if you struck a witch, you could die!
169216: A man had mocked a sorcerer who lived between Nokere and Waregem. Afterwards the man could no longer get out of the woods and had to beg the sorcerer to help him.
169262: A woman caused much misfortune on a farm. All the butter and milk on that farm went bad.
169296: On Saint Anne's day (1) the factory workers had to go to the funeral of a man who had worked with them at the factory. Normally the workers would have had to go back to work in the afternoon, but the boss announced that there would be no work that day because it was Saint Anne's day. The men went to a café and played 'gaaibol' (2). When the men got hungry, meat was fetched. Afterwards the workers went on to 'd'Hutte' of Sint-Anna to drink beer. One of the men, who then went home alone in the dark, lost his way. The man had been ridden by 'the mare'. After wandering about for a long time, the man did get home. He slept until eight or nine in the morning. Then his wife said to him: "You came home yesterday without your coat, without your shoes and without your hat!" The man went to the house where he had last been and asked about his clothes there. Those people sent the man to the town hall. The man went to the town hall and then to several other people he had visited the evening before. On the way he met someone who could tell him where his clothes were hanging. The clothes were hanging scattered in various places. Although the man had come home in his socks, strangely enough his socks were not dirty.
169301: At a farm in Huise there was a tree in which a light could always be seen hanging. People claimed the light was a dead person who had returned. When a calf died on the farm, the occupants went to the Augustinian friars, who told them to pray a novena. Some time later the people could no longer churn butter. When the farmer told the friars about the light in the tree, the priest advised him to have another mass said for his late father. The friar also said to the farmer: "If you want to see your father again, you must get up one night." Afterwards the farmer claimed he had seen his father leaning over the stable door at night.
169328: A mother had a six-month-old child that became restless at midnight and jumped out of its cradle. The mother went with her child to the fathers, who said: "The child is bewitched. A woman will come to visit, but you must not give her coffee." Some time later a woman did indeed come by, and she confessed her guilt when the mother questioned her.
169330: A woman who had had a baby was not allowed to borrow anything from anyone or let in strange women visitors until she had been churched. Otherwise a witch would cause the child to die.
169332: One day three woodcutters found three crosses. At that moment the bells began to ring. The woodcutters took the crosses to the church. But the next day the crosses had vanished and were lying again where they had been found. Later the Kruiskapel was built on that spot.
169358: In Ouwegem a werewolf roamed about, who jumped onto the shoulders of passers-by and made them carry him. The werewolf hid his skin above a baker's oven. One day, however, the skin had been thrown into the oven. But as soon as the skin caught fire, the werewolf was already standing by the oven to save his skin.
169360: On a farm in Hemelveerdegem all the animals died through witchcraft. One day the people there saw an ugly beast in their stable, stroking the cows. They discovered that the cows were being poisoned by that beast and killed it.
169387: Two brothers from Erpe went poaching one night. When one brother stood ready with his gun, a little cat came and sat in front of the barrel. The man moved, but the little cat followed. Because the man could not chase the cat away, the two brothers believed the cat was a ghost and fled home in fear.
169393: Sorceresses could infest people with lice.
169444: The hellewagen (hell's wagon) was devils who passed by with their wagon making a great deal of noise. When people went and stood on the road to see the wagon, they heard nothing more.
169447: A large crucifix stood in Kwaremont. It was said to have been put there because someone had once been stopped at that spot by a sow with piglets. That person promised to put up a crucifix there if he could go on.
169468: If you saw a black cat on Friday the thirteenth, you could be sure that misfortune would come.
169505: In the woods a child was given a piece of sugar by a woman. The following night the child lay crying the whole time. In the morning the child was taken to the Augustinian monastery in Gent. Three days later the child died in terrible pain.
169534: In the old days there was a lot of dancing in an inn in Zulzeke. Suddenly people saw a ball of fire rolling there. The next moment the devil came dancing in.
169536: Strange things happened on a farm. One morning one of the horses had its neck wrung. Another day all the cows were standing outside in the yard. The farmer went to the fathers, who said: "A beggar woman always comes to you. If she comes again, you must let her sit on a chair by the stove. Under that chair you must put a relic." The farmer did as the father had advised. When the woman wanted to get up, she began to sweat heavily and could not get off her chair. Suddenly the woman saw the relic, picked it up and left. After that no more strange things happened on the farm.
169576: Sometimes children were pricked with pins. If it went too far, the children died. To prevent such misfortune, many people promised to dress their children only in blue and white until the age of seven.
169585: A mother was doing the washing when a gypsy woman came in. The gypsy woman laid her hand on the child's chair and a moment later was gone. Then the child began to cry. The doctor was at a loss and advised the mother to have her child overlezen (exorcised by prayer). When the priest did so, he sweated terribly. A father from Affligem also prayed over the child, sweating. The mother had to place a relic under her threshold. The next day, when the mother saw the gypsy woman passing by during a thunderstorm, she called out: "Won't you come in for shelter?" The gypsy woman came up the hill but could not get over the threshold.
169653: When people went out in the evening by moonlight, they often saw white rabbits running before their feet. If they pretended not to see the rabbits, they all suddenly vanished.
169675: A man who was ridden by the mare could no longer breathe or move and felt as if a cat had crawled on top of him. When the man heard his name being called, he was immediately freed of his burden.
169682: A house in Nokere was haunted. Every morning the door stood open, even though it had been properly shut. The parish priest or the friars said that the haunting was caused by the person who would be the first to visit the next day. The next day the neighbour was the first to come by. The man sent his neighbour away, after which the door no longer stood open in the morning. Other strange things still happened, however, so that the man eventually moved to Kruishoutem.
169708: A woman with a bad reputation went to ask a farmer whether he would sell his dead foal. At that moment the farmer himself did not yet know that his foal was dead.
169720: In Nederename someone walked about saying: "Where must we put them?" Someone would then always answer: "Put them where you got them."
169721: Several witches lived in Aaigem. One day a witch came into the kitchen of a farm and threw an apple on the floor. The apple kept rolling around the kitchen the whole time. The people tried to catch the fruit but did not succeed.
169744: An old witch had gone to live in the convent. But they could not keep her there, because all the animals died. Every day she sat in the same place in the chapel. When someone had stuck an Easter nail under her chair, the witch went to sit somewhere else.
169747: Werewolves wore a skin that fell to the ground if the werewolf was wounded. When he then ran off, the skin did follow him. Werewolves lost their power when their skin was burned.
169800: On a farm a stable hand was told to go and fetch a sieve. The farmhand only came back in the evening. He was drenched in sweat and said: "I'm completely worn out." The farmhand had been ridden by the mare.
169810: In Bevegem a black cat roamed about, which was said to be a witch in animal form.
169858: A woman who had drunk a dram at a witch's house got a 'pearl' on her eye. The doctor told the woman it was strange that the inflammation did not heal. Only after the woman had made a novena to Our Lady of Lourdes in Oostakker did her eye heal.
169868: A man who was a werewolf dressed up in a skin and had himself carried by passers-by in the evening. After people had carried the werewolf for a while, the beast threw them into the water.
169885:
Some people eating sandwiches saw a witch walk past the sawmill. Just then a carter came in and called out: "That's the trouble with those old people, they're always in the way!"
When that woman came begging, the people saw that the nut had fallen out of their saw, although normally it took a lot of force to remove that nut. They then put a paasnagel (Easter nail, a blessed nail) under the machine to protect themselves against witchcraft.
169912: In a house in Geraardsbergen knocking was always heard. The sound was probably caused by the man of the house, who perhaps walked in his sleep.
169913: A lacemaker heard footsteps in a passage every evening. When the woman went to look one day, she saw a man in a large black hat going to the cellar. The man came to a wall, which opened and revealed a golden crown.
169924: A little boy fell ill after getting a sweet from an old witch. The boy had a big lump on his head. When his mother put him on one side of the house, he cried. On the other side of the house, he was quiet. When her child was completely emaciated, the mother went to the fathers of Affligem. On her arrival her son suddenly became very heavy, so that he almost fell from her hands. A father said: "You have brought her along. She will have to leave." A moment later the child weighed no more than a feather. He lived nine more days after that.
169965: A rag-and-bone man agreed with his son that whoever died first would come back after his death to tell how things were in the hereafter. When the son had died, the devil appeared to the father and said: "They keep a strict account there and forgive nothing." The father answered: "If you are sent by God, speak. If you are sent by the devil, fly away. If you have power, throw me into the ditch." The next moment the father flew head over heels into the ditch. Devils had a great deal of power, after all.
170028: If you heard a dog howling somewhere, you knew that someone would soon die.
170056: At a farm where a cow had had a calf, a neighbour woman came to ask for buttermilk. The farmer's wife explained that she could not give any buttermilk, because she would not make it until the next day. The neighbour replied: "When you pump tomorrow, you'll have more than enough milk!" When the farmer's wife went to pump water for the coffee the next day, nothing but milk came out of the pump.
170081: A boy with a terribly sore throat could not be helped by the doctor. The sore throat became so bad that the boy could no longer even swallow. The boy had to rub his throat with a white substance, but that did not help. In the end the boy died.
170085: A farmer had a farmhand who had sold his soul to the devil. When the field had to be manured, the farmhand took his dung fork, stuck it into a heap of manure and said: "I mine and each his own." The next moment a devil stood at every heap of manure. In no time the whole field was manured.
170100: People who were ridden by the mare lay stiff as a board in their bed and felt as if a heavy weight was pressing on them. Those people could no longer call out and found it hard to breathe.
170106: On a farm in Latem a white lady was seen passing by in the dark in the evening. Nobody dared speak to the lady. In the end it became so bad that nobody dared go to that place in the dark any more.
170153: In Sint-Gillis-Dendermonde there used to live people who dealt in evil. When the parish priest knew such people were in the church, he left his missal open. Because of this they could not leave the church until they had renounced witchcraft.
170159: In Vrasene there was a large house with a little chapel, where a witch lived. At night the cats came to dance around that house.
170211: A maid worked on a farm where it was always haunted. Whenever that maid came into the cowshed, the cows were all standing the wrong way round.
170214: On the Lange Akker stood seven lime trees. In a clay house lived a mother and daughter who had a bad reputation. When a boy was courting the daughter, he wanted to get to the bottom of it. One evening, sitting in that house, he pretended to have fallen asleep. He watched as the women took a pot of witch powder from the chimney. Both women sprinkled the powder on their hands and the soles of their feet and said: "Over hedge and fence, we wish ourselves to the seven limes in Lede." Then they flew away. The boy, who had seen everything, wanted to copy them, but he made a mistake and said: "Through hedge and fence." Badly injured, he arrived at the seven lime trees, where the women were singing "Saturday, Sunday" and dancing in a ring. The boy sang along but added "Monday" and shouted: "Just as fine as yours." At that the whole scene vanished.
170224: On a bewitched farm people always heard banging at a small window, although no one could be seen. One day the farmer's wife was visited by a woman suspected of being a witch. The witch asked for an egg, but in the end it turned out she could not get it down. When the witch asked for some sausages, the meat was rotten. The people sent for the priest, who went to bless the attic until he was drenched in sweat.
170241: A mother with two children lived in a small house in Ename. In a nearby street lived a woman who was said to be a witch. The mother's children were bewitched and died of a heart disease. The witch and her husband passed their magic power on to their son or daughter. Before that had happened, the man could not die.
170242: A farmer heard a rumbling in his attic, although there was nothing to be seen there. One day the farmer scattered flour on the attic floor. When the rumbling could be heard again, footprints were seen in the flour, but otherwise there was nothing to be found.
170263: Three men sitting at a table wanted to play cards, but they were one player short. A little later there was a knock. A man stood at the door who wanted to join in, and the three were delighted. When one of the players bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the stranger had a long tail and two goat's legs. The man cried: "The devil is here with us!" The next moment the stranger had vanished.
170266: People who had been ridden by the 'mane' or led by the 'alf' (elf) lost their way.
170302: On a farm in Heldergem something that looked like a dog's skin was found. They immediately believed the skin belonged to the farmhand who had to go about as kledde (a shape-shifting bogeyman). They sent the farmhand far away and set the skin on fire. A little later the farmhand was already standing by the oven, moaning with pain. When the skin had burned up, he was relieved because he was freed.
170331: When the parish priest turned around during mass and said 'dominus vobiscum', he saw the sorcerers and sorceresses sitting in the church. If he left the missal open after mass, the sorcerers and sorceresses could not leave the church. By placing an Easter nail under the threshold, one could make sure that no sorcerers or sorceresses could come in. Since the Gospel of Saint John has existed, such witchcraft no longer exists.
170332: A boy who was ill promised to build a little chapel for Our Lady, and he told his aunt about it. "I will do it," the aunt promised. Shortly afterwards the boy died. The aunt fell ill and died too. Nobody else knew anything about the promise. On the first evening after the aunt's death, the brewer's wife was home alone. When she went to bed, she heard a lot of noise, although there was nothing to be seen. The following evening the woman again heard all kinds of noises, including the rattling of chains. On the third night the brewer was at home. He went downstairs, opened the door and saw his dead sister standing before him. The brewer asked: "In the name of God, what do you want of me?" The spirit said that her son had promised to build a little chapel and that he had not been able to fulfil that promise. The next day the brewer went to the parish priest and told him what had happened. Afterwards a little chapel was built in Nederbrakel.
170405: One evening four men were returning from a visit to a friend. At the Driestraten in Puivelde the men met a woman who called to them. But the men did not dare come closer because that woman dealt in evil. A child of one of the men had once been bewitched by that woman.
170434: In Onkerzele lived people who went haunting everywhere. One day these people put some ointment on their heads and then said: "Over hedges and hedgerows, straight to the Nunnekesbos." A man who had overheard this said: "Through hedges and through hedgerows straight to the Nunnekesbos." That man flew straight through everything.
170474: A mother always heard a drop of water fall when everyone was in bed. The mother had a child who was very ill. One night the father got up and called to his wife that there was a toad in a bucket under the water pump. The wife said: "Don't throw the toad away, because the evil is in it." The father did not believe a word of it and emptied the bucket. Half an hour later the child died. No trace of the toad was ever found.
170480: Because black cats were often witches, people never dared to hit these animals in the evening. They preferred to take a detour.
170493: A boy from Sint-Goriks-Oudenhove was in love with a girl from the Wolvenhoek. But the boy's mother did not approve of the relationship, because the girl came from a poor family of nine children. The mother had warned her son that he would surely meet black cats one day if he kept seeing that girl. When the boy came to a wayside crucifix, he saw black cats running everywhere. The cats accompanied the boy until he was home. There the animals suddenly vanished. Some people claimed that the boy's mother had a bad name.
170522: People who took fruit to the market in the morning and met a black cat on the way knew they would sell nothing that day.
170568: In a house in Mater, people suffered a plague of rats. When the rats sat on the electricity wire, they looked like birds. That was sorcery.
170602: A man who had a lot of rats saw the animals running over the roof one morning as he went out. The last rat was one that limped. At that the man said: "Oh, you lame one, you had to be there too." The next moment all the rats came back.
170626: A woman claimed that her dead mother had returned and had spoken to her.
170627: In Nukerke a man had died who was said to have been a Freemason. The man had always said that after his death he would come back to haunt in the shape of a large dog. One evening a sister and brother were out together. Suddenly the sister said: "Look there, what a big dog!" Her brother, however, could not see the dog. When the apparition had been seen many times, a cross was put up at that spot. After that the haunting stopped.
170630: A man coming back from an inn where he had drunk a few glasses of beer went straight to bed when he got home. But the man could not fall asleep and got up again. The man's godfather said: "It's a witch's fault that you can't sleep. You must put your clogs upside down by your door. Lay one clog with the point up and the other with the point down." After that the witch could do the man no more harm.
170655: Two boys from Deftinge had heard that you could meet the devil by standing at a crossroads at midnight with a black hen under your arm. They decided to try it and towards midnight went to the Diepestraat with a hen under the arm. What exactly happened is unclear, but at a certain moment both came rushing home, followed by a big black dog.
170680: A bachelor who worked for a farmer liked to go to the café regularly. One evening, coming home past the bridge, he saw a fire burning in a meadow by the brook. He went to see what it was and saw tall gentlemen dressed in black sitting around the fire. When he asked if he could light his pipe at the fire, they answered: "Light your pipe and move on. The day is for you and the night is for us." It was probably a meeting of sorcerers and devils.
170725: In Melden there was a farm that was bewitched. At night music could be heard in the stable there. The cows stood up and looked behind them. When someone went to look, the sound stopped, but as soon as the door was shut it began again. Other noises were heard there too, as if, for example, a bucket fell on the floor.
170728: A woman attending catechism in Wallonia heard noise behind the closed church door. It sounded as if everything in the church was being turned upside down. A dead person lay buried in the sacristy. The noise was caused by the ghost of that dead person, who had returned.
170748: A family had been to the fathers about a sick little daughter. One day the mother said: "Make sure the witch doesn't come in here today, because it's the ninth day and otherwise we're lost. If she does come in, give her nothing and don't speak to her." That very day the witch came to ask for a ball of thread because she was sewing and had run out. The witch had barely gone outside when the little daughter began to cry and pull at her eye. The girl lost her eye.
170757: In a meadow near Hof Ten Berghe the devil is said to have left his paw print in a tree.
170809: If a child in a house fell ill or people had a lot of misfortune after a certain woman had visited, they no longer let that woman in. For people believed she brought the evil hand upon the inhabitants of the house.
170814: In a field beside the road to Lede a farmer had seen one evening that his turnips were very big. When he wanted to harvest them the next day, he found that dozens of needles were stuck in every turnip, so that he had to leave everything for the birds.
170885: In Ophasselt a man went about disguised as kledde (a tormenting spirit that leaps onto people's backs). One day a woman threw a handkerchief at kledde when he leapt on her. Kledde unravelled the handkerchief completely. The next day the threads of the handkerchief were seen stuck between kledde's teeth.
170908: On a farm in Sinaai all the animals died. One night the farmer got up just before twelve o'clock and found rats running all over his farmyard.
170928: A man coming back from Appelterre saw a big black dog walking behind him at the Sint-Pieterskapel on the road to Zandbergen. The man was afraid of the growling dog. He walked past the chapel and made the sign of the cross. When the man looked back after that, the dog had vanished without a trace.
170971: A man coming back from work saw a goat walking with a chain. He tried to catch the goat, but did not succeed. A moment later the whole scene had vanished.
170988: A man who had gone to play cards with his brother-in-law was walking home at night in the rain. The man stepped into a furrow and broke his leg. At that moment the man swore and shouted: "I'm not far from X here!" X was a witch who lived nearby. The next moment the witch came running up, whereupon the man said: "Get out of here, you ugly bitch! You broke my leg!"
170995: At night a train could be seen running along the ridge of the roof of the little castle on the Naostveld.
171053: After the First World War the priest of Grijzeloke was arrested by a German gendarme because he had said in his sermon that the war would last long but that the Germans would lose. The Germans declared the priest mad and sent him to a monastery. After the Armistice the priest returned to his parish. One day, coming back from mass, the priest saw two young thieves sitting in his apple tree. The clergyman had bewitched the thieves so they were stuck in the tree.
171074: Two poachers who had been waiting for game for two or three hours saw three dogs coming towards them. The dogs lay down in front of the poachers. One man said to the other: "You shoot at the dog on the left. I'll shoot at the dog on the right." The men did so, but their guns did not work. Scared to death, the men went home. They were followed by the dogs the whole way.
171083: In Nokere the ghost of a dead woman appeared with the message that people should no longer pray for her, since she was already in heaven.
171122: In Petegem a ghost used to walk about in the evenings. If you stood by the fountain, you could see the ghost walking along the cobblestones. One night there had been a break-in at the farm, although no one could be seen. When the barn door was opened, the ghost was seen sitting there beside a pit full of sheets, turnips and bread.
171126: A man going from Watripont to Ronse saw a large white woman with a dark veil on the way. The woman accompanied the man the whole way on the other side of the road. The apparition was twice the size of an ordinary person.
171127: On a farm worked a man who consorted with the devil. Although the man did not work, his tasks were always done by evening. When one day he had to manure the field, he waited until evening and then said: "I mine and each his own." The next moment the whole field was manured.
171148: A witch from Mullem had bewitched a child in a house where she went to fetch milk. Afterwards the child began to cry. The weakened child was taken to the fathers, where they were given a relic. But it was already too late, for the child had already died. After that the witch never came to fetch milk from those people again.
171149: A girl who had to go spinning in Berchem put a few spools of yarn in her pocket because she had to pass a copse and was afraid. When the girl saw a werewolf appear there, she threw three spools of yarn at the beast. When she got home, the girl told in tears what had happened to her. When the girl's fiancé came to visit the next evening, the girl's brother said to the man: "Well, where is your bearskin?" The fiancé was so ashamed that he no longer dared to show himself there.
171166: A farmer had an uncle who had horse's feet. People who had them found it hard to walk. The uncle was a rich man who left his whole fortune to the farmer at his death. The farmer was supposed to have at least thirty masses said for his uncle, but he did not. After that strange things happened on the farm. When savoy cabbages had been planted, a little later they stood upside down with their roots in the air. When butter was churned, there was ash and coal in the cream. The hens' eggs were empty. The children were beaten by an invisible force, so that they were always screaming and crying. The farmer's children all died. One day prints of horse's hooves were found where the savoys had been planted. The farmer was a Protestant who had once shown the priests the door. When the farmer wanted to call the priests because so many strange things were happening in his house, at first they refused to come. In the end a priest did come and asked the farmer whether he had anything on his conscience. The farmer confessed that he had not yet had the masses said for his uncle. When the farmer had had four masses said, the strange happenings came to an end.
171174: People who were ridden by the mare had a stoppage of the blood. Sometimes one could lose one's way in the snow through the doing of the mare. If one kept one's thumb inside one's fist, one could not get lost.
171175: Will-o'-the-wisps were lights that bobbed up and down in low-lying areas. Some people claimed they were the souls of the returning dead.
171177: A man who was ridden by the mare felt as if a thousand stones were lying on him and could no longer move.
171211: In Grembergen lived a woman who owned books. That woman's brother was a real drunkard. When the man came home one evening, he could not find his door. The witch must have bewitched that door.
171232: A farmer had an old orchard. Kledde (a shape-shifting bogeyman) had hidden his skin in one of those trees. One day kledde was freed because his skin had been burned in the oven.
171247: In a house there were always sounds as if a wheelbarrow were rolling down the stairs. Music was also heard in the chimney. A girl sat under the table. That girl went cross-eyed from fear.
171290:
A man whose foals all got a disease that gave them water in the knees promised Saint Anthony his first foal that stayed healthy. One day the man went to the church with a foal to sell the animal at auction. The man wanted eight hundred francs for the animal and gave that money to the missions.
After the man had done that, no more of his foals died.
171302: In the old days there were people who went about in a sheet or a bearskin to frighten others. There were also people who hung a cowhide over themselves and put their hands in the legs of the hide. Such werewolves consorted with the devil and at night jumped onto passers-by's backs to be carried.
171329: A man standing by a stone wall suddenly saw someone push a black newspaper between his legs. A moment later the man saw something running that looked like a little monkey. He tried to catch the animal, but did not succeed.
171357: A farmer was milking when a witch walked past. A moment later the farmer was thrown under his cow.
171358: A woman was weeding flax with some other people at the neighbours'. In that group was also a woman whom people feared. At a certain moment that woman stood up, saying: "I have to go home, because my son will come home and he'll bring a nice little brown dog." The others were surprised because they knew that woman's son was stationed with the army in Antwerp.
171426: In Oudenaarde there were three fields where it was haunted. Locally they were called 'de drie stukskes' (the three little pieces). Someone had once fallen dead on the middle field. People believed that the ghost of that dead person came back to haunt.
171427: When there were many magpies about, a woman from Velzeke believed bad news was on its way.
171430: Some boys who slept in the attic heard noise outside by moonlight. They looked through the window and saw a calf walking through the tobacco field. Nobody dared go downstairs to chase the calf out of the field. When the boys went outside the next day, they found that the tobacco field had not been damaged.
171485: At five in the morning, in the rain, a man went to the station of Zingem to take the train to the fathers. At the churchyard, to his great fright, the man met a woman who was said to be a witch. The man told the fathers that his little brother was bewitched. One of the fathers then asked: "Did you see anyone on the way?" When the man told of the woman he had met, the father said: "It's too late. There's nothing more I can do. When you get home, the child will be dead. Tonight you will hear knocking at the door, but you must not open it, or you will have misfortune." That night, at twelve o'clock, there was indeed a knock by someone asking the way to Aalst.
171518: A woman who believed it was already day got up by moonlight to go and help her neighbour hackle flax. "What are you doing here? It's only one o'clock at night!" said the neighbour, to which the woman replied: "Someone knocked on my door three times." The neighbour then said: "That was my husband, who died long ago. He comes back every night and knocks three times on the door."
171589: A farmhand who owned a skin with which he played Ossaard (a shape-shifting bogeyman) was sent far away one day. Meanwhile the skin was thrown into the oven. But the next moment the farmhand was already standing by the fire to save his skin.
171597: A woman coming back from the fair was followed by a pack of cats. The woman was very frightened and quickly went into an inn. There the cats leapt against the door. As long as the door was not opened, however, nothing could happen.
171602: One evening, people in a house saw a large black dog come in. The animal walked around the table and then went back outside.
171627: A man took his girlfriend home and heard rattling and other strange noises in the girl's house. When he got home, the man told his father that the house of his girlfriend was haunted. When the man was with the girl again the following Sunday and asked where those noises came from, the girl said: "That's nothing. It's always like that here." That girl was the daughter of a woman suspected of being a witch.
171633: A man was in a relationship with a girl who had special powers. The man's mother tried to change her son's mind, but he would not listen. One evening the man was followed by a black cat on a road in Schorisse. When he got home, the man told his mother, moved, that his girlfriend had followed him. When the man's brother heard this, he opened the door and shot at the cat with a double-barrelled gun he had dipped in holy water. After that the man never saw his girlfriend again.
171652: If the parish priest did not close his missal after mass, the sorceresses could not leave the church.
171676: A man was returning with a little dog from a visit to his girlfriend. On the way the man saw someone standing in the corner of a hedge, listening to two neighbours who were speaking Latin. The man saw that his little dog kept creeping fearfully between his legs. Because the man had become frightened too, he hurried home. At home the man told his brother what had happened. The next day, when the man was loading clover into his wheelbarrow, every shovelful was immediately thrown off again. While the man was working there, a woman came up to him and said: "X, is it true that they come to bewitch you?" Because some people believed the man was mad, he was taken to an institution. Some time later he was cured and allowed to come home. In reality the man had undone a case of bewitchment. A woman from Velzeke had bewitched someone, and two men who spoke Latin had come to the spot to undo the witchcraft. Because the man had told his brother what he had experienced, it had still been possible to intervene.
171679: In Mater lived a woman suspected of being a sorceress. In a house where a little boy lay in a cradle, a hen came in and jumped onto the child's cradle. The boy's father threw the poker at the hen and hit the animal on the head. The next day the sorceress was seen to have a bruised cheek.
171688: When the boys came back from the fair, they were always followed by a black cat. When they got home, they heard a loud bang on the door.
171690: A man who worked at the airfield was coming home in the dark one evening. When the man was halfway and standing in the field, he could no longer find his bearings. Only when he met an acquaintance on the main road, who asked him where he was going, did the man know where he was. The man had been ridden by the mare.
171736: When a witch from Mater had been at a farm, the piglets there died or the children got a 'pearl' on the eye.
171737: A woman who lived by a chapel used to give peppermints to the children. If such a child fell ill afterwards, people believed that woman had bewitched it. The baker put a paasnagel (Easter nail, a blessed nail) under his door. After that the witch left the shop through the keyhole. Sometimes it also happened that people could no longer make butter after that witch had visited.
171772: In the old days people were often ridden by the mare. When they lay in bed, they felt as if a heavy weight was pressing on them, so that they went completely stiff and could no longer breathe.
171781: If you heard a magpie or a crow chattering in the morning, you would have bad luck.
171812: On her way to mass, a woman met a witch and said to her brother: "Look at all those black hens!" The brother saw no hens at all.
171814: A farmer from Zonnegem was still working in his field one evening when he saw some men pass by, dressed in black and wearing bowler hats. The men said: "Man, you must stop ploughing. The day is for you, but the night is for us." The farmer saw that the gentleman had goat's legs and hurried home, for he realised the devil was standing before him.
171844: Werewolves jumped on people walking home and had themselves carried.
171873: A man going home one evening saw a white calf standing in the middle of the road. The man wanted to chase the animal away, but it did not budge. Even when the man hit and kicked the calf, it stayed put. When the man had gone less than five steps further, he heard footsteps behind him and the calf had vanished. After that incident the man lay ill in bed for a week.
171899: In a house where people were having their evening meal, someone was heard striking the windowpane and saying: "Listen to how the bells of England are ringing!" The next moment that woman, who was a witch, vanished.
171902: A man going to the Marolle saw, near Diepenbeke, a headless donkey with a headless man sitting on it. A little further on the man saw a sow with piglets. There were so many pigs that the man could not get through.
171945: In a café in Schorisse where there was much drinking, an apparition with a hide came and sat by the stove. It was the devil, who crawled around on hands and feet and left again an hour and a half later.
171960: In a street in Opbrakel, every evening a priest and an altar boy were seen walking along on their way to give the last rites. The priest and the altar boy were often accompanied by a headless horse. The people told everything to the village priest, who said to them: "If that priest comes past there again, you must take a white cloth and a blessed candle in your hands and ask what the clergyman wants." At ten o'clock in the evening a woman from Opbrakel offered herself to go and face the ghostly priest. In answer to her question, the clergyman replied: "You promised to put up a cross after the death of a certain man from the village, but it still has not been done." The next moment the priest and the altar boy had vanished. The next day a cross was put up, as the priest had asked.
171967: If you saw a magpie on your left side, good luck would come. If you saw a magpie on your right side, you could expect bad luck.
171971: People who were ridden by the mare had a bad dream at night.
171987: A farmer who could not bake bread suspected that his flour was bewitched. The priest came to pray over the flour and sprinkled it with holy water. He also advised the farmer not to let a certain woman in anymore. The farmer had to put a paasnagel (Easter nail, a blessed nail) under the door. When the witch came to visit in the afternoon, she could not get in.
171990: One December evening a fourteen-year-old boy had to fetch a jar of honey from a local beekeeper. On his way home the boy heard a sound in the woods that went "Krrr.... Krrrr.... Krrr". The boy ran home as fast as he could. There they laughed at the fright he had had.
172027: In Viane a child was born so thin that its organs could be seen through the skin. The child did not grow and cried all the time. The fathers of Edingen claimed that the child was under the influence of evil and said: "There is a woman who wants to come in, but you must not let her in. She will come and stand at the window and ask how the child is, but you must not answer." After that the child became healthy.
172072: A werewolf had hidden his skin near a farm. When the farmer was about to throw the werewolf skin into the oven, the farmhand knelt down there, saying: "Let me crawl into the oven one more time before you light the fire, and then you will never see me again." That farmhand had sold his soul.
172082: On a farm a werewolf's skin had been taken away and burned. Afterwards the werewolf wandered about a great deal and suffered terribly.
172103: Two farm boys were in love with the same girl. One of them sought the devil's help because he wanted the girl for himself alone. Whenever the other boy wanted to go to the girl in the evening, he always met a black dog that growled menacingly and bared its teeth.
172132: A farmhand collapsed at the feet of a farmer, his eyes wide with fear. Only in the morning did the farmhand haltingly tell what he had been through the night before. He said that in Kruishoutem he had been approached by a woman dressed entirely in black. The farmhand walked to the brook, followed by the black madam. On the other side of the brook he saw a white apparition, which cried: "I can't get across. I can't get across." In the apparition the farmhand recognised his sweetheart, who had drowned in the Scheldt. When he reached out his hand to her, he was dragged away by the black madam, so that he saw his sweetheart drown, screaming. Then the black madam let him go with the words: "Me here and you there." The farmhand then ran to the farm, scared to death.
172135: A midwife who went to fetch the doctor around midnight for a woman in childbed heard cats mewing at a crossroads. The doctor raised his stick in the air and signalled the midwife to be silent. The doctor said something unintelligible and the next moment the cats were gone.
172143: A man whose wife had died always heard something come back at night. The parish priest asked the man whether he had ever promised anything. The man then remembered that he had once promised to go to Scherpenheuvel. After the man had made the pilgrimage, he no longer heard ghostly noises.
172156: A fiddler who played at fairs was walking home one evening singing, because he had earned a lot. When he came to a meadow, he saw lots of ladies and gentlemen dancing there, although there was no music. Because the fiddler was tipsy, he had the courage to ask what was going on. He was told it was a wedding party. The fiddler then asked if he could play some music. After he had provided the music, his hat was full of silver coins, and he said: "God bless you, good people." The next moment the whole scene had vanished and the money had turned into mud.
172159: Werewolves wore a skin and ran at passers-by. If you ordered the werewolf to carry you, the werewolf had to do so. If you threw an apron at the werewolf, he had to unravel it completely. The next day the werewolf could easily be unmasked because he had the blue threads of the apron between his teeth.
172177: A smith in Zingem had to fetch the doctor for a woman who was about to give birth. Just past the bridge the smith saw a black dog approaching and threw a stone at it. When the smith told the doctor what had happened, the doctor said: "If that happens again, don't throw anything, because you can never know..." It was witchcraft.
172201: At the priest's request, a Dutch skipper had made all the witches stand hand in hand in a row between the parish and the Scheldt. The skipper had gone to the priest because his child was bewitched, and the priest had denied that there were witches in the village. When the skipper's child was buried, the witch who had bewitched it sat at the back of the church. On the coffin sat a little black creature. The skipper had tried several times to crush it to death, but had not succeeded, because the witch prevented it.
172212: A boy walking home on a Sunday evening saw a bicycle leaning against the front of a house. Because there were not many bicycles in those days, the boy went closer. At that moment the boy saw that the bicycle had vanished and that a big black dog was running away. When he got home the boy was deathly pale. He told his mother he had seen a bicycle turn into a dog.
172267: When the witches wanted to fly through the air, they set off from a meadow. A boy walking past a meadow with his father at dusk saw a woman standing there with a brush. His father said he must not look at it. But the witch had heard and replied: "If you say that again, I will bewitch your child and he can fly along with me!"
172272: A vet had to visit a man who was suffering a plague of rats. The vet wanted to be left alone in the stable for a moment with the door ajar. The vet then drove the rats outside. The next day the track along which the rats had run away could be seen in the meadow behind the house. The vet had led the rats to the water. They were rats that had been sent by sorcery.
172289: In a street in Ophasselt, a woman kept seeing a hen walking in front of her feet. When the woman grabbed at the hen, the animal suddenly vanished without a trace.
172293: In Bevere a doctor had said of a sick child: "The child can only live twelve or twenty-four hours more. There is no more hope." A man came into the sick child's house and sent everyone outside. That man began to pray until the drops of sweat rolled down his face. Then he kicked at the corners of the room. The child recovered.
172295: People who were ridden by the mare felt a heavy weight pressing on them at night. When they wanted to sit up, they could no longer move. In the morning they saw something climbing upwards in a corner of their room.
172311: At the Watermolen in Aspelare noise was always heard. Because that place was haunted, the occupants had been told not to stay home alone. When one evening the woman nevertheless lay alone in bed, a head came and stood on her feet and said: "Now your Pie is not home and he will never come home again." The man indeed never came home again.
172329: A cowherd from Schendelbeke was ridden by the mare every night, which made him very tired.
172333: The father of a miller went to keep watch at night on a farm where a foal was about to be born. During the night the man was ridden by the mare. One of his hands moved and he felt as if a hundred kilos were hanging from that hand.
172355: In Doel a child had died after being stroked by a woman. After that people said that woman was a witch.
172369: In the old days, when farmers could not make butter, they believed the churn was bewitched.
172398: A butcher whose stable had been struck by the zwarte hand (black magic) once kept watch and saw a cat walking in his stable. The cat was wearing lots of little bells. The butcher cut off one of the cat's paws. The next day a woman from the village, who was said to practise the zwarte hand (black magic), had a broken leg. The woman was still wearing the bells.
172440: A man who had to keep watch at a farm had heard the bleating of a goat in the trees for three nights in a row. After that, people came from Brussels, Ghent, Antwerp and France to listen to the bleating. The priests put an end to the haunting, but it was said to have returned later.
172487: A ferryman always saw a woman in a black hooded cloak standing there, calling: "Over!" The ferryman always went out on the water, even in bad weather. On the other side he still saw the woman standing there, but when he wanted to let her onto the ferry, she had suddenly vanished. That was haunting.
172501: A hunchback saw some cats dancing and asked if he could join in. The cats took the hunchback into their dance and sang: "We dance, dance, paw on paw, Father Felix, he is dead." At the end of the song the hunchback was flung against a tree, and he lost his hump. The man's brother also had a hump and decided he too would go dancing with the cats at midnight. After the dance this man was flung against the same tree, so that he now had a hump not only on his back but also on his chest!
172552: In Hamme lived a woman who could bewitch small children. When the woman saw a small child in a cradle, she went up to it and stroked the child's cheek. Usually the child then fell ill, so that it had to be overlezen (exorcised by prayer).
172560: One Sunday a man went out in a new suit he had bought on Saturday. But the man was 'led astray by the dag', so that he lost his way. He ended up in a thorn hedge and his suit was completely torn.
172609:
A woman who was ridden by the mare could not move. When the mare had gone, the woman sweated terribly. The woman went to the friars for advice about her problem.
In reality the mare was perhaps a stopping of the blood.
172612: One Sunday evening a boy was visiting his girlfriend. In that house a pig had just been slaughtered when suddenly a rattling was heard. The people immediately connected the noise with a witch from the village. The boy saw a dog as big as a calf in the hallway. He kicked the animal, after which the other people said to him: "You'll regret that. Now you'll become the witch's victim." When the boy wanted to go home the following Sunday, he got lost and ended up in Denderhoutem. He had been led astray by the alf (an elf or spirit that misleads travellers). The boy was walking in a field when a violent thunderstorm broke. Soaking wet, the boy then also stumbled into a pit. The next day people said: "That was the witch taking revenge."
172675: In the old days people were often ridden by the mare. When that happened, they sweated a great deal. To protect yourself against the mare, you had to put your clogs crossed under the bed.
172681: Will-o'-the-wisps were candles that pranksters set floating on the water. It was sometimes said that such lights were the souls of the returning dead.
172696: A man walking home one evening was followed by a pack of black cats. The man kicked at the cats, but the more he did so, the more cats he saw. In the end the man ran away in fear. When he got home, he heard terrible laughter. He was convinced that all those cats were witches.
172731: People who were possessed by the devil were given a skin with which they had to go about. If that skin was burned, those people were freed from the devil's influence.
172748: In Napoleon's time the troops of Berlare hid in the Boskens. One evening a star with a long tail was seen. It was an omen of terrible events.
172750: In the old days people sang a song about a woman who had bewitched her own daughter by giving the girl two apples. The father was often away from home for a long time. When he came home once and asked for his only daughter, his wife said: "X is lying in her bed with a little baby." The man was so furious that he burned his wife.
172753: Because of bad weather the procession of Saint Amalberga was postponed. When the priest came to the church the next day, he found the statue of Amalberga smeared with mud at the church door. The statue had walked the procession alone.
172761: A man going home at night saw a foal that kept coming closer. When the man went back to look at that spot in the morning, there was no foal to be seen.
172774: On a farm in Sint-Denijs-Boekel there was a seven-year-old child. On Sunday the mother searched the wardrobe for a certain piece of the child's clothing. Because it could not be found anywhere, the mother sent for the priest, who read in his magic book for hours until drops of sweat rolled down his face. When the mother looked in the wardrobe again the next day, the piece of clothing was hanging there.
172781: Near Huise a dead woman came back to haunt in the form of a small light that always settled in a tree.
172835:
A woman who believed she had become the victim of witchcraft went to the fathers of Ghent. The fathers then said: "A woman will come into the house. She is the guilty one."
People whose child fell ill also sometimes believed it was bewitched. In reality such children could not tolerate milk.
172850: Some children always went to play near the churchyard in the evening. One evening they saw a little white rabbit there. The rabbit appeared there again every evening and no one could catch it.
172888: A man coming home around ten in the evening suddenly heard beautiful music and saw kings and queens eating and dancing. The man was invited to the table. But when he sat there, his feet were standing in water.
172924: On a farm in Kwaremont a fire was made in the hearth. During the day the people there saw a tall black gentleman standing beside them.
172963: A pregnant woman went to mass in Nederename on All Saints' Day. In the church the pregnant woman saw someone sitting who had a very bad reputation. The pregnant woman sat down in front of the witch. When she went home after mass, she felt so short of breath that she barely made it home. In February the baby was born. It was black and blue in colour. The midwife said the child would be all right. After a while the child did get a normal colour, but it did not eat much. Because the doctor could not help the child, the mother went with it to the fathers of Ghent. One of the fathers said to the mother: "In the coming nine days it will be one thing or the other." On her way home the mother met the witch, who was rummaging in a black bag. Before the nine days were over, the mother was home alone with her children one evening. She heard a knock. A moment later the priest came in uninvited. He asked for holy water and prayed over the child without anyone having asked him. The clergyman sweated terribly as he did so. Then the priest left without saying anything. On the ninth day the baby died.
173009: You must not walk under a painter's ladder, or else you would have bad luck.
173042:
A thirty-one-year-old man who had caught a cold had become seriously ill. After the man had spent six weeks in a Brussels hospital, he was sent home. The man was dying, but he could not die. His mother was an old woman from Maastricht who had always worked at a castle. That woman was said to have once been cursed by her parents. When she sat with her son in the evening, she often saw a figure come in that the others present could not see. A neighbour who was visiting advised the mother to make the sign of the cross with holy water.
The curate was sent for, who said: It is nearly over. But this boy cannot die because evil is hovering around him. The priest began to pray, but soon had to stop because he began to sweat heavily and could not go on praying. At about a quarter past eleven the priest left, promising to come back the next day. In the evening the people suddenly heard a sound at the door, as if someone were coming in, although the door was locked. The neighbour sprinkled herself with holy water and walked resolutely to the door. When she opened it, she saw to her great fright a big black beast with a long tail standing there. It was a four-legged animal that slowly crept away. The animal went to the outer door and a moment later had disappeared. Two minutes later the man was dead.
The neighbour was praised by the curate, who said: Congratulations, you chased that away! The neighbour had prayed the litany of all saints for the dying the whole evening.
While the young man was still dying, the Capuchins of Neuville had been sent for. After his death the house was blessed by a father from Maredsous.
The mother of the man who had died claimed that she had been bewitched in childbed in Liège, before she had been churched.
173056: A drunkard coming home threw a statue of Christ off the mantelpiece. When the man went to work the next morning, he had to pass a crucifix. The man could say nothing but: "They are breaking my arms and legs" and fell dead.
173065: A man who was ridden by the mare wanted to cry out but could not make a sound. The man had seen the mare coming after him, but he had not been able to escape.
173114: Black cats or hens that one came across were witches. A black cat is once said to have spoken to a man: "X, where are you going?"
173170: A miller wanted to build a barn. He met a man who had learned building abroad and who said: "Before the cock has crowed three times, the barn will stand there, but you must not come and look." At night the farmer's wife went to the henhouse with a lamp, so that the cock began to crow early. The barn was not yet finished at that moment. In the morning the building collapsed.
173188: To protect yourself against the mare, you had to place one slipper with the heel towards the bed and the other with the toe towards the bed. The mare could then no longer get out of the slipper and could not go on.
173233: A farm in Volkegem was haunted. The cows and horses there were untied at night without anyone having been in the stable. There was also misfortune with the children. The farm once caught fire as well. In the end the fathers were sent for.
173236: During the harsh winter of 1942 a nun was staying with sick people in Buggenhout. At night the knocking of a hammer could always be heard there. Eventually the knocking could even be heard during the day. Because the phenomena had gone on for ten or fourteen days, the nun became so frightened that she no longer dared to keep watch at night by a dying person. The priest advised the nun to pray a paternoster. On Good Friday the priest wanted everyone to go to confession. But the knocking did not stop. When the priest was at the barracks one night to give a boy the last rites, the knocking could be heard again. The nun hurried to the priest and took him to the room where the knocking could be heard. The priest stayed there ten minutes. After that the nun heard the sound only once more. When the nun told the priest that the other nuns had mocked her for being so frightened, the priest said: "Sisters, you must not laugh about it, for that was the beginning of great calamity".
173270: A sorceress used to live in De Klinge. When that woman had laid her hand on someone's head or shoulder, that person was bewitched. One grandson of the sorceress died of the witchcraft and another grandchild was unhappy his whole life.
173294: A priest coming from Lede was attacked on the way. The clergyman stepped back and said to the robber: "You will stay standing here as long as I want." The thief stood stock-still. A little further on the priest met someone, to whom he said: "Tell that man over there that he may leave now." Then the thief could move again.
173318: In Ename lived a woman who was suspected of being a sorceress. In a family the sorceress often visited, one of the children cried all night. When the mother went by train to the friars of Gent, she saw that the sorceress was also on the train and got off at the station in Gent. The mother said to the friars: "The person I mean has followed me." One of the friars answered: "Madam, you must not speak to that lady. Leave her alone. When you get home, she will be sitting there." The mother was also given Easter nails to put under her door. When she got home she did indeed see the sorceress sitting there. She quickly put an Easter nail under the door. Then the sorceress went out by the back door, although she had intended to leave by the front door. After that incident she never visited again.
173319: A sorceress stroked a cow's tail. Shortly afterwards the animal died.
173343: A woman whose husband had died got up and asked: "What have you come for? Have you been sent by Our Lord or by the devil?" The ghost answered: "You must have five more masses said, and then all will be well again."
173353: A witch sat in church with her back to the altar. Because the sexton had stuck an Easter nail under her chair, she could not leave the church. The priest had to help her outside.
173368: On a farm worked a farmhand who had sold his soul to the devil. One day the farmhand's skin was found in a tree stump. While the farmhand was at work in the field, the farmer heated the oven and threw the skin in. The next moment the farmhand was standing there. He called on Lucifer for help. But after his skin had burned up, he thanked the farmer because he was freed.
