173388: A man who went to check on his cows in the evening saw a light burning in a nearby house. Because it was already midnight, he found this strange and went to have a look. He saw the woman kneeling by a cupboard, sticking pins into a rubber doll. That was how the witch tormented the children.
173405: A carter drove his horse and cart to Wallonia to fetch coal. On the way a woman suddenly jumped into the road, so that the horses stopped. "Get out of the way or I'll run you down," the farmer threatened, to which the woman replied: "Go ahead and drive!" The horses stood still there for at least an hour. Then they suddenly started moving and the witch had disappeared.
173432: A man who was a soldier in Napoleon's army had deserted. At night the man came to a village, where he saw a barn with a light still burning. The man went closer and saw a woman in the barn milking her cow. The woman looked up and threw a floorcloth in the man's face.
173462: On a farm it was always haunted at midnight. The cows were drenched in sweat and the plates rattled on the cupboard.
173533: A man who was ridden by the mare got lost in the Achterstraat. After wandering around for a while, the man made the sign of the cross and found that he was standing right in front of the church.
173538: Werewolves consorted with evil. At a place where a werewolf skin had been found in a tree stump, they decided to throw the skin into the oven. At that very moment, however, the werewolf was standing by the oven. He consorted with evil.
173564: People who were ridden by the mare in fact had a stopping of the blood. A man who had been ridden by the mare twice had felt as if his heart was being squeezed, and he had seen two men coming towards him through a door.
173575: A man went to visit his girlfriend. A witch also lived in the house where the girl lived. On his way home the man kicked at a cat that kept running between his legs. When he got home, the man quickly shut the door so as not to let the cat in. A little later he saw the cat sitting on the windowsill.
173576: On a farm in Outer the sheep were possessed by evil after a sorceress had visited. After the people had gone on pilgrimage to Affligem, the misfortune came to an end.
173626: On a farm there was a sick child. One day a neighbour was asked to come and watch over the child at night. As the neighbour sat praying, she noticed that at midnight a wind seemed to blow through the house, slamming all the doors open and shut. A big black cat was also walking about. These strange events repeated themselves every night.
173627: In a large, poor family in Grotenberge one of the daughters had fallen ill. The girl could no longer walk and lay all curled up in her bed. The parish priest was sent for, and he read prayers over the girl until he was drenched in sweat. Because the priest could not drive out the evil, he had to put it onto the goat the family kept. The father did not like this because he needed the goat to give his children milk. A few days later a woman came to visit and asked how the sick daughter was. The woman said she had given the daughter an apple some time before. Eating that apple had made the child ill. In the end the priest bought the family a new little goat.
173659: People who were ridden by the mare did not know where they were. If you felt something jumping onto your bed, people also believed it was the mare.
173689: A woman suspected of being a witch lived with her unmarried son in a house in Cottem. The son drank a lot and died before his mother. People claimed the woman sensed she was going to die and had made sure her son would die first. A short time later the mother died too.
173741: A boy who could not sleep at night heard the ghost of his dead father say: "You must go to the corner of our field." When the boy had done so, the ghost went on: "Pull out that post and set it further onto our side."
173780: If you stuck an Easter nail under the door, no witches could come in or go out. When someone in Hofstade had stuck an Easter nail under the church door, three women could no longer leave the church.
173782: A sorceress often appeared in the shape of a toad. People who saw such a toad could throw the animal into the stove. The next day they would find that the neighbour woman had burns.
173803: In the old days there were 'loedies' (werewolves) who wore a skin and jumped onto people's backs in the evening. They then had themselves carried as far as they liked.
173824: At four in the morning a woman was returning from the house of her sister, who lived in Beerlegem and had just had a baby. On the way the woman met cattle dealers who were on their way with their cart to the market in Gent. The dealers cursed up a storm, for they were convinced they would have bad luck because they had met the woman.
173842: Whenever a sorceress passed the door of a stable, she always fell to her knees.
173883: In the evenings a sorceress always sat in her cloak under an elder bush in her garden. One day the sorceress visited a woman from the neighbourhood who had a baby. "Oh, what a lovely baby!" the sorceress said to the mother. After the sorceress left, the baby began to cry. Eight days later it was dead.
173887: A black cat often walked in a meadow. People did not dare to catch the animal because it was a witch. After the cat had bewitched the grain, the people had a bad harvest.
173889: Every year Bohemians travelled through Bevere with a bear. The gypsies went to the farmers to ask for meat for the bear and milk for their children. A farmer's wife who did not like giving the gypsies anything did not dare refuse and gave them what they asked. That evening, however, she noticed the cows in the stable lowing without stopping. The next day she went to the friars, who gave her Easter nails to put under the front door and the stable door. When the Bohemians called on her again the following year, she gave them the milk they asked for. The Bohemians poured the two bottles of milk out at her feet because they could no longer do her any harm.
173928: In Viane people did not dare let a certain woman onto their farm. Whenever that woman had been there, a pig always died.
173932: A man from Waregem walking home at night through the woods of Wortegem met two men, who said: "Your money or your life!" The man took out his wallet and gave the thieves a banknote he had bewitched. The two thieves stood stock-still and the man went on. When the sorcerer passed that spot again the next day, the thieves were still standing there. He recited a formula and let the thieves go.
173957: A boatman who had gone for a drink was walking back to his boat. On the way he felt a big cat jump onto his neck. The boatman could not move for an hour. When he got to the boat, he told his wife what had happened to him. His wife said exactly the same thing had happened to her; she had been dragged out of bed by a big beast and could no longer move. The boatman and his wife went to the priests of Dendermonde, who said: "Listen, tonight at twelve o'clock you must go from the Dendermonde Bridge to the station of Grembergen. You will meet something, but you need not be afraid. You must say: 'If you are of God, speak. If you are of the devil, vanish.' If the apparition vanishes, the evil will be gone. Otherwise much more evil awaits you." No sooner said than done. On the way the boatman and his wife saw a little cart painted entirely red. After the boatman had said "If you are of God, speak. If you are of the devil, vanish," the cart vanished. After that the boatman and his wife never experienced anything strange again.
173960: One evening a young man was taking his girlfriend home. On the way the young man stopped for a moment because he needed to pee. While he was gone, the girl was attacked by Ossaerd (a shape-shifting bogeyman). She struck at Ossaerd with a black satin cloth and so managed to save herself. When her boyfriend came back, the girl saw that fibres of the satin cloth were stuck between his teeth.
173985: On a farm worked a farmhand who always hurried outside after meals. The farmer discovered that the farmhand played kludde (a shape-shifting bogeyman) and had hidden his skin in a pollard willow. One morning the farmer sent his farmhand to a distant field that needed manuring. Meanwhile the farmer threw the skin into a burning oven. As soon as the skin had caught fire, the farmhand was standing by the oven to save his skin. The farmhand begged to get back just one little hair of his skin, but he was refused. When the skin had burned up completely, the farmhand was freed.
173987: On a farm where the horses and cows did not become pregnant because of witchcraft, the people went on pilgrimage to Gent. The friar who listened to their story began to pray until he was drenched in sweat. Then he advised them to make a novena and to take an Easter nail with them. A year later all the cows on that farm were in calf.
173990: One moonlit night a basket weaver had come across a black sheep floating above the ground. The sheep went up onto the verge and disappeared.
174007: A farmer from Moerzeke mocked a witch who lived in the village. The witch got angry and told the farmer that a wheel would come off his cart. The farmer laughed in disbelief and set his dog on the witch. But the animal would not move a paw. When the farmer drove to his field that afternoon, a wheel did indeed come off his cart.
174039: In Dikkelvenne lived an old woman suspected of being a sorceress. The children were all frightened when they met her. If a child got 'the old man' shortly after birth, people believed it had been bewitched. In reality it was simply not getting enough to eat.
174062: A ship on the Dender was inhabited by a sorceress. Because the sorceress had no more sheets, she asked a woman from Denderleeuw if she could buy some. The woman gave the sorceress the sheets for free. After the boat had sailed, however, the woman was troubled by witchcraft, so she went to the friars. According to the clergymen, the woman should not have given the sheets away for nothing. After the woman had walked to Halle, she had no more problems.
174074:
On a farm where a new stable was being built, a woman from the neighbourhood came to ask the farmer for eight eggs. The farmer, who was building the manger, said to her: "You shouldn't be asking me that, go inside!" The woman asked the farmer's wife for eight eggs, but she never came to collect them. Later a disease broke out in the cowshed, and all the animals had to be put down.
They sent for a woman who sprinkled the whole house with holy water and said prayers until she was drenched in sweat. The next morning the people had to say a prayer to the spirits before they opened the outside doors. They had to keep this up for nine days. The friars would not intervene there because the evil was too powerful. During the novena the people could see all the evil spirits passing by, but they were not allowed to harm them.
174095: Will-o'-the-wisps were lights that could be seen in the woods when there was a lot of wind. They were the souls of the returning dead.
174142: In the old days there were many women who could do witchcraft. In a haunted house, people found in the morning that their clothes had been stuffed into the stove. Strangely, the clothes were not burnt.
174158: Four women set off together one morning for Kezere. At the police station in Kruishoutem, one of the women suddenly saw four identical white goats crossing the road. Strangely, the others had seen nothing. At café 'De Leeuwerik' the goats came from the other side and crossed the street again. This time two women had seen the scene. Between Hemelrijk and den Doorn the goats appeared again. Three women saw the animals. When the women began talking about the apparition, they became frightened and considered turning back. The fourth woman, however, also wanted to see the goats once, so the women went on. At the Kezer chapel the goats came walking up again, and this time all four women saw them. The women went on and decided to go on pilgrimage. When they walked back home afterwards, they saw no more strange apparitions.
174175: On a farm where many animals died and where the horses were sweaty at night, a strange shepherd worked. One day a farmhand found the skin with which the shepherd played the werewolf. Wearing such a skin bound one to the devil. When the farmhand burned the skin in the oven, the shepherd lay moaning.
174254: All sorts of pins were found in a child's pillow. A neighbour who often came for coffee in the afternoon had magicked the pins into the pillow. The people then put a medal in their house, after which the neighbour could no longer come in.
174264: A woman who had special powers looked after her sister's baby. When the mother asked for her child back, the woman said that the child would then not live another two days. In the end there was nothing for it but to leave the child with the sister.
174267: In a house a cat always prowled around the cradle at night. The child in the cradle cried the whole time. The man threw something at the cat. The next day he saw a neighbour limping.
174287: The farm on the Kamdries is said to have been badly haunted in the old days. In the Middle Ages the castle of Filips van Hofstade is said to have stood there.
174294: A witch had made a little doll with a top hat out of candle wax. The witch stuck pins into the doll and bewitched people that way. A milkman who fell victim to this witchcraft never sold milk again.
174313:
A woman suspected of being a sorceress visited a farmer. After a while butter could no longer be churned on that farm. Every morning during churning a toad sat croaking in the water drain. The people went to the friars of Ghent, who advised them to make a novena and catch the toad. Shortly afterwards the people threw the toad into the fire with the poker. The next day they saw that a woman from the neighbourhood had burns on her face.
On another farm a remarkable number of animals died. The people went to a man from Waregem, who said: "Go home. On the way you will meet someone, but you must act as if you do not see that person". On their way home the people met a woman suspected of being a witch. Although the woman spoke to them, the people walked on without saying anything. A few days later that woman visited them to ask whether she could have a piece of land to work. When the people refused, the woman became angry. The man from Waregem had also advised them to stick paasnagels (Easter nails) into the woman's chair. When the people did so, the witch could no longer get up from her chair. After that she never visited them again. The books from which such witchcraft was learned were all collected by the friars.
174346: A woman became bewitched after visiting a sorceress. She had to have the curate read prayers over her.
174410: A man walking between two hedges felt a tap on his side and was jumped on by a werewolf. The man had to do everything the werewolf said.
174433: In the Damputstraat there was a haunted house. Although the house stood empty, the neighbours always heard knocking there. In the end people from the region north of Antwerp even came to see 'de Klopper' (the Knocker). The police went there, but the officers could find nothing that could cause the knocking.
174448: Some people who came to live in Nokere could not keep pigs. The animals did not grow fatter and they ran up the walls. The people came from Kruishoutem and had been bewitched there. The priest threw holy water in all the sties and prayed until he sweated.
174482: A man was visited by a woman from Eine. When she left for home in the evening, she asked the man to come with her and carry her bag. The man went along and on the way was given a pinch of snuff, which he soon dropped. When he got home, someone told him he had gone along with the greatest witch in the region and that he would feel the consequences. The following Sunday one of the man's cows was to calve. The cow and calf were in poor health, so the man quickly fetched the parish priest. The clergyman stayed alone in the stable for a while and came back sweating, saying: "The cow will probably recover, but for the calf we will have to wait and see." The man had to make a novena. On the ninth day the cow was cured. When the calf stood up, it screamed and fell dead. Everyone believed the misfortune had been caused by the witch.
174531: A woman suspected of being a sorceress walked to a farm where the pigsties were being cleaned. The sorceress saw a pig walking about and said: "That's a fine pig!" When they went to put the pig back in the sty later that day, the animal was dead.
174548: In a family in Nederename a boy had died of an illness. That family had always been visited by a certain woman who would not be chased away.
174585: In Brussegem there was a thick linden tree where the ghosts gathered. Seasonal workers who went to work in France were sometimes approached by women who asked whether that thick linden was still there. They had once had a lot of fun there.
174588: On a stormy September evening a man came running up, sweating and pale with fear. He claimed he had seen the devil near the little chapel in Huise. The devil had appeared in the form of a burning man who spun around, howling and raging. The man had had great trouble freeing himself from the devil's grip.
174613: In Sint-Denijs-Boekel lived a girl who was very ill. The girl's father went to fetch the priest. While the man was away, the mother opened her daughter's wardrobe. She took hold of one of the child's little dresses and said: "Oh child, will you ever be able to wear this again?" Then there were three knocks on the wardrobe. Some time later the priest came to read prayers over the girl. When the mother told him about the knocking she had heard, the priest said: "That is something that does not come from God". After that the girl recovered.
174625: In a house there was always misfortune when a witch came to visit. The witch always appeared at noon in the shape of a big spider that could not be killed. One day a small pan of boiling water had been set ready. The spider fell into the water. A few days later the people met the visitor. Her face was completely burned.
174627: In Eine (Ename?) stood a castle formerly inhabited by counts. The later inhabitants of the castle always heard knocking in the chimney at night. They also often saw gentlemen walking back and forth in the castle. Outside, sounds were heard as if wood was being chopped. The desperate inhabitants sent for the Augustinian friars of Ghent. One day the people found a copper pipe full of money in the chimney. After that the haunting is said to have ended.
174631: At a certain spot in Moregem a little candle was always seen. One evening a man saw the candle jump from one tree stump to another and soon after vanish into a hole in the verge. A few days later the man came home along that same road drunk. When he saw the candle approaching again, he quickly lay down on the verge and pretended to be asleep. The candle lifted the man and shifted him to beside the hole. Then the candle crept into the hole. After a long while the candle reappeared and laid the man back where he had first lain. From then on the man never had a healthy hour again. In the hole a bowl full of leather money was found.
174646: In Outer the white lady often appeared. A woman on her way home saw the white lady come out of a field path. The woman quickly went into a house. When she came out again, the white lady had disappeared.
174647: In Berlare, whenever a beggar woman had been at a farm, the pigs fell ill afterwards and the cow miscarried. People had to pray for the witch and must never give her a slice of bread with their left hand.
174672: A man was annoyed by a cat that always sat mewing by the water drain, and he poured a bucket of boiling water over the animal. The next day the man found that the face of a sorceress from the neighbourhood was completely burned.
174688: A man on his way to Brussels asked a woman the way. But when the man rode on, he kept ending up at the same spot, so that he became dead tired.
174697: In the past people did not let certain women near their child's cradle for fear the child would be bewitched. A woman from Viane who did not go to mass was suspected of being a sorceress.
174718: A wicked woman who worked in the 'bad' houses in Brussels was dismissed when she grew too old and went to live with her sister in Huise. Shortly afterwards the woman fell ill and the doctor had to be called. A priest came too, but the woman refused to confess. One day she died without having confessed. A neighbour said that as many as a hundred and fifty tomcats had appeared that night. They were all devils from hell. The body was taken to the church on an open cart with four women sitting on it. At every crossroads the prayers were read. The horses needed an hour and a half to cover a road that normally took only half an hour.
174719: A man had bought piglets that grew very quickly. One day a woman with a bad reputation came to look at the piglets. After she had stroked them, the animals did not gain another gram.
174777: Whenever her snuffbox was empty, a woman would bring out her cat. She would give the cat a tap, and then the snuffbox was full again.
174793: A family had a baby that lay whimpering in its cradle all the time. Because the mother believed her child was bewitched, she sent her husband to the friars of Affligem. The friars gave him holy water and an Easter nail. The clergymen told him he must not harm the sorceress who had caused the trouble. Some time later the sorceress came to visit. She could not get in by the back door because the Easter nail lay there. She then came in by the front door and went straight to the cradle of the family's other child. The father immediately gave the sorceress a kick so that she fell down the stairs.
174823: If people heard a magpie chattering, they believed something bad would happen.
174824: A woman was visited by a neighbour who asked if she could bake her bread in the woman's oven. The woman agreed because she did not yet know that the neighbour dealt in evil. As she left, the neighbour threw something into the air vent of the pigsty. The next day a pig lay dead in the sty.
174827: A rich farmer from Sinaai had a farmhand and a cowherd who both slept in the room where the baking oven stood. The cowherd, who was twelve or thirteen, noticed that the farmhand was always away at night. They discovered that the farmhand got up at about nine or ten in the evening and took a large skin out of a tree stump. In that form the farmhand jumped onto the backs of passers-by and made them carry him. One morning the farmhand was sent along with the priest to a certain place. Before the farmhand took the train, a gentleman had given him a five-franc coin. Meanwhile the oven was heated to burn the farmhand's skin. But as soon as the skin caught fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven to save his skin. Because he did not succeed, the farmhand was freed from evil.
174856: A boy who wanted to go to the fair in Deftinge got his dog cart ready. When a woman from the neighbourhood said she wanted to come along, the boy decided to go by bicycle because he preferred not to have her near him. When the boy reached the fair, he saw the same woman already walking about there. After he had hung an Easter nail on his door, the woman could no longer get into his house.
174878: At the 'kat' in Ophasselt a farmer had killed a cat by throwing something at it. That cat was a witch, who cried: "You have killed me. Now someone will die here every year!" And that happened.
174898: If you heard the magpies chattering, you could expect misfortune.
174925: On a farm the cows stood back to front, tied to the manger by their tails. That farm was bewitched.
174947: In Munkzwalm lived a man suspected of being a sorcerer. He also had a brother who ran a café. One day the café owner told a customer: "Yesterday they came here to the farm to thresh. But they couldn't get the threshing machine moving. So I put my cow in the harness and said 'gee up'. Then the threshing machine was out on the street at once."
174967: Because of a witch who lived nearby, every child in one family got 'the old man' at the age of two months.
174969: At midnight a boy saw a woman walking in a hooded cloak. He wanted to open the cloak to find out who it was. "Now you will know who it is," said the woman. The boy died.
175019: In Kallo lived a woman who was said to have magic powers. That woman could predict the future.
175021:
When a child suffered from a heart disease, people said the child was bewitched.
A woman from Ename had a baby that always had scabs on its head. The parents took the child to the friars, who gave them a small loaf of bread. While the friars read prayers over the child, sweat dripped from their faces. Cabbage leaves were laid on the child's head, but the child did not recover and eventually died. After the child's death, as many as fifty worms about twenty centimetres long crawled out of its nose and mouth.
175032: On a farm where beans had been picked, a man was allowed to collect the leftovers for his rabbits. He put everything in a basket and covered it with a cloth. On his way home a woman spoke to him: "Before you get home, it will all have wilted." Yet the woman did not know what the man was carrying in his basket.
175079:
A man from Edelare who worked in France got a bit of rye stalk in his eye one morning. That same morning the man's wife was visited by a friend, who said: "I have been hearing a magpie chattering since four o'clock this morning." This frightened the wife. At ten o'clock she received word that her husband had had an accident.
An innkeeper from Edelare had a son who had to fight in the Second World War. The innkeeper asked a girl from the neighbourhood to copy out the prayer of Emperor Charles, because whoever carried it could not drown. The son, however, was taken prisoner of war and put on a ship, which was torpedoed by the English.
175085: Because coal was expensive, many people went to chop wood for a farmer. The farmer kept the trunk and the workers got the branches. A man chopping willow branches told of a woman from the area who was said to have special powers. Another man working there did not believe a word of it and said: "Let her come here then!" A quarter of an hour or half an hour later the man saw the woman standing in the distance and shouted: "Hey, haven't you got a cup of coffee for us? You must be able to make coffee, since I've heard you can do all sorts of tricks! Don't try it on me, or I'll give you a good clip round the ear!" The woman answered: "If you were clever, you'd keep your mouth shut. You haven't even the sense to move your wheelbarrow and your dog. Meanwhile you're cutting down a tree that will fall right on that wheelbarrow." The man laughed and said: "I suppose you think we've never felled a tree before!" At midday, when the tree was almost cut through, the men went to eat. When they came back, they found the dog dead and the wheelbarrow crushed under the weight of the tree, which had fallen.
175123: A farmer had a good harvest, but he had no barn to store it in. Someone offered to build him a barn in one night. The barn would be finished before the cock crowed for the first time in the morning. The farmer told his wife about the agreement he had made. But the wife was suspicious and suspected that the man was a sorcerer. A quarter of an hour before the barn was finished, she got up and clapped her hands, so that the cock began to crow early. Because the barn was not yet finished at that moment, the farmer was saved. That barn still stands in Halle.
175150: A boy worked at the brickworks by the Schelde. People had frightened him with stories about a sorceress who roamed there. One day the boy saw the sorceress sitting behind a heap of rubbish. He asked her what she was doing there and ran after her in his clogs. The sorceress ran to a nearby meadow.
175168: In church a woman sat behind someone suspected of being a sorceress. The sorceress often went to church but never went to confession. She kept kicking the woman's feet the whole time. One Sunday the woman lost an eye.
175171: In Mater lived a farmer who had four maids. Opposite that farmer's farm a chest of counterfeit money was said to be buried. The chest was pulled up with horses, but it could not be opened. At night the horses of that farm reared up. In the end the friars went there to put an end to the trouble.
175224: In Meerdonk lived a sorceress who always sat at her window watching the children coming home from school. She owned a small round box containing a little black ball. She would throw the ball across the room and all the furniture flew after it.
175235: A father did not know what to do with his child, who cried all the time. The man went to his wife and found that she was sticking pins into a wax doll. With every pin prick the child was in pain.
175259: A boy went with a calf dealer to Ressegem to collect a dead calf. At the Dikke Linde in Aaigem the calf dealer said to the boy: "Make sure you don't step on a cat or a toad, because it could be a witch coming to a meeting at the Dikke Linde."
175277: A man from Iddergem who owned a goat made porridge every evening. When the man was stirring his porridge one Thursday evening, a mewing black cat came in. The man gave the animal a little porridge. The next day two cats came at the same time. By Sunday there were already four cats, which jumped up against the man's legs. On Monday evening the man bolted his door. That evening, however, the man saw five cats appear in the form of ghosts. On the seventh day the man went to the friars of Affligem, because he was convinced the cats had something to do with witchcraft. The friars advised him to pour holy water under his door. When the cats stood in front of the door, he was to pour boiling porridge over them. That same evening the man saw seven cats appear. He did as the friar had advised. The next day seven burned women lay in front of the door of the house.
175342: When people finished work in the evening, they usually took a sack of clover or grass home for their animals. A hunchbacked woman walking home one evening met someone who asked what she was carrying on her back. The little woman answered: "A sack of rats." The passer-by said: "So be it." When the woman emptied the sack for her rabbits that evening, rats crawled out of it.
175348: In Bevere some horses stood stamping in front of a cart. A witch who was standing nearby said: "Why don't you move on?" But the carter could not move on. Only after the witch had been given a good thrashing did the horse and cart start moving.
175354: Every night while he lay asleep, a man felt a hand pulling at his hair. When the man told the priest about it, the clergyman said: "That is someone asking for your hand. But you must not give your hand, for then it will be completely burnt. I will give you a cloth to lay on your hand." The next day the dead person's hand was burnt into the cloth.
175372: A woman who owned a few animals could make her hens lay eggs on command. Every time she walked past, the hens had laid an egg.
175373:
A man had gone to pick cherries in Mater. The man had drunk so many glasses of gin that he no longer knew which parish he came from. When he went home, he got lost and had to wander about all night.
People who were ridden by the mare dreamed and were drenched in sweat. To protect yourself against the mare, you had to put your clogs crossed beside the bed.
175376: A boy lying in his cradle was bewitched. There were always lice and other vermin in the cradle. In time the child got a swollen head. People believed the child had been bewitched by a sorceress from the neighbourhood. After nine days the sorceress came to visit. She could not get in, however, because there was a paasnagel (a nail blessed at Easter) under the door. The priest then came to lift the spell.
175423: A woman whom people were afraid of often visited a farm in Meerbeke. After her visit a pig died and a cow broke its leg. A week later the people had hardly any animals left in their stable. The parish priest of Meerbeke said a special prayer and began to sweat while doing so.
175438: A man driving to the market in Geraardsbergen saw a sorceress come out of her house on the way, and she asked if she could ride along. Because the woman still had to change her clothes, the man said he had no time to wait for her. When the man arrived in Geraardsbergen, he saw the same woman already walking about there. She was wearing different clothes.
175486: In the old days people were afraid of black cats because they believed those animals brought bad luck.
175530: In the past people sometimes struck at a toad sitting on a windowsill. The next day they would sometimes see a woman with bruises on her face.
175553: A man from Oordegem who worked as a seasonal labourer in France once went into a café there. The landlady asked him where he came from, and the man answered: "From Oordegem." The landlady went on: "Ah! Then you know where the Dikke Linde of Bavegem stands. I went there many nights and had a lot of fun there. But I am glad that it is over now."
175555: One Sunday afternoon two men dressed in black came into an inn. The men immediately began playing the organ and dancing in the loft. The customers of the inn quickly ran outside, however.
175591: In a family from Dendermonde the children had to go to the toilet in the evening before going to bed. The boys would then frighten their little sisters by saying that there was a green cat under the pump. One day one of the girls asked her mother where that green cat came from. The mother told her that as a child she was playing in the house when a woman came peddling thread, laces and buttons. Every time this woman saw the little girl, she said: "What a lovely child!" She wanted to get closer to the child but could not. In that house all the children wore a holy relic with an Easter nail. Every time the peddler had visited, people saw a cat sitting on their doorstep. In the morning that cat urinated by the door. Every time the mother had cleaned the doorstep with water, she felt unwell for a while. The woman sought advice from someone, who told her: "Someone wants to harm you. That person often visits you to sell something. At this moment, however, she cannot harm you." When the woman was visited by the peddler the next day, the peddler said: "I have had to suffer so much! I have been very ill, but the friars could not give me the last rites." A short time later the woman saw a big cat sitting in the Veirstraat, hissing at her. A little later the woman saw the cat drop dead. When she got home, the woman heard that the peddler had died.
175597: Some boys went to dig potatoes at their uncle's. On the way, in a lane of poplars, the boys saw a tree stump with young twigs growing on it. Every time the boys passed there in the evening around half past eight, the twigs waved back and forth, although there was no wind and the poplars did not move. One evening the boys saw a person crawl out of the stump. The next day a wild pigeon flew out of it. On yet another evening they saw a candle come out of the stump.
175611: A meadow was always haunted at night, so no animals could be kept there. The white lady appeared there and chased the animals away.
175629: A farmer whose stable had been struck by evil, and whose animals all fell ill, had to tear down his stable and then rebuild it.
175631: A café became haunted after a woman had come in. From that moment on the stove would no longer burn. The chickens in the henhouse sat backwards on their perch.
175632: A woman who lived opposite a sorceress had had a baby. While the midwife was washing the child, the young mother saw a toad come in through the water drain. The woman went for the toad with a hot poker. The next day the woman found that her neighbour's arms and legs were burned.
175638:
A man had sold his soul to the devil, so that the devil did all his work. When the man had to mow a cornfield, he only had to mow the four corners, because the devil did the rest. The same happened when planting potatoes. After a while, however, the devil demanded half the harvest. The man decided to give the bottom half to the devil. Since the man had harvested corn, the devil was tricked. Then they agreed that the devil would get the top of the next harvest. That time, however, potatoes were harvested, so the devil was tricked again.
The devil made a bet with the man for ten thousand francs. At two o'clock the man had to appear at the corner of the Kettermijt with a strange beast. The devil had to do the same. Whoever brought the strangest beast would get the money. The man smeared his wife with syrup, then covered her in feathers and put a hen on her head. The devil came along with a camel with three humps. The man won, because he had brought the strangest animal; it was one that had been born without a tail and had an udder between its front legs.
When the farmer had to give his soul to the devil, the two came to an agreement again. They would both fly into the sky with a kite. Whoever flew highest would win. The farmer put on a pair of trousers which he pumped full of air with bellows, so that he could float easily. When the man and the devil were flying in the clouds, someone cut the string of the devil's kite, so that the devil flew away and disappeared for good. When the man came down, all his neighbours were waiting for him.
175654: In Aalst lived a witch who made life miserable for old women. This witch caused her own mother to go bald. In the end that woman went mad.
175681: A witch had bewitched an entire farm, so that the cows and horses died and no butter could be churned anymore. One day, when the witch left the house after a visit, something was heard on the dung heap. The next day all the witch's clothes were hanging out to dry.
175699: A woman who had promised to go on pilgrimage to Zwevegem always saw a cat sitting by a thicket. After that, the woman's family had nothing but misfortune; the cow and the pigs died and the daughter cried every night because something grabbed hold of her, though the others could see nothing. The people then sent for the friars of Gent. When the clergymen arrived, they heard someone pulling at the latch of the back door. The people were not allowed to go and look, however. After that they had no more trouble.
175773: A farmhand going home around eight o'clock met a dog as big as a calf. Because the dog kept circling him, the boy began to cry. The more he cried, the more the dog barked. Deathly pale with fear, the boy ran to the first house he came to. When he went outside again, he no longer saw the dog.
175787: In a house where a rattling was always heard at night, the woman crawled under her bed at night out of fear. When the woman lay there, her head was jerked from one side to the other the whole time without her being able to do anything about it. The haunting only ended when the woman married, but the noise could still be heard whenever a strange man was in the house.
175795: When a cow died on a farm, people believed the animal had been bewitched. Dead cows were buried by the people themselves in a deep pit.
175844: On a farm, a woman had been in the cowshed. She was suspected of being a witch, but the people living on the farm did not believe it. After the witch's visit, however, the cows did not give another drop of milk.
175898: A woman who was often ill believed she had been bewitched by her aunt, who lived with her, and sent for the friars of Edingen. The woman remained ill for quite a while afterwards, but in the end she did recover.
175915: A mother was going to work with her four-year-old son. At the Kasteeltje in the Steegstraat the woman saw a little rabbit running and tried to catch it. But the more often the woman grabbed at the rabbit, the more rabbits appeared. The woman managed to catch quite a few rabbits and carried them home in her apron. When she got home, to her great dismay, she found she no longer had a single rabbit.
175919: On a farm in Zandbergen worked a farmhand who roamed about as kledde (a werewolf-like spook). One day the farmer had found the farmhand's skin in a hedge and thrown it into the oven. The farmhand begged the farmer to give his skin back, but it was already too late.
175967: A man who had been led astray by the 'dag' or by the 'alf' (elf) wandered around a field all night, after which his clothes were completely torn.
175990: An old woman who peddled brooms came to a farm with three children. The peddler always wanted to hold one of the children and always gave it a sweet. After the woman left, the child cried all night. One day the sweet was taken from the child and thrown into the stove. The next time the peddler came by, her hands were burned. She was sent away at once.
176007: In a house, a small child had fallen ill. The child's neck and little legs became completely stiff. When the parents took the child to the brown friars of Gent, the clergyman said, "It is a pity you did not come sooner," and read prayers over the child. On their way home the parents visited a man who had invited them in. The child died. For when one goes on pilgrimage, one may not go inside anywhere along the way.
176018: Some people had cut off a piece of a black cat's tail with a spade. The next day the people saw a woman walking about who had lost part of her leg. The woman claimed that something had fallen on her.
176029: On a badly haunted farm, the cowherd slept in the attic. One night the farmer and his wife heard the bread tins dancing in the attic. The farmer went upstairs and found the cowherd on the stairs. He had pulled a blanket over his head in fear. When the farmer got upstairs, the bread tins were back in their place. The same thing happened there several times.
176099: The little castle on the Nieuwe Baan was haunted. In the evening a big black tomcat always came there and made a lot of noise. One evening the man who lived there threw a glass of holy water at the tomcat. The tomcat then turned into a human.
176108: A boy and a girl were coming back from the fair along the Nieuwstraat around midnight. At a certain moment the boy said to the girl: "I have to go away for a moment. You will meet someone, but you need not be afraid. You must throw your handkerchief at the figure's snout." No sooner said than done. The following Saturday the girl noticed that the fibres of her handkerchief were between her boyfriend's teeth.
176113: A farmer had a farmhand who played kludde (a werewolf-like spook). While the farmhand was in the field, the farmer found the boy's skin. The moment the farmer threw the skin into the oven, the farmhand stood by the fire, ready to jump in. When the skin had burnt up, the farmhand said: "Now I am freed from it."
176133: A woman coming home around half past eight in the evening saw a white sheep come out of the ditch by a chapel on a corner. The animal had no legs and seemed to float above the ground.
176189: In Kemzeke there was a street called 'de Kattestraat' (Cat Street) because at night cats came to dance there, holding each other's paws.
176237: Near the orchard of the 'drie Egijpten', will-o'-the-wisps could often be seen hopping about. They were the souls of the returning dead.
176258: People who had been ridden by the mane (mare) at night could no longer find their way in the dark.
176278: A café in Elsegem was haunted. The door always flew open there and all the objects were moved about.
176282: A man got lost, even though he was walking on a road he took every day and was only fifty metres from his house. The man saw a light burning, but kept ending up in the same place. He had been ridden by the mare. Only at daybreak did the man reach his house.
176292: If you stuck an Easter nail under the door, no witches could come in. When someone in Heldergem had stuck an Easter nail under the church door, seven witches could not leave the church.
176306: In a washhouse where rattling was heard every afternoon, a toad always came in through the drain hole for the water. After the woman had sprinkled everything with holy water, the toad no longer came there.
176326: In a little street in Huise a werewolf always used to go about, jumping on people's backs and making them carry it. It was said that if you could damage the werewolf's skin, it would fall off. The werewolf went about on certain days during Lent.
176336: A midwife had to stay for three weeks with rich people in Elst (1), where a woman was pregnant. The day after the child was born, it did nothing but cry. The doctor was called, but he could not help. The people then consulted the Augustinians in Gent. The friars asked whether they had perhaps lent something to someone, which they had indeed done on the day the child was born. The people were then advised to fetch the lent item back from the witch, pray for nine days and put a relic under the child's pillow. Nine days later the child no longer cried.
176361: After their wedding, a man and a woman went to live in Munkzwalm. They moved into a house that had stood empty for a long time. The neighbours said to the new occupants, "Come and live here and help us..." In the attic the man found a bright blue jacket that had never been worn. He threw it into the stove and never had any trouble in the house. Had he put on that jacket, he would not have lived much longer.
176416: On a farm where the bread spoiled and the milk turned sour, people went to the friars of Affligem, who advised them to make a novena. Every evening a cat was seen on the farm. On the ninth day the cat, which was in reality a witch, came back. A loud bang was heard, after which the animal disappeared. After that those people had no more problems on their farm.
176437: A very rich man who was extremely stingy had been given a packet of biscuits as a gift by a woman. The man would not accept the gift, however, without paying a franc for it. In this way he wanted to protect himself against witchcraft.
176467: In Nukerke lived an old woman who could work magic. On a farm, the cows were all standing in the meadow in the morning, although nobody had let them out.
176476: In Woubrechtegem lived a girl who was always ill. A cat always sat on the girl's windowsill. A witch often came to the farm. She was said to have been that cat.
176477: A farmer had misfortune with his piglets after a woman had walked past the meadow. The farmer went to the parish priest, who said, "Hasn't a woman been near your piglets?" A short while later the animals died.
176522: A devil and a bear are said to have once come to 't Duvels Voetstap. The devil had pressed his paw into a bluestone. Then the devil flew to a tree and from there to the town of Leeuwergem.
176640: At the Paambeek, people always heard at midnight the screaming of a dead man who had come back. Because people were afraid, the farmers went looking for the man with axes, but they found nothing. The haunting lasted a good month.
176660: A man coming back from Aspelare said to two women he saw standing along the way: "What are you doing here?" The next moment the two women had vanished without a trace.
176669: Werewolves were men who leapt out from behind a bush and jumped on passers-by to be carried.
176677: Two brothers always saw a ghost standing on the road when they went to the station in the morning. One day one of the men took a shovel along to hit the ghost. When he tried to, however, the ghost flew away and disappeared for good.
176695: In Wannegem a woman saw the hellewagen (hell's wagon) driving around a farm at night. On the hellewagen there were perhaps angels or devils. Wonderfully beautiful music could then be heard, and a beautiful young lady walked past the stable. When the farmhand threw something at the young lady, he immediately got a slap on the ear. The print of the young lady's hand left a burn that the farmhand had to carry for the rest of his life.
176807: A milkman found rats in his pigeon loft that had been sent by a witch. When the man heard noise in the loft, he quickly went to look. But he was already too late, for a rat had bitten his best pigeon to death. The man set a rat trap, which killed another young pigeon.
176808: One morning two schoolgirls of eight or nine met a gentleman in a fine black suit. In his hand he held a pretty little box. He said that the girl who could run fastest would get the box from him. The girl who won the race got the box. At fifteen the girl went to work as a maid on a farm. From that moment on, however, everything went wrong on that farm. The cows were untied and the pigs died. When the farmer sent for the priest, the clergyman said the new maid was probably the cause of all the trouble. To make sure, the farmer had to order the maid to catch the hens on the ceiling above the oven. If the girl really was to blame, the oven would collapse as soon as she sat on it. The oven did collapse and the maid was scolded. Still she could not part with the box. Only after the girl had once made a half-hour confession to a mission priest did she throw the box away. After that it was all over. The girl married, had children and became happy.
176855: A girl threw a handkerchief at a werewolf and shortly afterwards discovered that her boyfriend had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
176861: A woman who was ridden by the mare lay rigid in her bed. The woman felt as if her blood had stopped and she could not manage to cry out.
176877: People who were ridden by the mare were drenched in sweat and felt something pressing on their stomach. To protect yourself against the mare, you had to put your shoes upside down under your bed.
176901: A man who had sold his soul to the devil received a skin in which he had to roam about at night to torment people. In the morning the man hid his skin in a tree. If someone accidentally found the skin and burnt it, the werewolf was at the fire very quickly to take the skin away. That werewolf from Zegelsem has died, but his skin is still stuck in the tree.
176919: In Marke-Kerkem a figure went about that did nothing but pester people. A carpenter poured holy water on his adze and struck the figure. Some time later the carpenter was visited by the priest, who said: "What have you done now? You've cut off x's head?"
176922: People who were ridden by the mare were usually drunkards who came home at night and got lost.
176927: One evening a woman was coming back from the fair in Sint-Amands with her boyfriend. Suddenly the woman stopped because she could not go any further. Her boyfriend then said to her: "You must lay your clogs crossed tonight". The woman did so, but heard the clogs being knocked apart.
176977: On a farm in Welden, a woman suspected of being a witch was cleaning and milking the cows. "Aren't you leaving for Mass yet?" the witch asked, and the farmer and his wife answered that they were leaving. When the farmer and his wife reached the church, they saw the witch already sitting there.
177001: A witch said to a farmer, "When you churn butter tomorrow, the butter churn will be full of chestnuts." And so it was.
177027: A mother heard him (her husband or her son?) come back every evening. The dead man walked in his clogs over the stones beside the house. The mother remembered that he had promised a pilgrimage to Kerselare. When the mother had gone on the pilgrimage herself, the dead man was no longer heard.
177049: A woman met witte wijven (white women) one evening, who did not answer when one said "Good evening".
177053: One winter evening a man saw a beautiful cat sitting at the edge of the woods. The cat walked up to the man and said to him: "Where do you come from?" The man was astounded and replied: "You beautiful spotted Mienen, why did you stroke me?" Then the cat ran off. A little further on the man saw a cow. He went after the animal. When he met a little old woman who asked where he was going, the man replied: "I saw a fine cow over there". The old woman then said: "You simple soul, there's no cow there at all!"
177054: On a farm in Erpe worked a farmhand who was away every night. One day, while the farmer was chopping tree stumps, he found a skin of kledde (a werewolf-like spook). He immediately believed that the skin belonged to his farmhand. When baking bread, the farmer threw the skin into the oven. The farmhand, who was working in the field at that moment, appeared at once, crying, to pull his skin out of the fire. He had to be held back by force, but as soon as the skin had burnt up, he was relieved because he was freed.
177122: A man coming back from the market in Ninove came across three heads without bodies in the sunken lane of Winnik (?). The frightened man hurried home. When the man reached the door of his house, he heard loud rattling and noise. He saw two large dogs go by, tied together with a chain, heading for the square of Winnik. The next day the man learned that the other villagers had also seen the dogs. That night three girls had died on the square.
177139: A man had struck a toad. The next day an old woman in the village lay dead.
177157: A woman who was ridden by the mare heard footsteps and could not utter a word. When the woman began to pray, the mare went away again.
177191: One night a man was digging in the moonlight on his field by the Meuleveld. Suddenly the man heard a heart-rending scream and a moment later saw a black tomcat with gleaming eyes standing right in front of him. The man kicked at the animal but could not hit it. The man was not afraid, but he gathered his tools all the same and went home.
177235: A few young fellows who had been drinking got lost on their way home. They claimed they had been ridden by the 'mane' (mare).
177241: A person who had got lost on the Pardassenhoek had been ridden by the mare.
177306: A family living on the Reep (1) had a small child. Every evening the child's cradle was seen rocking back and forth. It was a cat pushing against the cradle. As long as the cat sat by the cradle, the child cried without stopping. One day the man stayed home from work so that he could see in the evening what was happening. The man kicked the cat, after which he saw a flame appear. The cat ran off and never came back, so the child had peace again. That same week a man was seen passing by with a limp. That man had turned himself into a cat to torment the child.
177324: In a house in Asper a sorceress had been with a child. Afterwards the child was full of lice, all sitting with their backsides in the air.
177327: Some women returning late one evening from Oudenaarde heard the rattling of a chain beyond a bridge. The women were startled and hurried on. A little further on, however, they saw a whole crowd of little white rabbits, which frightened them even more, and they took a back road.
177332: If you sat down by an elm at midnight with a black hen, a black gentleman would appear. That was the devil, to whom you could sell your soul.
177408: In Berchem lived a woman suspected of being a witch. This witch could make people get a heart disease so that they had to go on pilgrimage.
177424: When the children were playing on the Kleie on Sunday afternoons, a witch from the neighbourhood always tried to give them a sweet or a drink. Nobody dared to accept, however, because the witch might have put poison in it.
177430: A woman visited a farm in Welden, stroked the pig and said, "That is a fine pig!" The next day the pig was skin and bone.
177462: A boy who was often ridden by the mare at night had been advised by someone to hang a flat beet stalk above his bed so that the mare would no longer bother him.
177482: On their way home two men suddenly saw a sow with piglets standing there. The men were afraid and shouted: "Get out of the way, filthy witch." The next moment the animals had disappeared.
177489: Two women who had to take butter to the market in Ninove in the morning had set their alarm clock wrong and accidentally got up at five instead of six. As the women crossed the Grote Veld, they suddenly heard two beasts splashing in the mud beside them. The beasts followed the women as far as the crossroads. There they knelt down to pray the Gospel of Saint John. The next moment the beasts had vanished.
177528: A woman lying in her bed felt a dog crawling onto the blankets. Because the woman could not get the dog off her bed, she had to call loudly for help.
177543: A man coming back from Smetlede was followed by a beautiful cat that would not be chased away. When at a certain moment the man heard a ringing, he fearfully knocked on a door and told his story to a farmer. The farmer advised the man to make the sign of the cross. After the man and the farmer had both done so, the ringing could no longer be heard and the cat had disappeared.
177574: In Ronse the priest said from the pulpit that witchcraft did not exist. The sexton stuck an Easter nail under the threshold of the church. After mass a good many women remained sitting in the church. The following week the priest said from the pulpit that he would name the witches if they did not behave.
177597: 'Berewulfen' (werewolves) jumped on people's backs. They had a skin that they hid above the oven. A man who was out in the evenings always carried a lance. When a werewolf came running up, he stuck the lance into the ground to consecrate it. Then he thrust the lance into the werewolf's skin, which then fell to the ground.
177601: One day the procession in honour of Saint Amelberga could not take place because of bad weather. The next day people were astonished to see that the statue of the saint was covered in mud. Amelberga had walked the procession alone. Since that event the procession has always been held, whatever the weather.
177605:
When the nun Amalberga was cast out of the convent, she walked to the Schelde. There a sturgeon appeared, swallowed Amalberga, leapt to the other side of the Schelde and spat her out there. Shortly afterwards Amalberga died and was declared a saint.
On the third day of Pentecost a procession was always held in honour of Amalberga. When once no procession was held because the weather was too bad, the statue of Amalberga was found smeared with mud the next day.
177623: At a little chapel a man met a small dog that kept running around him. When the man kicked at the little dog, the animal changed into a large horse.
177659: Two sisters went out to the field one evening to bind the corn. On their way home the women had to pass a spot where a haunting priest reading his books had been seen. On a hill, to their great fright, the women saw a black circle with a light in the middle.
177679:
On a farm worked a man who had sold his soul to the devil. At night, at a crossroads, he had signed a contract with his own blood.
When the horses on that farm could not pull a dung cart, the man put his shoulders under the cart and set off. The wheels of the cart did not touch the ground.
177681: A young man visited his girlfriend twice a week. When he came home across the fields around midnight or one o'clock, he often saw ghostly apparitions. One night he met someone who had a whole herd of kid goats with him. The man had to struggle hard to get through the herd, and then he ran off.
177688: In a house in Asper, a man was going somewhere by train. A woman who was to go along came by and left some gold jewellery as a pledge because she did not have the train fare with her. As long as that woman's gold was in the house, the people had trouble with their animals.
177726: A girl coming back from a visit to her aunt stumbled into a ditch and could not get out again. It was as if she was being held back by a strange power. The girl had been ridden by the mare.
177729: A small child did not dare to go onto the stairs alone in the evening, because the child saw a black woman sitting on the stairs. A priest came to exorcise that house.
177747: A man walking at night past a field where a small chapel stood saw three witches dancing and making music there. The man said: "Ah, pussycats", to which the cats replied: "If you had not spoken so nicely, we would have broken your neck!"
177768: A woman coming back from her meadow stopped to rest by the chapel. When she then wanted to gather up her things again, a ghost helped her put them on her back. The woman said: "A thousand thanks!", to which the ghost replied: "I have been coming here so long for a single word of thanks, and now I get a thousand! Now I am released."
177799: In one family a little child had fallen ill after a woman had come round peddling. Because the child cried day and night and the people were desperate, they went to the friars, who told them, "Go home. In the drawer there are three little statues. If you stand those statues upright, the child will be cured." After the people had followed the advice, their child no longer cried.
177817: In the Boekenstreek there were many robberies. A rich farmer who owned some four horses lived on a farm somewhere there. At night that farmer always heard a terrible noise. The cows lowed and the horses fought. One night at twelve o'clock the farmer went to fetch the priest. The clergyman got up and said to the farmer: "Just go on home". When the farmer reached the Boeken, he already saw the priest heading back home. The clergyman had already been to his farm and said: "Rest easy, it will not happen again".
177819: In Louise-Marie lived a woman who often gave the children sweets to bewitch them. Afterwards the children fell ill. Their stools consisted of wheat or maize. One of the children decided to pay the witch back by putting a coin marked with a cross under her chair. The boy never got the chance to do so, however. The witch drowned herself at home.
177843: Sometimes werewolves had themselves carried by passers-by.
177916: A woman went to the market together with a sorceress. On the way, the sorceress tapped the woman's arm several times. At the market the woman grew tired of it and said to the sorceress: "Just leave me alone, will you!" The next moment the sorceress had vanished. The woman found that her arm was covered in lice.
177918: On a farm where the harvest was being brought in, the farmer's wife regularly brought drinks to the workmen. Because one of the men had not always been given something, he made sure that a little later the farmers could not leave with their cart. When the farmers realised what the problem was, they offered the man a glass of beer. The next moment the horses started moving.
177921: One evening at dusk a man heard rattling near Zevenkoten. That place was known as a haunted spot. The man heard the rattling coming ever closer. A moment later he saw that it was a goat following him. When the man reached a street with houses, the goat had suddenly vanished.
177923: In a house in Bevere there was a child who was seriously ill. One day an old woman was seen standing at the door of her house. She was forced to undo the harm she had done. The woman then went inside and took a little doll from the mantelpiece, into which she had stuck pins. She pulled the pins out and said: "Go home now. Your child will be cured."
177928: People who lay crying out and sweating in their beds were said to be ridden by the mare. Some claimed that the mare was a stopping of the blood.
177961: A house in Nederbrakel was haunted at night. Cows could then be seen standing in the stalls, although the house was abandoned.
177969: A woman who was ridden by the mare every night held a knife on her chest, which allowed her to unmask the mare.
177986: A smith who had gone to install a stove was walking home through the Zwavelstraat around midnight. In that street the man saw something approaching in the distance. He took his knife in hand, but a moment later the apparition had already vanished. That neighbourhood had a bad reputation. In the houses mice wearing spectacles sometimes appeared.
178002: A man who had a sick child went to the friars, who said, "A woman sometimes visits you who puts the evil hand on your child. Put an Easter nail under the door and the culprit will no longer be able to come in." And so it was. Thirteen months later, however, the child died. Shortly afterwards that woman came to visit again and said, "It is my fault, but I cannot help it."
178005: When farmers did not manage to make butter, they believed the butter churn was bewitched.
178029: A woman from Meerdonk brought ruin on her own farm. That woman could only die after she had passed her magic power on to someone else.
178045: Werewolves were jokers who dressed up and sat by the roadside to jump on passers-by and be carried by them.
178090: On a farm worked a farmhand who roamed about as a werewolf. When one day people wanted to burn the werewolf skin, the werewolf screamed loudly. It had been his last day, but now he had to start all over again.
178091: Werewolves wore a skin over themselves and jumped on passers-by.
178111: A woman who went sewing somewhere was met every day by her fiancé, whom she did not know owned a bearskin. One day the woman walked home alone because she did not see her fiancé coming. That day the woman met a werewolf. She threw her clog at the werewolf, which had to smash the wood. Then the woman threw a spool of yarn, so that the beast had to untangle the threads. The next day the woman told her mistress what she had experienced. Her fiancé stood beside her and said: "The things you are afraid of!" As he laughed, people saw that he had the threads between his teeth.
178121: People who were ridden by the mare felt a heavy weight pressing on them at night. It did no harm, but it was very unpleasant.
178149: A man who could not churn butter was advised to go to the friars of Gent. A friar said to the man, "You will go home and on the way you will meet the culprit. She will insist on coming into your house, but you must not speak to her." The farmer did indeed meet a woman, but he followed the friar's advice and could make butter again.
178152: A man coming back from a visit to his girlfriend had to go home through the woods in the evening. In those woods the man was followed by a dog as big as a calf. When the man went to his girlfriend again the following week, he took a pistol with him. The man shot at the dog, but the next moment he was surrounded by porcupines.
178157: In the past people kept watch over their linen at night so that it would not be stolen. Sometimes the people would see a lady walking in a beautiful long rustling silk dress. The people spoke to the woman, but she did not answer. The people had to pray for the woman to go away.
178170: A girl who worked as a maidservant in Brussels had promised to have masses said. But the girl died of an illness before she could fulfil that promise. The two new maidservants always heard knocking in the house at night. The parish priest advised the girls to sleep in separate rooms so that they could find out for whom the knocking was meant. The girl who heard the knocking asked: "In the name of God, what do you want of me?" A voice answered: "Have masses said." The priest advised the girl to lay a white handkerchief over her hands, since the ghost would come back to thank her. The dead girl did indeed burn her hand into the handkerchief.
178191: A witch did evil while she was baking bread. When she stood at the kneading trough, her spirit was elsewhere.
178229: A woman had changed herself into a mouse in order to bewitch the pigs on a farm in that shape. When the mouse tried to crawl into a hole, a cat pounced on her, and she nearly died.
178251: A farmer ploughing his field in the evening saw a group of gentlemen dressed in black approaching. The gentlemen said the farmer had to go home and continued: "The day is for you, but the night is for us." Those were the devils out on the prowl.
178281: In Nederhasselt a woman is said to have once fallen into the stone-lined well. When the woman came out of the well, she was strangely not wet. People said that the woman was a witch and were afraid of her.
178311: In the past people hid their money in a wall. If those people died before they could tell anyone where the money was, they returned after their death to point it out.
178317: A man whose four-year-old child had stopped growing went to the friars of Affligem, because he blamed the trouble on a wicked woman who had visited him. The friar could not solve the problem, however. Some time later the curate came to read prayers over the child. After that it recovered.
178318: A woman suspected of being a witch went to live in the hospital in her old age. Bread was baked at that hospital. One day, when the witch walked into the kitchen while bread was being baked, the dough fell apart into lumps. A nun who wore a key chain on her habit was astonished when all the links of the chain suddenly broke.
178323: A farm in Elsegem was badly haunted. One day seven billy goats were seen in the orchard there, picking plums.
178377: In a house where they had a beautiful little black cat, a rabbit went missing one morning. The cat got the blame and was beaten to death. The next morning all the rabbits lay dead. The cat had been some devil that had come to earth in the form of an animal.
178381: During the First World War many poor families lived near 't Kruisen. One night two men went to smuggle a sack of potatoes. When the men stopped to rest for a moment, they saw two figures with a lantern behind the hedge, burying a box of money with a spade. As soon as the two apparitions had gone, the smugglers dug up the money to share it between them. One smuggler spent all the money on drink; the other bought a farm with it. But that farm always had bad luck. The man's wife fell ill and died. Shortly afterwards the man himself fell ill and died too. The farmer's wife who later came to live on the farm with her husband also died. Sometimes the cows had been untied, and at other times they were tied so tightly that nobody could untie them. The chain that held the gate shut had so many knots in it that the gate could no longer be opened. All these strange events were caused by the spirits of the dead, who had returned because their money had been taken.
178382: A man went to Halle with a friend. Two men who had left for Halle much earlier arrived only after them. On the way they had met a witch, who had made them lose their way. One of those men was going to Halle for the fortieth time.
178383: If you saw a spider in the morning, it would be a busy day. If you saw a spider in the afternoon, you would have good luck. If the spider appeared in the evening, you could expect love. If you saw a spider sitting in its web in the morning or during the day, bad weather was on its way.
178425: A man stayed home alone with his child lying in the cradle while his wife was at the six o'clock early Mass. When the man had gone outside for a moment and came back in, he saw a little woman fiddling at the child's cradle. Shortly afterwards the child got a heart disease, so the father made a pilgrimage to Wannegem-Lede on a Sunday. After that the child recovered. The father had also been to the friars of Gent, who had asked him whether he knew the culprit. The man had answered, "Yes, I know her very well." The friars told the man to leave that woman alone.
178445: A man who was bewitched always thought he saw someone approaching who was invisible to everyone else.
178471:
A man walking home in the evening saw a pretty kitten on the way. He stroked the animal and said: "Pretty spotted kitten, where are you going?" When the man came to that spot again the next day, he heard a whole troop of cats singing in the air: "X stroked me, pretty spotted kitten where are you going?"
The witches were singing that song, but the man could not see anything.
178497: Every Sunday a man drove his mistress to church in the cart, because the farm lay far from the church. Just after they had left the farm, they saw a witch from the village walking along. After a twenty-minute ride in the cart they reached the church, where the witch, strangely enough, was already standing by the holy water font.
178524: A sick little boy could not be helped by the doctor. Every evening there was a knock at the door of that house. When the father went to look, he saw a red tomcat running away. The priest was called in, and he told the people they must not believe in witchcraft. Only three or four weeks later was the tomcat no longer seen, and the boy began to recover.
178525: A werewolf was someone who dressed up in an animal skin. When the werewolf met someone, he had that person carry him.
178554: A father had had a child who died at the age of two. The souls of children who died before making their Solemn Communion were lost. One evening the man saw a star fly upwards. That was the soul of his dead child. Will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of children who had died before they could make their Solemn Communion.
178572: A witch had been lying at the entrance to a field for at least twenty-four hours. Nobody dared go near her. At a certain moment the witch had vanished without anyone seeing where she had gone.
178597: A soldier was ridden by the mare every night, so that he could not breathe.
178644: In Kastel there was a haunted house. Someone in that house was always ill.
178645: In one house two children had died within eight days. The people believed the misfortune had something to do with witchcraft. One day a man from Wallonia came into the house and said, "You will have more misfortune. When the witchcraft on the children has run its course, the animals will be the victims. If you want to be rid of the evil, you must slaughter one animal." The farmer slaughtered one of his animals and indeed had no more trouble.
178647: Sometimes the returning dead would come into a house in the evening and stop the spinning wheel, so that people could no longer go on working.
178675: A witch from Moerzeke had caused several cows to die at a farmer's in Kastel.
178692: Sorceresses had a little pot hanging on a wall. When they put their hand in the pot and said: "Over hedge and hedgerow," they were flying through the air a moment later.
178719: A man who stood under the Dikke Linde (Big Linden) of Bavegem at night could make a thousand black cats and dogs come to him. That man probably kept company with witches.
178728: A farm in Doel was haunted. The farmer's wife saw the wizard who was at work there, but the farmer did not see him. One day the wife said: "He's there again!", whereupon the wizard dragged her through the chimney three times, so that she was completely black. The farmer only saw that his wife had suddenly turned black.
178789: In Zarlardinge there was a wood called 't Wolvenkot' (the Wolf's Den). In the old days it was dangerous there because people were often jumped on by werewolves.
178816: A man from the Overdijkstraat was coming back from the inn one evening. At 't Toreken the man came across a pack of cats. Because the man had often heard that cats were ghosts, he said: "Hello, cats." The man turned around and got away as fast as he could.
178842: A witch lived in Ronse. A woman walking past that house in the evening with her husband, her mother and her father saw a large black dog walking behind her. The woman's mother saw the dog too, but the men saw nothing.
178875: On a farm where no butter could be made, angels were always seen at night by the chapel the family had put up in front of their house. The angels moved back and forth between the farm and the chapel. One day someone shot at the angels. But in vain, because the bullet had not been laid in holy water.
178917: In a house in Sint-Gillis, stones fell into the children's cradle. The parish priest announced from the pulpit that these practices had to stop, or else he would name the culprit. Fortunately the strange events came to an end.
178950: A farm in the Doelestraat was always haunted. A sexton who came to the farm to give someone the last sacraments heard music coming out of the ground there.
178982: A farmer going to manure his field got stuck with his cart and sent for a friar from Gent. One of the friars said: "The person causing this will come during the day to fetch a bundle of straw. You must give it to him." The people did as advised and had no more trouble.
179001: Some people returning from a visit to their uncle saw three cats sitting on the steps of their house. The cats kept scratching at the wall, so that the people could hardly get in. Once inside, they found their five cats sitting on the floor eating around a dish. The people could not make sense of it and went back outside. The three cats that had been sitting there had vanished.
179066: In the old days, if people saw rats running on a farm and had no more milk, they believed the farm was haunted. Several hundred years ago a woman is said to have been burned on the Toveresseplein because she was accused of witchcraft.
179121: In a haunted house in Nokere the people always had bad luck. The animals died and the occupants fell ill. One of the occupants who had died had to come back after his death because he had not divided his inheritance properly. People believed this was the cause of the bad luck.
179148: A man saw train carriages flying through the air by his door. It also looked as if there were people in the carriages.
179149: In the old days the Kete was badly haunted. When the farmer's wife was alone in the house because the others were milking the cows, she saw the clogs dancing. When someone went to look in the horse stable at midnight, all the horses had changed places and were tied up back to front. So they went to the friars in Gent. A friar who came to read prayers over the farm sweated terribly. He advised the people to send the cowherd away. After they had done so, the strange events came to an end.
179177: Ossaard wore a bearskin and made people carry him. He associated with the devil. When people burnt Ossaard's skin, they had to send him far away. But as soon as the skin caught fire, Ossaard was already at the oven to save it.
179193: In Nazareth a witch had bewitched a child. After the dean had read prayers over the child, it recovered.
179200: In the evening will-o'-the-wisps could be seen on the hills and in the churchyards. They were the little souls of the dead who still had to do penance.
179202: A man crossing the main road during the war walked face first into the hedge. Then the man ended up knee-deep in water. But he kept on walking until he finally reached his house. The man had been ridden by the mare.
179257: In the past there were many women who did evil. To protect themselves, people put Easter nails under the threshold so that those women could no longer come in. Children who had been touched by such a woman were possessed by the evil hand.
179310: At the roadside chapel on the Huigenveld in Sint-Antelinks it was haunted. A man who passed there one night between twelve and one heard a mournful wailing. That convinced the man that the place was indeed haunted.
179314: If you had put your clogs upside down beside the bed, you could be ridden by the mare, which made you sweat a lot.
179336: A woman who had pearls (spots) on her eye believed she was bewitched and used herbs to cure her eye.
