179344: A newly married woman was visited by a witch who put curses on her. Shortly afterwards all the woman's animals died. The last animal to die was the cat. The friars of Lokeren came and found a thick book at the woman's house. After the book had been burned, the witchcraft came to an end.
179357: A house in Denderwindeke was haunted. At night knocking on the door could always be heard there. When the occupant went to look, he saw something white fly away.
179413: People who had been ridden by the mare had a stopping of the blood. A man who had been ridden by the mare wandered about for two hours and kept ending up in the same place.
179433:
In one house a daughter had fallen ill and died. Eight days later another daughter in that family fell ill. When the girl had already gone blind, the father went on a pilgrimage for her. While the father was away, the girl could suddenly see again. By evening the girl was cured. That same evening a witch from the neighbourhood came to bring a little tart. The father was not allowed to harm her, the friars had said.
The witch had to come and undo the evil she had done by putting the tart under the girl's pillow.
179437: One evening a cattle dealer was driving with his wife past the Dikke Linde in Bavegem. There the man said to his wife: "They say the devils come here at night. Well, let them come now!" The next moment the carriage was surrounded by little men in red caps. The man left as fast as he could and never went to that place again.
179455: A man out hunting saw a flock of wild ducks in front of him. The man wanted to kick at the ducks, but he could not hit them. When he got home the man felt so ill that he crawled into bed and died.
179459: During high mass, a woman who was home alone always heard a terrible noise. Someone came to look in at the window and make gestures. The horses began to move about and the chains rattled, though there was nothing to be seen. People believed it was an apostate priest who came back to haunt after his death.
179460: A drunkard who stood cursing by a crucifix saw a coach with two white horses approaching. The man was drenched in sweat and was thrown back and forth in the ditch. After that the man would not go to that place in the dark for all the money in the world.
179529: Every Sunday when High Mass began, a hare ran across the cobblestones in Stekene. No one managed to catch the hare. One day the hare was chased into the church. A moment later a blow was heard on the corpse door. Someone then said: "Damn, that's H. haunting, he's keeping people from their Mass." In the end H. was caught, tied to a stake at the Bormte and burned alive. His ashes were taken to the churchyard.
179534: Black cats were often witches. At midnight they held gatherings at crossroads to work their magic.
179547: When a toad came into a house, people said: "That is a witch coming in. Kick it and throw it in the stove." No sooner said than done. The next day people heard that a woman from the village had hurt herself.
179554: In Leupegem lived a witch who walked three times around a tree in the woods and then had loaf sugar. People said: "Make sure you never pick up sugar, because it belongs to x. She is a witch and you will be bewitched too."
179557: Before midnight witches had no power, because the Gospel of Saint John was still in effect then. Once, in a stable in Outer, two animals disappeared through the doing of witches.
179579: A man from Galmaarden went to the friars of Affligem because his family was plagued by illness. The friar predicted that the man would see something special one night. One night around one o'clock the man did indeed see something flying. The friend who was with him had not seen the strange phenomenon.
179581: A witch was helping to bind the harvest on a farm. When a thunderstorm threatened to break, the woman bound a few sheaves together and said: "I mine and each his own." A moment later the whole harvest was bound.
179608: On an old farm there was dancing and music every evening. The people living on the farm even saw the king appear with his wife. Because the farmer's daughter was terrified at the sight of the ghostly apparitions, the farmhand had to sleep at the farm. But when the farmhand was seized by the throat one night and nearly strangled, he declared he would not sleep there any longer.
179614: It was said that witches held meetings at the Poederbossen. When one day a wasps' nest had to be removed from a tree, people happened to find a werewolf skin there. They wanted to burn the skin, but at that moment a neighbour stood by the fire, begging to get his skin back; he had paid seven stuivers for it and had to visit seven parishes with it. They agreed that the neighbour could earn seven stuivers without being a werewolf. They gave the neighbour back the skin and told the priest everything. The priest said that the man had sold his soul to the devil, went to the man and began to pray. During this intervention the devils pulled the werewolf by his hair up to the ceiling. He even fell ill from it.
179651: If a witch had touched a child's head, you had to strike the witch herself as well to make her powerless.
179709: A woman was working in the scullery when suddenly there was a big frog on the floor. The woman stamped on the frog with her clog and crushed the animal. But when she lifted her foot, the frog had vanished without a trace. The woman could not find the frog anywhere. A while later she saw a witch from the neighbourhood pass by. She walked completely bent over, as if her back hurt.
179728: A brewer's wife was involved in evil and was forced to turn her husband's beer into water. The brewer always saw a black cat walking near him and once threw the animal into the oven. The cat burned its paws. The next day the brewer's wife was found with burned hands.
179745: On a farm in Aalst there was much misfortune. There was often too little milk or none at all. In winter people stuck bundles of straw in the stable windows for warmth. The next day the straw lay scattered all over the farmyard. A friar from Affligem came to the farm, but he could not stand it there. Two friars had to come to the farm twice. After they had read prayers over the place, they said: "The person who is doing this to you will come and ask what has happened, but you must not tell her." When the witch came by, the people did not say what had happened. At that the witch cried: "But how is it then that you no longer have any misfortune?"
179769: Fireballs were caused by cosmic energy. But people also told of will-o'-the-wisps that wanted to be baptised.
179770: Along the road to Bazel stood a row of tree stumps where a man came to preach in the evening with the words: "Sante craie, mila mensa creza, the pulpit on which I stand should fall to pieces". Then the apparition vanished.
179801: Witches could change themselves into calves or cats. If you met such an animal in the evening, you were not allowed to harm it.
179871: Some men wanted to carry the statue of Saint Martin from the church of Eichem to that of Appelterre. But when they reached Appelterre territory, they could go no further. So they had to bring the statue back.
179880: On a farm in Denderleeuw the farmhand had to take the horse to the clover field at night. When he was about to leave, however, he saw two horses standing there. He jumped onto one of them. The horse ran off with the farmhand and the boy was never seen again.
179935: Two men driving to Uitbergen saw kledde (a werewolf-like spook) lying in front of their wheel on the Gentweg. The men did not dare drive past it and trembled with fear. When they got home, the men found the skin of kledde and threw it into the oven. At that very moment a man from the neighbourhood appeared, pleading: "My skin, my skin!" Had he not been held back, he would have jumped into the oven. When the skin had burnt up, the man was freed.
179966: Every evening a woman heard footsteps in the attic. She told her husband and had a young man come with a gun. Together they went upstairs, but there was nothing to be seen. The parish priest asked the woman whether she had forgotten a promise. The woman remembered that she had promised to have a mass said for her first husband. After the woman had kept that promise, she no longer heard the sound.
179985:
A man from Welden who was going to the market in Ename came into the house of a family in Ename who had a child. After the man had given the child a pat on the back, the child's father quickly gave the man a tap on the head. After all, sorcerers were powerless if you could strike them higher up.
A man coming back from Oudenaarde gave the children of that family a cake. Luckily the children had shared the cake, so the magic was weaker. Still, one of the children fell seriously ill, and the friars had to be consulted.
180016: People faced with witchcraft used to go for advice to the friars of Ghent. One man had been given bread by the friars to feed to his animals. In the old days, when people had misfortune they could not explain, they put it down to witchcraft.
180021: Some seventy years ago Daknam was said to be haunted. A woman had said: "Go to that tree, pull on it and lots of five-franc pieces will fall out." What the woman predicted did indeed come true. But when the people wanted to pick up the coins, they found that the money had turned into leaves. According to the witch, this was because the men had bent down to pick up the money. They should have gone down on their knees.
180030: A man went to work for people who had special powers. The man had much misfortune. He fell ill and the parish priest could not help him. The man's hen walked around for three days without being able to lay her egg. When the egg was finally laid, there turned out to be a little black creature inside. If you touched the creature's tail, blood came out. One day someone advised the man to tell the priest that he had worked for those people. When the man did so, the clergyman said: "In future you must never wait so long again. You must tell this to no one. Never accept anything from that family again, and if you must, say 'God reward you' or 'merci'."
180056: In the marshes between Erondegem and Impe an eerie sound like the bleating of a goat was heard at night. Because people feared it was the spirit of a damned soul, they went to the priest for advice. Three priests came, including those of Impe and Erondegem. The priests went into a house and asked that the windows be opened. Strangely enough, the strange sound was never heard again after that.
180105: In a house in Bevere there was a child who one evening began to cry ceaselessly in its bed. The parents suspected a woman from the neighbourhood of having bewitched their child. Someone advised the parents to set the child's clogs upside down beside the bed, so that the witch could not get past them. When this had been done, the witch kept walking restlessly up and down the street. She always came as far as the door of the house, but she did not come in.
180106: A woman walking her children to school saw an old woman with an umbrella approaching. The old woman gave the children a mint. One child did not dare eat the mint, but the other did. When she got home, the mother found that the child who had eaten the mint had a stomach ache.
180143: Strange things happened at night at a butcher's. Whenever the butcher went somewhere to salt a pig, it looked as if his whole house was on fire. A moment later the flames had disappeared. A man was always seen standing in a cherry tree.
180144: Every evening a boy and a neighbour boy took food scraps to a farm where animals were kept. One winter evening at around half past eight the boys saw a pretty girl standing there. The boys recognised the figure as a girl who lived in their neighbourhood and began talking to her. The girl did not answer, however. A little later the figure turned into a whirlwind. The boys ran away in fear and were drenched in sweat when they got home.
180145: People who were ridden by the mare felt as if a heavy weight was pressing on them. They wanted to cry out, but no sound came. Perhaps these people had a stopping of the blood.
180240: On a farm the cows lay in the trough with their legs in the air. During high mass the sheep stood in the stable with their heads askew. The friars gave the farmer an Easter nail to put under the threshold.
180255: In the old days, of someone who behaved wildly it was said that he or she had been ridden 'by the mane' (mare).
180287: In Ouwegem lived a woman who people said could do witchcraft. A lawsuit was brought against her because she was said to have put 'de koek en het hertegespan' (a bewitchment causing a lump and heart-tightness) on someone.
180314: A farmhand owned a bearskin that he hid in a tree by day and in which he roamed about at night as Osschaart (a werewolf-like spook). After consulting the friars, the farmer had found his farmhand's skin and thrown it into the oven. A friar read prayers over the farmhand while his skin lay in the oven. The friar sweated terribly and the farmhand was very restless.
180336: On a farm in Aspelare where there was much misfortune, the parish priest came to undo the witchcraft. When a woman appeared on the farm, the farmer shot at her. Then the woman flew through everything, scorching the green beans. The clergyman knew what had happened and said to the farmer: "You risked shooting yourself dead. You must not do that. Now I have to come again to drive out the witchcraft. If you had not shot, it would already have been over."
180346: One evening a woman from Zele saw a little nun walking around outside with a rattling rosary. In reality the little nun was a ghost.
180357: A woman whom everyone feared often gave the children a sweet. Most of the children threw the sweet away at once. One child who had eaten its sweet was never healthy again afterwards.
180392:
A man went to Brussels to look for work on the railway. He wanted to lodge with a farmer, but the farmer explained that nobody would stay the night with him because his farm was haunted. The man was not afraid, however, and went to sleep in the horse stable on condition that the farmer stayed with him. At twelve o'clock the horses began to kick and make a racket. The men saw a rat sitting on the horse's back and stabbed the animal with a dung fork.
The next day the farmhand told the farmer that his wife had a hole in her back. After the farmer had explained what had happened in the night, the farmhand said: "I'm going home at once. My wife must confess everything or I'll kill her." The woman confessed everything and began to cry. They then went to the friars, after which the witchcraft came to an end.
180395: A farmer had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a new barn that had to be finished before the first cockcrow. When the farmer saw that the barn was almost finished, he ran to the henhouse and clapped his hands, whereupon the cock began to crow. Because the barn was not quite finished at that moment, the farmer was allowed to keep his soul. But the hole in the barn roof could never be closed.
180476: A man went to the friars of Affligem for his bewitched son. The clergymen explained to the man who the culprit was and said: "Within twenty-four hours she will come to visit with a packet of sweets or something else. But you must not accept it." A while later a woman did indeed come to visit, bringing sweets for the boy. After the man had sent that woman away, she came back to ask for a clog nail. This time too the father showed her the door. Eight days later the son was cured.
180509: In Vlekkem lived a man who was often ridden by the mare. He would hear a fluttering, after which the mare crawled onto him and he began to sweat and could no longer move. A short time later he heard the mare flutter away.
180539: A woman came to a farm to say that the sow had given birth to twelve piglets, one of which was stillborn. That woman knew it before the farmer had seen it.
180574: If you spun a chair on one leg anticlockwise, you would have bad luck. Children were also not allowed to turn the bowls on the table in that direction.
180593: A werewolf often used to go about in the woods at Axelwalle. One evening the werewolf tried to jump on someone's back. But its skin fell to the ground, and the werewolf was recognised. The werewolf pleaded that his time was almost up and persuaded the person who had recognised him not to tell anyone.
180601: A carter had to fetch a cartload of wood in Sint-Gillis. As he drove past the church, he saw a saint hanging against the wall in a little wooden shrine. The carter said: "He looks so sad standing there. He can come for a ride with me." He took the saint out of the shrine and put it on his cart. From that moment the horse began to sweat terribly and could barely move forward. When the carter came back from Sint-Gillis with the sweating horse, he put the statue back in its shrine. After that the horse went on without any trouble.
180605: Once it happened that the sexton rang the bells of the Church of Our Lady before they had been consecrated. During a stormy night the devil tore the bells from the tower and threw them into a deep pond, where they sank. That pond was called de Helleput (the Hell Pit). The sexton was found unconscious.
180631: A farmer had to drive his horse and cart up a hill to reach a farm. A man stood watching the scene. Because the horses could not get up the hill, the farmer began to curse.
180647: A man from Bevere was always ridden by the mare at night. He felt as if there was a sack lying on his heart and could hardly breathe. The man was advised to get up and keep his thumbs inside his fists or to hold a knife.
180667: A woman known as a witch filled the meadow with magpies by witchcraft.
180681: A man coming back from Voorde one evening saw will-o'-the-wisps above a marsh at the Zevenhoek. People claimed these will-o'-the-wisps were the souls of unbaptised children.
180701: A man from Nederbrakel heard knocking at nine in the evening. After midnight there was even more noise. In the end the priest was sent for to drive out the haunting.
180736: On a farm where all the goats were dying, the friars of Ghent were sent for on the advice of the parish priest. The priest claimed that he did not have enough power to drive out such evil. From the friars the woman bought two kilos of blessed salt and she also had a bucket of water blessed. For nine days she had to sprinkle all the places with that salt and that water. She also had to make a novena to Saint Hubert, Saint Roch and two other saints. After that no more animals died on that farm. The people had been the victims of a witch.
180753: In a family from Iddergem there was always a child ill. The people went to the friars of Ghent. When they changed trains in Denderleeuw, a crow flew up and followed them all the way to Ghent. That crow was a witch. The people told the friars of Ghent everything and were advised to make a novena. On the ninth day they were not to go to bed before midnight. That night, at twelve o'clock, the people heard a loud bang. A moment later the witch stood in the middle of the floor, although all the doors of the house were bolted. After the people had thrown blessed palm sprigs, their child was cured.
180762: On a farm in Nukerke people heard at night how the stove plate was thrown onto the floor and the bottles in the cellar were broken. Upstairs a wheelbarrow could be heard rolling. At night headless horses roamed about. When people went to look, there was nothing to be seen. A man who walked past that farm at midnight suddenly saw a cow poke her head through the hedge. "Oh beast, what are you still doing here at midnight?" said the man. When he went behind the hedge, the cow had vanished without a trace.
180782: The devil once came into a farmhouse in Nukerke. When a sheet had been thrown at the devil, people found that his hand was burned into it.
180786: On a farm a cow had given birth to a stillborn calf. When the cow had lain in the straw for eleven days without eating or drinking, the farmer's wife went to the friars of Dendermonde, who read prayers over her. While this was happening, the woman felt terribly cold. The friar said: "Go home now. You will see another animal." When she got home, the farmer's wife found that the cow was cured. A short time later another cow was due to calve. Exactly the same thing happened with that cow. When this misfortune had lasted for ten years, the farmer built a new stable. After the animals had been put in that stable, the misfortune was over.
180813: A man who was not afraid of witchcraft was at his wits' end when his horses had made noise for three or four nights in a row. On the following nights the horses' manes were plaited. The man temporarily housed his animals on his parents' farm, but there too the horses' manes were plaited, although no hands could be seen when it happened. So they sent for a friar. The clergyman discovered that the old woman who lived there had been to church, had accepted holy water from someone and on getting home had sprinkled the horses with that holy water. The people had to go on a pilgrimage to Affligem and take along a hair from every living creature in the house. When the people walked to the station, they were followed by a black cat. At midnight the people had to walk around the chapel of Affligem and throw the hairs over their heads. On their way home they would see a black cat, the friar had predicted, but they must not harm the animal. The friar had to visit those people three or four more times because they had let the evil go so far.
180838: A mother had a six-month-old child. On the occasion of the fair the mother, like the other women, went to sit on the Plaats with her child. A woman came to look at the child and said: "What a lively little child!" The next day the child began to cry. In the end it died.
180840: A man who went to the geleegputten (clay pits) in the evening saw a black cat there and said: "Oh, beautiful black cat, where are you going?" The cat followed the man and more and more cats appeared. They were witches, who sang: "Janneke asked me, beautiful black cat, where are you going?"
180852: On a farm on the Fietelmeers a cow had given birth to a deformed calf. The animal had the head of a dog and the legs of a pig. Moreover, its tail stood upside down. The vet said the farmer could get rich by selling the animal at the fair, but the farmer did not want to. Two weeks later the calf died. Some people came to ask whether they could stuff the carcass, but the farmer refused again. He was convinced he had become the victim of a witch he had met when he came home with the bull.
180861: Near the castle of Erelgem a sorcerer was approached by robbers who said: "Your money or your life." The sorcerer replied: "When I come back, you'll get both." The robbers stood stock-still, rooted to the ground, until the sorcerer returned.
180880: The mare could ride people or make them lose their way. A man from Hofstade had once experienced this too.
180926: A farmer coming back from his field one day saw a wheelbarrow moving through the orchard with no one pushing it. The farmer went inside and told his sister what he had seen. The sister saw the strange phenomenon too. A few days later the farmer's cart even drove around the yard by itself without anyone driving it.
180993: A man went to the friars of Affligem for his bewitched son, and they said: "The witch will come tomorrow at eight o'clock to fetch a clog nail, but you must give her nothing. You must not accept sweets from the witch either." The next day the witch did indeed come to fetch a clog nail, but they ignored her.
180996: If at dusk you saw four women standing at a crossroads, you could be sure they were witches. You then had to make a detour if you did not want misfortune in your stable.
181005: A werewolf had hidden his skin in the woodpile. One day the skin had been found and thrown into the burning oven. When the farmhand who had to play werewolf found out, he ran home crying and raging.
181023: Someone who had been ridden by the mare got lost.
181086: On a farm in Ottergem worked a farmhand who owned a skin in which he roamed about every night as kledde (a werewolf-like spook). When he was once spied on, people saw that he hid his skin in the hollow of an apple tree. One day the farmhand had to take a horse to the annual fair in Wetteren. While he was away, they heated the oven and threw the skin in. Not even five seconds later the farmhand was already at the oven, writhing in pain. When the skin had burnt, he was very glad to be freed of his burden.
181108: In Liedekerke a man was coming back in winter from the station, where he had taken the last train home. All the way he was followed at the same distance by a gentleman dressed in black. The man began to grow afraid. When he was almost home, he made the sign of the cross. Then he heard a crackling behind him and saw that the gentleman had vanished.
181194: A boy had gone through the snow to the fair in Sint-Blasius-Boekel. As the boy walked past the Franskouter, he heard a noise behind him and saw a large black beast standing there. The boy then began to run as fast as he could. The beast, however, kept chasing him. It later turned out to be a goat that had broken loose somewhere.
181195: Some young people coming home late on a Sunday evening saw someone walking with a lantern in the stable. When they went to the stable, however, there was no one to be seen.
181199: A mother whose child had died through bewitchment called on a woman who could undo bewitchment. That woman smoked like a chimney. You had to accompany that woman when she went on a pilgrimage against witchcraft.
181217: On a farm in Sint-Goriks-Oudenhove an animal had to be put down after a woman had visited. After that the woman was no longer let in. The people also sent for the friars, who put an Easter nail under their gate. When the suspected woman came to the gate again after that, she turned back.
181235: A man and a woman in Eilaart visited a woman who had pneumonia. While the couple sat with the sick woman, the light suddenly went out and the woman flew out of her bed. On their way home the man and woman were followed by a mewing black cat. The man wanted to throw his clog at the animal, but his wife stopped him because she was afraid.
181254: The Mierenhoek was haunted. Someone with goat's legs and a hat walked around there.
181277: A woman from Lokeren came begging in Zele every week. She always took the children out of the cradle, stroked them and gave them some sweets. After she left, it was found that the child's body was full of pins. The woman therefore got the reputation of being a sorceress. To protect themselves against her, people had to stick a wax candle into the water drain in their house. One day the sorceress was murdered in Sinaai because she had done so much harm.
181286: Nuts hung in a witch's house. While the witch was away, some boys had stolen her nuts. The next day the witch immediately knew who the thieves were. She said to the boys: "If you do that again, I will bewitch you."
181287: A man with special powers was out at dusk with a lot of money on him. When four or five robbers approached him, he said: "Stand there until someone comes to tell you that you may go on." The next day the robbers were still standing in that spot as if rooted to the ground. Then someone came by and told them they could go on.
181305: In Ename lived a hunchbacked woman who was suspected of being a witch. Because of the witchcraft, a child in the neighbourhood became deathly ill. The child's cradle stood by the window. At midnight a noise was heard across the street as if all the devils of hell had broken loose.
181334: A woman whose little children were very often ill went for advice to the friars of Ghent. One of the friars laid the sick child on the altar and said that it was already too late to save the child. The friar did tell the mother who was responsible for the evil, but the mother was not allowed to do anything to that person.
181358:
A woman whose daughter was seriously ill went to the friars of Ghent. One of the friars said: "I know why you have come, but your child died while you were on your way here."
The witch once came into a house to hammer a nail into her clog, although the strap was not loose. When the witch's daughter bought a farm in Maarte, her mother said: "How can you buy such a thing? The harvest will fail completely!" The witch already knew that in the month of March.
181367: A large cat came to a house in Melden every evening. The woman who lived there claimed the cat had something to do with witchcraft.
181392: You must not bite into an apple you had been given by a witch, or else you could become bewitched.
181448: A baron's nineteen-year-old daughter married and went to live in a large castle. When the girl went to that castle for the first time, she saw a ghost in the lane there. The apparitions continued while the girl lived there. Two years later the girl died.
181449: Twenty-nine years after a dead man had been buried, a knock was heard at the door. It turned out the dead man was standing outside.
181467: If you heard a magpie chattering, you could expect misfortune. Others claimed that magpies had something to do with witchcraft.
181494: A miller at work suddenly saw candles dancing. The candles went in through the front door and out through the back door. The miller came closer and saw that they were all nuns walking around with a candle in their hands.
181496: An old woman was suspected of being a witch. Whenever that woman walked past a house where bread was being baked, the bread always failed.
181547: When a man had died in the hospital, a black dog always prowled near the body. The dog jumped onto the body and then ran off. It was a devil.
181550: A man walking to Kruishoutem met a woman who asked: "Where are you going?" When the man answered: "My own way," the woman said: "You will go where I go. Follow me in my footsteps." At a stream the man quickly hid in a large pipe that ran under the road, assuming the woman would not see him. An hour later, however, the woman was still standing there. The man's brother had to go and fetch the dean of Kruishoutem, or else the man would never have been freed.
181551: If the hens cackled in the evening around five o'clock, it would rain.
181557: During his life a man had moved a boundary post to get more land. After his death the man came haunting, saying: "Where shall I put it? Where must I put it?" After a drunkard answered: "Put it where you took it from," the ghost was released.
181570: A woman who always wore a scapular believed that a rat sitting around a house, by a threshold or a wall was in reality the devil. She lived with her son in a small house. One evening the son had to go somewhere and did not come home until about three in the morning. The woman had gone to bed around nine but felt unwell. She had a terrible nightmare and woke with a start, drenched in sweat, when her son came home. The boy called: "Mother, I open the door and such a big rat jumps out!" The mother had dreamed there was a rat in her bed that wanted to bite her to death. She looked at her scapular and saw it had been gnawed all over. Only the face had remained intact.
181593: A woman appeared to her daughter because she wanted all her children to take communion. After people had done what the dead woman asked, the ghost did not appear again.
181605: A woman found it strange that the bread she baked failed every week. One day the woman was visited by a neighbour who offered to bake in her place for once. The woman allowed it and after that never had problems with her bread again.
181622: On a farm two piglets had been bought for forty francs. Because a witch had been near the piglets, the next day the animals had a hump and ran up the walls.
181624: In a house in Woubrechtegem lived a witch. One day that witch had made the animals and children on a farm fall ill. The farmer went to the friars, who said: "A rat will come into the house, but you must not harm the animal." A rat did indeed come. The friars chased the animal away. After that the misfortune there was over.
181650: In the early nineteenth century there was a wicked inn in Hofstade, where the devil is said to have come in several times. Once he is said to have put his claw on the mantelpiece, and the print could never be wiped away. The parish priest no longer wanted to pass that inn with the procession.
181688: Horses that were ridden by the mare in the stable had foam on their lips. People would then hang a stone cross with blessed relics in the stable, which drove the mare away.
181712: A man who had ended up in a meadow by way of a turnstile got lost and could no longer leave the meadow. He had been 'ridden by the Dolf'.
181745: A man coming back from the fair found on arriving home that his wife was already there, even though she had left later than he had.
181767: A woman was visited by a sorceress, who put her hands between the woman's knees. The next day the woman was nearly dead.
181792: In Pollare a black cat often roamed about, following people. Through such cats one could fall victim to the kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's curse).
181811: In Iddergem lived an old woman with a bad reputation who wore a cloth on her head, went to mass every day and then went to ask a man for a slice of bread. When that man had misfortune in his stable, he sprinkled the woman's bread with holy water. After that the woman never visited him again.
181816: In the old days people went every Sunday by boat from Kallo to Leuven. Because something was always wrong with the boat, people said a witch had been meddling with it again.
181841: On a farm there was a cow that was about to calve. Since it was still early, the men decided to play a game of cards first. At midnight they jumped up and ran to the stable. A woman suspected of being a sorceress was standing in the stable. No one had seen how she got in, for the little gate had been closed. The cow could not deliver her calf.
181869: A man had bought a tree that he wanted to use as a post. When the man went to take the tree away, a witch said: "You must leave that tree standing." But the man stood his ground and took the tree. The witch then tapped him on the shoulder and said: "I'll find you yet." After that the man was never healthy for another hour. Whenever he lay in bed, he always saw the witch in the shape of a black cat walking on the stairs.
181915: A woman always went to work on a farm in Etikhove. When the woman went home late in the evening past the churchyard, she saw a large black dog there that blew its nose the way a person would.
181991: If you saw a spider or heard a magpie chattering, misfortune would come. A black cat, on the other hand, brought good luck.
182042: A boy was afraid to go to the churchyard because he had been told that will-o'-the-wisps could be seen there. They were little souls that danced in the churchyard at night. Especially the souls of people who had made a pact with the devil wandered about there because they were being tormented.
182044: A small chapel had been hung on a farmhouse in Zingem because it was haunted. An uncle of the family had disappeared. Every evening a figure that looked like a werewolf came and sat at the window. In reality it was the ghost of the dead uncle coming back.
182048: A man walking in the woods was approached by two robbers who wanted his watch. The man handed over his watch, saying: "What are you going to do with it? You may have my watch, but take good care of it and bring it back home." But the men could not move another step. That evening they were still standing there. When the man came back to the robbers, they were glad to hand over the watch. The man said to them: "Never again ask to have old people's belongings."
182063: Three farmer's sons wanted to go out in the evening, but they were not allowed. The boys put a ladder against the window of their room and decided to sneak out at night. The first one who was to climb down, however, said: "I'm not going. Look what kind of sheep is standing there!" The two brothers saw nothing, but they did not dare climb down either.
182069: A woman who was cleaning outside emptied her bucket of dirty water into a ditch. A black cat sitting in the ditch got soaked. When the woman passed the house of a witch a little later, she saw the witch sitting dripping wet by her stove.
182082: A man taking his sow to be bred had to pass the house of a sorcerer. At that spot the sow could go no further.
182104: A woman went to drink coffee in Lebeke (a hamlet of Denderhoutem). That house was haunted. The picture frames fell off the walls as soon as the woman came in. The people went to the fathers of Affligem, who read prayers over them and advised them to give nothing more to a certain woman. When the people no longer let that woman in, the haunting came to an end.
182105: A woman from Sint-Niklaas came begging at a rich farmer's in Zele. When the farmer's wife refused to give the beggar anything, all sorts of ugly words were hurled at her. The beggar also said that the farmer's wife would not have a single pig left. Shortly afterwards a good hundred pigs died on that farm. When only one pig was left, the farmer went to fetch a father from Sint-Niklaas. The priest said: "You must tie that one pig up tightly and pour boiling manure over it. Then you must tear down the sty." The people did so and were freed from the misfortune.
182108: A man returning from Appelterre saw lots of black cats lying in the gutter. Only after the man had made the sign of the cross could he go on.
182136: A man from Leeuwergem was working in a beet field in France when an old woman passed by and asked: "Where do you come from?" The man answered: "I come from Sint-Goriks-Oudenhove," and the woman said: "Ah, we once had a lot of fun there by that linden tree, but now I am no longer part of that gang." That woman was a witch.
182140: On a farm where all the animals were wasting away, people set fire to a stack of six bundles of straw. Everyone then had to go to bed. The next day the neighbour woman lay in her bed all 'verkalkt' (burnt up). After that the farm had no more problems.
182160: A farm was badly haunted. Every night there was a noise as if a hundred thousand devilish spirits were at work. When the farmer's wife again heard a lot of noise in a nearby room one night, she took a little bowl of holy water there. The door of the room was open. The woman went in, sprinkled everything with holy water and said: "In the name of the Trinity, God the Father, God the Son and God the Holy Spirit". The next moment the door was slammed shut with a loud bang. The woman went to the Augustinian friars in Gent, after which one of the friars came by train to read prayers over the farm. After that the haunting was over.
182196: One day a man from Vlierzele saw an old woman with an umbrella passing by, who asked him whether he knew where the Dikke Linde stood. The woman went on: "Because I often amused myself there at night." That woman must have been present at the night-time meetings of the sorceresses there.
182224: If a sorceress could get hold of a hair, a nappy or a handkerchief of a child, she could bewitch that child.
182241: A man who had struck a cat one evening met a woman the next day who had a cloth wrapped around her head. When the man asked the woman what was wrong with her, she answered: "You should know that!"
182262: On a farm where a mare could not give birth to a foal, the vet could not help. The cows got loose there and the butter churned itself at night. Money was counted and there was dancing and leaping. When people went to look, there was no one to be seen. When the mare was due to foal, they sent for the priest, so that the foal was born without any trouble.
182268: A man from Dorselaar suddenly turned into a pig. When people wanted to destroy the man's skin, he suddenly arrived on the spot to save it. In the end the man was glad to be freed of the skin.
182270: In the churchyard of Gooik lights could be seen in the evening. It was said that these lights were the souls of the returning dead.
182297: In the past it often happened that people got lost in the dark and in foggy weather. It was then said that they had been ridden by the mare.
182317: A girl walking past a little chapel was startled when a black figure came and tapped on her toes. The girl made the sign of the cross and began to pray, after which the figure vanished. After that the girl never dared to pass that chapel alone again.
182320: A gentleman who was really the devil dropped a sack of grain onto the dung heap to give the other devils work. A little later the dung heap was full of devils who had to gather up all the grains.
182347: A woman had found a werewolf skin in the clover field. The next moment the owner of the skin came running to beg the woman not to burn it. If you burn such a skin, you burn the owner himself.
182359: A man who had gone to play cards after a visit to the barber came home around midnight. At a crossroads the man saw a black dog as big as a calf. The man was drenched in sweat from fear and went on. When the man reached the little chapel, the dog had vanished.
182365: A man was home alone because his wife had gone to early mass. Suddenly a woman came in to knock her 'kloefleder' (probably the leather of a clog) into shape. Uninvited, the woman went into the room where a baby lay. After the woman had left, the child did nothing but cry. The man went to the parish priest because he believed the child was bewitched. The priest came to the house. When the man said he was going to beat the witch to death, the priest said: "Don't do that, but it won't happen to you again anyway." The baby died.
182381: A witch lived in Moerzeke. Whenever that witch had touched an animal in the cowshed, it died or could never calve again.
182383: Two men followed a horse at night because they suspected the animal had broken out. Great was the men's horror when they saw that it was a horse without a head.
182406: In Huise a man had died who during his life had not paid his rent regularly. As punishment the man had to return after his death.
182434: A woman who had an ailment in her legs went to Affligem. On the way the woman met a witch, who followed her the whole time. The witch asked the woman to come and eat with her, but the woman refused. A little later the woman could not take another step.
182502: It was haunted at de Olifant. At night a white saddled horse stood on the threshing floor there. A little later a rider rode off on that horse.
182506: A woman suspected of being a sorceress was avoided by everyone, because people were afraid of being bewitched. Above all, people took care not to let sorceresses near their child's cradle.
182528: A man who was jumped on by a werewolf walked home with the beast on his back and shouted: "Wife, open up, I've got a wolf with me!" The werewolf begged to be let go, and in the end the man did so.
182530: Two brothers who had been sawing wood in the forest met a woman at two o'clock at night who was dressed all in white and did not say a word.
182551: Some people picking hops were gossiping the whole time. After a sorceress had passed by, tendrils were suddenly thrown about. The people went to a priest, who advised them not to talk about bad things next time.
182602: A man who had been out on a Sunday came home at night. When the man wanted to go in, he saw a woman walk past. The man turned around and saw a whole herd of white rats running towards him. The man put his foot on the first step of the stairs and no longer saw a single rat.
182629: In one house the baby always cried when a certain woman was visiting. The priest advised the people to put a relic under the visitor's chair. The people did as advised and found that the visitor could not get up from her chair until the relic had been removed.
182652:
A man who was going to Sint-Maria-Oudenhove got lost. The man saw a light burning in a friend's house and went there. The friend put the man back on the right road.
The man had been ridden by the mare.
182691: A girl who was in a relationship with a werewolf went spinning in the evening. On her way home the girl was jumped on by a werewolf. The next day the girl saw the threads from her spinning wheel hanging between her boyfriend's teeth.
182748: In Outer a sorceress roamed about in the evening. People were advised to bring their child's nappies inside before sunset. Otherwise the sorceress would bewitch the nappies.
182752: In Nederhasselt lived two witches who were always together. These witches could make themselves invisible from one moment to the next.
182775: On a farm in Volkegem the pigs braided cords from their straw because they had been bewitched by a sorceress from the neighbourhood.
182810: A man went with a little boy to fetch the midwife for his wife. On the way, however, the two got lost, so that they walked towards Michelbeke and had to go through the marshes, where the water came up to their knees. The two had been ridden by the mare.
182833: A man kicked at a cat that kept getting under his feet. The cat then leapt against the man's chest. The cat's paws had burned through the man's clothes.
182851: In Ename lived a sorceress who could make one of her farmhands eat spoiled bread.
182862: No one dared to take the road towards Berchem to go to mass in Kwaremont any more. A man had died there who, after his death, leaned over the stable door and watched people.
182904: If people met a black cat in the evening that rubbed against their feet, they must not kick the animal. They had to say: "... and the Word was made Flesh."
182932: In Baasrode lived a witch who always tried to get near babies' cradles. Afterwards the baby fell ill. In the end it came to the point that everyone ran away whenever that woman came near.
182953: A man returning from Oudenaarde met a witch on the way. When the man walked past the witch, she said: "You won't stop, but you'll have a lot of trouble getting home." The man did indeed barely manage to get home.
182962: In the pine wood a sorcerer was approached by a robber who asked him for money. The sorcerer took a five-franc note (1) from his pocket and gave it to the robber, who already had his hand out. When the sorcerer came to the same spot the next day, the robber was still standing there stock-still with his hand out.
182986: A farm where someone had recently died was haunted. A man went to the friars because he still had a promise to fulfil. After the man had done what he had to do, the friars predicted that he would meet the ghost on the way back. On the way home the man did indeed see the ghost come flying towards him.
182987: In one family several children had died shortly after birth. Every time the mother was about to give birth, a certain woman from the neighbourhood stood at the window. The next morning the baby was dead.
183012: Anyone who had come across a toad and stamped it flat would feel someone come and count his toes at night.
183030: A man who was out at night was often stopped on the way by witches. The witches did him no harm, but he had to wait until they said he could go on.
183052: One day a man who knew everything preached: "Dear parishioners, there is a thief in my orchard, but he won't get away from there before I arrive." And so it happened.
183055: An innkeeper who had to cross a bridge one evening was afraid that kludde (a shape-shifting goblin) would throw him into the water. So the man took another route. There he met two beautiful cats that kept getting under his feet, staring at him with big eyes. The cats, however, did him no harm.
183072: By the thick linden tree in Aaigem there were three tree stumps where music could be heard. There were sorceresses in those stumps. A man staying in France had heard a Frenchwoman say that she had flown to that place every night after rubbing herself with ointment.
183115: A farmer had a farmhand who was away every evening. Because the farmer found this suspicious, he decided to follow his farmhand one evening. So the farmer saw how his farmhand went to a meadow, took out a skin there and put it on. The farmer sent his farmhand far away and then threw his skin into the oven. A moment later the farmhand was already at the oven to save his skin. He had to be held back, or he would have jumped into the fire. When the skin had burnt up, the farmhand was freed of his affliction.
183116: A priest with special powers knew during Sunday mass that someone was in his cherry tree. The clergyman said: "He won't pick a single cherry and he will stay sitting there as long as I want." After mass the cherry thief could not climb down from the tree. When he got home, the priest asked the thief what he was doing there, and the thief answered: "I fancied a cherry." The priest continued: "Well, pick a few then," but the thief could not. Only when the priest had explicitly said that the thief could come down did the man get out of the tree.
183171: Of people who could no longer find their way home, it was said that they had been ridden by the 'mane' (mare).
183183: Someone came to Meerbeke peddling pins and laces. The peddler said he had been threatened and robbed by two men who had a dog that counted for twenty, because it was the devil.
183225: In Leeuwergem stood a little clay house in which lived a woman suspected of being a witch. Because the house was not very sturdy and also had a thatched roof that could easily go up in flames, the occupant was afraid someone would damage her house. So she shouted at every passer-by: "Stop, I'll murder you!" That woman always wore a long skirt and a little cap tied under her chin.
183240: On a farm people went to have a cup of coffee after putting a newborn calf in the pigsty. As they sat in the kitchen with their coffee, they suddenly heard a bang, the bolt flew off the door and the calf appeared in the kitchen. The people were very frightened. A sorceress had caused all of it.
183245: One morning a sexton had set out the bier because an anniversary mass was to be said that day for a deceased person. When the sexton left the church, he heard a sigh. The man was very frightened, for he believed the sound was made by the ghost of the dead person who had returned.
183264: The sexton had turned the saint's statue in a little chapel the other way round. When he got home, he had terrible cramps. Only when he had turned the statue back again was he relieved of his pain.
183281: In the Halve Dreef cats and rabbits gathered at midnight to dance.
183315: If you saw a magpie walking, you could expect bad news.
183332: A house in Winnik was haunted. All night long plates could be heard falling to the floor there. Strangely, in the morning there was nothing to be seen.
183334: A man from Denderhoutem could make people be ridden by the mare. He would roll his knife up in a handkerchief and say: "I'm going to send the mare there."
183341: A man lying in his bed heard someone coming up the stairs to his room. The figure opened the door, came to stand by the bed and grabbed the man by the throat. The man could not even call out. Later he learned from his father that he had probably been ridden by the mare.
183342: Some people hid in the evening and wrapped a bearskin around themselves to jump on passers-by in that guise. Werewolves then had themselves carried.
183383: A man who was ridden by the mare stood in the meadow and no longer knew which direction he had come from or where he had to go. That man had a stagnation of the blood. He stood there calling for help.
183400: A mother sat outside while her baby slept indoors. A neighbour came and sat beside the mother and began talking to her. At a certain moment the neighbour went inside to look at the child. A black cat went in with her. After that incident the baby was always being tossed up in its cradle. In the end it died.
183430: A man was taking a sack of grain to the mill. When his wheelbarrow tipped over on the way, he cried: "If the devil exists, he must come and help me." Then the devil appeared in the form of a snake, which put the sack back on the wheelbarrow. Afterwards the man fell ill and his hair turned grey.
183454: On a farm in Vlierzele a big wagon stood in the barn. One morning the wagon stood in the oven house, although it could not have got in through the doors or windows. The devil had done that.
183476: In the past people went to work with their thumbs clenched in their fists. That way they could never be ridden by the 'maar' (mare) or by the 'dag', which made people get lost.
183520: On a farm ghosts hung over the door.
183523: If children got an apple from a sorceress, they were not allowed to eat it. Otherwise they got 'de oude man' (the old man, a wasting illness).
183542: At the funeral of a man from Sint-Antelinks who had appropriated monastery property, the pall flew up and the candles were knocked over, so that the priest ran away. On the following Sundays the priest preached that the members of that family were damned to the fourth degree if they did not return the monastery property. The people fulfilled the priest's wish. A light had always been seen above that man's grave. After the monastery property was returned, the light disappeared.
183560: A mother had a child that still could not walk at sixteen months old. The child's cradle was always full of maggots. One night the mother woke with a start because a big rat had bitten her finger. A while later a woman with a large scarf over her head came tapping at the window. That woman came to visit every day, but they decided not to let her in any more. Then the woman said to the child's father: "I will do you harm until four years after my death, so that you won't even have a slice of bread left to eat." The woman made good on her threat.
183598: A man who had much misfortune found that his oven would not burn. When it finally worked after a while, the man saw that his bread was spoiled. He blamed the misfortune on a woman who lived near him.
183602: A man walking past the copse in the Hooimansstraat in Sinaai at night saw a group of small priests walking ahead of him as far as the path to the Boskapel.
183625: By a bridge over a brook in Leeuwergem lies a large stone said to bear the print of the devil's paw.
183627: At a little chapel in Nukerke music was heard in the air. A voice was also heard saying: "the day for you and the night for me". Then silver spoons and forks came flying down.
183654: A man coming back from the weaving mill one evening saw a foal floating over the ground. This frightened the man to death.
183719: A man from Kruishoutem walked to Oudenaarde one Sunday afternoon. When he came back in the evening, slightly tipsy, he was jumped on the hill in Ooike by a monster that came out of the ditch. The man said: "All right, my friend, I'll carry you a bit, but we take turns!" The werewolf and the man took turns. When, between Wannegem and Kruishoutem, it was the werewolf's turn again, the man ran away. Shortly afterwards a skin was found in a woodpile in Ooike. When people wanted to throw the skin into a burning oven, it flew around so fast that the fire went out. The people closed the oven and fetched the priest. The priest came and prayed for a while, put the skin in a sack and took it away.
183768: One evening a carpenter from Ooike was jumped by a 'loedie' (werewolf) that made him carry it to his house. But when the werewolf jumped on him, his chisel had fallen from his hands. Because the chisel had fallen on the earth, it was consecrated. The carpenter pulled the chisel out of the earth and drove it through the werewolf's skin, and the werewolf ran off howling and raving.
183780: A man was always ridden by the mare when he went to take a nap in the orchard after midday. The man could then no longer breathe and sweated terribly.
183783: In the old days people were afraid of black cats because they believed those animals brought bad luck.
183811: A woman from Everbeke heard that a musician's instrument had been stolen. On a Sunday evening the woman sent the musician to a man, who said: "Go home. You will pass a rye field. You will also see a dung heap there that has been dug up. Your instrument will be lying there." And so it was.
183840: A man who was ridden by the mare lay stiff as a board in his bed. People who were ridden by the mare probably had a stagnation of the blood.
183865: A man whose animals had all died and whose wife had died within a few days was desperate when his daughter got an illness in the head that made her deaf. The man sought advice from the fathers, who said: "Someone with a bad reputation always comes to visit you." The father said to that little woman: "You must not come here." After that the little woman began to pray.
183873: In the Molenveld a sheep always appeared at night and chased a man.
183915:
A family in Onkerzele had a daughter who was ill. Every day a neighbour woman came to that family to fetch milk. One day the people came to believe that the neighbour had bewitched their daughter. When the neighbour was inside, they locked the door and forced her to undo the harm she had done. Because the neighbour said she had nothing to do with it, they put her in the wood fire and burned her. 
Later it turned out that the daughter had been seduced by a man. 
The father who killed the neighbour was beheaded in the market square of Geraardsbergen and his wife was branded.
183933: A woman whose child was bewitched went to the fathers of Affligem, after which the situation improved. Six or seven years later the woman was visited by another sorceress. After that her child died.
183989: On a farm in Nukerke people were binding the corn by moonlight at midnight. Suddenly a woman said: "Let's go inside, for a gentleman is coming with a lady with a parasol." When they walked past the woman, the people heard the silk of her dress rustle.
184005:
Kledde (a tormenting spirit that leaps onto people's backs) was a man who dressed in an animal skin and in the evening leapt onto passers-by's backs to be carried. People believed such men were in contact with the devil.
One day people decided to play a trick on such a joker from Leeuwergem. They sent him off to Wallonia to fetch coal. Meanwhile they went to his house, looked for the animal skin and threw it into an oven. But as soon as the skin caught fire, the man was already standing by the oven to save it.
184065: A man who was ill had to be washed with water from the brook. The man, however, was not cured by it. Whenever people sat watching over the man, they always saw a little animal running around that nobody could catch.
184068: A freemason who had listened to the priest's sermon went to the clergyman after Mass and asked: "Do you believe everything you said there? You should come to one of our meetings." The priest asked the bishop for permission and went to a meeting of the lodge. When a man dressed in black appeared there, the priest made the sign of the cross. The next moment a flash of lightning was seen and the priest was standing outside the hall.
184077: A farmhand working on a farm had to roam about as a 'loetie' (a werewolf-like spook). The man had received a skin from the devil and had hidden it in an oven that was no longer used. When the farmer found out that his farmhand was playing werewolf, he sent him to a remote plot of land. Then the farmer wanted to burn the bearskin. The farmhand instinctively felt that something was wrong and hurried to the farm. Had he not been held back, he would have jumped into the oven to save his skin.
184098: The church of Amougies was troubled by witchcraft. When the women left the church, they found their cloaks torn. The parish priest said the witches had to stop, or else he would name them.
184122: Werewolves were people who dressed up in a skin and jumped on others in that guise. Werewolves were paid for their activities.
184126: There used to be many phantom animals on the Kruisveld. People who happened to come home that way saw hundreds of cats sitting in the trees there. The cats made a hellish noise, so that the people ran home sweating with fear.
184130: Will-o'-the-wisps were the spirits of the returning dead. Some people saw from their window a man passing by, followed by a will-o'-the-wisp. At a certain moment the will-o'-the-wisp jumped over to a neighbour standing close to the street.
184186: A bewitched fifteen-year-old girl was always cold when she sat by the stove. When she sat elsewhere, she sweated. The people went to the fathers of Affligem, who advised them to put an Easter nail under their stairs. After that a certain woman could no longer get over those stairs.
184205:
A man whose cows were all bewitched could no longer churn butter. The man went to the fathers of Affligem, who blamed the misfortune on a woman who always brought peelings to the farm. The man was no longer to accept the peelings and had to pour cow dung into the butter churn. After that the man could churn butter again. 
If that woman came to bring something, it must never be accepted for free.
184224: On a farm the roof tiles could always be heard rattling in the evening. When the farmer once went outside to look, he saw a hay wagon driving up, followed by a black dog. The man struck at the dog with a hammer but could not hit the animal. At that moment he heard laughter behind the farm. After the farmer had the priests read prayers over the farm, he heard no more rattling.
184252: One dark winter morning a man went to early Mass. On the way the man saw a werewolf sitting on the corner of a half-door. The werewolf jumped onto the man's neck and had itself carried. When the man arrived at the church, he was drenched in sweat.
184276: A man on his way to work at the factory in Sint-Gillis got lost and ended up in the meadow. The man had to start work at six o'clock. Because he had wandered around that meadow for two hours, he arrived late for work. The man had been ridden by the mare.
184318: A man who worked on a farm threshed from five in the morning until seven in the evening for five stuivers. That farm was haunted. Noise was always heard there and figures appeared at the window. When the man was walking home one evening, he was surrounded by 72 cats. That was the work of the devil.
184341: A man who sometimes had to play the werewolf said to his girlfriend: "Here is a handkerchief. You will meet an apparition and you must wave this handkerchief at it." The girlfriend did as she had been advised. When her boyfriend came back some time later, she noticed that he had the fibres of the handkerchief between his teeth.
184358: A man had a child of eight or ten weeks old that suffered from 'de oude man' (the old man, a wasting illness) because it was bewitched. When they took the child to the fathers in Ghent, the priests said: "A woman will come by with a parcel, which you must accept." A woman did indeed come with a parcel. The child died nonetheless.
184364: In a family where the father had died, the rosary was prayed in the evening. When the two sons were quarrelling over who would lead the prayer, a stone suddenly flew down the chimney. At that everyone cried out in fright: "Father is back already!"
184366: A woman in childbed died after a long death struggle. When the woman was dead, a visitor came by, who knelt and began to cry. At that moment all the clocks in the house stopped. The dead woman's husband was convinced that the visitor had come in this way to confess that she had done harm.
184375: In Volkegem lived a woman who was said to be a sorceress. A man from Volkegem worked in France together with the sorceress's son. At one point the sorceress was standing there in the field with them without anyone having seen her arrive.
184407: People said that nuns came to haunt a watermill in Leupegem. That is why the mill was called 'de Nonnemolen' (the Nuns' Mill). A farmhand from Kruishoutem sometimes went to a café in Leupegem. When the farmhand came home, he was always followed by the nuns from the bridge to the Appelke. So the farmhand no longer dared to take that road home.
184453: To avoid being ridden by the mare at night, one had to place one's clogs crossed under the bed.
184479: In the old days farmers let their horses graze in the clover field until ten or eleven at night. Werewolves often appeared in the field and frightened the horses. One day a farmer managed to get hold of the skin of such a werewolf. After the skin was burnt, the farmer was no longer troubled by the werewolf.
184481: A man who associated with the devil had received a skin, which he had hidden in a hollow tree. While the man was away, however, the skin was found and thrown into the oven. A gentleman appeared at the oven, Smitje the devil, who tried to save the skin.
184520: One night a farmhand had to go to the vet in Kruishoutem. Around midnight the man met a priest in the lane, carrying a large book under his arm. The man said "Good day", but the priest did not answer. Further on the man again met a similar figure. Frightened, the man hurried to the vet.
184521: A man had once seen someone lying outside his grave in the churchyard.
184539:
A man worked in France during the First World War. On Sunday afternoons the workmen went for walks. In a small inn where they went for a glass of beer, they spoke Dutch to each other. At one point an old woman came out of the kitchen and asked whether the men came from near Aalst. When one of the men answered: "Yes, we are from Lede," the woman went on: "Is that big linden tree still standing on the long field? I went to the meetings there many nights."
A lot of noise and music could indeed always be heard at that spot.
184572: A man and a woman had a child that had always been paralysed. The people went to the fathers and were given a medal to put under the threshold. After that the child soon died. It was discovered that the culprit was a neighbour woman, who had put the evil hand on the child.
184582: Of people who had got lost, it was said that they had been ridden by the mare.
184606: In a café where blasphemous things were said, one day a figure with horse's legs was seen standing at the bar. One of the customers quickly jumped on his bicycle to fetch the parish priest of Velzeke. The priest had to pray until he was drenched in sweat to drive the devil away. After that the figure with the horse's legs never returned.
184607: Near the Meulenstraat there used to be many pits where splashing could be heard, although there was nothing to be seen. No one ever found out what caused those sounds.
184609: A childless couple lived in Smetlede. The husband and wife had promised each other that whoever lived longest would have a funeral mass said for the other. When the husband died, however, the wife did not keep her promise. One dark evening a white figure appeared, calling: "Funeral mass, funeral mass!" Terrified, the woman promised to have a funeral mass said. After the woman had fulfilled her promise, she never heard her husband call again.
184637: A man who had already lost six children went to the parish priest when his seventh child also fell seriously ill. The priest advised the man to talk to no one. The child survived, and afterwards the man had two more healthy children.
184644: A midwife had to go to Wijnhuize at night because a woman was giving birth. Suddenly she saw a big dog on the road that did not move. The woman threw her rosary at the dog, after which the animal ran off. It was a devil.
184680: Some farmers bringing in the harvest, who drank a glass of beer or a dram in between, had paid no attention to a man who had passed by. When the farmers wanted to leave a little later with an empty cart, the horses strangely could not move. One of the bystanders realised they had not offered the passer-by a dram. They called the passer-by back and were told: "If you see me pass by again, let me drink with you. Then you'll get going all right!"
184700: A family had bought a house in Keiem near Diksmuide. During the first night the woman of the house woke up at about twelve o'clock because of a noise. The woman saw a large hand moving the twelve plates on the mantelpiece. The other occupants could not see the hand. Then the hand floated under the bed. Because the woman was too frightened to go on living in the house, her husband went the next day to the neighbours, where three strapping farmer's sons lived. The next night the farmer's sons kept watch in the house. The three men were playing cards when, at midnight, they suddenly heard a noise like a clap of thunder. The hand appeared again, moved the plates and then flew under the bed. "I'm never coming in here again," said one of the farmer's sons in fright. The next evening the curate was sent for. When the hand appeared, the curate said: "Tomorrow I'll come back and then we'll make that little fellow work for once. Just push the bed aside and break up all the tiles." Under the floor they found a little pot full of filth, at which the clergyman said: "Oh, that is a soul in distress because it still needs prayers. That soul has come to point something out. Take that little pot and have masses said for the unknown soul." Behind the plates on the mantelpiece they also found a gold chain and a cross full of diamonds. After all the valuable finds had been used to have masses said, the hand no longer appeared.
184701: In a poor family a baby lay dying. The people believed the child was bewitched. Three people went with the dying child to the Augustinian fathers in Ghent. A father read prayers over the child and said: "Hurry home." An hour after the people got home, the child died.
184708: At the Steenwerk in Belsele bells are said to have once sunk into a pit. Sometimes those bells could still be heard ringing.
184714: A woman whose house was full of lice sent for the vet. On his advice, everyone had to undress completely in the evening after dark. All the clothes had to be thrown into the washtub outside. The next morning the lice had all disappeared.
184749: When a witch had died in Ronse, a little doll full of pins was found in her house. When the witch wanted to torment a child, she stuck pins into the doll.
184775: A man out hunting in Ottergem suddenly saw a big hare come running up, which began to speak to him. The man wanted to shoot at the animal, but his gun did not work, so he was forced to go home.
184785: Between the Rooigemmolen and Sint-Larieslinde there always used to be a werewolf. People walking there on Sunday evenings were jumped on by the werewolf. In the end it got so bad that nobody dared go there in the evening any more. A werewolf was a big beast with an 'oorkap' (ear flap?).
184833: Working was forbidden during high mass. A man who nevertheless wanted to play cards during high mass saw a gentleman dressed in black come in, who said: "Would you like to deal the cards?" But the man had seen that the gentleman had horse's legs, and he refused. The gentleman then walked out angrily, saying: "You'll hear more about this!" He kicked the wall so hard that a brick fell out. Since then no one has ever managed to fill that hole in the wall.
184858: At a little chapel a man met a cat that jumped between his legs. The man kicked at the cat several times but could not hit the animal.
184878: A man coming home from work in the evening sometimes heard chains rattling near the presbytery. Sometimes he also saw a coffin. Such strange phenomena were caused by returned dead, who wanted to let a living person know that a promise had not been kept.
184898: On a farm two large wagons of tree trunks had to be transported. Two strong farm horses were harnessed to the cart, but they could not get it moving. A man with special powers said: "Let me try. I'll sort it out." With a light racehorse the man got the load moving.
184904: A woman visiting her daughter in Horebeke heard magpies chattering during a walk and said: "What bad news will we get now?" The next morning her brother came to paint the gate of the house. At a certain moment the man lay dead beside the gate.
184923: On a farm there were two magnificent Brabant farm horses. Strangely, it never proved possible to keep a foal of those horses alive. The piglets born on that farm also died before there was a chance to sell them. In the end the people sought advice from the fathers of Affligem, who came to pray and advised the people to close up a hole in the stable. After that the farm had no more trouble with the animals.
184943: A man who had been ridden by the mare got lost and stumbled all the way to Gent.
184944: A sorceress from Voorde said to some women: "I'll come with you, but you can go ahead, because I still have to wash." When the other women reached their destination, they saw the sorceress already walking there.
185004: A man returning from Hofstade saw a fire burning in the Oonegemmeers. He went over and saw many gentlemen sitting around the fire smoking pipes. They asked what he had come to do there, and he answered: "I've come to light a pipe and warm myself." The gentlemen replied: "Light the pipe and move on. The day is for you and the night is for us." Those were the devils and their helpers who gathered in that meadow.
185026: On a farm the pigs lay in the sty with broken legs after a witch had come to visit.
185047: In Petegem there was a billy goat sitting in a tree. People said it was some kind of ghost.
185053: In Grotenberge lived a woman who could work witchcraft. When the woman lay on her deathbed, people went to the chapel of Saint Ranonkel in Velzeke because the witch could not die. When they came back, the woman's slippers stood upside down next to the bed, although no one had touched them. Witches had to suffer a great deal before they could die.
185055: In Oudenaarde there used to be ugly witches who stopped horses and carts. The horses would stand there foaming at the mouth and the carter would curse. As soon as the stable hand spotted the witch and gave her a good thrashing, the witchcraft was over.
185100: Two brothers who went to fetch milk suddenly heard a knocking on the lid of the milk can. A moment later the lid flew to the ground. One of the brothers went to get the lid and heard a voice ask: "What are you doing here?" The brother answered: "Fetching milk," but he saw nothing. When the brothers came to that place again the next morning, they saw that the field there was completely under water. A fierce wind was also blowing that uprooted the trees.
185101: A farm in Mere was haunted. Every morning the horse's mane was braided, although no one had heard or seen anything. The occupants went on a pilgrimage to stop the haunting.
185104: One Sunday afternoon a woman from Deerlijk went to visit family in Nokere. When the woman learned that her nephew's daughter was bewitched, she said: "Tomorrow the guilty one will come to your farm." The next day the witch did indeed come by.
185127: A man from Zegelsem went to live near the wood in Doppe with his pregnant wife. A woman from Schorisse always came to see the pregnant woman on Sundays. One day that woman brought them a brooding hen. After that several animals died at their place. The man went to the friars of Doppe, but they could not come. Then he went to the friars of Gent. A friar came to the house and said to the cow: "You will not die." Then he said to the man: "You would have been next, but they could not have harmed your wife because she had looked after herself." The woman had already been to the friars of Doppe earlier.
185153: Some people going home in the evening were hindered by a cat that kept getting under their feet. X called to the cat: "You are a pretty pussycat", to which the cat replied: "X, you are a pretty pussycat". The man had to carry the cat.
185180:
A farmer who was ridden by the mare at night laid his knife on his belly in the evening for when the mare would come.
In reality the farmer had a stagnation of the blood.
185212: When people saw a magpie, they believed bad news was on its way.
185216: The lights that were sometimes seen were the spirits of the dead who came back.
185220: On a farmstead in Wannegem-Lede the animals stamped about and the horses were untied. The maid who worked there slept in the attic. Whenever she had been lying in bed for a few minutes, she always heard a racket. One day a basket of potatoes was even emptied out in the attic. The friars were called in; they investigated the matter and had the potato cellar bricked up. After that was done, no more strange things were heard on that farmstead.
185241: If people met a woman with bruises after they had kicked a black cat, they believed that woman had turned herself into a cat.
185262: A woman from Nokere had arranged with her neighbour to go to the market in Waregem together. When she arrived at her neighbour's, she urged her to hurry a little. Because of this the neighbour left without sprinkling herself with holy water. The two women had only just passed the castle when they met a black gentleman, who said to the neighbour: "Why did you not bring that person's soul on that day? You can see to it quickly, or I will send evil to your own children." After that incident the neighbour was not at peace for a single second.
185303: People said that nuns came to haunt a watermill in Leupegem. That is why the mill was called 'de Nonnemolen' (the Nun Mill).
185304: On a farm where all the pigs died, a woman regularly came to visit. The farmer was advised to go to Affligem. The farmer went to Gent and had one of the friars come to his farm. The clergyman came, read from a book and sprinkled everything with holy water. The next day the farmer was allowed to put his piglets in the sty. After that there was no more misfortune on that farm.
185332: A woman was always ridden by the mare at night if she had placed her clogs the wrong way under her bed. People who were ridden by the mare felt as if their throat was being squeezed shut and could not make a sound. One was in a state between waking and sleeping and felt as if a heavy weight was pressing on the body. If someone called one by name, one was freed from the mare. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to place one's clogs with the opening under the bed.
185416: In a house in Steendorp, people were sitting together one Christmas Eve, waiting to go to mass. At a certain moment the windows and doors flew open. In the garden a cherry tree stood in bloom, although it was the dead of winter. The next day the people sent for the friars of Beurm. After that no more strange things happened in that house.
185436: A woman got scabs all over her face because the day before she had given a witch something to drink.
185491: A house in Bevere was haunted. One day a woman from the neighbourhood came to visit those people. The woman had to sit in a circle with a bewitched child on her lap. The parents sat in the circle too. No one was allowed to leave the circle. The people prayed and sprinkled everything with holy water, while the statues of Mary and the saints danced on the mantelpiece. A woman always appeared at the window and grabbed at the child. In the end the child died. The people had been to the friars, who had given them Easter nails to put under their threshold.
