185497: In a house that a witch had visited, the children got convulsions or lice were found all over their beds. For all these ailments, seven children and a woman to accompany them had to go on a pilgrimage to the little chapel of Sint-Cornelis.
185521: In a family in Orroir all the children had a heart disease. The parents went to the friars, who said that the woman who had caused the harm would come one more time. After that the trouble would be over.
185538: In a house in Eine there was always a black cat that came in through the water drain. One day boiling water was poured over the cat. The next day people saw a woman who was covered in burns.
185543: The house of a widow was badly haunted. At night an invisible figure stood cutting meat on a chopping block. Every night a beguine walked through the house. The devils were involved.
185577: One evening a man had gone to a witches' feast and taken someone along. The guest was not allowed to mention salt. When he did so anyway, the whole company suddenly flew up into the air.
185599: A boy who worked as a farmhand on a farm in Vlekkem during the First World War told his employers that the black hand reigned in his home. The bread went bad. When the bread was left in other people's keeping, it did not go bad.
185601: People who suffered from a heart disease or had a pearl (a white spot) on their eye were bewitched. They then went to the friars of Gent, who gave them blessed bread. They also had to make a novena and eat that bread for nine days. After that they were cured.
185619: Some people returning from Eine were surrounded by mewing cats.
185628: When people heard the magpies chattering, they believed misfortune would come.
185650: A man who was ridden by the mare always cried out: "Father, she's been sitting on me again!"
185682: If you could find the skin of Ossaard (a werewolf-like spook), you had to throw it into an oven. In no time Ossaard would be at the oven to save his skin.
185700: On a farm worked a farmhand who one day had to manure the field. But the farmhand had fallen asleep under a tree. When it was already late and he still had done nothing, he said: "It doesn't matter. We'll each stand at a little heap of manure." The next moment the whole field was manured.
185704:
When a cow lay dead on a farm, people often believed the farm was bewitched.
On a farm in Velzeke three cows died within eight days. The animals lay dead in the cowshed in the morning and nothing strange could be seen on them. The people sent for a priest, who in turn informed the diocese. Then a friar came who walked around the farm praying all day and sprinkled everything with holy water using a palm branch.
185706: A farm in Lozer was haunted. The milking stools there were moved and always returned to their place in an inexplicable way.
185728: A woman with a bad reputation always came to visit a certain farm. On that farm the people could not keep a single cow alive.
185799: A man who was going to bury a dog met a witch on the way. When the man wanted to lay the dog in the pit, the animal suddenly jumped up and ran away. The dog was never seen again.
185822: A man walking through the Kattedreef one night saw a black cat on the road. The man kicked at the animal. The next moment some four or five hundred black cats appeared, so that the man could not go on. The man had to stay sitting where he was. Half an hour later the cats went away and the man could continue on his way.
185830: Two boys whose mother had recently died were staying with their aunt. Around midnight the boys woke up because they had heard a loud thump (?) on the shutter (?). The boys believed the sound was made by the ghost of their dead mother.
185874: A man often visited his half-sister, who lived in an institution in Sint-Pauwels. Whenever the man came home, he found that strange things had happened in his house. One day the man scattered flour in his house before he left. When he came home, he saw abnormally large cat paw prints in the flour. That was witchcraft.
185877: A pigeon fancier had shot a witch's black cat. When the witch found that her cat was dead, she said: "I will find the culprit!" Six months later the pigeon fancier was dead.
185968: Two old people had died in a house near the Jagerij. The children found it strange that they could not find any money, because they knew their parents had always saved a lot. From the very first evening after the funeral, a rattling was heard in the bread oven. When they started digging there, they found money.
185991: In a café lived a man who could work magic. When a man with a horse and cart came by, the café owner said: "Do you want to see those horses stand still? He won't get another step out of his horses." The café owner bewitched the horse and cart to the ground. Five minutes later the café owner said: "I'll go to the door now and then they'll move on." And so it happened.
186013: A man on his way to Ottergem was followed near the woods by a meowing grey cat. A little further on the man saw seven cats walking behind his cart. He was very relieved when he got home, for he was convinced those cats were witches.
186055: A man from Asper was jumped by a werewolf at the mill, and he had to carry it on his back until he was drenched in sweat.
186069: After M.'s father had died, C. and a friend had to pass the dead man's house. People said it was dangerous to pass the house of someone who had died, because it could be haunted there. When C. and his friend came past the house, they heard a voice call: "What are you doing here? Stay away!" C. was convinced he had heard the voice of a dead man.
186071: A family in Volkegem had a cat that was bewitched. People believed they could torment a witch by doing her violence when she appeared in the shape of an animal.
186090: A witch came into a woman's house and asked to see her child. After the witch had held the child, there was a big caterpillar in the cradle. "She will come and undo it," said the friar, and he was right.
186094: In Melden a woman had been with a little child. She had rubbed the child's head and said: "Oh, what a lovely child." After that the child was unrecognisable. People sought advice from the friars of Kortrijk, which brought some improvement. The child never fully recovered, however.
186144: A woman from Houtem had been given a plant by a visitor. Ever since that plant was in the house, the woman could no longer sleep at night. She always had the urge to go and smell the plant. One night the woman's husband thought he heard someone walking in the house. For five or six nights in a row the woman saw the alarm clock move a good two metres back and forth. In the end they threw the alarm clock away. The next night the same happened with the bedside table. It seemed as if an invisible person was moving the table. The man and the woman went to the friars. Two friars came and asked the people whether they had ever been given or won anything. The man thought of the plant and told the friars that a visitor had given it to them. The friars then said: "Pour petrol on that plant and burn it far from your house."
186149: A farm was badly haunted. People believed the haunting was caused by returning dead who were dissatisfied because they had been promised masses. Sometimes it was so bad that the cows in the stable were tied up by their tails.
186186: A man woke at night because his child was crying incessantly. The man went outside and saw a large white cat walking around the house.
186267: A woman who was ridden by the mare got lost. She was wearing only one sock and had lost her clogs when she reached her house in the Botermelkstraat. Later she found her clogs again in the Drie Dorekensstraat.
186291: In the past women wore aprons of linen. When a woman met kledde (a werewolf-like goblin that leaps onto people's backs), she threw her apron at the beast. Kledde had to unravel the cloth completely, so that the woman had the chance to run away.
186295: A man went making baskets with his brother. When the two men came back from Boeregem, they saw a lady approaching who wore a rustling silk dress. The lady took a snuffbox from her pocket and offered the men tobacco. One man wanted to strike the figure with his stick, but his friend held him back. At that moment the lady flew up into the lime trees and disappeared.
186318: On a farm the cows began to moan every morning at about seven o'clock without anyone being in sight. The people had the friars come to read prayers over the farm. After that nothing strange happened any more.
186319: A woman was ridden by the mare while she was awake.
186341: In the old days, when children were given an apple by an old woman in a little cap, their parents did not allow them to accept it. The parents would say: "Don't eat that apple, children, because it is bewitched!"
186386: A man coming home one evening saw a good hundred people mowing in the field.
186411: A man with a wooden leg swore all the time. One day, when he was standing in a meadow, he heard chains rattling and saw an animal's legs.
186427:
In Bevere lived a woman of whom people were very afraid. If a child fell ill after that woman had been nearby, people believed she had bewitched it. In the old days children often got 'de koek' at the heart (a heart disease). When that happened, people went on pilgrimage to Wannegem to offer cakes there.
Before her death that witch from Bevere gave her books to the priest. In the old days priests were able to undo witchcraft.
186438: In Pollare lived a witch who could make all the apples fall from someone's trees in a single night.
186471: A woman who slept in the attic saw a dead little old woman come back. The woman knew that the little old woman had made a promise concerning laundry. The woman told the spirit to go to the person who had inherited her belongings. After that the dead woman did not return again.
186493: One evening in Mullem a man met a white lady in a rustling silk dress. The man said "Good evening", but the lady did not answer. When the man looked back a little further on, the lady had vanished without a trace.
186496: On a farm in Erpe worked a farmhand who roamed about as kledde (a werewolf-like spook). One day people discovered the skin the farmhand had hidden in a place a good half hour from the farm. They heated the oven and threw the skin in. At that moment, however, the farmhand already appeared at the fire to save his skin. It took three men to hold him back. When the skin had burnt up, the farmhand was relieved because he was freed.
186511: Some people going to the annual fair in Geraardsbergen on Monday had to pass the house of a witch. The witch had been sitting spinning since early morning. When she saw the horse carts go by, she called: "Don't worry about me. I may well get there before you." When the people had only reached Onkerzele, they saw the witch already coming towards them. She had already been to the market.
186520: People who were ridden by the mare placed one clog with the heel towards the bed and the other with the toe towards the bed. They believed this protected them against the mare.
186544: A family had a sick child. Because the people suspected a woman who lived near the churchyard, a friar said: "I will put a cake on the churchyard wall. That woman will come and fetch the cake, but you must make sure she does not look in through your window." A short time later the cake had vanished from the churchyard wall. The priest had forced the witch to go and fetch it.
186577: If magpies were heard calling, something would happen, people believed. A man from Leupegem was working as a seasonal labourer in France while a typhus epidemic raged in his village. On the day the man's wife died, the man heard magpies chattering above his head the whole time. The next day the man received a letter saying that his wife had died.
186603: A man who was ridden by the mare tried to call out, but no sound came. People who had fallen victim to the mare were unable to do anything in the morning. To avoid being ridden by the mare, one had to place one clog with the heel towards the bed and the other with the toe towards the bed.
186621: One evening some farmhands found a horse skin in the farm's oven. When the farmhands pulled at the skin, a terrible horse suddenly stood before them. The animal ran off towards Aaigem and a little later disappeared into a thick linden tree. None of the farmhands dared go and look. The next day they told the farmer everything, who found the skin in his oven and set it on fire. At that moment a stranger came running, crying and begging for his skin to be given back. Had the man not been held, he would have jumped into the fire. When the skin had burnt up, the man said he was relieved because he was freed. He left and was never seen again. It must have been a werewolf.
186639: In Nederbrakel a werewolf always used to roam about in the evening. In a family with many children, where the father had to work hard to provide for his family, the mother wondered why her husband always stayed away so long in the evenings. One evening when the man was out again, the woman went outside. On seeing a werewolf she threw her apron at the animal and shouted: "Take this and unweave what has been woven." When the man came home some time later, the woman saw that he had the threads of the apron between his teeth. The woman shouted angrily: "What have you done? You are the werewolf!", whereupon the man wept and said: "Now I have to start all over again." Werewolves were only paid after seven years.
186640: In de Kete there was a cellar that was haunted. Noise could always be heard there. No one dared to enter that cellar. During the war a bomb fell into the cellar, after which the haunting came to an end.
186708: A man going through the meadows to Gent struck at a cat on the way. The next moment he heard wailing and a voice that said: "Little mother Marie is dead". The man was so shocked that he went into a café and told his story. In that café sat a cat, which said: "Is mother Marie dead?" and then ran off. That cat was never seen again.
186728: A man and a woman were just going to bed when there was a knock. It was a woman selling goat meat. The peddler said: "I hear you have a little son now! You already had so many girls and now you have a boy!" Then she went to the cradle to see the child. On Sunday night the child began to cry without stopping. The doctor thought the child was teething, but nobody could stop it crying. The mother went to the friars of Affligem. The child got a swelling on its chest and died.
186825: A man was often ridden by the mare at night. When that happened, he felt as if he was suffocating. When someone spoke to him, he was freed.
186860: A witch from Zarlardinge had made two of her brother's children ill and caused their deaths.
186899: Some men looking in through the windows of a house one evening saw that a witches' gathering was going on there. Suddenly one of the men said: "My godmother is there too!" The next moment the whole scene had vanished. Witches were not to be named, or else they disappeared at once.
186927: A woman came to a farmer whose animals were sick and no longer gave a drop of milk. The woman advised the people to have a clergyman read prayers over the animals. The people followed the advice, but the clergyman could not cure the animals. While the clergyman stood in the cowshed, there were many onlookers. The clergyman then said: "Everyone must leave, because the woman who bewitched the animals is here too." When the clergyman was left alone in the cowshed, he could pray much better. After that there were no more problems with the animals.
186935: One Sunday evening a young man was coming back through the woods from a visit to his girlfriend. On the way he suddenly saw a cat jump into the wheel of his bicycle and run off a moment later. A week later the cat appeared again at the same spot. When the cat appeared for the third time the following Sunday, the young man, irritated, grabbed the animal, took it home and threw it into the pigsty. The next morning the man saw no cat in the pigsty, but a skull. The man was so frightened by this that he died soon after.
186942: In one house there was a child who was bewitched. The people went to the brothers, who gave them an Easter nail to put under the door. The clergymen had said: "Tomorrow a woman will come by who will not be able to get into your house." The next day a woman did indeed come to ask how the child was, but she could not get in. The child died all the same. It had got a heart disease through witchcraft.
186945: In the Zevenbergen there was a dance every Sunday. At two in the afternoon many young people arrived there, leaving again around half past seven. One day it was said that the devil had danced there. He had horse's legs, on which iron could be heard rattling.
186966: Music was often heard in the evening in an oak stump in Kwaremont.
186972: In the old days people believed they would have bad luck if they saw a magpie in the morning.
187015: People possessed by evil had to roam about in the evening and at night in the shape of Osschaart (a werewolf-like spook). Such people wore a skin. When someone had found that skin and wanted to destroy it, the owner felt it immediately and quickly came to save his skin. Whoever wanted to destroy such a skin had to quickly read prayers over it and then throw it into the oven. Osschaart was capable of jumping into the oven himself to save his skin.
187019: A man visiting his girlfriend in Sint-Antelinks had to cross a haunted meadow. The man saw at least a hundred cats there and called: "Cats, all come here!" The ghost cats, however, did not appear. That place was called 'de kattenmeers' (the cat meadow).
187020: A woman went to the friars of Gent with her little daughter who was always crying. She believed the child was bewitched. The friars said everything would be all right again, and they were right.
187080: A man lying in his bed one evening heard someone coming up the stairs. Then the door opened and someone came in with a dog. The dog jumped onto the bed and went for the man's throat. The man had the greatest difficulty pushing the dog off. Finally he managed to jump up and go to the next room to fetch his mother. The mother saw that her son was drenched in sweat and believed he had had a bad dream. Because the man no longer dared to sleep alone the next evening, his father came to sleep with him. A short time later the man again heard noise on the stairs, after which he felt a weight of a good hundred kilos on his body. Only after the man had lain tossing and kicking for ten minutes did his father wake up. He had seen nothing strange. The next evening the man again wanted his father to sleep with him. This time the man got up as soon as he heard something. When he crawled back into bed a little later, a woman came and lay down on top of him. Only at the moment his father called his name was the son freed. One day the man went to the parish priest for advice. When the priest had heard the man's story, he said: "You've only just come back from the army. You probably have a stagnation of the blood from the change in rhythm of life and food." The priest also advised him to say a prayer before going to sleep. Because the man was desperate, the priest gave him an Easter nail to stick under his door. After that the man had no more trouble at night. He had probably been ridden by the mare. The man's brother, who slept in the room above his, had had it too. Since he had married, however, he had no longer been bothered by the mare.
187085: In Wortegem there once lived a witch who owned books with all kinds of spells. When people went to Waregem in the morning, they always met that woman. One day the woman brought a bottle of wine to a sick man. The man, however, said the wine tasted of paraffin. Every time he saw the witch coming, he shouted: "Shut the door, the witch is here again!"
187088: A sorceress lived in Nederename. One day in a house a cat was thrown down the chimney. The next day that sorceress's head was burnt.
187175:
In Sint-Antelinckx lived a woman who sold washing powder. If people did not buy much washing powder from her, she got a bit angry. Once she had said to a woman: "I'll get you all right!" Two days later that woman felt at night that she could no longer breathe. People who were ridden by the mare felt as if something jumped on them. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to place one's slippers with the heels towards the bed. After an Easter nail had been stuck under the threshold, the washing powder seller could no longer get in. She always wore a skirt that reached down to her ankles.
The woman who had been ridden by the mare fell off her bicycle, injured her knee and had to stay in bed for several years.
187215: On a farm chestnuts were found in the butter churn instead of butter. The farmer's wife was very ill and a woman from the neighbourhood had tried to visit her. Because she met someone who lived on the farm at that moment, the woman did not get in. The next morning she stood at the door of the pigsty. A little later the sow was found dead.
187217: A butcher who had gone to salt a pig one evening met a cat that kept circling around him. When the butcher struck the cat on the head with his axe, the animal turned into a woman. Terrified, the butcher ran away. When he looked back afterwards, he saw nothing anymore.
187231: A farmer from Moerzeke-Kastel had a lot of bad luck. Now an animal died, then the stable burned down or a child died. His wife advised him to go to the friars. A friar who came back with the man saw a toad sitting in the water drain in the evening. With a red-hot poker the friar drove the toad away and said to the farmer: "It will be over now." The next day a woman was seen with two burnt cheeks. People believed that woman was a witch.
187280: A man saw cats dancing at the corner of a field. They were witches who had taken the form of an animal. When a friar who had always preached against the witches had died, the cats sang: "We dance, dance, paw on paw, Father Felix is dead!"
187281: A mother saw a witch pass by, who patted her little son on the shoulder and said: "Oh madam, such a healthy child." The next day the boy began to cough, so the mother had to take him to the friars of Affligem. There the woman was advised to put an Easter nail by her door. As the friar had predicted, the witch came to visit the child on the second day. But she turned back when she reached the door.
187299:
A woman whose six-year-old child was ill sent for the doctor. But he could not help. One day an old woman had rubbed the child over the shoulders.
Because there was always noise in the attic, the father went to look once. He saw a neighbour's cat sitting there and struck at it. The cat defended itself and lashed out at the man's face. The man then fetched a broomstick, which he sprinkled with holy water. When he struck at the cat with the broomstick, he hit it at once. The man threw the dead cat into the cesspit. Because the people felt bad that they had killed the neighbour's cat, they went to visit her. But the man was astonished when he saw the neighbour's cat sitting under the stove. He went back home, emptied the cesspit and found that there was no cat in it any more. The neighbour had turned herself into a cat. After the incident she had lain in bed for four weeks.
In the end the parish priest was sent for to read prayers over the sick child.
187335: On a farm in Volkegem, people could not churn butter. Rats even crawled out of the butter churn. When the priest came to read prayers over the churn, he sweated terribly.
187362: When people heard a magpie chattering, they believed misfortune or a death was coming.
187406: A woman came to a farm to buy eggs. Just after the woman had left, the farmer's wife went to the cowshed to milk the cows. A moment later the woman was standing beside her again, saying: "I didn't know you had two cows. You really ought to sell me that little goat." But the farmer's wife did not want to sell the goat because it gave a lot of milk. Then the woman also asked for half a kilo of butter. The farmer's wife went inside to fetch the butter, although she had little butter left herself. The next Sunday the little goat gave no more milk and in the evening it lay dead in the shed. That woman never came to buy anything again.
187407: A man and a woman returning from Zegelsem one evening had to pass the Olifant near the Kattezak. People said that place was haunted. When the man and the woman got there, they saw cobblestones falling from the trees. A little further on the haunting came to an end.
187511: In one family many children died. The daughter claimed the children were bewitched. When another child lay dying, at midnight a noise was heard in the attic as if the devils had broken loose from hell. The grandmother went upstairs with a lantern and saw a cradle there with grain lying on it. Rats jumped from the cradle to the floor.
187533:
Stable hands were sometimes ridden by the mare when they slept with the horses. If one could still move when one felt the mare coming, one was immediately freed of it.
One night a man felt something at his feet. The man sat up, told his sister to fetch a lantern and searched under the bed and in the corner for a rat. Then the man's father said: "That was no rat, that was the mare. You chased the mare away when you sat up."
187535: A four-month-old child was seriously ill. Around midnight the mother sent her husband to his brother, so that he could fetch the doctor. When the man came home with his brother, a woman with a handkerchief was standing at the door. The child's uncle followed that woman as far as the Jezuïetenplein, where she vanished without a trace. Ever since that incident an Easter nail was always put under the front door in that house.
187538: On the Bosberg a man heard a foal walking behind him. The man got scared and started to run, but the foal kept following him. At his wits' end, the man climbed a ladder onto a haystack. After that he no longer saw the foal.
187539: In one family the youngest daughter had become seriously ill because of a witch. The parents went to a fortune teller. Then they also went to the friars, who gave them medals to put under the doors of their house. In the end, however, the daughter died all the same. Two children in that family had already died earlier at the age of eighteen.
187561: In Orroir lived a witch whose daughter had five little daughters of her own. Her son-in-law did not allow the witch to visit her grandchildren. When the daughter gave birth to her sixth child, a boy, the witch nevertheless managed to get to the child. The next day the child was dead.
187563: On the bleuwe Hoefweg in the Spaans Kwartier (1), a man saw a pack of dogs standing beside the road. When he came closer, the dogs formed a bridge by holding their front paws against each other. The man could not get past the dogs and went on his way. A little later he saw a coach drive past, followed by an animal. The coach stopped at a farm and then drove on. When the man passed the farm, however, he saw that everything was shut up and the lights were out. The next day he heard that the farmer who lived there had died in the night. The coach he had seen was driven by the devil, who had come to fetch the farmer's soul.
187587: There used to be a fountain in Erpe. When someone went to fetch water from the well there one evening, he heard a terrible howling and saw a white apparition walk to the presbytery. The next day scorched patches were seen from the fountain all the way to the presbytery. People believed it was a man who had come back because they had forgotten to say an anniversary mass for him.
187621: In Ename a witch's cow had been stolen. When the cow heard the witch walking through the meadow, it lowed. That way the witch found her cow at once.
187644: A woman was raising her sister's little son. Because the child never cried and was abnormally thin, they sought advice from the friars. When the woman went to Zingem by train one morning, she met a woman at the little bridge over the Schelde who was said to be a witch. After that the woman cried the whole way to Gent. She told the friars what had happened. The clergymen said she should not think too much about such things and sent her home. The child recovered.
187671: A man who went moving boundary posts at night kept calling: "Where shall I put it, where shall I put it?" One evening a drunkard answered: "Damn it, put them where you found them!"
187676: A man who was going to fell trees on a Wednesday had already cut into the trunk of a tree the evening before, so that he could bring it down the next day. The women coming back from the market with their baskets passed the place where the man was working. A woman from Michelbeke said to the man: "Well, going to knock another one down? That one won't fall, you know!" The man worked until after noon, but indeed he could not fell the tree. When he went back to the spot the next morning, the tree was lying on the ground.
187711: A farmhand working on a farm was often away in the evenings. One day the devil's skin in which the farmhand roamed about at night was found under the oven. They threw the skin into the oven and burnt it. While this happened, the farmhand came running. He screamed that his time was almost up, because he only had to roam about as a werewolf twice more. Now, however, he had to start all over again.
187712: One evening a man saw a nun dressed entirely in black. The man tried to catch up with the nun, but he could not. At a certain moment the nun moved slightly to the left and disappeared into the drainpipe. At the other end of the pipe a flame shot out.
187732: A farmhand with a bad reputation worked on a farm. A woman who went sewing there had already been leapt upon several times on the way by a werewolf that made her carry it. One day the woman threw a handkerchief at the beast. When she saw the farmhand sitting at the table the next day, she noticed that the threads of the handkerchief were hanging on his clothes.
187809: A man had to take maize to a woman from Volkegem who was suspected of being a witch. When he got home the man found that all the seams of his trousers had come apart, although he had not had to crawl under any barbed wire.
187831: A farm in Zele was haunted. Every morning the overhang (1) of the thatched roof lay on the ground, even when there had been no wind during the night. In the mornings butter often could not be churned on that farm either. Although the animals were always tied up in the evening, they were untied every morning. After the friars of Dendermonde had read prayers over the farm, the strange events came to an end.
187870: In Moregem ghosts walked about at night, calling all the time: "Where shall I put them? Where shall I put them?" They were dead people who had returned because they had moved the boundary post of their field. One evening a drunkard answered: "Put them where you took them from!"
187877: In Brakel lived an old woman who could work magic. She could make mice by rubbing elm leaves.
187912: On a farm in Everbeek worked a farmhand who was a werewolf. One day the farmhand had to fetch coal in Oudenaarde. Meanwhile his skin was found on the farm and thrown into the oven. Before the fire in the oven could be lit, however, the farmhand came running to save his skin. The farmhand begged to get his skin back, but the farmer grew angry. In the end the farmhand had to leave the farm.
187914: In a family of poor people there were frequent quarrels about money. One day the husband came home with a large sum of money. He had sold his soul to the devil and had to pay the money back a year later. A year later, however, the man could not pay. A gentleman came to his wife and asked for the husband. When the woman made the sign of the cross, the devil vanished. The print of a horseshoe could be seen in the floor, for the devil had horse's legs.
187916: A young lady was out with her boyfriend. At a certain moment the man fell behind a little. Just at that moment the young lady was leapt upon by a werewolf. She quickly threw her scarf at the werewolf, after which the beast had to unravel the cloth completely. When the young lady saw her boyfriend again a little later, she noticed that he had the threads of the scarf between his teeth.
187920: In Balegem the farmers could not churn butter whenever a certain woman had come to visit.
187938: A boy who had gone out on a Sunday evening had not come home. The next day some neighbours went looking for him. They found him in a ditch, with a coat wet with tears. The boy did not really know what had happened, but he did remember getting lost and ending up in the ditch. Then an apparition had appeared that had tormented him by pushing his head between his knees and then sticking a broomstick through the backs of his knees and behind his neck. The boy screamed, but no one could hear him. In the morning the stick was gone, but the boy felt as if his back and neck were broken.
187965: The horses of the baker of Voorde were restless and leapt about. The baker cursed, but could not calm the horses. A little later a wheel fell off the cart. The baker saw that his wife was standing watching the scene. After she went inside, the horse fell to the ground.
187970: A mother from Leupegem whose children were always ill was often visited by a woman from the neighbourhood. She was advised to go to the friars of Gent. There the woman was given a small loaf and three paasnagels (blessed Easter nails) to hang above the door and put in the cradle. A friar predicted that the visitor would come by the next morning to fetch shoe polish or laces. The mother, however, was not to let the visitor in. When the mother opened the door to the visitor the next day, she said angrily: "You will never cross this threshold again!" After the mother had taken her child out of the cradle, she saw a frog sitting there. The mother made a novena, the visitor never came by again and the children recovered.
188027: A man who could do magic freed a farm from a plague of rats. The rats could be seen running away neatly in a row. The last rat that ran away was crying.
188030: In a busy café there was often talk of witchcraft because of a farmer who could not churn butter.
188073: People who had been 'led by the alf' got lost. A man who was ridden by the mare at night was drenched in sweat and could not move. He tried to call out, but no sound came. It could take up to an hour before people were freed from the mare.
188104: A German shepherd could open a bolted door by throwing a stick against it.
188109: On the tram a man saw a woman who was said to be a witch. Just as the man wondered whether that woman could really bewitch people, she looked in his direction. After that incident the man no longer got on the tram when that woman was on it.
188127: A mother who ran a café had several times had her child prayed over at the abbey because it had been touched by the evil hand. It always happened the same way. The witch put her money on the counter and the landlady picked it up with her hand. She should not have done that, however; she should have picked up the money with a cloth.
188128: A man who was ridden by the mare one night lay calling out and felt as if something was sitting on him. When the man woke up in the morning, he saw the mare running away and threw his clog at it.
188157: In an apartment lived a woman with a bad reputation. When the neighbour went with her child to the medical check-up, the witch was there too. She asked to see the child and stroked its cheek. The next day the child could no longer cry or eat. After the mother had prayed and burned candles for nine days, the situation improved. After that the witch never again asked to see the child.
188178: In Viane lived a witch whom everyone avoided. Whenever a child was born somewhere, people were terrified that the witch would come to visit it.
188182: A farm in Sint-Gillis was haunted. It always looked as if the building were in flames.
188185: When a sinner had died in Vlierzele, the priest preached about hell and said: "I fear for the man who has just died." Because there was a dispute over the division of property (inheritance?), the relatives wanted to make the dead man come back. Since the priest could not do this, they went to an exorcist. When the dead man appeared, they asked him why he would not return for the priest. The ghost answered: "Because he passed judgement on me," and vanished.
188215: On the Eikenberg in Maarke there was a farm that was haunted. When the people there had been in bed for a quarter of an hour, the chairs and tables downstairs began to dance. When the people came downstairs, there was nothing to be seen. The people went to the friars of Ghent, who promised to send someone. The clergyman had to be picked up at the station and then they had to drive as fast as possible to the horse stable. The people did so. When the friar examined the house, he sweated heavily. After his intervention he got back into the carriage and drove to Oudenaarde. After that the people on that farm never had problems again.
188238: A woman from Everbeek had been to the market in Brakel. When she got home she gave a boy a mastel (a round bread roll). The boy ate the roll. In the afternoon the boy became seriously ill. After the parish priest had prayed over him, he recovered.
188255: A man was coming back at night from visiting his girlfriend in Nieuwkerken. On the way the man saw a beautiful white cat and took the animal with him. When he got home the man said: "Mother, I've brought a lovely little cat". The mother got up and saw a beautiful young lady sitting on a chair. Seeing this witchcraft, the man was terrified and went to the priest for advice. The clergyman said to the man: "Take the young lady and bring her back. When you touch her, she will turn into a cat again". When the man had done so, a voice said to him: "You are lucky that you did not mistreat me and that you brought me back here, or else I would have wrung your neck!" In a single night the man's hair had turned white from fear. That is why the man was afterwards called 'the white Midnight'.
188288: A boy became frightened after hearing stories about a skeleton without head or tail that wandered about at night. He never saw the skeleton himself, however.
188343: A man who was out at seven in the evening was suddenly surrounded by a glow as red as blood. People said it had been a falling star. It was 'the northern lights', which foretold a great disaster.
188377: A man who had a fine heifer was visited by a woman who wanted to see the animal. The woman had barely left when the heifer lay down in the grass and died.
188379: Some men who were reaping grain suddenly saw a beautiful lock of hair come flying out of the sky. It seemed like a thunderstorm. The men also heard a roaring in the air.
188383: In Roborst there was a lime tree that was always full of black cats at night. Sometimes there were also black or white rabbits. One night there were even men or women in white skirts standing behind the lime tree. Nobody dared go near that tree.
188394: The Catholic king's daughter Amalberga lay in the sea, about to drown. A sturgeon came swimming up, lifted Amalberga and brought her to Temst. Every year many people made a pilgrimage lasting three and a half hours. Once, when the weather was very bad, no pilgrimage was made. Afterwards the statue of Amalberga was found all smeared. She had gone on pilgrimage alone.
188400: A poor farmer whose barn had burnt down and who did not have the means to rebuild it received an offer from the gnomes. On condition that the farmer would give his last pledge to the gnomes, the little dwarfs would help him rebuild. The barn would be finished the next morning before the first cockcrow. When the farmer told his wife what agreement he had made, she realised that her husband had sold his soul. When the barn was almost finished, the wife ran outside and stormed to the henhouse, so that the cock began to crow early and the furious gnomes ran off with a great deal of noise.
188401: A woman from Aspelare bewitched many children by leaning over their cradles and giving them an apple or a sweet. The next day those children were ill.
188428: A boy who had to bring the cows to their stable one September evening went to call his father because one of the animals lay sick on the ground. That night someone had to keep watch over the sick cow. The blacksmith would stay with the animal until midnight, after which the boy's father would relieve him. Between eleven and twelve o'clock the father already heard the blacksmith calling: "Come quickly, I don't dare stay here any longer! I see strange shades here and the chests are all dancing up and down. It's haunted here!" The father thought the blacksmith's imagination had run away with him. But when he went to look, the father also saw ghosts of dead people floating about. Not far from that field were 'moorputten' (clay pits), which the brickmakers dug in summer to have water. A man had once drowned in one of those pits. Perhaps it was his ghost floating about there.
188562: On a farm where five of the six horses had already died, a witch said: "The last one will die too." A friar loosened a stone under the horse's hooves. Under that stone there turned out to be a toad. As soon as the toad was gone, the misfortune on the farm came to an end.
188564: In a house in Kerken a dog appeared every evening, and it was very restless. The priest had to come and drive the animal away. It was a witch who had changed herself into a dog.
188592: Werewolves crept into the hedge. They had signed a contract in their own blood in which they declared they would do everything they were ordered to do. After that they had been given a skin, which they had to hide in a hawthorn hedge during the day. Between sunset and sunrise the werewolves had to roam about with that skin. If something was thrown at a werewolf, the werewolf first had to bite that object to pieces completely before he could do anything to his victim. A seamstress once threw her scissors at a werewolf. To be released, the werewolves had to go to confession and make a public confession in church, while being tormented by the devil.
188664: On a farm where the people sat by the stove in the evening, around eight o'clock they heard a rooster crowing at the keyhole. The people went outside to look, but there was nothing to be seen; in the henhouse the rooster was sleeping peacefully on its perch. The people had barely come back inside when they heard the crowing again. This time too, however, there was nothing to be found. When the people went to bed, they heard no more crowing, but the horses charged violently back and forth. The next day the people went to the friars of Dendermonde, who gave them a paasnagel (blessed Easter nail) to put under the threshold of the horse stable. The friars said: "The person who brought the evil to the farm will also make it disappear, but you must leave that person alone." A few days later a woman they knew came to the farm. The occupants left the woman alone as they had been advised. After that no more strange things happened on the farm.
188674: A man coming home one night saw a beautiful black cat walking around him the whole time. The man rolled the animal up in his cloak and took it home. When he got home, however, he found that there were seven cats in his cloak.
188677: A woman went to visit her family. Because the family was not at home, the woman went into the neighbours' house and asked whether she could eat her sandwich there. In that house there was a little boy of three and a half. The woman gave the child a biscuit. After that, however, the child developed a heart disease.
188699: In a café in Ronse there was dancing twice a year for the fair, although the priest opposed it. One winter's day someone with horse's legs came to dance there. Those were devils.
188724: At Easter, after mass, a woman went with her husband to a café where there was dancing, although her parents did not like that. When the two came home in the evening, they heard music in the air and saw a beam of fire. In the sky they saw a row of horses and soldiers riding towards France. The woman was so shocked by what she had seen that she burned her hat when she got home.
188745: A man coming back from the fair, who had visited an inn on his way home, got lost and ended up in a brook. The man had been ridden by the mare. That meant that his heart was already asleep (?). Only after walking for two hours did the man reach his house, although it normally took him only three quarters of an hour.
188772: Seven cats roamed by the 'tree of the seven sacraments' in Leeuwergem. They were witches who had changed themselves into animals. The priest was called in, and he sprinkled the cats with holy water.
188808: A horse had to pass a house where a sorcerer lived. Under the road was a bricked conduit with water flowing through it. The horse could not get across and began to rear. Three times the horse tried to step over that spot, but it did not succeed.
188848: In the woods a man broke a branch off an ash tree and beat his donkey with it. The next moment the man heard a cracking as if the whole wood were being torn down. When the man saw a cat, he struck at the animal. The next moment a hundred cats appeared, crying: "Little mother is dead".
188856: A girl from Zandbergen always got biscuits from an old woman coming back from the market. In the end the girl died of the witchcraft.
188886: Four women from Herfelingen who came to pick hops in Denderwindeke were suspected of being witches. While those women were sitting in church, the sexton stuck a piece of a blessed candle under the threshold. After mass those four women could not leave the church.
188945: A sick woman from Huise could not be helped by the doctor. At midnight the woman's condition was always at its worst. One day someone said to the woman's husband: "Your wife is bewitched. Put her bed in the middle of the room and take your chopper at midnight. Then walk around the bed for ten minutes, hacking. If you can hit the spirit, things will improve." The next day the man met a fellow in the street with a bandage round his neck. That was of course the culprit. When he got home the man told his wife what had happened to him. The woman recovered.
188948: A farmhand who slept in the cowshed was often ridden by the mare at night. The mare would lie on top of him, so that he nearly suffocated.
188976: When one walked past the 'Goadijk' in the evening, one always heard music there, although there was no house nearby.
188995: A man who had promised to walk the procession of Kerselare had neglected his promise. After his death the man had to come back at night to look for someone willing to fulfil the promise in his place. The person to whom the dead man had appeared went to the parish priest for advice. The priest advised that man to go on pilgrimage for the dead man and to hold a white cloth in his hand. For at the end of the pilgrimage the dead man would appear to thank his benefactor. And so it happened. The dead man burnt his hand into the handkerchief.
188997: On 's Hondsknok a man met a woman who wore a silk dress. The man said "Good evening", but the woman did not answer. When the man looked back a little further on, the woman had vanished without a trace.
188998: To prevent witches from entering your house, you had to stick an Easter nail under the threshold. But it had to be a proper Easter nail. Several were stuck in the Easter candle, but only the priest knew which was the right one.
189017: On a farm opposite the church of Vlierzele worked a farmhand who had to roam about as kledde (a werewolf-like spook). One day someone found the farmhand's skin and threw it into a hot oven. A few moments later the farmhand stood by the fire to save his skin. As soon as the skin had burnt up, however, he was happy because he was freed.
189022: A man was playing cards with some friends. In the corner of the room a witch sat sleeping in her armchair. Because the man had been away from home for a long time, his mother came to call him. The mother claimed she had met the witch on the way. She had said "Good evening," but the witch had not answered. Yet the man had seen that same witch sitting in her armchair all evening.
189024: A woman often came to a farm to ask for milk. She would then peel the potatoes on the farm. One day the farmer's wife got a swollen head and went to the friars. The friars gave her a paasnagel (blessed Easter nail) to put under the gate. The woman responsible for the misfortune would then keep walking back and forth by the gate. That is how the farmer's wife found out that the woman who came to peel potatoes had bewitched her.
189042: At the time of the French Revolution a priest had to hide. When the French came upon the priest one day, the clergyman turned himself into a tree stump.
189085: A woman who was ridden by the mare could no longer find her bearings.
189124: People were ridden by the mare especially in stormy weather. A man who heard the mare coming sat up in his bed and in this way managed to drive it away. The mare was a spirit that was forced to wander about. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to turn one's clogs upside down.
189145: Anyone who was bothered by a werewolf had to throw a handkerchief at the beast. The werewolf then had to unravel the cloth.
189147: A maid going home one evening was attacked by a werewolf in a wood. The maid threw her blue apron at the beast and got home safely. When the maid came back to the farm where she worked the next day, she noticed that one of the farmhands had blue threads between his teeth.
189181: A man who lived on the Polderweg was ridden by the mare and wandered about all night. Towards morning the man found that he was near the Sluiersbos.
189207: In Eine a girl worked as a maid. When the man and woman she worked for had gone to town, the girl went to the door at about half past ten to see whether they were coming back yet. In the distance on the church square the girl saw a group of white women standing hand in hand, dancing. When the girl went back inside and opened the windows upstairs, the apparitions had disappeared.
189218: On a farm the animals lay moaning every night. When someone opened the door to see what was going on, everything went quiet. Those animals had been bewitched.
189243: A woman from Grotenberge had special powers. She did not shrink from putting a dried toad in someone's meadow. If the animals ate such a toad, they died.
189324: On a farm people heard that something was wrong in the stable. A man went to look and just saw something fly away through the ventilation hole of the stable.
189330: A mother had a child that had been bewitched by a witch who lived in Nederbrakel and who often walked past her house on her way to the village. When the child had died and was about to be laid in the coffin, people saw the child's back move. The doctor was sent for at once to revive the child. The next day the child was alive and well again. The mother was advised to put a broom by her door to keep the witch away. After that the child stayed healthy.
189363: A woman who was related to a witch called some children inside to read her a letter written in French. When the children were inside, they suddenly said: "Look, our cat is walking around here." To this the witch said: "Yes, but you have plenty of cats. I want a cat too." When they got home the children were scolded by their mother for having gone into the witch's house. A short time later the family's cat disappeared for one or two weeks. When the cat came back, it was completely filthy. It was shut up in an attic, but there it pulled the stones out of the wall to escape.
189385: A man had let his friends dare him to fetch a skull from behind the church. When the man picked up a skull, he heard a voice say: "Leave that, that is my grandfather's head." When he wanted to take another skull, the voice said: "Leave that, that is my mother's head." At his third attempt the man heard: "Leave that, that is my head!" At that the man ran away terrified. He never dared walk past that place again.
189388: In Melden lived a woman everyone was afraid of. When people saw that woman coming, they locked their door and ran off with their little child for fear it would be bewitched.
189392: On a farm the attic was full of rats. The farmer's wife could drive the rats away by saying a particular prayer. The woman had to say: "Rats and mice, you shall move away from here, straight through your hole to where you came from, back there." So the farmer's wife sent the rats to the watermill. Afterwards she had to go and drive the rats away there. Those rats had been sent by someone, because the animals were not afraid at all.
189438: A girl had fallen ill after visiting a woman suspected of being a witch. The girl kept vomiting and could no longer eat. After she had been to the friars, she recovered.
189439: On a farm a noise was always heard in the cellar at night, as if something was being moved. The occupants went to look, but they saw nothing. When they were back in bed ten minutes later, the noise started again. This game went on all night. It was haunted there because the occupants had made a promise that had still not been fulfilled.
189466: A man who lived in a house in the woods always heard noise and a plaintive voice in the attic at night. When one night the man saw large rats crawling down a copper wire, he took a dung fork and went outside with his dog. A moment later a violent storm suddenly arose. The dog had disappeared. The man went back inside and saw six cats approaching, which sat down in front of him three abreast. One of the cats was almost as big as a small dog and had a tail as long as an arm. When that big cat sat down right in front of him, the man quickly ran away. He told everything to the friars, who then came to look at the farm and said: "You may still experience strange things, but in nine days the haunting will stop." The frightened man nevertheless sold his farm. He was convinced that it was the spirits of the former inhabitants who came to haunt.
189489: A man walking home one evening saw a large black cat running around his feet. The man gave the animal a kick, so that it ran off yowling. The man never had a healthy hour again after that.
189523: On a farm three healthy sheep had been bought. Through witchcraft the animals were dead the next day.
189583: If you heard bells ringing, you knew you could expect good luck.
189609: Werewolves were people who went about in the evening wearing a sheepskin to frighten others. They also often made passers-by carry them.
189631:
One day the brass band of Elversele went by wagon to a festival in Lokeren. A man standing on the cart made a mocking remark towards a woman who stood watching. The woman then said to the man: "Don't laugh too soon. You're not in Lokeren yet. You'll be glad to be able to come back on foot!"
About eighty or a hundred metres further on the wheel axle broke, so that the men did indeed have to walk home.
189661: People who were ridden by the mare in their sleep felt as if something was sitting on them. They could be freed when their name was called.
189691: On a farm with one cow, a calf had been born. Two weeks later the heifer lay down on the ground and did not get up again. During that period a witch always came to visit with her daughter.
189711: A fruit picker who was out one evening saw a beautiful cat walking behind him. The man picked up the cat and put it under his cloak. After a while the cat began to scratch the man, so the man threw the animal on the ground and gave it a hard kick. The next moment the man was surrounded by some twenty-five cats. The man then ran home in fear.
189715: In a house in Nederename a ten-year-old child became seriously ill. A woman suspected of being a witch came to visit those people every day. When the child died, that woman was also standing at the door of the house.
189742: In Kruishoutem a werewolf went about, jumping on lonely passers-by in the evening and making them carry it all the way home. People had a suspicion who was playing the werewolf, but they could not find his skin. So they were never able to burn it.
189777: When the skin of Ossaard (a werewolf-like spook) had been thrown into the fire, Ossaard was working in the field. But he knew at once what was going on and was at the oven in no time to save his skin. Ossaard would even have jumped into the oven if he had not been held back.
189790: The Boskant in Elsegem was haunted. Once, when the people there were playing cards, they suddenly heard noise. Their cards all flew out of their hands.
189896: A teacher had burned her arm. The teacher did not want to be helped by a witch, but said: "If you put a paasnagel (blessed Easter nail) under the threshold, you can let her in." The witch came in and healed the teacher's arm. The next moment, however, the woman fainted. She was carried outside and was never able to return to her home.
189904: Some sisters were coming back from the fair one evening. The girls were all walking one behind the other. At a certain moment the first girl saw a cat lying on the road. She kicked at the animal. The cat stayed lying there. When the last girl had passed, the cat jumped up and again lay down in front of the first girl's feet. This game went on until the sisters were home. At night, cats were to be left alone.
189923: A sorceress wanted to teach her son witchcraft, but the boy refused. That is why the sorceress returned after her death.
189964: Two farmers took a stillborn calf weighing seventy-two kilos to the slaughterhouse. On their way home the men saw a woman walking to Wortegem. When the men drove past the woman, she asked if she could ride along. The farmer explained that he was only insured for transporting animals and refused to let the woman ride along. Before going home, the farmer stopped at a farm where there was a sick daughter. She was a young woman of nineteen or twenty with a swollen belly whom the doctor could not help. While the farmer was with those people, the woman he had seen on the way also came in to ask for a drink of water. The farmer said to the girl's mother: "Just kick her out!" But the mother did not listen and gave the woman some water. Two hours later her daughter was dead.
189980: A woman whose bed was full of ants and who had toads in her belly had prayers read over her, because the doctor could not help in such cases. The woman had fallen victim to a neighbour who regularly came to visit after her best friend had died. Since the neighbour's frequent visits, strange things had happened in the house. All kinds of noises were heard. One day a big black cat jumped onto the stove, then crept under the sofa and left the house without anyone seeing it go.
190006: A pregnant woman had gone to a farmer to scutch flax. A woman with a bad reputation also worked on the farm. During the meal that woman suddenly fainted onto the pregnant woman sitting next to her. Everyone ran outside in fear. When the woman gave birth in September, her child turned out to have a heart disease. It lived only eight months. On the day the baby died, another daughter of the woman had been to a funeral. On the way she had met the witch, who had said: "You are the daughter of X." The daughter had quickly run away. When she got home, the baby was dead. That evening a cat half a metre tall sat in front of the back door. The cat jumped at the door handle three times.
190011: In a house where a black cat always came haunting, the people had poured boiling oil on the animal. The next day they saw a woman from the neighbourhood who was covered in burns. When she was asked what had happened to her, she answered that she had fallen on the stove.
190027: On a farm people heard the doors and windows being broken out, although there was nothing to be seen. The next morning there were no traces of the haunting to be found.
190029: A woman suffering from a nervous illness, whose mother had been murdered, could no longer move on in the street and believed she was bewitched.
190085: In Erpe there once lived a witch whom people feared. In the week before the Erpe fair, the bread on a farm failed time after time. The witch was behind it. After a friar had prayed over the farm until he was drenched in sweat and had said: "Now bake as much as you like. You will have the finest bread in Erpe," they could bake bread without trouble again.
190087: A young man from Moregem went to learn a trade with a master in Schalafie and had to set out on foot every day. On the Kouborre-kouter there was a tree stump that always had cats sitting around it. Even when the boy took another road, he met cats there too, which attacked him and tumbled about in front of his feet. That tree stump in Kouborre was called 'de Katteneik' (the Cat Oak).
190088: In the past people put a paasnagel (blessed Easter nail) under the threshold to make sure no witches could come in.
190155: A man talking in a café in France heard the landlady say: "Are you from Heldergem? I often went to Aaigem. I sat in the thick linden tree there. I did get free of it. I always had to go from France to that thick linden."
190178: A witch always came to a farm. One time a farmer walked past the place where the witch was herding her cows. At that moment the farmer heard a sound like rats squealing. A one-year-old cow belonging to the farmer died after the witch had stroked the animal.
190197: A rich farmer had promised to give the poor as many sacks of grain as there were grains that would fit in the hole of a meuken (1). Because the farmer could not keep that promise, he always saw a big black dog lying by his bed. The farmer had to give all his possessions to the clergy to get rid of that dog.
190203: A farm in Huise was haunted. The bull there was untied every morning, the cows ran loose and butter could not be churned.
190284: One evening a man and his son went to look at a farm that was on fire. The neighbours were trying to put it out, but however hard they tried, the flames would not go out. Laughter could also be heard in the house. The people grew afraid and thought it had something to do with haunting. The curate came and began to pray. At that the laughter in the house suddenly stopped. Five minutes later the fire was out.
190293: At midnight you could hear the witches calling. If you heard that, you could expect misfortune. A woman who had heard the screaming found the next day that her child lay dead.
190345: In Aalst there lived two women whom everyone feared. One of them had a crooked nose and walked with a bent back. She was suspected of being a sorceress. People were especially afraid that she would bewitch small children. People said that this woman had a wax doll into which she stuck pins to torment a child.
190347: A woman went on a pilgrimage for the healing of her child. At night the woman walked around the church praying. Suddenly the woman saw the rural policeman approaching. The woman did not want him to see her and so quickly looked for an exit in the churchyard. A moment later the woman was standing in the street, although she did not know how she had got there.
190349: People who were possessed by the 'maan' (mare) got lost.
190351: A cowherd who worked on a farm in Vlekkem slept above the cowshed at night. One night the boy woke up because he heard noise above him. The next night the boy heard someone sawing and carving, and it seemed as if the roof tiles were rolling down and the roof was being torn off. The next morning, however, nothing strange was to be seen. When someone came to sleep with the boy, the sounds could be heard again. In the end the witchcraft did come to an end.
190374: On a farm in Waatsbrugge the cows lay with their legs in the air every morning. For nine consecutive days the parish priest came to pray away the evil. After that no more strange things happened.
190401: In Sint-Gillis-Dendermonde lived a woman suspected of being a witch. Whenever that woman came by a dung heap, something always happened to the animals on that farm.
190406: A strange man who was often out and about in the evenings was harassed at a small chapel by a cat that kept running between his legs. The man became so frightened that he died of fear. If you struck such a cat, you would in fact be striking the person who had turned into that animal.
190427:
A woman travelling to Wallonia with a child had not been able to prevent the child from being given a biscuit by someone on the way to the platform. Shortly afterwards the child began to cry. Because the doctor did not know what to do, they took the child to a friar. He said, however, that the child could no longer be saved, but that they should have the parish priest pray over it so that it could die easily. They followed the advice and the child died. Exactly the same happened with the second child those people had. That child too had been given a biscuit, had fallen ill and eventually died.
When the woman who had once gone to Wallonia with the child went to the market, someone jabbed her in the side. Because the woman could hardly walk the next day, she went to consult the friars, who said: "Every day a big dog with a chain will come up to your door. But you must not do anything to that dog. In nine days you will be healed." And so it happened.
190461: Superstitious people who had got lost believed they had been ridden by the mare.
190477: My father used to tell that a candle flew along with someone who was out on the road at night, and it flew with him all the way to his house, and when he shut the door he heard a great bang on the door, and they said those candles were all souls that came back.
190481: On a farm a fierce wind could always be heard blowing at night. When the people went outside to look, however, there was no wind. The piglets born on that farm were not healthy; one had a crooked leg, another had something wrong with its ear, and so on. The piglets all died before they were full-grown. In the end the sow had to be sold.
190530: Magpies foretold good weather and crows bad weather.
190551: A woman was afraid of spiders because she believed those creatures brought bad luck. When she was in hospital, she saw a black spider on the wall there. She called the nurse and asked her to squash the spider. The nurse, however, did not do it. The next day the woman was dead.
190575: On a bewitched farm a winnowing machine stood turning on the roof at night without anyone nearby.
190602: In a bewitched house a priest had said: "Tomorrow a woman will come here, but you must not harm her." The next day, while they were cleaning the stable, they saw a woman with a white kerchief on her head approaching, who was going to the chapel. They showed the woman the way. When she had walked a little further behind the chapel, they suddenly could not see her any more.
190605: After midnight one was not allowed to walk along the Molenbeek any more, because a black woman appeared there who only disappeared again at six in the morning. A man who had been there at one o'clock at night anyway saw a whole pack of dogs coming at him.
190659: A man who had to guard his horses by the wood saw a light burning in the wood at night and went over. He saw gentlemen sitting around a fire, apparently having great fun. When he asked if he could light his pipe at the fire, they said: "Light that pipe and move on, or we'll break your neck, for the day is for you and the night is for us." They were devils holding a gathering there.
190664: On a farm in Kerksken there was a fine heifer. A witch who came to visit said: "That's a fine beast, isn't it." The next day the heifer gave birth to a dead calf. The parish priest came and sprinkled the stable with holy water. After he had been alone in the stable for a quarter of an hour, his forehead was covered with drops of sweat. That is how hard he had had to work to drive out the witchcraft.
190731: Two girls going to their work at the jam factory heard a magpie chattering on the way. "I don't like hearing that," said one of the girls. When that girl came home at noon, she learned that a man had died.
190736: On a farm in Pollare the loaves always went bad on the third day after they were baked. The farm also had a cow that kept falling ill. The farmer's wife told the fathers of Affligem that she suspected a woman of being responsible for the misfortune, because that woman had been in the house while they were baking. Everyone on the farm had to go to confession and take communion. The next morning everyone left for Mass except the mother of the household. When everyone was gone, the mother was visited by a friendly old woman who came to ask for a cup of coffee. The mother gave her the coffee because she did not dare refuse. Afterwards she told the father what had happened. The father said that the guilty one had come back to undo the evil. After that day they could bake bread on the farm again and the cow no longer fell ill.
190746: During the Peasants' War the bells were taken from the church tower of Belsele and placed in a pit across the road. Those pits are still called de Klokputten (the Bell Pits).
190775: In Ronse a child was ill. The child, who had cramps all the time, could not be helped by the doctor. One day a man came to the child and said to the parents: "Go to the woods. There you will see an old woman sitting at a spinning wheel. At a certain moment the woman will stop spinning and make a movement." The people did as they had been advised and saw the woman sticking pins into a little cushion. That was why the child was in pain. The next day the parents went back to that place to give the old woman a thrashing.
190796: A wizard lived near Gijzegem. On a neighbouring farm people could not sleep at night for fear, because the whole house was full of rats that could not be killed. One day the people went to the wizard for advice. He came over and told the farmhand to fetch the barrel from the attic. The farmhand went upstairs but came back a little later without the barrel. He could not carry it because it was so heavy. Then the wizard said: "Never mind. You dig a pit and I will fetch the barrel." Although the wizard was at least eighty years old, he brought the barrel down with one hand. It was full of rats, their tails hanging out over the rim. The barrel was put into the pit. After that the farm had no more trouble with rats.
190801: A poacher saw a pack of hares dancing and leaping right in front of him. The man wanted to shoot at the animals, but his gun would not work. So the man went home to fetch an Easter nail. When he fired after that, the hares flew howling into the air.
190828: In the old days there were pranksters who wore an animal skin, ran about shouting and raving, and jumped on people's backs. The people fell into the grass, but otherwise the 'Loedies' (werewolves) did them no harm.
190856: In a family in Zonnegem three daughters died shortly after one another. The father always saw a witch sitting by the window. One day the man urinated in a bottle, which he then sealed tightly. Shortly afterwards the witch lay writhing in pain and begged the man to pour out the bottle. The man was not allowed to tell anyone the witch's name, or else she would break his neck.
190878: A man who had summoned the devils knelt and called on Our Lady and all the saints. No one would help him. Suddenly the man said: "And the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us." Then the man suddenly got so much strength that he could stand up. He saw something in front of him that looked like a donkey with a plumed tail. That was the devil.
190964: A boy who worked for a farmer in Ooike saw a candle on top of a barn one evening in a lane. When the boy reached the gate, he saw a candle dancing on the latch. A hundred metres further a priest came out of the alder bushes. Nine days later the apparitions had stopped and the animals on that farm died. The priests exorcised the place.
190966: A man had to carry werewolves from Gaver to Asper. Werewolves never jumped on anyone who had a cigar or cigarette in his mouth. A farmer's wife from Volkegem who was going to bake bread found by the oven the skin of the farmhand who had to roam about as a werewolf. When she had thrown the skin into the oven, the farmhand came running to save his skin.
191025: Sometimes people were ridden by the mare at night, so that they could no longer breathe and felt as if something was sitting on them. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to place one's slippers with the toes towards the bed.
191027: Around 1880 in Sint-Pieters-Leeuw a child fell ill after being touched by a neighbour woman. The child's mother went to the fathers of Affligem, where she was advised not to be too quick to link such incidents to witchcraft.
191030: A man who had been playing cards until late in the evening was walking home along a brook with a plank across it. A figure was sitting on the plank. When the man had kicked at the figure, he heard a voice say: "Stop, I gave my father only one kick too." Then the figure was gone. It was the ghost of a dead man who had come to receive his punishment for a kick he had once given his father.
191035: In a haunted café people always saw four women sitting drinking shots the whole time. As soon as someone grabbed the door handle to enter, the whole scene vanished. An hour later, however, the women could be seen again.
191061: A mother who was often visited by a neighbour woman had a baby that cried all the time. One day the mother found beans of extraordinary thickness and size in the child's nappies. The mother sent for the fathers of Flobecq. After that the neighbour woman never visited again.
191080: Nine days after giving birth, a mother saw a black horse's head coming in through the window. It looked like a devil. The woman quickly lowered the shutters. After that her dog would no longer eat. When the woman made her churching, someone with a bad reputation tugged at her skirt.
191117: A man with special powers sat by the roadside cutting grass for his rabbits. He saw some farmers loading flax onto a cart. The farmer's wife gave those people a dram, but she offered the sorcerer nothing. When the stable hand wanted to leave with the cart a little later, the horses could not move. Someone called to the farmer's wife: "Fill the glasses again and give that man over there something too!" When she had done so, the horses moved on effortlessly.
191121: In Ename lived a man who often went to play cards. One day the man had been playing cards with a woman who behaved strangely on the way home. The man was ridden by the mare and got hopelessly lost.
191147: In the past children were often urged not to accept anything from a certain woman because she was a witch.
191149: In Kwaremont a cat was sitting on a turnstile. A passer-by said to the animal: "Beautiful spotted cat, where do you come from?" The cat replied: "Jan stroked me, beautiful spotted cat, where are you going?" The man walked on, terrified.
191155: A little boy who had been touched by a witch grew very thin. After a father had read prayers over the boy and given him a medal, he could sleep at night again and no longer saw ghosts.
191224: In Volkegem lived a man who had much misfortune in his stable. Because he blamed his misfortune on a witch who lived in the village, he had the parish priest read prayers over his stable.
191234: On a haunted farm the people always heard banging in the attic, on the windows and on the cupboards. When the people had visitors, strangely enough the visitor did not hear the noise. The White Fathers were able to put an end to the witchcraft.
191286: A woman was ridden by the mare for fourteen nights in a row. The woman felt as if a very fat man was lying on top of her. After the woman had received a relic from the priest to put under her bed, she was no longer troubled by the mare.
191291: A farm in the Bosstraat in Oudegem suffered much misfortune. One day a skin was found there in a tree stump. When they burnt the skin with petroleum, kledde (a werewolf-like spook) was heard howling and moaning.
191315: You must never swear at a crossroads, because the devil might appear. A braggart coming back from Meerbeke station had sworn. At midnight a black man appeared who wanted to take the braggart with him. The braggart quickly ran away. After that he never went to a crossroads at midnight again, because he knew it was not a good place.
191328: Werewolves consorted with the devil, who gave them a skin to go about as werewolves. If a werewolf was wounded, its skin fell off. A farmhand hid his werewolf skin among the damp wood that was put in the oven after baking to dry. One day the farmhand forgot to take his skin out of the oven. When his skin was in the fire, he ran to the oven howling and raving. He was in great pain, but afterwards he was freed from his duty to go about as a werewolf.
191337: In Melden there was so much trouble with witchcraft that the parish priest said from the pulpit that it had to stop, or else he would name the guilty ones.
191356: A young girl from near Brakel was run over and killed on her way to work. The girl's family received compensation, and her boyfriend was also entitled to a quarter of the damages. The girl's brother, however, did not regard his sister's boyfriend as family and refused to give the young man his rightful share. The dead girl is then said to have haunted her brother to express her displeasure at this. The brother thought he saw a light by the brook. The priest advised him to go on pilgrimage and to put flowers on the girl's grave regularly. After the brother had visited a spiritualist a few times, his sister appeared no more. The boyfriend also received his rightful share of the damages.
191362: People who were ridden by the mare felt as if something jumped on them while they slept. To protect themselves against the mare, people sometimes placed their clogs upside down next to their bed.
191363: A man and a woman were coming back from Smetlede at around eleven in the evening. By a meadow between Smetlede and Papegem sat lots of cats making a great deal of noise. The man trembled and sweated with fear because he believed those cats were all ghosts.
191383: A woman who saw a candle fly past her farm believed that her uncle had suddenly died and had come back.
191409: In the evenings, foals always roamed the Winnekeveld. One evening people decided to go and catch a foal. When they grabbed one of the animals, it turned out to have no head.
191419: A farmhand who worked at a castle was very afraid of witches. At Candlemas the farmhand had to fetch blessed candles from the church. On his way home an old woman spoke to him who also wanted a blessed candle. The farmhand answered: "I cannot give a blessed candle to a witch like you." Once, when the same woman was visiting someone and the farmhand came in, he cried: "Sir, that is a witch!" The next moment the witch had vanished.
