191435: On a farm the farmer's wife went with her workers to the field to weed the flax. Suddenly one of the women stood up and said: "You dare to say that I bewitched your pigs!" The farmer's wife denied having said that, but when she came home she found four pigs lying dead in her stable.
191460: A man from Etikhove, riding back from the doctor in Oudenaarde because his wife was about to give birth, was stopped by ghosts at the Nonnemolen in Leupegem. The man promised the ghosts he would build a little chapel on that spot if they let him go home unharmed. So the man got home safely. Later a little chapel was indeed built on that spot.
191464: On a farm noise was heard every night at twelve o'clock. When people went to look, they saw the cupboards and chairs knocked over. The people sought advice from a friar. If a clergyman had read prayers over the farm before midnight, nothing happened. In reality, it may have been a farmhand who was responsible for the ghostly phenomena.
191548: A boy could no longer stand on his legs after a witch had given him a piece of sugar.
191574: A pregnant woman was visited by a witch who said: "I would like your unborn child to get Saint Cornelius's disease." The woman replied: "I will keep what I have." Two months later the woman had much misfortune. Her child got that disease fifteen times.
191619: If you heard a magpie chattering, you could expect misfortune.
191628: A maid working on a farm saw two gentlemen dressed in black come in with suitcases at half past ten in the morning. When the mistress came home, the maid told her what she had seen. The mistress went in to search everything but found no trace of the gentlemen. Yet they could not have got out by another door or window.
191703: A witch lived in Ophasselt. Some people were having the greatest trouble bringing a number of wooden beams from Idegem to Ophasselt. The witch walked up to them and carried the beams to Ophasselt on her shoulders.
191718: On a farm in Grotenberge a footprint of the devil can be seen in a piece of bluestone. After the clergy intervened, the devil is said to have walked from Hof Ten Berge to Hof Te Wassenhove.
191763: A man who was outside the village with a neighbour suddenly saw a werewolf jump onto the neighbour's back. The neighbour begged the werewolf to leave him alone, but it did no good. He had to carry the werewolf on his back for a good half hour. Then the werewolf jumped down. The neighbour was drenched in sweat.
191785: In the woods of Hofstade there once lived a witch who had a big black cat. One day the neighbours had stoned that cat to death. The next day there were hundreds of black cats in the woods. This lasted three days in a row. People believed a witch had sent those cats.
191819: On his way to market a man was jumped by a 'berewulf' (werewolf) that asked him something. As long as the man refused to answer, he had to carry the werewolf. The second time the werewolf jumped on him, he had a pin with him. He pricked the werewolf with the pin, and its skin fell to the ground.
191846: A man who worked at an oven on a farm went home to sleep every evening. There he was ridden by the mare every night. He could no longer breathe and felt as if a heavy beast had come to lie on him.
191907: A young man was very ill because he had already been ridden by the mare eight or ten times. The man first felt the mare at his legs. Then he was seized and it seemed as if someone was squeezing his throat shut. The man tried to call his mother, but no sound came from his throat.
191917: A mother had a child that fell ill after being touched by a newspaper seller at the station. The child's little face became that of an eighty-year-old and the doctor could not help. In the end the child died and the newspaper seller was blamed.
191937: A girl went to a farmer to gather potatoes and do other odd jobs. On her way home the girl and her friend were chased by a werewolf, so she ran away quickly. When the girl told the farmer what she had experienced, he replied: "You need not be afraid, girl. You must tie knots in the strings of your apron. If you meet the werewolf again, you must throw that apron at him and then he will have to undo all those knots. If I knew the werewolf was someone from my farm, I would throw him out at once." When the girl met the werewolf again, she did what the farmer had advised. The next day one of the farmhands still had the fibres of the apron between his teeth. Then the farmer said to the farmhand: "As soon as you have eaten, I want you to leave my farm." When the farmer came to his oven, he found the werewolf's skin there. He wanted to throw the skin into the oven, but the farmhand came running and said: "Farmer, do me this favour. I won't need the skin much longer. Don't throw it into the oven or I am lost." The farmer gave his farmhand the skin back.
191938:
People who were ridden by the mare saw at night in their dream a flash of lightning in which a person appeared. Then they felt that person's hands on their throat, making it hard to breathe. Anyone who had been ridden by the mare was therefore dead tired.
A woman who was ridden by the mare saw a bird with long legs. The woman tried to chase the bird, but it seemed as if she had heavy weights on her legs.
Sometimes the woman did not dare to go to sleep, because she heard creaking on the stairs and felt that someone was in the house. When the woman lay in her bed, she sometimes heard several knocks on the roller shutters. The woman then wanted to get up and turn on the light, but she could not move. The woman wanted to call out, but no sound came.
When the woman told the doctor what was wrong with her, she was advised to go to the fathers of Affligem. The woman did not go to Affligem, but consulted another man. That man said the woman had to find a flat willow or alder branch in the shape of a sickle and put it under her pillow. Such a branch had also been ridden by the mare. When the woman had put that branch under her pillow, she was no longer troubled by the mare.
191941: At the mill in Pollare a sheep was always seen at night. When it grew light, the sheep had disappeared.
191995: If you went along with a midwife, you could be ridden by the mare. A man who had been ridden by the mare in Zingem had to walk for a good hour and a half before he got home.
191997: Some men tried to get closer to a will-o'-the-wisp. But each time the light moved a little further away. When the men approached for the third time, the will-o'-the-wisp moved towards a marsh where a house stood. Suddenly the marsh was completely full of fire. Terrified, the men ran home. They resolved never to look at a will-o'-the-wisp again. The men went to bed and died of fright. Will-o'-the-wisps were spirits. It was believed that this will-o'-the-wisp had been the spirit of a man who still had money hidden somewhere and therefore roamed about.
191998: On a farm a four-year-old child had been given a sugar lump by a witch. After that the child cried all the time and stopped growing. When a father from Affligem read prayers over the child, sweat rolled down his face. The father advised the people not to let that old woman in any more. After that the child slowly recovered.
192001: The werewolf sometimes made people carry it. There were also people who, as a joke, went and emptied a potato clamp somewhere.
192019: On a bewitched farm the horses dropped dead and the barn doors were tied shut with chains. One day a cat was seen there poking its paw under the door. The farmer's daughter chopped off the cat's paw. The next day the daughter found that her mother had lost an arm.
192073: A man coming home drunk from the draft lottery for the army saw an altar with a clergyman at a crossroads. At that the man was instantly sober.
192081: A man returning from Ronse at night heard beautiful singing behind him. He looked round and saw a magnificent procession.
192135: In the toverbosje (enchanted wood) in Stekene a café could be seen in the evening, although there was nothing there during the day. In that café there was light and music, and people were dancing.
192187: A farm in Melden was haunted. The cows were untied there and the chains rattled. When one came into the stable, strangely enough there was nothing to be seen.
192192: In a house in Idegem people sat playing cards one evening until after midnight. Suddenly the candles in the house went out, which made the people very frightened.
192193: Three months after his sister's death, a man saw his bedroom window open one night. An elegant lady came in, dressed all in white and holding a lamp. The man tried to get out of bed, but could not. The white figure stayed standing by the window. When the man finally did get out of bed, the figure suddenly vanished. The next day the man told his mother he thought he had seen his dead sister. His mother said: "If she comes again, you must say: 'If you are sent by God, speak. If you are sent by the devil, go away.'" But the man never saw his sister appear again.
192197: A man who was ridden by the mare felt as if a heavy weight was lying on him. The man's throat was squeezed shut. The man tried to defend himself, but it did not help.
192219: In Sint-Blasius-Boekel lived a woman who was suspected of being a witch.
192253: The women who went to the lace school in Ename met men who had dressed up as werewolves and jumped on their backs. The women often had to carry the werewolves a long way, until they were drenched in sweat. Sometimes it was their own sweetheart sitting on their back.
192279: A woman visited a house in Berlare and looked at the little baby lying in the cradle there. After her visit, they found a good hundred pins in the cradle.
192286: A man who had sold his soul to the devil had to manure his field. The devils did all that work for him.
192303: Near Mater there was a farm where beautiful girls lived. When a twenty-nine-year-old girl died there, her hair was cut off to be kept. From then on the farm was haunted every night at twelve o'clock. There was thunder and everything flew about. The women who lived there all died of tuberculosis after they married. The priest went to the farm and urged the people to throw the hair into the fire.
192327: The castle of Burst was so badly haunted that the rural policeman and the police had closed the building. Bells were always heard in the castle, though nothing was to be seen. Even when shots were fired in the castle, the ringing did not stop. In the end the castle was exorcised with prayers. People believed the castle was so badly haunted because its former occupants had appropriated a great deal of money.
192349: On a farm they always heard a winnowing machine turning in the attic. When they went to look, strangely enough there was nothing to be seen. The cows stood in their stable with their legs crossed. The people suspected a witch of causing these strange things.
192377: In the rectory meadow stood a fine cherry tree. When the priest was in the pulpit, he fell silent for a while and then said 'Amen'. After mass the priest led all the people outside so they could see how he had bewitched someone so he was stuck in his cherry tree.
192379: A man who was forced to put on a skin every night was one day sent to the polder with a dung cart. When the man was far away, his skin was thrown into the oven. The next moment the man was already at the oven to save his skin. But the skin burnt up completely and the man was freed.
192519: A woman always went about with her little white dog in her arms. One day she threw the dog at a woman worker coming out of the factory. The worker began to cry and shout and hurried to the parish priest. Shortly afterwards the worker got a rash on her ear.
192529: A statue of Mary used to hang at the little chapel 'Te Beukenboom' in Voorde. One night the statue was stolen. The next morning the church where the statue had been put was full of beech trees. The trees were removed, but the next day they were there again. The statue was then taken to a consecrated lime tree and the place was renamed 'Onze-Lieve-Vrouw-te-Beukenboom'.
192558: In the Kruisstraat red and blue little caps always appeared. When the horses stood in the clover field, a witch in the shape of a cat always jumped onto the animals.
192560: In Mater lived a witch who behaved strangely. In church she often jostled and shoved people. She especially targeted people who were ill or pregnant. In a stable where the witch had been, three sows died.
192588: When it rained at night, the witches were out and about. A miller working at night during a rain shower saw a witch pass by, who said: "Come down from your mill, for it is held by only one nail." The miller had barely got back to the ground when the mill fell over. If the miller had stayed on his mill, nothing would have happened, for he himself was that one nail.
192590: To protect yourself against the mare, you had to place your slippers crossed next to the bed with the soles facing up.
192616: One evening a cattle dealer who could work magic was approached by robbers. The man said he had no money, gave his stick and his hat to the robbers and went on. When the sorcerer went home that evening, the robbers were still standing stock-still in the same spot. The sorcerer took back his stick and his hat, said: "If you meet Mr B. again, let him go, because he has no money on him anyway," and let the robbers go.
192617: In Sint-Maria-Horebeke lived people who heard their animals walking in the attic. It was said that these were the dead parents of those people, who had returned.
192664: On a farm in Etikhove they decided to go to the friars of Gent because all the animals were dying. A friar came, asked for a chisel and a hammer, and cut a hole in the wall. A toad jumped out of that hole. The people believed that toad had caused all the misfortune.
192688: If the parish priest had not closed his missal, the sorceresses had no more power, so that they could not even leave the church.
192708: If you heard a magpie chattering, you could expect bad news. If you heard two magpies, good news would come.
192750: One night a man had to fetch the doctor for his wife, who was in childbed. On the way he was attacked by a werewolf that made him carry it. Because of this, mother and child died. The man suspected who the werewolf was and wanted to shoot that person dead. He dipped his gun in holy water and shot at the werewolf. After that the man saw nothing but fire. In the end he went mad from it.
192780: When someone had done something foolish, people often said: "You must have been ridden by the mare!"
192810: A woman had been visited by someone suspected of being a witch. Afterwards the woman's sewing machine suddenly stopped working. The woman went to have the sewing machine prayed over by the fathers of Affligem.
192813: At the Nonnemolen, nuns dressed in white walked around at midnight.
192815: Two people on their way to Geraardsbergen saw a woman standing outside, who asked where they were going. After they answered, the woman said: "That's still a long way from here. You need to be good on your feet for that. I couldn't do it." When the two arrived in Geraardsbergen, that same woman was already there coming towards them.
192836: Three men said at the statue of Saint Roch in Appelterre: "You've stood like that long enough. We'll turn you with your back the other way." Once the men had done so, they could not move on until they had put the statue back in its original position.
192839: In Volkegem lived a woman with special powers. A girl went with her uncle to the field to dig up a basket of potatoes. The uncle said to the girl: "Make sure you don't stand still, for a witch is coming." The witch went to the girl, took a potato from the basket and said: "They're fine ones." The uncle meant to take that potato out of the basket when he got home, but he forgot. The potatoes were fed to the pigs. One of the pigs was to be slaughtered. When the farmer let the pig out, it began leaping wildly about. So the man put the pig back in the sty. Every time the pig came out, it went wild.
192870: In the old days people were very afraid of werewolves. People who were jumped by the werewolf and had to carry it some distance did not dare look back.
192880: A man went to visit his girlfriend, who had a bad reputation. When the man came outside, he was attacked by a cat without a tail, which stayed sitting on his windowsill all night.
192900: In the Warandestraat in Nazareth there was a farm that was haunted. There was a milking stool there that always returned to the same place when it had been moved. On the advice of the curate, the people smashed the stool. A while later, however, it stood fully repaired in the same place. Only when the curate had burned the stool did the haunting come to an end.
192924: A woman who had a small child always saw a strange cat sitting by the tub when she was washing her child. After a while the child fell ill and cried all the time. The mother went with her child to the friars of Gent and left her other children home alone. They were not allowed to open the door to anyone. Shortly after the mother had left, the children heard a cat meowing at the front door. The cat could even speak and asked for a little milk. The children answered that they were not allowed to open the door. After a while the fire in the stove began to die down, so the children went out the back door to fetch coal. When they came back in, they saw the cat drinking milk in the scullery. Later that day the parents came home with the child. But the child had cried the whole way and was not yet cured. Two days later the cat appeared at the washtub again. Then the child's father said: "Leave me alone here with that cat for a moment," and he gave the animal a sound beating. The next day people saw a neighbour pass by covered in bruises. The woman claimed she had fallen down the stairs, but the child's parents knew better.
192926: At the place where a man had hanged himself, a figure came every night begging for masses to be said, for penance to be done or for prayers for him.
192979: A hen always came out of a wood in Nieuwkerken at night. The hen flew around with a candle. A man had once got lost and died in that wood. The body was never found. The hen was the spirit of the dead man.
192993: On a farm in Sint-Denijs-Boekel the oven had to be lit to bake bread. By the oven they found the skin of a man who played werewolf. When they wanted to burn the skin, the werewolf said: "Look, my time is almost up. If you burn it, I have to start again."
192994: The white madam was a lady dressed in white who had come back from heaven. The white madam could make things haunted.
192996: A man from Voorde went to visit his girlfriend in Appelterre. On the way the man saw a dog that knew him well because he often passed by there. When the dog began to bark, the man called the animal's name: "X, is that you?", to which the dog answered "yes". Then the man was chased by the dog. The man kicked the dog. After that he regularly got a blow on the back of his neck. When he went into a farm, he saw that the gate there had been smashed, although the occupants had heard nothing.
193016: A man coming home at about half past ten at night suddenly saw a tree trunk rolling towards him. A little later a sow with piglets leapt out of the hedge. Because the animals chased him, the man quickly ran off. All of it was the work of a witch.
193019: In the old days boys sometimes went to another parish to meet girls. On their way home the boys took the shortest route to Voorde. In the moonlight they saw a frog sitting in the meadow. They took the frog with them to the inn of a sorcerer. After having a drink there, they went home. When he was lying in bed, one of the men found that he was full of lice.
193044: A man who was ridden by the mare at night cried so badly that the other people woke up in fright.
193071: A wizard returning from Aalst still had to start baking at four in the morning. At three minutes to four the wizard said: "Stand on my feet." The wizard was home at four o'clock. His feet had struck the church of Erembodegem.
193072: Two officers had once lived at 't Kasteeltje de Brewaen. As soon as the later occupant, K., went to sleep in the evening in his bluestone bed, he and his wife heard all sorts of noises. The coffee grinder made a racket, the chairs were moved and there was a jingling as if someone were counting five-franc coins. K. went to the priest of Eine (Ename?), who put the events down to K.'s imagination. But the man kept insisting that the priest spend a night in the castle. One night K. got up to see what was going on. But there was nothing to be seen in the room. When K. was standing outside talking with a neighbour, he suddenly saw in the moonlight four gentlemen at the top of a tree, sitting on chairs at a table playing cards. Half an hour later a great noise could be heard outside; all the trees were being chopped down. The next morning, however, it looked as though no one had touched the trees. Other strange things happened in the castle too. One of the girls, who also slept in a bluestone bed, got epilepsy. Three boys had convulsions and died. One day a plasterer working in the castle found a hollow in the chimney in which a fortune in leather money was hidden. A little further on he also found silver money and a small grey silk cloth. Because K. was sick of the haunting, he decided to move. After K., a handloom weaver came to live in the castle. When the weaver went to bed in the evening, he heard his loom start weaving by itself. Every time the man went to look, the loom stood still. The weaver went back upstairs and saw a tall grey gentleman appear from behind the door. Suddenly the gentleman boxed the weaver's ear, so that his cheek was completely burned. That same night the weaver left the castle.
193073: On a farm the cows stood head to head in the orchard at night. After the farmer and a farmhand managed to bring the animals inside, the cows went almost wild and stood with their legs leaning against the stable wall. Two fathers from Buggenhout came and went round the stable reading from a book. The fathers were drenched in sweat. One of the clergymen said: "Yes, you will have to be careful, for tomorrow the guilty woman will come to visit. But you must not offer her anything, or else you will have more misfortune." The next day the woman did indeed come to visit at about nine o'clock. The farmer's wife was not allowed to speak to her, so she left again at once.
193077: A man who was often visited by a wicked woman had a child that cried all the time. The child's father went across someone else's farm to the Poor Clares in Dendermonde. When he arrived, however, he was told: "We cannot help you, for you came across someone else's yard." That evening the animals lay sighing in the field. The next day the man went to Dendermonde again. He had to bring two bundles of wood and set them alight at twelve o'clock. But the wood would not burn. The man had also been advised not to let that wicked woman in any more. To that he had replied: "What would you say if I killed her?"
193080: When a man had drowned in Nederename and his body was laid out, a woman from the neighbourhood brought a bunch of flowers. "Give those flowers here; we'll say a prayer for them," said the dead man's sister. But the sister threw the flowers into the cesspit, because the visitor was suspected of being a witch.
193142: People who were ridden by the mare suddenly felt as if someone grabbed them by the throat. A man from Eksaarde who was often ridden by the mare could hardly breathe at such moments.
193144: The dead came back in the form of will-o'-the-wisps that bobbed up and down. One had to be afraid of will-o'-the-wisps.
193164: A woman who was ridden by the mare could not move because she felt as if twenty-five people were lying on her. Some people claimed that this feeling was caused by a stomach ailment.
193174: A woman walking past a little chapel suddenly saw a large black triangle appear there, which kept stepping on her toes. The woman could neither speak nor move. She made the sign of the cross and stammered: "If you are of Our Lord, then stay! If you are of the devil, then go away!" After that the black figure disappeared.
193196: A man saw a beautiful young lady sitting by the road. The man tried to touch her, but he always grasped at nothing. In the end the man ran away in fear. People believed the lady was the soul of a dead person who came back to be released. That no longer happens now because the dead are blessed in the grave.
193218: In a marsh there was a spring where people went to fetch water. Afterwards the people were escorted home by a dog almost as big as a foal.
193252: In Opbrakel there used to be an orchard that was haunted. People saw headless horses walking around there.
193261: The cellar of a house in the Kete in Wannegem was haunted. In that cellar there was a sharp iron spike on which, during the war, a soldier was said to have been left to die. People believed the ghost of that soldier came to haunt.
193289: A woman had become bewitched after accepting peppermints from a witch. The woman went to Affligem, where a father put a cloak over her and advised her to make a novena and wear medals. Nine days later the woman was freed from the witchcraft.
193309: In the past people stuck an Easter nail under their threshold to protect themselves against witchcraft. If an Easter nail had been stuck under a witch's chair, she could no longer get up.
193312: Some people coming back from Schendelbeke were jumped in the Kampstraat by a prankster playing the werewolf.
193380: On a farm there was so much misfortune during the Second World War that the family decided to move. Then another farmer came to live on the farm, and within three years three horses and several other animals died. Even one of the farmer's sons died. The farmer went to the fathers of Dendermonde, who advised him to set his farm on fire. But the farmer thought that a waste, especially in wartime. His two sons began to pull the farm down. One of them fell from the roof and died. After that they set the building on fire after all.
193404: A man coming back from Nukerke around midnight met a woman with a bad name by his neighbour's farm. That same night two of the man's pigs died.
193407: A man from Sint-Goriks-Oudenhove is said to have returned after his death, leaning on a three-pronged dung fork.
193430: A farm was badly haunted every evening. Around nine o'clock a lot of noise was heard there. The cows walked back and forth in the stable, although there was nothing to be seen. The occupants went to the friars of Ghent, who came to read prayers over the stable. After that the farm was no longer haunted and the people could live there undisturbed again.
193433: A farm was haunted. People saw a pig sitting in a tree, and it could not be caught. At night no one could sleep because the whole house shook and there were five or six rats on every rung of the ladder. The farmer's son had five francs in his pocket. When he had climbed up the ladder, he found that his money had vanished.
193438: A young man claimed that a woman wanted to ruin his business through witchcraft.
193452: A man who went to the market in Geraardsbergen bought something there from a woman. When the woman asked him where he came from, the man said: "From Geraardsbergen." The woman then asked: "Is that linden tree still standing there? I went there many nights and had a lot of fun there, but I am glad that it is over now."
193469: In the old days there were people who dressed up as werewolves and made a passer-by carry them some distance.
193488: A man and a woman went to the friars for advice. One of the clergymen said that their child was bewitched. A witch always came into their house. The people were advised to look inside the child's pillow; it would be full of pins. A while later the child died. The parents had no idea who the witch might be, until one evening they saw a toad entering the house through the water drain. The farmer cut off one of the toad's legs with a knife. The next day they saw their neighbour walking about. The woman had lost a hand.
193514: A man always had to carry kledde (a werewolf-like spook) when he came back on Sundays from visiting his sweetheart. One day he managed to overpower kledde with his knife and steal his skin. When he got home, the man wanted to throw the skin into the oven. The farmhand working on that farm claimed he had jumped over a hedge and that this was why he had so many scratches. But when his skin lay in the oven, he begged to get it back.
193529: A mill was haunted every night. When the miller was home alone, he heard noise in the stable. The man went to look and found that all his pigs lay dead.
193570: People sometimes told of those who had dealings with the devil and had to return after their death.
193572: A man had met a girl during the pilgrimage days in Kerselare. After the man had taken his girlfriend home, he spent the rest of the night in the pub. Drunk, the man had stumbled into the brewery's meadows. The next day he was very ill. A woman went to visit the man together with her mother. When the two women went back home in the evening under a full moon, they saw a big black dog with a plumed tail walking in front of them. It seemed as if the dog had no legs and floated above the ground. A little further on, to their great dismay, the women saw that the dog had turned into a small kitten. The women were so frightened that they walked home along the ditch. They no longer dared to look back. When they got home they were deathly pale with fear.
193605:
In a house music could always be heard, though nothing was to be seen. The man went to the fathers, who advised him to pray for nine days. After that the music was no longer heard.
One day that man's daughter had to go to Affligem because her child always cried. After the pilgrimage had been made, the child stopped crying.
That house was always visited by a woman from the neighbourhood.
193629: A mother left her child with a woman so she could carry on working herself. But the child could find no rest. Some people even believed the child was bewitched.
193634: One day the parish priest was invited to Hof ten Broeke with bad intentions. When the priest went home again, he was followed by two men. Because he felt that something was not right, he said to those men: "You will stand here until I am home. And not much will be left of Hof ten Broeke."
193679: Some men walking through the meadows clearly heard someone speaking to them, although no one was to be seen.
193689:
Witches were ugly old women with crooked noses who often visited mothers who had just had a baby. The witch would bend over the cradle and say: "What a lovely baby, eh!" Then she touched the baby's hands, head and neck, and so the child was bewitched. Such children got 'the old man'.
One day a witch came to visit someone who had a baby. The parish priest had advised the mother not to let the witch in, but the mother had not managed to keep her out. The priest, however, had hidden in a corner. When the witch went towards the baby, the clergyman jumped out and shouted: "You filthy witch!" He sprinkled the witch with holy water and made the sign of the cross. At that the witch flew out through the walls.
193717: A farmer from Sint-Goriks-Oudenhove sold his soul to the devil because he still had to bring in his harvest and it had started to rain. The next morning all of the farmer's grain lay in the barn. The crows had brought it in. That is why the farm was called 'Hof Ter Kraaien' (Crow Farm).
193719: A boy was out with his sister in Elsegem. Suddenly the girl said: "Oh look, a white dog is jumping in front of my feet!" Her brother, however, saw nothing. A little later the girl said: "Look, now it's jumping over the ditch!" Again the boy saw nothing. The girl claimed that it was the spirit of a dead woman from the village who came to haunt. Because that woman often haunted there, a small shrine was hung on a tree.
193723: A man had to cross a brook where a headless calf always lay. Sometimes people saw the calf quietly disappear.
193739: A man had stopped his horse and cart very close to a wall. A witch who came by squeezed between the cart and the wall, and the man said: "Say, can't you go along the street!" At that the woman began to curse loudly. When the man reached his field a little later, his cart overturned and was completely smashed.
193761: A man who was ridden by the mare could hardly breathe. When the man turned on the light, there was nothing to be seen. But as soon as the man lay down again, the mare was back. The man jumped up and did some work. When he went back to sleep afterwards, all remained quiet.
193809: A mother went with her child in her arms to a shop in Welden. A woman came in who touched the child or gave it a biscuit. When the mother got home, her child cried all the time. The mother went to the Norbertine canons of Ghent, who advised her to pray for a certain number of days. When those days were up, the woman came into the house drenched in sweat. It was witchcraft. A paasnagel (an Easter nail) was put under the door. After that there were no more problems in that house.
193811: After the framassons (freemasons, believed to have magic powers) had flown through the air, an old woman suspected of being a sorceress walked towards a neighbour. The neighbour struck at the sorceress, after which the sorceress looked back and flew away.
193845: When a man was buried in Essche, the bearers found that the coffin was exceptionally heavy, even though the dead man had been very thin. The man's mother said to the bearers: "It was I who was in it!" That woman had once cursed her son by saying he would waste away completely.
193850: In Sint-Maria-Latem a dead woman came back. She came in through the front door, even though it was locked.
193896: In Kemzeke lived a witch who always roamed about at night whenever a child or a cow had been born somewhere.
193901: Some people coming back from the field with a cart full of hay met a woman who had a bad name. "Boys, your cart will tip over," said the woman. But the men knew they had loaded the cart well and did not worry. Before they had reached the end of the street, the hay cart tipped over.
194034: When the farmers saw the horses kicking, they knew it was going to rain.
194035: In a field in Opbrakel a man always walked about at night, calling: "Where shall I put this post?" One night someone answered: "Put it where you took it from!" After the man had put the post back, he no longer appeared. It was the ghost of someone who had moved a boundary post during his life.
194036: In Petegem lived a woman who could cure people who had 'pearls' on their eyes. But some were afraid of her, because such an ailment could indeed be taken away, but it then had to be passed on to others.
194047: A man sat up at night with his wife, who was very ill. He was joined by two of his wife's brothers and a neighbour woman. As they sat talking, something suddenly leapt onto the front door and a terrible noise was heard outside. The neighbour woman said they should pay no attention to it, but the man pulled the door open and saw something black fleeing in the distance. "You didn't see anything, eh!" said the neighbour woman, and the man did not say what he had seen. A while later the man heard the same at the back door. This time he did not go to look, for he knew it was the neighbour woman who was causing all these strange things.
194051: B., a man who had studied to be a translator-interpreter, had to go to Italy in winter with two colleagues to give a lecture. The two men and the girl slept in one hotel room. As the three sat having a drink in their hotel, an Italian came in and struck up a conversation. The Italian said he was also going to that lecture and suggested they drive there together the next day. B., however, insisted on renting a car himself and suggested he would follow the Italian. The next day B. set off with his female colleague. K., his male colleague, got into the Italian's car, which drove in front. The Italian took the three to an old farmhouse where drinks were served. The women there all had a triangle carved into their cheek. In the triangle was a six. B. and the girl did not quite trust the situation and decided not to drink anything. K., however, had already drunk and was completely out of it. Everywhere in the farmhouse B. saw the number '6'. B. and the girl wanted to leave as soon as possible, but had great difficulty persuading their colleague. In the end the Italian drove back to the hotel with K., followed by the car with B. and the girl. On the way B. saw to his great horror that the Italian's car had the number plate '666'. When the Italian took a side road and stopped by a copse, B. began honking. He said to the girl: "You take the wheel. I'll get out and fetch K. out of that Italian's car. If I don't come back, go to the police at once." At first B. could not open the door of the Italian's car, but after much kicking and shouting he managed to drag his colleague out and bring him to the rental car. When the three reached their hotel, they found to their great astonishment that the Italian was already waiting for them there. He asked them: "Why are you afraid of me?" B. brushed the Italian off and asked for the room key. The three had been given room 6. K. vomited all night. The following days were filled with work obligations. On the last day the three had to go to the airport in the morning. That day the Italian was again waiting in their hotel at seven in the morning. The three handed in their room key. The Italian said to B.: "You are still one letter short, but it will come soon and then you will know what you have done to me." The three went back to Belgium. When B. got home and unlocked his suitcase, he was stunned. On top of his clothes lay the hotel room key he had handed in that morning. B. told his parents everything. A friend of the family who had also heard the story said: "666 is the sign of the devil. You already have two sixes: that of your room and that of your key." The following week was B.'s birthday, which fell on the sixth of the month. Before that day the people took the key to a meadow. They poured petrol on it and tried to burn it, but it would not burn. Then they took the key to the friars of Dendermonde. A friar listened to the whole story and then accepted the key from them. On 6 February, B.'s birthday, fortunately nothing strange happened.
194055: In a family in Zegelsem a daughter had died. At midnight the occupants of the house woke up and saw their child standing before them. Because this happened every night, the people hardly dared go to sleep anymore. After praying and sweating a great deal, the priest advised them to reach out their hand to their daughter at the next appearance. They did have to keep their sheet over their hand. After the people had done so, their daughter never appeared again.
194077: A pig used to wander around the churchyard of Wortegem.
194085: In a house in Opbrakel the mother had been in the bakehouse for an hour baking bread. When the children went to take a look, they found their mother standing there stock-still, as if all life had gone out of her. The children hurried to the parish priest, who said: "Leave her be. Life will come back into her." And so it did. The woman's spirit had been away to practise witchcraft.
194106: A man saw a big rat in his stable. He took a dung fork to stab the rat to death, but he missed. Later a friar said to him: "Good thing you didn't do it, for you would have stabbed a woman to death."
194108: In Buda (Meerbeke) lived a witch who had caused the death of the pig on a farm.
194140: Some people returning from Brakel by bicycle saw fire everywhere near the Oossenest at around three o'clock in the morning.
194153: A man had mocked the special powers that a fellow from Nokere claimed to have. That evening, however, the mocker could not get home, and the following night he suffered a plague of rats, so that he had to send for the sorcerer to drive the rats away.
194175: To torment a child, witches stuck pins into a little doll. The more pins they used, the more pain the child felt.
194197: One evening in a house three knocks were heard on the door. The man went to look but saw nothing. The donkey stood in the barn trembling on its legs.
194200: A poacher who was out at night under a full moon shot at a hare that came into his sights. The hare, however, stayed where it was, and three or four more hares even joined it. The man fired again, but missed again. When still more hares came, the man fired once more, but in vain. The hares came up to the man and sniffed at the barrel of his gun. The man went home and was sick with fear for several days.
194202: In Sint-Pauwels there was a bell pit. People often tried to dig out that pit, but the bell once hidden in it was never found.
194223: A witch was visiting a house and sat talking with her back to the door. Meanwhile the man who lived there took two Easter nails and stuck them under the threshold and under the chair the woman was sitting on. Nevertheless the woman got up without any trouble and left the house the way she had come in.
194258: A farm in Sint-Maria-Latem was haunted. The animals made a racket there and broke loose. The farmer claimed he heard a witch walking about in his house and wanted to shoot at her. Other people, however, did not hear the witch.
194305: A grandfather sat with a stick in his hand beside his grandchild's cradle and said: "She won't touch it, that ugly redhead!" Yet the woman did come in and gave an apple to the eldest little daughter. Luckily it had been seen, so the apple was thrown into the stove. The next day that woman was seen walking about with burnt eyes.
194326: People who were ridden by the mare in their bed were suddenly afraid and felt as if they were being attacked. People were ridden by the mare mostly when they slept on their back. To protect themselves against the mare, people placed their clogs upside down next to their bed. People who were ridden by the mare actually had a stoppage of the blood.
194342: A woman lying in bed in the evening felt unwell and could not get out of her bed because she was being ridden by the mare. To make sure she was no longer ridden by the mare, the woman had to place her shoes or clogs crossed under the bed.
194397: A father who disapproved of his only daughter always going dancing said one day: "I wish the devil would bring you home some time." The father's wish came true, for one day the girl was escorted by someone with horse's legs.
194404: A family had lost a child through the doing of a neighbour woman. The next child born there had a mental disability. The family went to the friars for advice.
194421: A man whose mother had died was helped by a friend in laying out the body. When the dead woman had been laid out, she suddenly moved and said: "I have been sent back for three more days to fight the world (?)." Three days later the woman was dead for good.
194423: In Sint-Pauwels there was a well in which a Holy Cross stood. The cross was taken to the church, but the next day it was lying in the well again. When people promised to have a mass said in the church every Friday in honour of the Holy Cross, the crucifix stayed in the church.
194425: Whenever someone walked past the brook, a light always flew along with that person, sighing like a human. The priest claimed it was someone who had not been baptised and advised the people to baptise the light with some water. After they had done so, the light was never seen again.
194429: On a farm the people always heard a sound at night as if a match were being struck across the stones. Sparks could also be seen. The people went to the friars of Affligem, who told them that the strange events would stop. And so it was.
194447: A field in Aabroek was haunted. At night a sheaf there always began to burn by itself.
194484: A boy always fainted whenever a certain woman came to visit. The boy would then foam at the mouth. Because people believed the child had been bewitched by that woman, they went to the friars for advice. After the friars had said prayers over the boy, that woman never again entered the family's house. That woman was possessed by the devil.
194485:
A witch lived in Oudenaarde. A man from Eine who had been to see this witch suspected her of causing his child's death.
A sick woman had once gone to this witch for advice. The witch had read in thick books and foretold that the woman would see something different every day and that she must do nothing about it. One day the woman heard cats meowing, another day she heard hammering and carpentering. Yet another day she saw a wheel turning on the chimney piece, and the next evening she heard a dog barking. The woman's husband could not see the dog, but he still tried to shoot at the animal with his gun. It was in vain. Some time later the woman went to the witch from Oudenaarde again. This time the witch said: "You did not do what I told you. You heard a dog barking and you shot at it."
194525: A house was bewitched from the moment a witch set foot over the threshold. The witch could make the cows throw off their chains.
194551: On a farm where all the animals were dying, the friars were called in to say prayers over the stable. The friars prayed until they were drenched in sweat and gave the farmer something to put in the animals' feed.
194557: At the rootputten (retting pits for flax) in Sint-Denijs-Boekel will-o'-the-wisps were often seen. They were wandering lights that floated about and at a certain moment went out. Superstitious people were convinced that such lights were the little souls of the returning dead. Better-educated people knew it was simply a natural phenomenon.
194593: The farm opposite the church of Zonnegem was badly haunted almost every night. A widow lived on the farm with three children. After the father's death, the eldest child slept with the mother in the finest bed. At night the bedroom door was flung open so violently that the bedstead was damaged. There was knocking on the doors and windows and the animals made a terrible noise. Two horses walked around the farmyard. Someone had once asked: "What do you want? A loaf of bread or something?", but there was no answer. In the evening the friars of Ghent came with a vigilant (?) to pray. While the clergymen were doing so, they were kicked on the shins, although nothing could be seen. After a while the haunting gradually stopped.
194616: On a farm where all the animals were dying, music was always heard in the house at night. The people sent for the friars. The clergymen found a little hair lying under the board of every dead cow.
194650: A man coming back from the fair in Ename was jumped by a werewolf that appeared from behind a stack. Werewolves had a skin.
194651: On a farm the animals fell ill after an old woman had brought bread and potatoes. The farmer went to the white friars of Gent. One of the friars came to the farm and fought the devil in the stables for a good two hours. After his intervention the friar said: "A pity about that little fellow, that must be the price." The friar gave the people an Easter nail to put under the threshold, so that no one with bad intentions could come in. The farmer's little son died two days later. The old woman never came in again.
194701: A man came to a crossroads on the dike in the dark. Suddenly he felt a tail in his face and something warm. He had met the devil. After that incident no one dared go to that crossroads any more.
194706: On a farm where strange things happened, the friars were sent for to exorcise the place. The clergymen threw a stick with a silver chain into a pen to banish the ghost there. After that no other animal could be put in that pen, for it never came out alive again.
194723: Near the church of Maria Latem lived a woman who had already had much bad luck. Because the woman always saw a toad sitting near her, she once beat the toad with a stick. At that same moment a sorceress from the neighbourhood had a fit. She was stirring her porridge and fell.
194733: The mare was a beast that pounced on people and disappeared again shortly afterwards. Victims of the mare could no longer breathe.
194747: A German shepherd who had sold his soul had to pour a viertel (an old measure of volume) of linseed into the well every day and order the devils to take every seed out again.
194784: A man who could do magic said to the mayor: "You are going to your girlfriend. I bet you won't get there." The mayor wandered around the meadow until late into the night.
194846: A child that had been bewitched by a witch cried all the time and eventually died.
194875: If you saw a magpie fly over your house, you could expect bad news.
194924: In a house in Oudenaarde there was always noise at night. It sounded as if everything was being smashed. When the light was lit, strangely enough everything stood in its usual place.
194925: On a farm lived a farmer who owned a bearskin, in which he disguised himself to jump on people's backs. While the farmer lay in bed, his wife burnt the skin in the oven. At that moment the farmer woke up and cried for help. He suffered terrible pain and finally died because he had broken his pact with the werewolves.
194939: In a house in Zingem there was always a toad. The children took a spade and cut off one of the toad's legs. The mother believed the toad had something to do with witchcraft and that the witch would be recognised the next day because she no longer had hands.
194940:
Some people went to play cards at a neighbour woman's house on a Saturday. After playing for a while, the neighbour fell asleep. When she woke up, she said that people had been talking about her at the mill. When the farmer who had been playing cards there went to the mill the next day, he learned that it was true.
The miller's son fell ill and died cursing. At night noises were heard there. The sails of the mill turned the wrong way and a black dog was always roaming about, blocking people's way into the mill. The miller went to the friars and promised to build a little chapel on the mill to be delivered from the evil. When another child fell ill, the priest gave the miller a medal and foretold that a woman would come to visit. No one was to speak to that woman. A woman did indeed come by. The miller and his wife had to restrain themselves from harming the woman. After that the child recovered.
194965: A man lived in a small cottage that was haunted. Every evening someone knocked on the door of the cottage. The wife, however, did not dare open it because her husband worked as a seasonal labourer in France and so she was home alone. The neighbour came to keep her company, but she did not dare open the door either. Exactly the same happened at the farm opposite that house, but nothing was ever seen. Three tough farmhands worked on that farm. All three farmhands died within a short time.
194987: A woman with many small children was visited by a neighbour who had baked waffles and said they were welcome to come and fetch some from her. The woman sent her eldest son to the neighbour's house. A little later the boy came back with the waffles. His father ate them eagerly, but fell ill that evening. He developed a high fever. The doctor could not help the man, so they went to the friars. The clergyman took a glass of water and asked how many members the family had. Then he put as many grains of corn into the glass as there were family members and said: "If one grain stays on top, that is the one who is sick." All the grains sank to the bottom except one. The friar then said: "You must go to mass every morning for nine days. The person who did this to you will meet you and greet you, but if you answer, your husband is lost." Every day the woman went to mass, she met the neighbour, who said to her: "Is this my thanks for what I brought you yesterday, that you walk past me without a word?" The neighbour had once brought eggs for the sick man. When one of the eggs was beaten, its contents turned out to be completely black. On the eighth day the woman could no longer control herself and answered the neighbour. On returning home she said to her husband: "Now we are lost, because I spoke." The man did indeed die.
194994: On a farm plagued by rats, someone who could drive away rats was sent for. The wizard walked around the house and left a little path open along which the rats could run away. The next day not a single rat was to be seen. The wizard had a particular prayer for this.
194998: A man passing through a forest was attacked and had to hand over his money. The man took out a five-franc piece and dropped it out of the robber's reach. When the robber bent down to pick up the money, the man bewitched him to the spot. The man went home and said to his farmhand: "There is a five-franc piece lying on the road. Pick it up in front of the robber who is standing bent over it."
195020: On a farm where several animals had already died, a friar came to say prayers over the stable. The clergyman sweated terribly while doing so and said: "One more little creature that you love very much will die." The next day the canary died. After that the misfortune came to an end.
195032: A man whose grandchild did not grow believed the child was bewitched. While the child lay in its cradle, a woman had touched it. When the boy was twelve or fourteen years old, he drowned while fishing.
195051: In the old days people sometimes saw a procession of white ladies floating through the air in the evening.
195104: A man from Mere claimed that a woman had bewitched his house. The day after that woman had come to look at the baby rabbits, the animals were all lying dead.
195107: People who had been ridden by the mare had in reality been led astray by stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps).
195183: Werewolves had a girlfriend and owned a werewolf skin. When they wanted to tease their girlfriend, they took their skin out of an elm and set off. To chase the werewolf away, the girl had to throw yarn at the beast.
195184: People who had got lost had been led astray by the 'dolf' (a misleading spirit).
195189: Every evening a man saw a black dog walk past his house to the little spring in the marsh. One day the man said to his wife: "If that dog comes past here again, I'll shoot it dead". But when the dog appeared and gave the man a piercing look, the man did not dare to shoot after all.
195210: A man returning from Parike stood dead drunk by the Viverdaal shouting: "Devils help me, devils take me!" A little later a gentleman appeared there, to whom the man sold his soul. From that moment on the man had special powers.
195211: A farm in Ooike was haunted. Whatever animal was put in that farm, the next day its neck had been wrung. Nobody dared go to that farm at night.
195217: One day a boy had to patch a hole in the chicken coop. When he had finished the job, he took the ladder back to the stable. There, to his great horror, he saw a white man standing. The boy ran inside in fright and told his mother what he had seen. His mother then went back to the stable with him, but there was nothing more to be seen.
195257: A man was going home pushing a wheelbarrow loaded with ten small crates of herring. Halfway there, he saw two sheep standing on the road in front of him. At that moment the man could no longer move his wheelbarrow.
195303: In Geraardsbergen shopkeepers were often bewitched by women from Meerbeke. A witch who wore a large cloak and carried a basket always conjured something out of the shops with her. Sometimes it was even a cloak or a coat. When she got home, the witch always had a full basket.
195304: A rich farmer lived on the border of Lokeren and Sinaai. One day a woman suspected of being a witch came riding up. The woman asked the farmer's wife if she could have some milk to drink. The farmer's wife did not dare refuse and gave the woman what she asked for. When butter had to be churned on that farm, however, it would not work, so in the end the people went to the black friars in Dendermonde. A friar advised them never again to give milk to anyone they did not know well. The people were also given an Easter nail and a medal of Saint Benedict. Nine days later butter could be churned on the farm again.
195322: Two men from Sint-Pauls went to a café for a glass of beer. Then they went to the field to cut grass. After that the men did not come to the café for a long time. When the men came with their cart to fetch the dry hay, they could not get their cart out of the meadow. A passer-by who saw the men were in trouble asked: "You haven't been at the café landlady's hay, have you?" That woman had special powers. After the men went to the café and paid for the beer they had drunk there some time before, they could move on with their cart.
195360: A witch had been with a sow and had vomited in the manger. The piglets born afterwards were all twisted up.
195361: One day a man went out with some friends. Among the company was a man of about seventy, who said: "If I want, I can make rats appear here." When the others did not believe it, the man grew angry and said: "Pull open the attic door and you will see the rats." The men did so and indeed saw masses of rats running about. A moment later, at the sorcerer's command, the rats had vanished again.
195371: People who were ridden by the 'maan' (mare) or led astray by the 'alf' (elf) got lost.
195381: In an abandoned castle lay a great treasure. Everyone who stayed in that castle died. One day three fellows heard about the castle. Two of them went there but never came back. When the third went to the castle in his turn, he took dough with him and began baking waffles in the castle. At twelve o'clock the man heard a voice call: "I'm falling", to which the man replied: "Fall then, as long as you don't fall on my waffles." Then a leg fell down. The same thing happened three more times, until at last a whole skeleton stood there and said: "Open that door." The man replied: "Open it yourself." The exchange was repeated three times, until the skeleton finally opened the door and the man saw his two friends sitting there. There was also a stone. Three times the skeleton said: "Lift that stone", but each time the man replied: "Lift it yourself." Under the stone lay a chest full of gold money. On the chest were the words: "This is for the church, that is for the poor and that is for the one who finds it."
195426: In Sint-Maria-Horebeke lived a poor woman who was suspected of being a witch. In reality, however, that woman could do no more than anyone else.
195473: A house in Wervik was haunted. At night the windows flew open and there was knocking on the door, although no one could be seen. The occupants lodged a complaint and the police came. That night the jokers had hidden, but a short time later they were unmasked after all, so that it was clear at once where the haunting came from.
195491: A woman had become bewitched after a witch walked in front of her in church. On getting home, the woman crawled straight into bed. Because the sick woman did not recover, her husband sent for a woman from a fairground stall who claimed she could undo the witchcraft. The woman came to the sick woman and read a prayer. The woman had to pray that prayer for nine days while walking around her house. After those nine days the sick woman was freed from the witchcraft.
195498: On a farm in Sint-Maria-Latem there was a hen that wanted to brood. For three days the animal sat dead still on her nest. Then the farmer said to his wife: "Put thirteen eggs there and set the hen on them." The hen, however, would not sit on those eggs. Near the farm lived a woman who could do witchcraft.
195555: When children got 'de oude man' (the old man), it was because the ghost of a dead family member was coming back. Because the ghost was unhappy, it took away the child's strength. In Liedekerke people went on pilgrimage against 'de oude man'.
195592: A sick boy became completely emaciated. The boy's cradle was full of ants, and whenever the child ate something, the food was also covered in ants. The child's mother went with a neighbour to the friars of Affligem. When they came back, the boy was doing well. A woman from the neighbourhood had bewitched the child.
195608: Along the road to Herzele was a wood where a kledde (a werewolf-like spook) always roamed, frightening a woman. Kledde always sat with his ugly snout in front of the window. When one day people wanted to burn kledde's skin, he stood whining to get even a single hair of the skin. Kledde was a man who had sold his soul to the devil for a certain time.
195618: On a farm where a maid worked, the food went bad. When the friars came to say prayers over the farm, they sweated terribly.
195644:
A house in Zarlardinge had much misfortune. Whenever a child was born in that house, a certain woman always came to visit. When that woman was there, the doctor left after only five minutes, whereas otherwise he stayed a good half hour and had a few drinks. The youngest child of that family did not grow. It became very thin and had diarrhoea. One day the child's mother went with another woman to the friars of Gent. The people looking after the child in the meantime noticed that for the first time the child no longer had diarrhoea. At that moment they said: "Now they must surely be at the friars'."
One Saturday a friar came to visit the family. When the friar asked the people whether they suspected anyone, they answered: "A woman from Alsace lives near here. She always behaves strangely. Sometimes she comes knocking at our door at night to ask for drops for her husband, who has toothache." The clergyman replied: "If she comes again, you must give her nothing more." Those words were scarcely spoken when the woman noticed that the witch was standing right behind her. She walked past the two of them and called out: "Good day, Father! Good day, X!"
195661: Some people from Michelbeke had promised to burn a candle for the salvation of their sick daughter. But after the girl had died, the promise had still not been fulfilled. In the evening footsteps were always heard in the attic. That was the dead daughter coming back. When the people went to the friars, they remembered the promise they had forgotten. After the promised candle had burnt down, the daughter no longer came haunting.
195746: If you kicked a toad, the next day you could see a woman walking about with a bruised face. For witches could turn themselves into toads.
195753: People who were ridden by the mare could no longer find their house and kept ending up in the same place.
195769: On 'de Gaver' the witches came at midnight to eat, dance and sing. When a visitor said there was no salt on the food, the whole scene vanished at once, because the word 'salt' was not to be spoken.
195775: A boy whose mother was a sorceress worked for a farmer. To show that he too had special powers, the boy took a small heap of earth and made mice run out of it.
195795: On a farm in Schendelbeke worked a farmhand who played werewolf in the evenings. He had hidden his skin in a willow. One day the maid sent the farmhand far away so that meanwhile she could fetch the skin and throw it into the oven. When the skin had caught fire, the farmhand stood at the oven lamenting that he had almost been freed and now had to start all over again.
195804: In a house in Sint-Lievens-Esse there were always sounds as if a train were passing. People even heard the train staff calling out. When the people went outside to look, strangely enough there was nothing to see. The man who lived there had once shouted furiously at a witch: "You ought to be on the train tomorrow, so you never get home again!"
195837: On a bowling lane along the road to Denderleeuw, Liedekerke was playing against Iddergem. When Liedekerke was winning, a Russian witch came by and said to a player from Iddergem: "Don't lose heart. You will win." After that a toad always ran in front of the ball, so that the Liedekerke players lost the game.
195860: On a farm in Nieuwerkerken the gates were always unfastened in the morning, although they had been locked the evening before. When the people once kept watch, the gates opened again without anyone being seen.
195867: Many animals died on a farm in Aalst. A woman always stood praying on a road near the farm. Because the farmer found this suspicious, he went to the white friars of Gent. There a friar said to the farmer: "That woman will ask why you are so finely dressed." On his way home the farmer was indeed addressed by the woman with the words: "Where have you come from, looking so fine?" That told the farmer who was responsible for the evil. Eight days later that woman was dead.
195889: When witches found no one to bewitch, their own children had to suffer for it. A girl with a hunchback claimed that a witch had given her that disability.
195908: A cow had been stolen from a woman in Nederename who was suspected of being a witch. In Maria Horebeke the witch heard her cow lowing. She went into that farm and took her cow back.
195923: Some people about to set off for Gaverland in a horse-drawn cart saw a neighbour woman coming, who asked if she could ride along. The driver refused, saying: "The cart is already full." At that the neighbour said: "Then you shall not ride either." A little further on the horse dropped dead.
195924: In Ename there was a farm that seemed to be on fire every night. The animals jumped about restlessly. When the people got up, there was nothing strange to be seen any more and the animals calmed down again. One night the farmer did see someone riding through the air on a fiery horse. The apparition went into the stable and left again a little later.
195944: A man and a woman had promised to offer gold and butter in the church for their sick daughter. The daughter died of her illness. The parents did not keep their promise. One night the parents discovered the ghost of their daughter churning butter. The dead girl said: "Mother, you must give that gold and that butter…" After they had done so, the daughter appeared no more.
195952: A man saw a creature flying that was about the size of a bumblebee. Strangely, the man saw the creature grow bigger and bigger, until it turned into a horse.
195970: Near the churchyard stood a farm with a monastery beneath it, in which ghostly friars and priests lived. All men who had a beautiful wife lost their spouse. People claimed that those women ended up in that underground monastery, for there were also many children in it. That is why the farm was called 't Vraanhof.
195971: On a farm worked a stable hand who had a skin in which he had to roam about in the evening as kledde (a werewolf-like spook). When the farmer was heating the oven one day, he found a kledde skin in the woodpile. As soon as he had thrown the skin into the oven, the farmhand stood by the fire to save it. When his skin had burnt, he was glad he was freed.
195987: Some witches holding a gathering stood hand in hand while they discussed where they would go. A farmer who had put his horse in a clover meadow by a chapel found that his horse had disappeared. The witches had driven the horse into the chapel. Four days later a goose-herd heard the horse neighing.
195993: A man was accompanied on his way home by a woman dressed entirely in white. The woman walked ahead of the man the whole time, and when he stood still, so did she. When he got home the man called his mother, but it took a while before she opened the door. While the man stood waiting, the woman stayed beside him the whole time.
196011: A man worked on a farm together with his cousin. After the midday meal the farmhands were allowed to rest for half an hour in summer. One day the man heard his cousin fall asleep against the haystack and start tossing and turning. When the man woke his cousin because the break was over, the cousin said he had been ridden by the mare. Anyone who in the evening placed one clog with the heel towards the bed and the other with the toe towards the bed would not be ridden by the mare at night.
196031: A man coming home from work felt a werewolf climb onto his back on the way. He had to carry the werewolf. But he threw his handkerchief on the ground and ordered the werewolf to unravel the cloth. This kept the man safe for a while, because the werewolf had to finish that task before it could do anything else. When the man got home, he climbed a ladder in the stable. As he stood on the top rung, the werewolf kicked the ladder out from under his feet. Luckily the man had just made it to the top.
196033: A man claimed that he had been struck by 'a blow of the wind', which made him fall into the ditch. The man was on his way to his girlfriend, and he regarded the incident as a bad omen.
196081: By the Bosbeek between Atembeke and Moerbeke there were bushes and hedges where meowing cats sat in the evening and at night. That place was called 'het Schof'. After dark people no longer dared to go there, because they believed witches appeared there in the shape of cats.
196108: In the old days there were people who went about with a skin over them as a 'loetie' (werewolf), jumping on people and making them carry them to a certain place. If the victim had a knife with him and could stick the blade into the ground, the loetie's skin fell to the ground and he could be unmasked. Loeties were people who consorted with devils. The only way to get them under control was by pouring linseed into a woodpile.
196187: A strange fellow used to live in Vrasene. Once a man went fishing with a friend between Dunkeldam and Klemlaar. In the Lammenstraat the man stepped into a wheel rut and could not get out again. The man's friend said he had seen the strange fellow, who was holding the man's foot.
196305: A man went to the barber with his friend. On the way there the friend claimed to see a dog, but the man saw nothing. A little further on the man saw the dog too. The man grabbed at the animal but could not touch it.
196307: Witches had a little figure into which they stuck pins whenever they wanted to harm someone. A girl from Everbeek died because of such practices.
196336: People claimed that ghosts dressed in white haunted a little chapel in the Zandstraat. If you tried to grab the ghosts, you could not touch them. Because the people in the Zandstraat had so much misfortune, a little chapel was built there.
196379: A farm had much misfortune. The mare miscarried and several pigs died. The people went three or four times to the friars of Affligem, who came to undo the witchcraft. After that the stable was torn down and a new one built. An Easter nail was placed under the chimney. The priest came to bless the animals' pens.
196382: At a miller's, all the farmhands were murdered at night once they had been in service for a while. One day a brave farmhand was hired who was not frightened by the stories told about the mill. In the mill where the farmhand had to sleep, cats appeared at night. The new farmhand asked the miller for a gun and a blessed button. When a meowing cat appeared in the night, the miller's hand shot at the animal. The next morning the miller's wife lay in her bed with a gunshot wound. A blessed button was found in the woman's wound.
196383: A boy went to visit his girlfriend in Sint-Maria-Lierde. When the boy came back at night, he saw cats all around him, so that he had to get off his bicycle. After the boy had made the sign of the cross twice, all the cats had disappeared.
196395: A man from Sint-Cornelis-Horebeke who was an hour's walk from the church of Schorisse got lost. At dawn the man sat down on the ground to rest. Then the man found his way again. He had been ridden by the mare.
196419: If someone had found an animal skin somewhere and wanted to burn it in the oven, the owner of the skin was immediately at the oven to save his property. As soon as the skin was burnt, however, that person was freed from evil.
196440: A rich gentleman had a relationship with a farmer's daughter. No one knew where this gentleman had come from. One day, when the girl picked something up, she saw that the gentleman had horse's feet. She went to tell the priest, who said she must not let that man in any more and must sprinkle everything with holy water.
196454: Three men who had gone to cut wood in Everbeek saw a big wild cat sitting on their way home. One of the men said to his brother: "Give that cat a kick", but the brother would not dream of doing such a thing. So the man kicked the cat himself, sending it flying into the field. A little later, however, the man was himself struck by the cat.
196465: Around a house in Kwaremont there was a fine hawthorn hedge. When music was suddenly heard in that hedge, the man took his gun, went outside and shot at it. At that moment a glove leapt out of the hedge. The man picked up the glove and told the priest what had happened. The priest advised the man to stand in the same spot the next day and throw the glove into the air with the words: "Glove, go back where you came from". The man did so and saw the glove fly away through the air.
196505: A man always went to fetch milk from a woman who had a good five or six cats. That woman was intelligent and knew French and Dutch. She always drank her coffee black. When the front wall of her house collapsed, she stayed sitting on her trunk of books. The woman also had two small horns on her head. When she was sitting at a neighbour's in the Kapellestraatje one morning, she could not get away, and she had to be taken home in a wheelbarrow.
196522: People who claimed they had been ridden by the mare were usually drunkards who had got lost in a wood.
196536: A man who had to go home through a meadow one evening could not get home because horses kept standing on their hind legs in front of him.
196594: When people saw a magpie, they believed it was an omen of bad news.
196623: A farmer's wife saw a little woman sitting in her stable, wearing a scarf with pink and red flowers on her head. When the farmer's wife went into the stable, the little woman had vanished and a fat toad sat by the oven. The farmer then went on a pilgrimage to Affligem.
196628: Some people returning from a pilgrimage to Gaverland met a cat in Sint-Gillis that began to speak. The animal asked for help and grew bigger and bigger.
196652: A man who had taken his cow to a farm to be covered found on returning home that he had lost his wallet. The man set out again in the dark to look for his wallet. He soon found the wallet, but got lost on his way home. If his father had not come to meet him with a flashlight, he would not have made it home. The man had been ridden by the 'maan' (mare) or 'led astray by the alf' (elf).
196654: A grandfather advised his daughter to bring in her baby's nappies. The daughter answered: "I've already folded them," but there was still a whole row of nappies hanging on the washing line. When the girl ran to the nappies, they flew away. In the distance she heard someone laughing. The girl then immediately ran inside.
196657: A carter out with his horses one evening promised to have a mass said for the faithful departed if a will-o'-the-wisp came to light the way for him. A little further on a will-o'-the-wisp did appear and accompanied the man to his destination. So the man had the promised mass said.
196674: People asked a wizard to drive away rats and mice. When the wizard did this, he always had to leave an opening through which the animals could escape. Meanwhile he had to read a text aloud from a book.
196689:
A brewer who could no longer make good beer had dismissed his brewer's journeyman. A new journeyman was hired. When the journeyman saw a cat sitting there while he was working, he took his knife and cut off one of the animal's paws. The next day the brewer's wife was missing a finger. It was that woman who had been haunting the place.
Witches first had to ruin themselves before they could harm anyone else. The coming of the Gospel of Saint John put an end to much evil.
196690: In the castle of Laken, every night at the same time, a sound was heard like a squeaking little cart rolling down the stairs. While a party was going on in the castle, a beggar came by and asked for shelter. Only the devil's room was still free. At midnight the beggar woke up and saw a ghost come in with a burning candle. The ghost held the candle to the nose of the beggar for a moment, who pretended to be asleep. Then the ghost opened a cupboard in a hidden wall, out of which hundreds of gold coins rolled. After the ghost had counted the gold coins, he put everything back in the cupboard. The next day the beggar told the lord of the castle everything, and together they took the gold coins out of the wall. As a reward the beggar received half of the treasure.
196731: A woman peddler always set down her baskets in a house in Elversele and asked for a cup of coffee there. One day the woman living in that house fell ill. Because no doctor could help her, she went with her mother to the friars of Dendermonde. Without the women having said a single word, one of the friars said they must no longer take in the peddler's baskets and should only give her a cup of coffee without milk. When the people followed this advice, the woman recovered. One day the woman saw the peddler sitting in the café. As soon as the peddler saw the woman, she left.
196786: In Etikhove beautiful music was heard in the air. The music came from the north and moved to the south. Several people in the village heard the music in the evening.
196794: On a farm where butter could not be churned, people believed the evil hand had something to do with it. After the people had been to the priest, the situation improved.
196795: One night a poacher shot at a hare. When the man went to pick up the hare, he saw some sixty-five animals lying on the ground. After that the man had a great deal of misfortune.
196865: At the fair a woman was approached by a little woman who asked if she might come by sometime. A little later the woman felt a large needle in her buttock.
196866: On a farm in Munkzwalm the farmer's wife wanted to bolt the door for the night. Because something was stuck in the keyhole, she called her husband, who himself had great trouble locking the door. Suddenly there was a loud bang and the door flew against the wall, sending wood splinters flying. That was haunting.
196869: A woman was ridden by the mare. She wanted to call out, but could not utter a word. The mare was a well-known woman from the village.
196893: A man travelling with his wheelbarrow stopped for a drink. When he had taken a swig from his bottle, there was a slug on his tongue. Yet the man was convinced there had been lemonade in the bottle.
196900: The Godsberg was haunted. Kledde (a spectral black dog) roamed there. One could also meet cats or a foal there.
196923: When people heard their ears ringing or heard a magpie chattering, they believed news was on its way.
196948: In a house the people had hidden leather money. When those people had died, nobody knew that the money lay under the sink in the scullery.
