In that house the pots and plates were heard falling off the sink every night. One night a farmhand went to keep watch in the scullery. At twelve o'clock the noise began. The farmhand was not allowed to move, for that would mean his death. The farmhand was shaken about and a voice said three times: "Are you sleeping, are you waking, or what are you doing?" The farmhand did not move a muscle and held his breath. The ghosts removed the pump stone, counted the money and then left. The next day the people were able to take the money from under the pump stone.
197018: 't Eiken was haunted. The table there suddenly began to dance. The next morning a woman there was dead.
197032: A woman suspected of being a witch always sat by a little chapel. A farmer who had met the witch was soon after chased by as many as two hundred cats.
197050: Some people always heard chains rattling at night and believed it was the devil. One day they could even see the devil.
197056: A man who was ridden by the mare lay in his bed and felt something walking on his feet. The mare came upwards and squeezed the man's throat shut, so that the man could no longer breathe. Anyone ridden by the mare had to turn onto their side to be freed.
197060: A seven-month-old girl was seriously ill. On a visitor's advice, the mother took the child to the priest, who gave her a medal. The child survived, but at two and a half years old it still could not walk.
197071: In the morning a dead person had been taken from a house in Huise to the church for the funeral. When a man passed that house later in the day, it seemed as if he was being held back by the lime tree that stood there. "What do you want of me?" the man asked, and was answered: "I made a promise that I did not keep. Would you fulfil that promise for me?" After the man had agreed, he was able to go on.
197092: A peculiar woman lived in Elversele. One day that woman asked some men if she could ride along with their horse to Gaverland. When the men refused, the woman made the horse drop dead.
197115: A mother had seen her dead daughter appear. The daughter was wearing a little scarf and said: "Mother, you made a promise and you have not kept it." The mother immediately went to the parish priest, after which she began to pray fervently.
197141: A father had a child of eight or nine months that ate well but always vomited. Because the child's legs were only as thick as a finger, the man decided to seek help. A kwezeltje (a pious spinster) who went to pray at all the chapels promised to go to the friars of Bornem for the child. From the friars the woman brought back blessed salt and some relics. The friar had told the woman: "The father cannot be touched by the evil hand, but the mother and the child must wear a relic." They were to put the salt in the child's porridge. When the child had taken two spoonfuls of the porridge, it began to cry. After that, however, it went on eating and no longer vomited. The parents had to make a novena and pray Our Fathers in the evening. On the ninth day the child cried from morning till night, but three months later it was completely cured.
197167: One day a farmer saw a black horse in his meadow. He harnessed it to the plough together with his own horse and set to work. In the evening the farmer took his horses back to the stable. The next morning he saw that the black horse had disappeared. When the farmer came to his field, he found that half the furrows had not been ploughed. That black horse had been the devil.
197194: A woman with a bad reputation had visited a farm in Volkegem. That woman had given the cows some food. Because the animals gave no more milk the next day, the farmer went to the friars of Gent, who said: "Keep your door shut until eleven o'clock and then you won't hear a single cow anymore." After that they were allowed to open the door again and the cows gave as much milk as before.
197201: A man who went to the market in Lokeren every Wednesday always met a black cat on the way, which circled his legs and sang: "X asks me, pussycat, where are you going?" The cat hindered the man and would not be chased away.
197219: A maid who worked on a farm had already been attacked several times on the way by a werewolf. The girl was advised to throw a handkerchief at the beast. When the girl did so, the werewolf had to unravel the handkerchief completely, which gave the girl the chance to run home. The next day the girl saw that the farmhand who worked on the farm had the threads of the handkerchief between his teeth.
197226: One evening an old man was jumped by the werewolf in a lonely spot. He had to carry the werewolf on his back to a certain place. There the werewolf jumped down.
197241: Every night at about the same time a man felt the mare crawl onto his bed. You could not throw anything at the mare, because that did not help. If someone slept with the man, he had no problems.
197247: A man wanted to burn the skin of Osschaert (a werewolf-like spook) in the oven because the friars of Dendermonde had advised him to. The skin was hardly in the oven when some fifty Osschaerts sprang up and pulled the skin out of the oven.
197251: A butcher coming home from work one evening was jumped by kledde (a werewolf-like spook). The man managed to stab kledde with a knife, so that the next day everyone knew who kledde was.
197261: Anyone walking past a churchyard at night often saw lights in the air. They were the spirits of children who had died unbaptised.
197284: An evil sorceress lived in Eine. When the sorceress's body sometimes looked lifeless, people said that she had gone off somewhere to work witchcraft.
197291: Half an hour after his death, a dead man got up and sat down on the stairs. When the priest came, the man opened his mouth and gave back the host he had received. Then the man stood up, lay down on the bed again and died once more. The priest assured the people that they should not think that giving back the host was a sign that the dead man was damned or anything of the kind.
197313: A woman had tried to summon the spirit of her dead daughter. The daughter had been run over at the age of twenty. To do such a thing, a certain number of people had to form a circle. They had to sit hand in hand and keep a photo of the deceased with them. The deceased only ever made contact with one or two people in the group. When the woman summoned her daughter's spirit, she learned that the child had not yet reached her destination, but was getting help from another dead relative who was drawing her towards that good place.
197315: In a house that was haunted every night, people always saw a little old person standing. The people no longer dared to go to sleep until a clergyman had been to the house. Later it became known that a freemason had lived in that house. The little old person they saw was the devil.
197370: People who were ridden by the mare were stabbed with knives by figures sitting on them. Victims of the mare were completely drenched in sweat. They were dreaming or had a stoppage of the blood.
197371: A woman could no longer churn butter after a neighbour had visited her. After the parish priest had come by and said some prayers, the woman could make butter again.
197375: On a farm they had the greatest trouble building a brick well. The man who had to do the job blamed the problems on a woman from Waterhooze who had come to watch the work.
197389:
A man going to visit his girlfriend on the Bormte in Stekene was leapt on in the Waterstraat by a bear that had itself carried. At the end of the Waterstraat the bear jumped into the field.
Later the skin of that bear was found in a hollow tree stump. When the skin had been thrown into the oven, a man came running up who also wanted to jump into the oven. The oven door had to be slammed shut to stop the man jumping into the fire.
197390: A miller going to the fair in Aspelare threw stones at a meowing cat that was following him. The next day the miller saw a woman walking with a bandage around her arm.
197433: A farmer who had moved the boundary post of his field quarrelled with his neighbour. After his death the farmer came haunting every night, calling: "Where must I put this post?" One day a drunkard passed by and answered: "Put it where you took it from." "Thank you," the farmer replied.
197438: On the Katteknok in Kruishoutem a large black cat always paced back and forth at night. People said it was a witch.
197439: A man had a wicked wife who was never in her bed at night. When one night the house was full of cats, the man threw a stick at the animals. The next morning his wife lay in bed with a broken leg.
197533:
A soldier who was quartered in Bachen during the war was ridden by the mare at night. The man felt as if someone was grabbing him by the throat. When he sat up, everything was normal, but as soon as he lay down again, it all started again.
His brother advised the soldier to place his shoes crossed next to his bed, so the mare could no longer get to him. The man followed the advice and was rid of the mare.
His brother could locate the mare by rolling a knife in a handkerchief and turning it around three times behind his back. If the knife then lay on the handkerchief instead of in it, the mare was at a place that had been named beforehand.
197578: People who had a pearl (a white spot) on their eye believed they had fallen victim to evil and went to the friars.
197579: In a man's house people were playing cards. Meanwhile the wife went to the rabbit hutch, which turned out to be completely full of mice. The woman went back inside to light the stove so she could pour boiling water on the mice. But the woman's husband then said: "The mice came by themselves and they will go away by themselves too". And so it was.
197594: Some men were walking home in the moonlight. By a little path one of the men was annoyed by a black kitten that kept getting under his feet. The man cried: "You damned red thing, I'll take you with me, since we have no kitten at home right now." The man took the kitten along. The next day the man lay dead and the kitten was gone.
197598: A man claimed that there was an evil spirit in his house. Once the man had put away two pots. A little later he found that the pots had disappeared.
197631: A girl had been to a café where many hop pickers went. When the girl left, a black cat jumped in front of her feet. The girl kicked at the cat but could not get rid of it. Terrified, the girl knocked at a door. After she had sat in that house for a while, the cat was again standing at her feet.
197632: A carpenter was working for a woman who was suspected of being a sorceress. Every day that woman went to the six o'clock mass. When the carpenter arrived at six, the woman was still at home. Yet a moment later she was already at the church. That was witchcraft.
197697: People who were ridden by the mare lay stiff as a board in their bed and could not move.
197700: A musician from Berlare had a relationship with a girl from Zele. When the man returned one night from a visit to his girlfriend, he could not get out of the field, so he had to wander around there all night. That man had been ridden by the mare.
197727: A child was playing alone because its parents were working behind the house. When the parents came in, they saw their child lying with its head on the table. Next to the child lay the core of a pear. The child had been given a bewitched pear by someone.
197746: A man coming home in the evening saw a big black dog standing in front of him. The dog was a good two metres long and had eyes like lanterns. When he got home the man saw the dog standing at his door. So the man went to a friend's house, who said the dog was a ghost. The friend went on: "I'll go outside for a moment, so you get the chance to get into your house". When the friend then reached his own front door, the dog was standing there.
197773: Some people were loading manure onto a cart. A passer-by from Schendelbeke, who had a few cows with him, said: "Are you loading manure?" and he put his hand on the cart. He said: "That is a strong wagon!" After that the wagon could no longer be moved. Even five horses could not pull the cart. The farmhands had no choice but to wait until the passer-by went back home, and they asked him to undo the harm he had done. The man went to the cart. After that, two horses could pull the load with ease.
197798: A woman who one morning had a large spot on her jaw and could not be helped by any doctor went to the friars of Dendermonde. The clergymen claimed the woman had been bewitched by a witch and advised her to do penance for nineteen days. After the woman had followed that advice, the spot was gone.
197819: Every night a red rooster came to crow at the little chapel in Nukerke. The chapel was built there because someone had failed to keep a promise.
197824: In the old days there were often people who went about at night as werewolves and made passers-by carry them. When the miller of the Molenberg had to grind at night, he often heard the werewolf's victims crying out. Anyone who refused to carry the werewolf was beaten on the back.
197826: A woman who was going to Mass with her father at Easter got a fright when a white veil suddenly flew against her face from behind the verge. That was a ghost sitting there.
197853: A man always saw his wife flying through the air in bad weather.
197860: A woman was visited by a female peddler. She bought nothing, however, because she thought the peddler looked like a sorceress. After that, five of that woman's children died.
197872: A wholesaler had to make deliveries in Nederzwalm during the winter. On his way home the man ended up in the same place three times. Only at midnight did he reach his house. He had been ridden by the mare. In reality the man had a stoppage of the blood.
197874: It was said of a hero of the Boerenkrijg (Peasants' War) that he had dealings with the black hand. A black hand was burned into the wall of his house. When the man was buried, a black dog jumped into the grave with him.
197887: At midnight a hare chased by a dog always ran through an orchard. One night a few boys went to that orchard. One of them threw a stick at the dog but could not hit it. Strangely enough, the stick hit one of his friends, who was standing quite a distance away. Apparently the dog had some kind of magic power that let it change the direction of the thrown stick.
197910: A man who worked at the Puithoek was sitting at the table in that farmhouse one winter evening by the light of a paraffin lamp. At a certain moment the light went out without anyone blowing it out. The farmer relit it and the people started eating again. A little later the light went out again. Then the farmer said: "In God's name, we will light it one last time". At the third attempt the light did stay lit, because the farmer had said "in God's name".
197927: A man woke up at night because he heard noise. He wanted to get up and look, but could not get out of his bed. When the man got up in the morning, he had no problems.
197932: A man was transporting trees with a horse cart. Although the cart stood on a meadow with hard ground, the horses could not move forward. The man got down and a little later was startled when the horses sank into the ground up to their bellies. The donkey was still standing on firm ground.
197951: A boy coming home late in the evening got a fright when three or four cats suddenly came out of the farm gate.
197961: A farmer had found in his oven the skin in which his farmhand played kledde (a werewolf-like spook). The farmer burnt the skin. At that moment the farmhand stood moaning and crying.
197986: On a farm in Nokere so many misfortunes happened that the farmer promised that someone would go to vespers every Sunday and that a chapel would be built in honour of Saint Usmarus. After the farmer had kept all those promises, he had no more misfortune.
198015: Werewolves were jokers who leapt out of the verge and jumped on passers-by's backs to be carried.
198045: In De Klinge lived a woman with six children. Their neighbour had no water, so the woman supplied her neighbour with water. One day the neighbour had called out that she needed water. But the woman had not heard it right away because her children were making a lot of noise. The neighbour was angry. Four years later all the animals of the family with six children died. The people then went on a pilgrimage, after which the misfortune came to an end.
198080: In Aspelare a man was walking sighing across his field when a gentleman came by and asked what his problem was. The man explained that his harvest would rot because he had no barn to store it all in. The gentleman said: "If you sell your soul to me, you will have a new barn tomorrow morning before the first cockcrow." When the farmer heard noise outside at three o'clock at night, he told his wife what he had done. The wife got up, went to the henhouse and clapped her hands, so that the cock began to crow early. At that moment ten roof tiles still had to be laid on the barn. Because the barn was not quite finished, the farmer was allowed to keep his soul. Later people tried to lay the remaining tiles on the roof themselves, but they always flew off again. Only when a cross had been hung in the barn did they manage to close the hole in the roof.
198111: In Bevere lived a woman who was said to be a sorceress. That woman bewitched the small children.
198112: A boy was in a relationship with a farmer's daughter. He had said to his girlfriend: "If you see a werewolf, throw your handkerchief at the beast and tell it to unravel the handkerchief." When the girl met a werewolf, she did as she had been advised. The next day the girl noticed that the fibres of the handkerchief were hanging between her boyfriend's teeth. The girl immediately ended the relationship, but the werewolf soon found another girlfriend.
198129: A man who had gone to fetch clover with his wheelbarrow met a wizard, who said: "If you are home early tomorrow, you can count yourself happy." The man wandered around all night and did not get home.
198135: People who were ridden by the 'maan' (mare) had a dream and could not wake up.
198138: Will-o'-the-wisps appeared when someone in the neighbourhood was about to die. Some people claimed will-o'-the-wisps were the returning souls of dead children.
198140: A woman who was often ill was lying in childbed. A visitor gave her newborn child a sweet because it cried all the time. Shortly afterwards the child began to waste away, so people believed the visitor had bewitched it. The father went to the parish priest, but he claimed that witchcraft did not exist. Because the man kept insisting that the priest intervene, the clergyman finally said: "The sorceress will visit you tomorrow and ask for carrots or other vegetables. You must not do her any harm." When the visitor came by again the next day, she said: "My reputation as a sorceress has been gone for so long. Are you going to renew it now?"
198168: On a farm where they could not churn butter, they consulted the friars. A friar came to the farm and pointed out to the people a woman who was churning butter behind a hidden hedge. After the friar had prayed for a while, he asked the people to pour a bucket of dung into the butter churn. A little later that woman's churn was filled with dung.
198231: A man returning from a visit to his aunt struck with a stick at a dog standing beside a barn. The man struck so hard that he fell to the ground himself. Strangely, the dog had vanished without a trace.
198252: The people of Elversele never laughed at a woman who always went to fetch hay in the Broek. Strangers who did not know the peculiar woman sometimes dared to mock her. Those people got stuck with their horse and cart in the mud of the Broek. Only once they had given the woman some hay could they move on.
198274: In Bost there lived a wizard whom people feared. One evening some people in an inn quarrelled with the wizard. When those people came outside, they were given a sound thrashing by an invisible apparition.
198291: In Sint-Gillis-Dendermonde lived a woman who was suspected of dealing with evil. One day that woman came to a farm to ask whether she could buy chicks. But she got none. The woman had barely left when all the animals on that farm died.
198294: A stable hand going home one night saw a group of rabbits running in the churchyard. The stable hand took the rabbits and put the animals in his stable. The next day the rabbits had turned into skulls.
198321: A sorceress from Haaltert often came at night to bewitch the children while they lay in bed. The children would then start crying and sweating. The friars of Affligem advised the people to place an Easter nail in the children's room, so that the sorceress could no longer get in.
198322: A wizard could send rats from one house to another. However, the rats had to have as much food at their new destination as in the house they came from.
198350: Witches sometimes pricked wax figures in order to torment children, make them ill or cause them to die.
198376: A father whose child was always ill was often visited by a woman. When the little child got the 'head illness' (?), the doctor declared he did not know what to do. The child's mother went to ask the priest to pray. She feared her child had been struck by an evil hand. The clergyman read prayers over the child until the drops of sweat rolled down his face. After that the child was cured. A certain neighbour never visited again after that.
198379: A witch was told by her son to go to confession at Easter, or else she could no longer live with him. The son spied on his mother from behind a pillar in the church. He saw his mother join the line for confession, but leave the church when it was her turn. So that witch probably owned books she did not want to give up. When she came home, the mother claimed she had gone to confession. But the son said he knew she was lying and sent her away.
198405: A man from Aaigem went into a café in France. The landlady's mother asked him where he came from. When the man said he lived near Aalst, the landlady went on: "Do you live far from Aaigem? I stayed in the Dikke Linde there for a long time, but now I have been freed from it."
198408:
In the past children were sometimes struck by the evil hand. In a house where a witch had come to fetch a piece of leek, a child fell ill.
Rich people who had four children went to the friars to get an Easter nail. When that Easter nail was stuck under the threshold, no witches could come in anymore. When a friar came to read prayers over a bewitched place, he sweated terribly.
Witches could bewitch children by giving them, for example, a piece of cheese or some sweets. As long as the child was not baptized, the mother often let no one into her house as a precaution.
198426: In Erwetegem lived a woman who was suspected of being a sorceress. If something went wrong somewhere after that woman had visited, people believed she had bewitched the house.
198473: A man who had grown up in Sint-Pauwels slept in a cellar room. When the man had been in his bed for a quarter of an hour, he heard a knocking and then felt a good two hundred kilos pressing on his body. After a while the weight disappeared. Because the man was ridden by the mare every night, after three weeks he hardly dared to go to sleep.
198501: A boy with scabs all over his skin was taken by his mother to the friars of Gent. The friar said: "Mother, I already know what it is. Instead of giving milk to your neighbour, you had better give it to your pigs." After prayers had been read over the boy and he had been given blessed rose petals to put in his milk, he was cured.
198526: In front of the Bloemenhof in Tielrode stood a small chapel, because that farm used to be badly haunted. At midnight loud music was heard in the cellar there and the devils rode past on horseback. A brave man who wanted to see all this up close hid behind a bush. When the devils rode past, one of them leaned his head behind the bush to ask the man what time it was. The man ran home terrified and never left his bed again. After that the fathers bricked up the cellar.
198543: A farm in Everbeek was so badly haunted that the building stood empty for thirty years. Next to the farm stood a pear tree in which white figures always hung swaying at night. The farmer who eventually got the farm almost for free was called 'pastor' by the people because he was the only one who dared to live there.
198545: One evening a man from Ooike met a witch in a hooded cloak. When the man went left, the witch went left too. If the man went right, she did as well. The man was so angry that he struck the witch and threw her into a deep brook, in which she normally should have drowned. But the next day the man saw the witch walking about again.
198550: A miller working in his mill at night kept seeing little lights jumping from one tree to another. The miller's hand believed they were stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps). The women went to pray at a small chapel so that the lights would disappear. The owner of the wood eventually had to sell his land. Under one of the trees leather money was found. Every night the ghost of a dead man had to come and count his money there. It was ill-gotten wealth.
198571: At a little chapel near Tielrode a white glow was always seen in the sky in the evening. People no longer dared to walk past that chapel in the evening. Strange things happened every week. It was haunted.
198609: A man who feared nothing went on pilgrimage to Sint-Job with some friends. The man said to the statue of the saint: "Tell your father we were here". The next day the man was covered in sores. He had to promise to make the pilgrimage to Sint-Job again, this time without mocking.
198612: In Orroir lived people who every evening at ten o'clock heard a horse stamping against their door. When they opened the door, there was nothing to be seen. After they had the friars exorcise their house, the strange events came to an end.
198658: On a farm they believed that a woman from the neighbourhood was doing them harm. So the people went to the friars. A while later that neighbour came to bring a jug of milk. Against her better judgment the farmer's wife accepted the milk. Later, however, she regretted it and poured the milk into the stove. She threw the ashes out onto the street. The next day the ashes were full of prints of clawed feet, so that the shocked people asked: "What has happened here?"
198661: On a farm they could not churn butter after a sorceress had walked past. Once they had had prayers read over the milk in Affligem, they could make butter again.
198708:
People who were ridden by the mare saw a witch come in and crawl onto their bed. Victims of the mare could hardly breathe and felt as if someone was squeezing their throat shut.
It was mostly people who were fearful who experienced such things.
198723: A woman often had to go to the toilet at night. One night, when she reached under her bed for the chamber pot, she felt another hand. Terrified, she let out a loud scream. Her mother lit the light and looked under the bed, but there was nothing to be seen. She said her daughter had probably been dreaming. The daughter, however, stood her ground and fetched an axe. When she felt the hand again, she struck with the axe. The axe stuck in the floorboards.
198729: A sorceress predicted that none of her children would ever have children of their own. And so it was.
198750: A stalkaars (will-o'-the-wisp) was a sorceress who could turn herself into a little light that moved about constantly. If you held out your finger towards such a light, it came closer and settled on the outstretched finger.
198774: A farmhand who wanted to go to the fair was told by a priest who could do magic: "You will not go." And indeed the farmhand could not get away.
198807: Every day on his way home from work a man was jumped by a werewolf. He sought the priest's advice, who said: "From now on, take a good cudgel with you when you come home." The man did as he was told and gave the werewolf a hard blow. The next day the werewolf was found dead. It turned out to be a man from the neighbourhood who had disguised himself with a skin.
198809: A man who had stayed up watching over a mare about to foal went home around two in the morning. On the way he saw a good ten cats jumping in front of his feet. Because he could not chase the cats away, he ran back to the farm terrified. When the man came to the same spot eight days later, he saw a woman sitting behind the hedge who was suspected of being a witch. That woman later had to pass her magic power on to her daughter.
198825: You must never remove a swallows' nest, because that brought bad luck.
198859: On a farm on the Prinskouter a cat was always seen coming in through the gutter. That family had a lot of bad luck, for all the children got the 'oude man' (old man, a wasting illness). One day the farmer jabbed at the cat's mouth with his poker. The next day the neighbour had burns on her face.
198938: A boy was courting a pretty girl. One evening, visiting his girlfriend, he pretended to have fallen asleep drunk. At half past ten the girl and her mother made the sign of the cross and said: "We fly to High Bohemia, high over gates." The boy, who had heard everything, said: "To High Bohemia, through gates." He was badly injured when he arrived at his destination. There someone arranged for him to be carried home by a pig. It would jump over a great stretch of water, but the boy was not allowed to look back. He did so anyway, and said: "That's quite some water!" The next moment the boy was standing all alone on the ground.
198950: A farmer always had to go out around midnight. One day people found a devil's skin on the road. They threw the skin into the oven. The next moment the farmer was at the oven to save his skin.
198963:
On a farm where a sow was about to give birth to piglets, a farmhand stayed in the sty. Every time the farmer came to look in the sty, the sow flew at the door.
One day, when the farmer was coming back from his meadow, he met a woman with a bad reputation. The woman said to him: "Come, have a pinch of snuff." The farmer replied: "I'll accept nothing from you! If you don't leave me alone, I'll stick a pitchfork in you!" The woman said: "If you don't take a pinch, you won't go any further." The farmer had to stay standing on the spot while the woman went home. The priest went to free the farmer, otherwise he might still be standing there!
The farmer always had a lot of bad luck on his farm. The buttermilk went sour quickly, the freshly baked bread was rotten, and when a hen had laid an egg, no egg could be found in the nest.
198991: A stalkaars (stable candle) was a candle that lay by the door when the cows were going to die.
198995: In the kitchen of a house the haunting always began in the evening. Little threads could be seen moving up and down. The priest had to bless that house again.
199018: People who had to deal with a werewolf threw a piece of cloth at the beast. The werewolf then had to unravel the cloth, which gave the person in question the chance to get away.
199044:
To protect yourself against the mare, you had to say:
Mare, tare,
You are a 'veroere' (?)
You must touch the whole world,
If you want to get to me.
199048: A man on his way to Lede was jumped by kledde (a werewolf-like spook) at a bridge. The man let himself fall backwards and gave kledde a sound thrashing, so that the next day people knew who he was.
199065: If people saw a black cat walking between their legs in the evening, they believed the animal had something to do with evil.
199083: A farm in Bevere was haunted. All the furniture was thrown about there.
199084: On a farm a large black dog was seen approaching, which turned around and then disappeared again. Whenever butter was churned on that farm, the butter tub was full of toads.
199089: In the evening a big black dog was often seen roaming about. That was a haunting.
199090: On a farm a farmer shot with a blessed gun at a hare sitting in the chestnut wood. But the farmer could not hit the hare. The next day a woman came to visit, wearing a bandage around her head. She was probably the woman who had turned herself into a hare. Every time that woman had crossed the threshold of the cowshed, a cow on the farm died.
199115: A woman had walked past a sorcerer without greeting him. When the woman reached the station, she found that she was covered in lice. She went back home and met the sorcerer again. He said: "Go on back, and next time say good day when you walk past someone". The lice were gone at once.
199137: In Beveren there was a field with three tree stumps behind which a woman sat. A man from the village went to fetch his gun because the woman would not leave the field. The man fired several times in the woman's direction. But when he came closer, he found that the woman had disappeared. Then the man saw the woman again and fired once more. He did not manage to hit her.
199145: On the Meulekouter there was a place where witches gathered at night in the shape of black hens to make music and amuse themselves.
199174: A sorceress came to a farm to ask how the animals were doing. Nine cows there had given birth to a stillborn calf. The next time the cows had to calve, they died themselves. When two cows had died, the farmer went to the friars, who advised him to make a novena. Shortly afterwards that woman came to visit again. But as soon as she was in the farmyard, she turned back and was never seen again.
199177:
On a farm they had just prepared the food for the pigs when a witch came to ask for alms. After the people had given the alms, they found that the buckets were almost overflowing because the pig feed had started to ferment.
That witch had given a marshmallow or an apple to a little child who lived nearby. After that the child had started crying incessantly. The friars came to read prayers over the child. Nine days later the child was completely cured.
199207: A farm in Oordegem was haunted. A large wagon that had been put in the barn in the evening was found in the loft in the morning.
199209: A boy who lived with his grandmother had gone out one evening. Because the grandmother did not want that, she blocked the door so the boy could not get back in. When he came home, the boy threw his cap against the gate, which made it open so he could get in.
199259: In Affligem lived a farmer whose barn was not big enough to store his harvest. At nightfall the farmer met a gentleman to whom he sold his soul in exchange for a new barn, which would be finished when the cock had crowed three times in the morning. Because the farmer was afraid, he told his wife at night what he had done. The wife got up in the night and clapped her hands, so that the cock began to crow early. The devils had to leave, cursing. There was still a hole in the wall of the barn. That barn was called 'the Devil's Barn'.
199260: An unmarried woman whose mother was a midwife without a diploma had had a baby. While the child lay playing in its cradle, two unknown women came peddling alarm clocks. One of the peddlers went to look at the baby and stroked its head. The young mother had no experience with such things and allowed it. After the peddlers had left, she told her own mother, who had been in the stable, what had happened. The mother responded: "What have you done!? You will bear the consequences." The child got 'the old man' (an illness) and for a long time cried incessantly with clenched little fists. Later the child was cured after all and grew up into a strong man.
199263: A man from Wallonia never wanted to go to mass. When the man's mother lay dying, the woman begged her son to go to mass just once. Shortly afterwards the woman died and the man did not keep his promise. In the corner of his bedroom the man saw a ball of fire appear on three consecutive nights, with eleven small lights around it. That was the mother with her eleven children. Because the ball grew bigger every night, the man sought advice from the parish priest. The clergyman asked the man whether he had ever made a promise, and the man admitted that he still had to go to mass. In the end the man did go to mass after all.
199295: A mother who had given away a bundle of straw for free met with misfortune. The next day one of her children was dead and the cradle was full of lice. The White Fathers of Dendermonde came to the house and said: "You must not give anything away for free. You must make people pay. You must not take the money yourself, but have it put down somewhere".
199318: If an Easter nail had been stuck under the porch door, witches could not leave the church.
199322: At the castle of Goeferdinge there were many problems. The animals did not grow and died. The people suspected a certain woman of having bewitched their animals.
199348: A man who had sold his soul to the devil worked on a farm. Because he often went to the pub, he quite often fell asleep in the field. When he woke up, he stuck his dung fork into a heap of manure and said: "I mine and each his own." A little later the whole field was manured.
199373: A hunter sometimes saw a hare that he could not hit with his gun.
199437: In the Collenhoek in Ophasselt there were stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) everywhere. These little lights appeared above the marshes where it was damp. They could not be reached. People said they were spirits.
199464: On a farm in Voorde, while churning, they found the butter churn full of chestnuts. The people went to the friars. When they churned again afterwards, the churn was full of pins. A woman regularly came to that farm to ask for something. The farmer's wife had always given what was asked for free. But if you made the woman pay for it, she could not bewitch you.
199476: A young man who claimed to be pursued by the ghost of a dead person sought advice from the fathers of Affligem.
199535: There was always a dog around a house that people could not get rid of. The priest had told the people: "If you shoot at that dog, you must load your gun with blessed bullets." When the people had done so, the dog flew off howling through the loft.
199536: A man who had dug over the bell-pit field found a handle from a church there. The people from the museum of Sint-Niklaas took the object away. It was said to have belonged to the church that had supposedly sunk at that spot. It was told that the bells of that church could be heard ringing every hundred years.
199564: People who were out a lot often fell victim to 'loeties' (werewolves) that leapt upon them. A woman who liked a drink and was out day and night also often had trouble with the 'loetie'. One day someone advised the woman to throw a bobbin of yarn at the beast. When the woman met a 'loetie' again, she threw blue yarn at the beast. That freed the woman from the beast and she could go home. The next day, however, the woman was visited by a man who had blue teeth. When the woman asked: "How come you have such blue teeth?" the man turned bright red. By the churchyard stood old tree stumps where people often went to fetch heath soil to fill their flowerpots. At that spot people found the bearskin of the 'loetie'.
199571: A farm in Sint-Maria-Latem was haunted. Some people saw cats there. Others could not get past it.
199604: A man had caught a rabbit in Appelterre and locked it in his clock case. The next day, to his great horror, the man found that the rabbit had turned into a skull. The priest advised the man to take the rabbit back to the place where he had got it. The man meekly followed that advice, for otherwise he would surely have met with an accident.
199628: A girl from Lede went for a walk with her sweetheart. At a certain moment the boy said he had to go into the woods for a moment. A little later the girl saw a werewolf come out of the woods, which sank its teeth into her clothes. The girl began to shout, whereupon the werewolf ran away. When the sweetheart reappeared, the girl asked why he had not come when she shouted. The boy answered that he had heard nothing, but as he said it, the girl saw that he had the fibres of her dress between his teeth.
199650: Rats can be sent by witchcraft to do people harm.
199692: When going to sleep, you had to place your clogs crossed under the foot end of the bed. People who were ridden by the mare felt as if their throat was being squeezed shut. In reality they probably had a stoppage of the blood. You could see the mare coming. It looked as if a goat or a sheep with horns was crawling onto the bed.
199707: A child was born in a café. The child was a real devil. It walked around on four legs. The child was killed.
199747: A sorceress from near Deftingen had leaned over the cradle of twins. An hour later one of the children died. The next day the other child died too.
199757: A sick girl kept crying out that her throat was being squeezed shut. Because the girl's brother believed his sister had been bewitched, he consulted the parish priest. But the clergyman said: "Boy, you mustn't be so superstitious!" The priest came to take a look anyway. He sprinkled the girl with holy water and read prayers over her. After that the priest had to admit that the girl had indeed been bewitched. The brother said he would go to the friars the next day, but the priest replied: "I must go myself, for it has gone too far already." So the priest himself went to the friars for the girl. Nine friars had to pray for the sick girl for nine days. The priests of Aspelare and of Sint-Antelinckx had to come and bless her in turns. For good has more power than evil.
199765: Some men in clogs returning from Steenhuize met a strange apparition on the way, so that they took another road and got lost.
199794: On the Vijfweg people saw a black hen or a black cat at night. That was witchcraft.
199818: A man from Bevegem returning from the station got lost. He wandered around for two or three hours only to find that he was standing in the churchyard of Zottegem. That man had been ridden by the 'mane' (mare). It was also said of the mane that she pounced on people at night, so that they felt they could no longer breathe.
199820:
A drunkard who had no money left stood cursing on the Hoogveld and shouted: "I would rather serve the devil than these stupid farmers here!" The next moment a gentleman appeared who said: "Will you serve me?" The drunkard answered "yes" and got as much money as he wanted. After that he could pull a cart full of corn with one finger. When he had to manure the field, he said: "I do mine and each his own." A little later the work was done. When the women asked the man: "When may we see your farmhands?", he answered: "You'll see them some time." In the evening each farmhand went off with a woman.
The priest grew tired of it and dragged the man to the church, where he freed him from the devil.
199844: One evening in an inn, people were saying that God, the devils and the angels did not exist. When the people came home at midnight, they saw a group of little men around them. They asked the little men where they came from, but there was no answer. When the men walked fast, the little men walked fast too. If they slowed down, the little men did the same. After that incident a chapel was built on that spot.
199846: In Oudenhove lived a man whose wife had died. Because the man had small children to care for, he decided to remarry. But his second wife was always troubled at night by a ghost. The woman was woken by the rattling of plates, cups and chairs. One night the ghost even began pinching the woman's toes. Because the haunting would not stop, the couple finally moved.
199909: A cattle dealer from Lamont met a beautiful white lady on his way home and said: "You are a pretty girl, aren't you." The lady nodded but said nothing. Then the man said: "Shouldn't you go to sleep?", at which the lady again nodded silently. When the man noticed that the lady kept following him, he grew frightened and promised to build a little chapel for Our Lady. The man went into his house, but the lady had to stay outside, since she could not get across the threshold.
199930: In a house in Ronse people always saw a rat running around before going to bed. They did not manage to catch the animal. One day they did manage to hit the animal on the head. An old woman who regularly visited there was wearing a bandage around her head.
199955: One evening dozens of rats almost as big as rabbits were sitting in a café. Because nobody managed to beat the rats to death, the café owner fetched his gun. Before he fired, he put the bullet in his mouth to bless it. He hit one rat, but at that same moment all the rats vanished. The next day he heard that a woman from the neighbourhood had lost an eye.
199981: A woman from Merksem could not get into a certain house through the front door because a holy object had been placed under the threshold. So the woman went in through the back door. The residents of that house had been advised to throw away and burn their cradle and to break off the top three steps of the attic stairs. But the people did not follow that advice. The next morning one of their pigs lay dead.
200002: On a farm in Schorisse a hellish noise was heard every night. They could no longer churn butter there either. After six weeks the farmer sent for a friar from Gent. The clergyman came and made a great many signs of the cross, all in the reverse direction, while the drops of sweat rolled down his face. Then the friar poured a bucket of dung into the butter churn and said: "Now the butter will be good. Try it now." After the friar's intervention, the farm had excellent butter again.
200029: A man coming back from work saw a black cat in a tree-lined lane. He picked up the animal and took it home. The next morning the man heard a noise. Behind the stove sat a woman, who said: "Take me back to the place where you got me".
200036: In a house in Ophasselt a child died about an hour after a witch had visited. The child had fallen ill after getting a sweet from the witch.
200060: A man who had gone to be fitted for a tailored suit had to go home past the Vogelenzang in Denderwindeke. At that place, which was bewitched, the grain suddenly went down. Then a hare jumped in front of the man's feet. The animal would not be chased away and the man was very frightened.
200061: At a farm in Wannegem-Lede the friars had to come several times because it was haunted. In the middle of the night everything there was thrown about and the butter churn could be heard turning. The friars banished the evil to the cellar and had that room bricked up.
200087: Some men who had seen a cat in the churchyard went closer. A little later there were many more cats sitting there.
200088: On a haunted farm, medals had been placed under all the entrance gates. Despite this measure the haunting did not stop. It took a long time before the occupants discovered that there was a large cellar under the farm. They asked the owner whether they could open the cellar, but they were not given permission. After the occupants had been to the friars for the second time and had fulfilled their vow (?), the haunting came to an end.
200095: When someone in Erpe was possessed by evil, they were taken to the fathers of Affligem. Once, when a father was spending the night in a house in Erpe, the clergyman woke up during the night and saw the devil standing there in the shape of a gentleman wearing a black suit with a white collar. Because everything was locked, the father asked the devil how he had got in. The devil replied: I need no keys or bolts. You may perform that exorcism, but it will not work, because there is a whole army of devils in him. Then the devil vanished. The exorcism indeed failed.
200143: A woman always saw her dead husband appear in the grandfather clock at midnight. The woman was afraid because she did not know why her husband was appearing.
200187: In Ouwegem a man had died who still had a large debt to settle. After his death the man was always seen leaning over the stable door. Only when the debt was settled did the dead man stop appearing.
200192: The Sponde was badly haunted. A man saw a cat come out of the woods there and spoke to the animal. Then the man went on. He met a spotted cow. When he tried to catch the animal, it jumped into a stable and vanished. A witch lived in a nearby farmstead.
200193: Two women who wore a medal were visited by a pedlar selling spectacles. He was probably a seminarian who had left the seminary early, because a small tonsure was shaved on his head. The pedlar looked both women in the eye and said they needed glasses. When the women refused to buy glasses from the man, he turned around and left. After that the women could not move until evening came. If they had not worn their medal, they would have been bewitched.
200202: Five maids and two farmhands worked on a farm in Sint-Lievens-Esse. At the time when the grain stood high, the maids were attacked every evening on their way home by kledde (a werewolf-like goblin that leaps onto people's backs), which made them carry it. When the maids told the farmer's wife, she suspected one of the farmhands. That farmhand came in every evening after the prayer to eat quickly and then leave again before the second prayer had been said. One day the farmer's wife told her maids: "I have heard that you must throw a cloth over kledde's head, because then he can do nothing until he has unravelled that cloth completely." The farmer's wife gave the maids a silk cloth with a very fine weave. When the farmhand turned up for work the next morning, he looked sleepy and had the threads of the cloth between his teeth. As soon as the farmer's wife saw this, she paid the farmhand off and sent him away.
200208: A farmer who had found out that his farmhand had made a pact with the devil sent the boy away on an errand. While the farmhand was away, the farmer took the boy's skin and set it on fire. The farmhand came running to save his skin, but he came too late. When the skin had burnt up, the boy said: "I am glad to be freed of it."
200247: On a bewitched farm the hens sang the Brabançonne and the cocks the Marseillaise. Sometimes they also sang the English song. When the people let the hens out, the animals all had little curtains on their combs.
200250: A woman had come to visit a house and had laid her hands on a little child's head. After that the child fell ill and died.
200300: A man who lived on the Kamdries went to work in France as a seasonal labourer. One day he was approached there by an old woman who said that she used to come to the witches' sabbath on the Kamdries often.
200301: At a certain place in Zingem a candle was always seen. Because people believed that a treasure might be hidden there, they began to dig at that spot. In the pit they found a black dog. The treasure had been changed into a dog to punish the people for their curiosity.
200302: Some people claimed that they always saw a strange apparition at the crucifix on the corner of the Heuvelstraat. After the people had received something from the friars of Edingen, they no longer saw the apparition.
200334: At night people had to lie in their bed with their arms crossed. Otherwise they would be ridden by the mare.
200363: A young soldier asked his father whether he would buy him out of the army. The father refused and reminded his son of his duty. When the father had died, the son did not want to give him a proper funeral. On the third day after his death the father came haunting in a white sheet. The boy hurried to the presbytery, where the priest told him: "You must have masses said every day. That is the ghost that comes and stands by the bed".
200403:
A police commissioner coming home from the Zandvloog got lost. Three times the man ended up at the same spot. The man knocked on a door somewhere and asked a farmhand to accompany him with a lantern.
On the way the man had spoken with a stranger and patted that person on the shoulders. That was why he had got lost. Anyone who had been ridden by the mare had to rest a while or talk to another person.
200413: A man who could curse like a heathen met a big black dog one day. From that day on the man no longer dared to come home alone.
200449: If you managed to wound a werewolf, you could recognise him the next day by that wound once he had taken on his human form again.
200455: Werewolves roamed in the evening and at night with an animal skin and jumped on the backs of passers-by to make them carry them. One day someone found the skin of such a werewolf and threw it into an oven. The werewolf then came running to save his skin from the fire. But it was already too late.
200460: When something went wrong in a household, people often believed it had to do with witchcraft. That was the case, for example, when a child fell ill after a woman had visited.
200475:
A six-year-old girl who was ill had already seen seven doctors, but could not be helped. The girl regularly had fits in which she felt as if needles were piercing her whole body. The child also refused to eat and grew very thin. One of the doctors sent the people to the friars in Gent. The parents left the girl with her uncle and aunt and set off for Gent. When the parents arrived in Gent at ten o'clock, the girl began to cry and a big black spider was seen running from her toes up to her head. The spider could not be caught. The friars said the girl would only be cured after two novenas. The parents were also given a cake to take with them, and they were not to accept anything from anyone.
In the afternoons a woman often came to the parents' house for coffee. At one point the mother had to go outside for five minutes to feed the cows. When she came back in, she saw her daughter looking at a big book she had been given by the visitor. The mother quickly threw the book into the stove. After that the woman never visited again.
On the eighteenth day the girl got up in the middle of the night and asked for a slice of bread. After that the child was never ill again.
200502: On a farm in Volkegem they could not churn butter. The people went to the friars of Gent, who said: "Hurry home and pour horse dung into your butter churn. The person who bewitched you will get the dung and you will have the butter." The people followed the friars' advice. When some time later they were visiting someone, that person said: "Oh dear, I've churned and I have nothing but dung in my butter churn!"
200503: A soldier stationed in Hofstade sometimes went to the inn. When he was asked there one day where he came from, an old woman said: "Is that old oak still standing in Hofstade? We often had fun there during night-time gatherings. But I have been freed from it."
200523: A brewer could no longer make good beer. He also noticed that his wife was gone every night. Then cats would dance around the little trees. The brewer sent for the friars, since witches could harm their own relatives. Since the existence of the Gospel of Saint John, however, such practices have almost disappeared.
200525: An underground passage ran between the old and the new castle of Petegem. In that passage a chest was once found, locked with heavy chains, with a dog sitting on it. Someone who had been cursed was said to have been inside that chest.
200532: A family had eight sons, seven of whom were shepherds. One day the shepherds had gone with their sheep to a clover field where they were not really allowed. When the farmer came running with a dung fork in his hand, one of the shepherds made an upside-down sign of the cross. The next moment all the sheep had turned into molehills, so the farmer could no longer reproach the shepherds for anything.
200556: A man who was ridden by the mare at night first began to shiver with cold. A little later he broke out in a sweat. After someone had put a piece of the Easter candle under the stairs, the man was no longer ridden by the mare.
200584: A woman had sworn that she would never forgive her husband for all the torment he had made her suffer. But when the man had been dead for some time, the woman was forced to forgive him after all. For the haunting husband turned everything in the house upside down day and night.
200587: Two people coming back from Eine had a terrifying experience at the Kasteeltje. They were both lifted up and slammed against the trees. Only after that could they go on.
200604: To avoid being ridden by the mare, one had to put one's clogs upside down next to the bed and pray the Gospel of Saint John.
200627: A freemason could not die because a large black dog sat in the room all the time. After the priest had prayed for a long while, the dog finally ran away. It was the devil.
200654: In a house where four children had already died, a priest predicted that a witch would come to ask for a colander. After the people had stuck an Easter nail under their door, the witch could no longer come in. Many people also bricked an Agnus Dei under their threshold to protect themselves against evil.
200679: A man and a woman went to the doctor because their child was ill. The doctor could not help, so the parents went to a healer. The healer said: "Your child is bewitched. Tonight at twelve o'clock you must go outside. You will see a black dog running. The first woman who asks you how your child is doing is the witch." Everything happened as the healer had foretold. The witch went to prison for what she had done.
200680: A family had a little daughter who cried all night long. The people believed their daughter's behaviour had to do with the evil hand and took the child to the fathers of Affligem.
200694: In Nazareth there lived a wizard who consorted with the devil. One day the wizard said to his farmhand: "Today at eleven o'clock there is a reception by the king of Mexico. I am going there and you must come with me." The farmhand replied: "You can never get there in time, it is already ten o'clock." The wizard snapped his fingers and the next moment the two were standing in Mexico. The farmhand, however, had grown two horns, so the two were noticed. Just as they were about to be arrested by the police, the wizard snapped his fingers again, after which the two were back home. Wizards could also fly through keyholes. Every time they flew past a church, they got a jolt.
200710: An inn in Lede was always frequented by people who feared neither God nor commandment and did not go to mass. One Sunday, during mass, a big dog appeared in the inn with a streak of fire on each paw. Everyone in the inn was suddenly very frightened. The dog then left again. All the people in the inn got up at once and many of them went straight to mass. People believed that dog was the devil.
200712: A man going on a pilgrimage was approached on the way by a sorceress who asked him where he came from. When the man answered that he came from Haaltert, the sorceress replied: "Oh, I have sat in the thick linden tree there!"
200739: A house where an aunt had died was haunted. Sometimes the bowl of milk above the stove had been emptied, or someone had been in the house, although no one had been seen. One day the people went to the friars of Edingen. In return for their inheritance the people should have had a number of masses said for their aunt, but they had not done so. After the masses were said, everything in the house went back to normal.
200741: A young mother whose newborn baby lay in the cradle suddenly saw her dead mother standing beside the cradle. Frightened, the woman asked: "But mother, have I wronged you?" The dead woman did not answer and went away. When the woman went to confession, the priest advised her to pray an Our Father if the dead woman appeared again.
200791: A man who was afraid of nothing was accompanied every day on his way home from work by a black cat. When he got home the man saw the cat sitting in front of his door or on the cobblestones. In the end the man died of fright.
200795: A gamekeeper whose wife had died slept at night on the haystack. Every night the man woke up and saw a woman walking among the sugar beets. One night the gamekeeper asked: "What are you doing here?", and his wife's ghost answered: "It is your fault that I missed mass so many times". After that the gamekeeper went to mass in her place just as many times. Since then he has not seen his wife's ghost again.
200808: On a farm, a farmer found the skin of a kledde (a werewolf-like creature) in his haystack. The farmer called some neighbours to discuss what to do with the skin. One of the neighbours was about to bake bread and said: "Throw the skin in my oven when it is burning." They did so, but as soon as the skin touched the fire, the farmhand was standing by the oven to save his skin. Several men had to hold the farmhand back. When the skin had burnt up, he was grateful because he had been released.
200889: A mother took her child to someone so that she could go out for a while. When she returned, the mother could no longer see her child. It took four days before the mother had her child back. She had gone to the fathers of Gent for that. After that, the mother never again dared to leave any of her children alone.
200890: On a farm four horses had died. The people also could no longer make good butter, because the butter went bad after just one day. The farmer had once already sent for a father from Gent. The sexton had stolen a nail from the Easter candle to stick under the farm's door. During mass the parish priest preached that the person who had stolen the Easter nail had to bring it back. The sexton did so. The priest came to the farm and said: "While I am here in the stable, a woman will come, but you must not harm her. After today she will never come here again." The priest sent everyone away so that he could stay alone in the stable for a while. When he left, the clergyman was drenched in sweat. Some time later a woman who made socks for the people came to visit the farm.
200904: Stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) were returning spirits, people said. You were not allowed to point at such lights, or else you would get a box on the ear.
200944: In a house in Etikhove a toad was always seen coming in during a party. The people kicked the animal because they could not catch it. The next day the people found one of their neighbours in their bread oven.
200956: 'Berewulven' (werewolves) were people who got a bearskin from the devil, in which they had to go about in the evening and at night jumping on people. The werewolves were paid for this. In Wannegem-Lede some young lads had hidden behind the door of the cowshed. When one of their friends, in the shape of a werewolf, leaned over the half-door of the shed, they quickly slammed the top half shut, trapping the werewolf's claws. The werewolf begged to be let go. One day, when the cowherd had to light the oven, he found a skin in the woodpile and threw it into the oven along with the wood. The skin had barely caught fire when the werewolf came running up, shouting. But it was too late, for the skin had already burned. The werewolf was afterwards punished by the devil.
200966: A man coming back from the café through the woods suddenly saw a rabbit, twice as big as an ordinary rabbit, jump in front of his feet. The man followed the animal to catch it and got lost. After walking around for a few hours, the man came back to the café. He asked for the landlady, but she was not there. A quarter of an hour later the man saw the landlady come in, completely exhausted and drenched in sweat. At that moment the man immediately realised who had made him lose his way.
201004: A man could conjure a café full of mice by reading from a little book. When the man clapped his hands, the mice were gone again.
201014: On a farm in Schorisse they could no longer churn butter. Instead of butter they found dung in the butter churn. The farmer went to the fathers, who advised him to pray for nine days. After that the farm had excellent butter again.
201067: A farmer's wife had given meat to a certain woman. After that the farm had much misfortune. The cows were due to calve, but half a year later it still had not happened. In the stable there were rats as big as cats. Of the twelve children they had there, only three survived. After the farmer's wife had received an Agnus Dei from the curate, the misfortune came to an end.
201097: In the Vlasakstraat in Sombeek stood a large house that was haunted. The man who had lived there told the new tenants: "I don't know whether you will be able to get used to it here. At night the windows and doors are flung open. Sometimes shouting can be heard in the house too". Because the new tenants could not sleep at night, they were advised to go on pilgrimage to the friars of Dendermonde. The friars gave the farmer medals to place at every entrance gate.
201100: A boy going to Sint-Martens-Lierde met a cat on the way. When the boy picked the animal up, he was suddenly surrounded by many cats. That one cat kept following him as far as the convent. Afterwards the boy was ill with fright for three weeks.
201125: A family had a newborn baby that had fallen ill. The people went to the fathers of Gent, who made the baby recover. However, the child was bewitched a second time by the same woman. After the sorceress had come to ask for a piece of lace and had received it from the child's mother, the child did nothing but cry all night. Nine days later the child died.
201170: In church you could recognise witches, because the priest passed them by without giving them a host. After mass the priest said to three women who stayed seated in the church: "If you don't go outside now, everyone will find it suspicious and you will never get out again." The women stayed seated, however. When they came outside after the priest had said something to them, a man said to them: "Look, here come the witches!" One of the women replied: "You have seen us now, but you will never see us again." The next moment the man was stone blind.
201173: A mother was always visited by a sorceress who came to look at her child. The mother had many problems with her child and had to go on pilgrimage to the fathers of Edingen. A father came to read prayers over the child, but that did not help. The fathers of Gent could not help either. In the end the little child died.
201189: A man coming home around midnight from visiting his friends saw a large white figure standing against the church wall by the presbytery of Woubrechtegem. It was a woman wearing only a white shift, with her hair hanging over her eyes. The man had always heard that spirits of the dead could come back to the churchyard at night.
201203: A man from Onkerzele returning from Geraardsbergen met a woman in a white cap on the way. The man said "Good evening", but the woman did not answer. So the man said: "Ah, you must be a witch" and went on. After that the man could not get home and had to wander about all evening. He had been 'led by the alf' (led astray by an elf). The man only reached his house at three in the morning.
201204: A farmer's wife whose husband had died in an accident moved because her house was haunted. But when the woman had lived a year in her new home, the haunting began there too. The windows were smashed although no one could be seen.
201208: When people heard a magpie chattering, they believed misfortune was coming. A man who had seen a magpie flying had bad luck shortly afterwards: his roosters did not win.
201234: A woman who had been touched by someone grew very thin and lost her appetite. At night the woman sweated and felt as if something was lying on her. Her aunt advised her to go to the friars. There the woman was given bread rolls. She also had to make a novena. In the end she was cured and she was never ill again.
201255: A man who worked for a farmer had to manure the field. When the farmer came to bring the farmhand his food, he saw that nothing had been done yet. "It'll be fine, master," said the farmhand, and he stuck his dung fork into a heap of manure with the words: "I mine and each his own." A little later the whole field was manured. That man was a devil in human form.
201258: A six-week-old child would no longer eat or drink and wasted away completely. Because the doctor could not help the child and people suspected witchcraft was involved, three of them went on pilgrimage to the fathers of Affligem. The fathers gave them an Easter nail, which they had to put under the chair where the witch always sat. The people did as they were advised. The next time the witch came to visit, she walked to her chair, then turned around and left. The people then stuck the Easter nail under their threshold and the witch never visited them again. The child gradually recovered.
201283: On a farm music was heard in the stable all night. When the door was opened, nothing more could be heard, but the animals stood huddled fearfully in a corner.
201303: In Grotenberge there was a stone in which the devil is said to have left his paw print. That place was called 't Duivels Voetstap.
201326: A man from Erpe who went hunting suddenly saw a very large hare, followed by a pack of little hares. The man shot at the animals but could not hit a single hare. Then the man put the shot in his mouth for a moment, so that it was blessed. When he shot again after that, he was able to hit one hare. The next morning it was found that a woman from the neighbourhood had lost an eye.
201334: A curate had to bring the Last Sacraments to a sick person in the Siesmestake district. Suddenly the priest was jumped by a large werewolf with red-glowing eyes, dragging a chain behind it. After the curate made the sign of the cross, the werewolf was gone.
201354: At the Wispelaer a man saw an ugly dog coming towards him. The man could not chase the dog away and was followed by the animal. The dog kept trying to jump on him. The next day the man experienced the same thing again.
201380:
During mass in the church of Mater sat a woman who could work witchcraft. That woman shouted the whole time in church. In the end the priest delivered her.
A bewitched boy always began to shout and rage when he had been lying in bed for ten minutes or a quarter of an hour. The boy's mother informed priest X, who came one afternoon and read from a book. The priest said to the people: "You will never experience it again in your lives, but that woman must stay out of your house."
201414: On the Braamsriet little lights could be seen dancing in the evening and at night. People said those lights were shrews and ghosts.
201442: To avoid being ridden by the mare, one had to put one's clogs upside down next to the bed.
201465: A farmer's wife from Erpe was ridden by the mare every evening once she had been in bed for a quarter of an hour.
201492: In Ronse there was a café where all the customers got lice.
201516: Werewolves did not attack people, but made passers-by carry them.
201540: A mother was always visited by a woman with a bad reputation. The mother always gave that woman half a franc. When the mother had problems with her little daughter, she went to the fathers, who said: "If that woman comes again, you must not put the money in her hand. You must put it on the table and she must take it herself." When the sorceress came by again, she left the money lying there. The little girl recovered.
201544: When the parish priest had forgotten to close his missal after mass, four women remained sitting in the church. Those women had to go and ask the priest to close his book, because otherwise they could not get out.
201567: A family had a child who could not sleep. Every evening the child saw a man come in and rock the cradle back and forth. The other people could also see the cradle moving. It was the ghost of a soldier who had died in a bombardment that was said to have once taken place there.
201591: A devil's barn was a barn that had been built by the devils and was not quite finished. The hole in the barn could not be closed, because the stones always fell out.
201611: A woman who set off on foot for Gent at night met a hare, which came and scratched at her feet. That was witchcraft.
201709: When people heard a magpie chattering, they believed bad news would come within three days.
201734: In a house where there was always a spider, they had trouble with the animals. One day they burned off the spider's legs. The next morning a neighbour had burned feet. That woman could change herself into a spider. She also often brought the kwade hand (the evil hand, a witch's curse) into houses with a baby, making the baby ill.
201762: A sorcerer could make masses of rats come to a particular place.
201788: A man from Impe went on a pilgrimage to Lembeek. In the evening he knocked at a farm and asked whether he could spend the night there. The farmer claimed he had no room and sent the man to a nearby café that had beds. When the landlady asked the man where he came from, she said: "I have often been in Impe at night. We came there with a whole group to play. Does Drieskese put still exist? And is that oak three metres wide still standing there? We had a lot of fun by the tree stumps there." When the woman saw that the man and his father were becoming frightened, she said: "You need not be afraid, because now I have been freed from everything and I am glad of it."
201824: A woman who had a relationship with a man from Ronse and who did not go to mass had special powers. When a baby was born in Ronse, the woman went to visit and said: "What a beautiful baby!" Some time later the woman brought a little cap for the child. After that the child got convulsions and died. When the poor mother later stuck an Easter nail under her threshold, the sorceress never came in again. It was very hard to get hold of an Easter nail, because the priests kept such things for their best friends.
201851: A farm in Oordegem was very badly haunted. One morning a wagon stood in the stable there, although it normally could not fit through the door. Another day that wagon stood in the loft.
201856: In Stekene there used to be a little chapel of Saint Joseph. From the day that chapel was demolished, the spot was haunted. Later a house was built there, but nobody lived in it for longer than a year. At midnight strange things happened there. Sometimes a black cat walked over the red-hot stove. Eventually the house was occupied by a man who was not afraid of the devil or hell. After that man's death the building stood empty again for a long time.
201885: Some people found that their barn was not big enough to store all their grain. They met a gentleman who said: "If you do what I say, there will be a barn standing before the first cockcrow." And so it happened. That barn was called 'the Blue Barn'.
201909: A farm in Smeerhebbe-Vloerzegem was haunted. The people had made a promise but had not fulfilled it. At night they always heard noise in the attic. After the promise had been fulfilled for the dead person, the strange noises were no longer heard.
201967: Some people from Uivelde coming back from work in the evening suddenly saw a big black cat on their way and felt a horse's head on their shoulder. A little later that horse had disappeared again.
201971: Sorceresses could not die before they had passed their magic power on to someone else.
201988: A boy was courting a girl whom his friends said was a witch. One evening the boy pretended to have fallen asleep in his girlfriend's house. Around midnight his girlfriend rubbed her hands with an ointment and said: "Yes, he's asleep anyway, I'll fly to Spain over hedge and gates." Then the girl had vanished. The boy rubbed his hands with the same ointment and said: "Through hedge and through gates." He was scratched all over when he arrived in Spain. There his girlfriend told him: "Two pigs will come to take us back to Iddergem. But you must not say a word on the way." When the pig flew over a large pool of water, the boy said: "Now that's quite a jump for a pig!" The next moment the boy fell into the water, and his girlfriend arrived in Iddergem alone.
201990: In Sint-Gillis lived a farmhand who was possessed by the devil and who owned a skin. When someone once threw the farmhand's skin into the fire, the next moment he was already standing by the oven to save his skin.
202002: A farmer took his horse to a stallion in Steenhuize. At a certain spot, however, the horse would go no further. The horse fell ill, began to sweat and dropped dead on the spot. Two years later the same farmer came to that spot again with a horse. That horse could not go on there either and died. Less than a hundred metres from that spot lived a woman with a bad reputation.
202080: In Leeuwergem people did not dare go to a certain spot by a brook because there lay a stone said to bear a footprint of the devil.
202081: A man who was ridden by the mare felt as if he would suffocate and could not move. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to pray the Gospel of Saint John in the evening before going to sleep.
202127: People who came home at three in the morning at full moon were ridden by the mare. In reality they were people who had stayed too long in the café and fell asleep in a ditch on the way.
202145: A machine did not work when it was driven towards the farm. When it was driven in the other direction, the machine strangely enough did work.
202163: During the Second World War cows were stolen from a farm. Without knowing who the culprit was, the owner of the cows walked to the thief's house and heard her cow mooing there. That was witchcraft.
202240: If you met a black cat in the evening, you were bewitched and suddenly saw cats everywhere around you.
202271: In Kieldrecht lived an old woman who was said to be a witch. When the children made little crosses in that witch's footprint, she turned around.
202308: Werewolves were spirits who pulled a skin over themselves. They stopped passers-by and made them carry them.
202338: In Sint-Denijs-Boekel lived a woman who was said to be a sorceress. That woman was always dirty. She said prayers and went on pilgrimage for the boys who had to draw lots for the army. She could also make sure the boys did not have to go into the army.
202358: A werewolf attacked people at night and made them carry it. To make a werewolf powerless, you had to give it a piece of cloth. It then had to unravel it completely.
202363: In a café in Steendorp three friends were playing cards with a stranger. The stranger always won. When one of the friends bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the stranger had a deformed foot that looked like a horse's hoof. The man turned deathly pale when he realised the stranger was the devil.
202370: In the old days people were told stories about the werewolf that would jump on them.
202401: A man bringing his cows home had to pass a house where a sorceress lived. At that house the man saw the woman come out and put her hand on the cow's rump. When the man got home, he saw the cow raise her tail and prepare to calve, although she was only four or five months pregnant. The man took his dung fork, went to the sorceress and forced her to undo the harm she had done. The sorceress came to the stable and made the cow calm again.
202402: In Mullem people were out with a horse and cart. By the side of the road they suddenly saw something, which made the horse get knocked over every time.
