202423: In Zottegem a woman used to come peddling pepper, mustard and laces. Many houses no longer let her in because people always fell ill after her visit.
202450: People had to make a new robe for the statue of a saint venerated against toothache. They had mocked it. The next day they all had toothache.
202484: In the old days it sometimes happened that people could not churn butter because of the evil hand.
202485: A man coming back late from the fair met a dog on the way that was several metres tall. The dog walked along with the man for a while and at a certain moment vanished without a trace.
202515: In a house the daughters saw a large beast walking around their bedroom. They also kept hearing knocking on the door. One of the daughters, a seamstress, was always thrown up in the air in her bed. In the end the fathers were sent for. The fathers went around the house reading prayers over it, while drops of sweat rolled down their faces. The daughter who was a seamstress had fabric for a dress she had to make for an old woman. A father found that fabric and said to the girl: "You must take that fabric back to the woman the dress is for." After the girl had done so, everything in the house returned to normal.
202567: The 'eendenkot' (duck shed) in Oudegem was haunted. People were heard singing and dancing there, so that nobody dared walk past at night.
202590: People with a sick child sought advice from the fathers of Affligem. They often blamed a woman who came to visit them.
202594: A family that had built a new house had nothing but misfortune. The people were struck by illness and the deaths of children. One day a woman said: "Open the roller shutter box." When the people did, children's clothes came tumbling out. During the building work someone with an evil hand had put the little clothes in there.
202617: Witches could not leave the church if the missal had been left open. When an altar boy in Nokere once forgot to close the missal, the parish priest had to be asked to close the book, because otherwise the witch could not get out.
202626: A woman always fetched milk from a farmer who had a small child. The woman often stroked the child. But because the child cried day and night, the farmer and his wife went to the friars, who gave them an Easter nail to put under the visitor's chair. Then they were to light the fire. No sooner said than done. Despite the heat the witch could not get up from her chair until the Easter nail had been taken away. Then the witch pulled lots of little pins out of the child. The child died all the same.
202647: Witches sometimes made little dolls in the shape of a particular person. They could then torment that person by sticking pins into the doll. Witches could give children a poison that gave them convulsions. Witches could bewitch someone with their mind. Sometimes a witch threw a bewitched apple into a liquid-manure pit. When that manure was used to fertilise the field and a cow was later put on that field, the animal dropped dead. By scattering poison, witches sometimes caused chickens or cows to die.
202648: A man who worked for a farmer in France was approached one day by the farmer's wife, who asked whether he knew where the Dikke Linde of Aaigem stood. When the man said yes, she went on: "I was there often and we had a lot of fun there. But I have been freed from it."
202668: Long ago a beggar from Woubrechtegem was murdered by the linden tree between Sint-Antelinks and Nederhasselt. Since then evil spirits dwelt at that spot, so that people no longer dared to pass by it.
202727: A man had sold his soul to the devil in exchange for a new house. The house had to be built in one night and had to be finished before the cock crowed in the morning. The man's wife went to the henhouse at night and clapped her hands, so that the cock began to crow early. At that moment one more stone still had to be laid. The man was saved, because his house was not yet finished.
202734: One evening a man was out with the parish priest in the marshes around the castle. A big black dog lay there, looking at the two men with a strange gaze. When the priest asked the dog what was the matter, the animal began to speak. But the priest never told anyone what problem the animal had.
202738: Sorceresses got money from the devil when they harmed people. When a child was bewitched, people sometimes said it had 'the old man'. Others called it 'the poor man'.
202754: A woman who had to be at work early left far too early. At one o'clock at night she met a werewolf. She threw a 'sleutel' (key?) at the beast, so that she had the chance to run away. The next day the woman heard it said that someone had seen her boyfriend with a piece of wool between his teeth.
202761: Some men were sitting in the Kriekeleer on the occasion of 'potje dek'. A man who had already had a few drinks said to a wizard: "Go ahead and bewitch me." When the men went home that evening, they all got lost. Only at dawn could they find their way again. They had been 'led by the alf' (led astray by an elf).
202783: Sometimes people felt a weight pressing down on them in their sleep. They wanted to call out, but could not. When someone sprinkled them with holy water, they were freed. These people had been victims of Osschaart. The victims were usually men. Some also claimed that such events were really due to the blood standing still.
202786: When a little child had died somewhere, stalkaarsen (will-o'-the-wisps) could be seen in the evening.
202844: At the Muizekapelletje the sorceresses held meetings at night. After such a meeting a certain sorceress could bewitch the stables on a farm. If she wanted, the cows' heads were all twisted round and their tails were braided.
202873: On his way home a man suddenly saw a dog with a plumed tail standing in front of him. The man was so frightened that he went back home. When the man was halfway, he saw the dog standing in front of him again. He heard the church bell strike midnight.
202879: A woman rented a piece of land from a farmer to plant potatoes. When one day the woman was told she could no longer use that land, she said to the farmer: "You'll regret that!" The next day one of the farmer's cows lay sick in the stable. Because people believed the woman had caused this harm, the farmer went back to her and said she could work the land without paying anything. The woman then said: "Go back home. Your cow is healthy again." And so it was.
202907: In Ouwegem there was a small house called 'het galgenhuizeke' (the little gallows house) because it was built where the gallows had once stood. The man who had lived in that house claimed that strange things often happened. Sometimes, for instance, the house was lifted up. The man believed the strange events were caused by the returning ghosts of the people who had been hanged there.
202929: A man was coming back from the market in Geraardsbergen at night. On the way, in Dichtinge, he heard beautiful music. He went into the building it came from and asked if he could have a turn at the organ. As he played, he cried: "Jesus Mary, this organ plays beautifully!" The next moment the whole scene had vanished and the man was turning the tail of a cat.
202932: In a family in Etikhove a girl was ill. The child got sores on her head and would not eat. When the priests came to these people, they said: "It will be all right, but for nine days you must not give anything to anyone." During that time a woman came in to change five centimes. The farmer took his gun and ran after the woman. A moment later the woman had vanished without a trace. No one had any idea which way she could have gone out.
202975: Werewolves disguised themselves with a skin and jumped on passers-by to be carried.
202993: A man who had seen cats in the churchyard did not dare to go on, because he believed the appearance of the cats meant something.
203005: On a farm in Erwetegem worked a farmhand who went about as a kledde (a werewolf-like creature). One day the farmhand was sent on foot to Gent to fetch two hundred and fifty grams of coffee. While he was away, they took his skin out of a tree stump and threw it into the oven. A little later the farmhand was standing by the oven, sweating. He thanked the farmer and moved away. He was never seen again.
203018: A man went via Kruishoutem to Oudenaarde. When he came home later that day, he kicked a cobblestone into the ditch on the way. From that moment the man was not himself any more. When he got home, his relatives also saw that something was wrong with him. Eventually the man went to the friars, who told him that there had probably been something wrong with that cobblestone. The man had to go back to that spot and bury the stone. The man did go to the spot, but he took the stone with him and buried it by his farm. After that the man always had misfortune on his farm.
203039: In a house the noise of horses and chains was always heard, although nothing could be seen. The children's shoes moved and came down the stairs by themselves. In the café the glasses were knocked together without anything breaking. One evening the child cried: "Mother, they're pulling my hair!", but the woman saw nothing. After the people had the friars of Gent exorcise their house, no more strange things happened.
203088: On a farm struck by the evil hand there was much misfortune. One time a horse lay dying, another time an animal broke loose. The people went to the fathers to get an Easter nail. But they did not get one, because there were always too few Easter nails for everyone.
203171:
A man who had sold his soul to the devil had been given a bearskin, with which he had to frighten people. One day someone discovered the place where the man had hidden his skin. If you lost the skin from the devil, you had to ask for a new one, and then had to roam about with it for another nine years.
When the curious person wanted to burn the werewolf's skin, the werewolf came running and, with much pleading, managed to save his skin.
203174: In Melden beautiful music was heard at night. One day someone lost a clog there. When they went to look for the clog, they saw a toad sitting there. When the people got home, they saw a clog stuck between the shutters.
203211: In Ouwegem lived a man who sometimes saw the ghost of his dead mother appear. The priest had advised the man never to give the ghost his hand. When the ghost appeared again, they gave it a towel. The dead mother burned her hand into the towel, since she came from purgatory.
203212:
It used to be said that the witches held meetings at a certain place in Velzeke. People therefore did not dare go to that place.
People also believed that some children or adults had died through the evil hand. In reality many people died because of the poor medical care of that time.
203298: An old woman visited a house where a baby lay in a cradle. The woman leaned over the cradle. A few days later the child lay dying. People advised the mother to put the cradle outside, because otherwise the evil would stay in the house. The mother did so and her baby died.
203301: A man returning from a visit to his friend in Hundelgem got lost and kept ending up at the Trialdus again and again. When the man saw the mill, he could find his bearings. He had been ridden by the mare.
203356: On a farm a little child was ill. Near that farm lived a witch who tormented the child by sticking pins into a wax figure.
203376: People who were ridden by the mare at night could no longer breathe and felt as if their throat was being squeezed shut. It seemed as if a good hundred kilos were resting on their body. If one placed one's shoes crossed in the evening, one could not be ridden by the mare.
203379: In Lede lived a farmer who had much misfortune in his stables. One day the farmer said of his old thatched house: I wish the devils would take my house. Hardly had he spoken when some five thousand crows appeared and began to peck the straw from the roof. The farmer regretted what he had said and hurried to an exorcist. He advised him to pour rapeseed into the hedge, so the crows would have work to do. The farmer followed that advice. All the crows that could not get to the rapeseed had to put the straw back on the roof. As soon as the seed was gone, the straw was back on the roof.
203400: Someone had been given a puppy by a woman who had special powers. When the dog was a few months old, it went mad. It knocked everything over and bit everything. One day the dog ran outside and jumped over the fence. The animal was never seen again.
203404: In Sint-Maria-Horebeke a child had fallen ill after a woman had come to visit. People who had fallen victim to witchcraft sought advice from the fathers of Gent. They had to bring something that belonged to the child. After the fathers had prayed, the people received a small loaf or a candle.
203407: A miller who was talking with a man claimed that witchcraft and ghosts did not exist. The man then said: "Ah, you don't believe in any of that! Just take a look in your mill". When the miller came into his mill, he saw that it was full of rats and mice. Half the sacks had been eaten through. The miller had to ask the man he had spoken with, kindly, to drive the animals away.
203422: In a bewitched house a black cat lay under the stove. When the woman said a certain phrase, the cat suddenly vanished.
203443: Two girls always heard wailing at midnight. They went to the fathers, who advised them to put a medal under the door. That is how the girls found out it was their own neighbour making noise at night.
203461: A man who had met a witch on the way was followed by a kitten in the Opperstraat. The man was afraid and knocked at a door. When he left those people again a while later, the kitten was still there and followed him until he was home. When he got home the man quickly slammed the door shut. Then the cat began to miaow. That was witchcraft.
203509: A boy walking home with his father one evening saw that he was being followed by a little light. His father said it was a ghost from the churchyard. If you left such a light alone, it would do nothing, the father said.
203543: Some people had gone to help on a farm. When a sorceress from the neighbourhood came walking to the farm, the farmer's wife was just taking the plates off the table to carry them inside. The farmer's wife dropped the twelve plates. The plates were all broken into tiny pieces. The sorceress was nowhere to be seen.
203545: After his death a greedy farmer came haunting on the kouter (open communal farmland) with a pile of posts on his back.
203546: Three men on their way to Pollare laughed at a statue of a saint standing by a chapel. They turned the saint around and went on. But at the boundary between Pollare and Appelterre the men could go no further. They had to go back and turn the saint to face forward again.
203571: At the Nonnenborre a castle and a convent are said to have sunk. On Christmas night the bells could still be heard ringing there at midnight.
203575: At 't Eindeken a hell wagon without horses always drove around. One night a boy was woken up to go to work, although it was not yet time. It was ghosts that had woken the boy.
203606: A butcher went to slaughter a pig for a woman who often bought lard and meat from him. When the butcher stuck the pig in the throat, no blood flowed. The butcher stabbed again, after which the pig moved its head and looked at him with a sad gaze. The butcher was so shaken by this that he dropped his knife at once and ran away. When he got home the butcher told his wife what had happened. Then he went back to kill the pig. This time the animal again looked at him strangely, so there was nothing for it but to kill the pig with a hammer. When the butcher was slaughtering a pig somewhere else, the sorceress came to ask for a clog nail. After the butcher had been to the fathers, the sorceress no longer came to him. When one day she did appear again, the butcher stood there with a knife in his hands. His wife said to the sorceress: "You'd better not come here any more, because my husband wants to stab you to death."
203627: A man playing cards saw an unknown gentleman come in and join the game. The players always lost to the stranger. When one man bent down to pick up a dropped card, he saw that the stranger had goat's legs. The man quickly made the sign of the cross, whereupon the stranger screamed horribly and then vanished. People said the stranger was the devil.
203644: A baker took on a new hand. The boy ate a lot, but he worked for three. The baker had told several people that he found it strange his hand was so thin. Some had replied: "We know what the problem is. Your hand is an Osschaart (a man who roams at night in an animal skin). He has to go about at night in an animal skin, so he cannot sleep". The baker found that his hand indeed did not sleep at night. He asked two friends to keep watch at night to see where the hand had hidden his animal skin. At midnight the hand fetched his skin from the woodpile and left. When the hand met someone in that shape, he put his forepaws on the passer-by's shoulders and had himself carried until his victims were drenched in sweat. The next day the baker said to his hand: "You have to work so hard and I don't feel very fit either. From now on we'll sleep a few hours every afternoon. I'll wake you when we start baking again". No sooner said than done. When the baker heard the hand snoring, he fetched the skin from the woodpile and threw it into the oven. The moment the skin caught fire, the hand woke up and cried: "Oh, my skin, they've burned my skin!" The hand himself was on fire too. When the skin had burned away, the hand stopped burning and thanked the baker for freeing him from evil.
203646: At the blacksmith's in Aspelare a cat came and sat on the chimney. Because the cat smashed everything, the smith cut off one of the animal's paws. The next day a sorceress who had lost a leg was walking about the village.
203670: A man walking around Voorde one night was surrounded by cats, so that he could hardly go on.
203672: A dead parish priest kept walking about with a post on his back. After a long time someone said: "Put it back where you took it from." After that the haunting priest was seen no more.
203694: In Tielrode lived a miller who could not keep a single farmhand alive. After their first night in the mill, all the farmhands lay dead. They had been killed by a pack of cats. One day the miller hired a new farmhand who was not afraid on hearing the stories about his predecessors. The farmhand asked for a dung fork before he went to sleep in the mill. But the next morning that farmhand lay dead too. Shortly afterwards another farmhand applied, who asked for a gun and a blessed button. At midnight the farmhand fired the gun with the blessed button at the cats that came running up. Then the cats all ran away. The next day, however, the miller's wife was ill, so the doctor had to be called. The doctor found the blessed button in the woman's buttock. She was a witch who went haunting at night and then laid a brush in the bed beside her husband.
203699: People who had been ridden by the moon could not get home and wandered around all the time.
203714: In the past a black calf used to roam the streets of Wannegem-Lede. However much people struck or kicked at the animal, they could not hit it. The calf chased passers-by.
203721:
On a farm all the animals died. It was believed this misfortune had been caused by a woman with a bad reputation who had once slept in the hay. Perhaps that woman had relieved herself in the hay.
In the end the farmer's sister went to the fathers of Gent. While the sister was away, the farmer saw a toad come into the house. The man threw the toad into the stove, but the animal escaped and crawled out under the door. After that there was no more misfortune on that farm.
203727: In Wannegem-Lede a dead man who had moved the boundary posts of his field returned. People kept seeing him walking with a post on his head, calling: "Where shall I put them, where shall I put them?" One evening a bold fellow answered: "Put them where you found them!" Since then the ghost has not been seen or heard again.
203737: In the church in Maarke-Kerkem all the people were covered in lice. They had fallen victim to a witch.
203762: On his way home a drunkard saw someone walking with a post in his hands, calling: "Where must I put it? Where must I put it?" After the drunkard answered: "For God's sake, put it where you took it from," the ghost vanished.
203786: If you heard a magpie calling, something bad would happen. A woman went to visit family in Ename. As she walked along the Schelde, she heard a magpie chattering behind her the whole time. When she got home, she learned that her son had been called up for the army.
203806: A man got lost in the churchyard of Mater. He had been ridden by the mare. Perhaps that man had simply drunk too much.
203844: In Volkegem a sorceress came back from town with an umbrella under her arm. On the way the sorceress tapped a man who was working with her umbrella. Afterwards the man's finger became infected. Because the finger did not heal, the man said: "She has bewitched my finger off."
203845: On a farm there worked a farmhand who went to café 'de Cochon' in Dendermonde at least twice a month. When one day, drunk, the man had to pass a stone bridge, he saw a cat sitting there. The man said to the animal: "What are you doing sitting here?" Of course the cat did not answer, and the man knocked the cat off the bridge with his stick. A little later, however, another cat appeared, which said: "Put back what you knocked off!" Before the farmhand got back to the farm, he was surrounded by dozens of cats, which kept crying: "Put back what you knocked off!" The farmhand called the farmer's wife he worked for. That woman had probably been given a prayer to read by some friar. Because of that, the cats were gone a little later.
203865: To become a werewolf, you had to stand at a crossroads at night with a black rooster. The devil would then appear and order the werewolf to attack women on the road. A woman coming back from work who was attacked by a werewolf threw her apron at the beast with the words: "You must unravel that apron completely and then come and show it to me" and ran away. When she got home, the woman saw her boyfriend standing there with the threads of the apron between his teeth.
203885:
A farmhand had hidden his werewolf skin in a hollow tree stump close to the farm where he worked. At supper the people on the farm noticed that the farmhand was always away. He would lie in wait for the people coming from the table.
One day the farmhand's skin was found. When it was thrown into the oven to burn it, the farmhand came running to save his skin. But however much he begged and cried, his skin was burnt.
203887: A woman who lived alone heard the mare come into her house and crawl onto her clogs. Then the mare threw itself on the woman.
203905: A farmer had put the skin of Osschaert (a shape-shifting spook) into the oven to burn it. Several Osschaerts jumped out of the skin, making a terrible noise. The farmer was never able to use that oven again.
203910: A man from Mere who had often had to carry kledde (a werewolf-like goblin that leaps onto people's backs) once took a knife with him, with which he gave the tormenting spirit a cut. The next day people knew who kledde was.
203916: A man who was ridden by the mare at night always saw the woman come in. The man went to the friars.
203978: A woman who suffered from asthma had a baby. She was assisted at the birth by a midwife. Because the child fell ill afterwards, people believed the midwife had bewitched it.
204005: A mother had to keep watch in her daughter's house. She was visited by a woman who gave her an umbrella as a present and had brought coffee herself. The mother made a pot of coffee with the coffee the visitor had brought, so they could drink it together. After that the mother was dragged around the house by her hair for three nights. She went to the fathers, who advised her to climb a hill. That was very hard, because the witch was hanging on the woman's skirts. The fathers prayed the whole time, so the woman did reach the top. On the hill prayers were read over the woman. Then she had to go down and give the umbrella back to the visitor. After that was done, the woman was delivered.
204037: A girl who went to do the washing for a family in the evenings always came home late. One day the girl told her confessor that she was often assaulted on her way home. The priest advised the girl to take a large red handkerchief with her next time and throw it at her attacker. The girl followed this advice. When her boyfriend came to visit the next day, the girl saw that the boy had the fibres of the red handkerchief between his teeth.
204063: At a farm where a ghost had appeared, the curate was sent for. After the clergyman had exorcised the place, the ghost never returned.
204069: At Pentecost a procession was held in Heldergem in honour of Saint Cornelius. A woman going to mass on Pentecost morning saw a large beast sitting in the grain. The woman was convinced the beast was a sorceress from the village and turned back to fetch a friend. In the village she heard the neighbour of the suspected sorceress say: "What have you been up to now, that those people no longer dared to pass there?"
204087: A man claimed that the devil sat in front of him when he lay in his bed.
204105: People who were ridden by the mare could first feel the mare at their feet and then could hardly move because their throat was squeezed shut. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to take a bottle with a cork to bed. If one felt something at one's feet, one had to knock the cork into the bottle. The mare would then ride into the bottle.
204110: A man going from Voorde to Smeerhebbe one evening was followed by a calf. The man went to the house he had to visit. When he had sat there for a while, he went outside again and found that the calf had disappeared.
204113: A woman who lived with a son of her sister was taken to the convent of Etikhove because she was ill. A mother who had a sixteen-year-old daughter and younger children lived close to that convent. One day when the children were playing outside, the woman from the old people's home threw some marshmallows down through the window. The girl called to her brothers and sisters: "You mustn't pick that up, because it's from a witch. She could bewitch you!" Some time later the girl met the witch on the road. The witch said to her: "I'll get you yet for what you said about me!" The girl ran to her mother's inn and told what had happened. When the girl had to fetch beer in the cellar, she saw fire everywhere. The girl had hallucinations all the time, but the doctor could not help her. The priest had also visited three times, but had said there was no evil in the house. One day the mother said to the priest: "You must come to my house or I'll set it on fire." Then the priest came to the girl together with the curate. He read from a prayer book and asked the girl what was wrong. The girl said a heavy burden pressed on her heart and that the priest was the only one who could free her from it. The priest tried to drive the evil into the corners of the room and into the stove, but did not succeed. When the fathers had also arrived, they said: "We can no longer save the girl. It is already too late." While the priest was praying, the girl died. During the priest's intervention the witch had made such a racket in the convent that people became afraid of her and she was no longer allowed to stay. She then went to Maarke and died there.
204130: People who had kicked at a cat at night were afterwards pounced on and crushed in their beds by a thousand cats.
204198: A child who cried all the time was helped by a German shepherd. The witch who had bewitched the child was also present on this occasion. The shepherd pulled lots of pins out of the child's heart. Meanwhile the witch was drawn closer and closer to the fire, so that she suffered greatly.
204216: At night a man always heard beautiful music in his bed, but he could not see anything.
204231: A farmer from Lede could no longer churn butter. On three consecutive days the farmer was visited by a woman who came to ask for butter. The farmer answered that he had no butter and slammed the door. The fathers of Gent advised the farmer to put holy water in that woman's milk can. When the farmer did so, the woman said: "Tomorrow you'll have butter all right." And so it was. The fathers had also advised the farmer from then on to leave that woman standing at the door when she came for milk and butter.
204238: A boy who had gone to visit his girlfriend at 'den Boek 't Sitie' went home at about one o'clock at night. At a crossroads where a crucifix hung, the boy suddenly heard music in the air, although there was nothing to be seen. A little later the boy saw a funeral procession pass by. Badly frightened, the boy ran back to his girlfriend's house.
204242: During the occupation the Germans in Liedekerke tried to steal two large church bells. They put the bells in the priest's garden, where they sank into the ground.
204243: In Horebeke worked a farmhand who very much wanted to go to the fair. But he was not allowed because he had to manure the field. The farmhand thought he would gladly sell his soul to the devil if that would get his work done. He sat down by a heap of manure and said: "I mine and each his own." Then the work was done.
204263: In Volkegem a seven-year-old girl had died. A woman always came to visit those people during high mass. The friars had told the people: "You can't do anything about it. That woman will still be sitting there when you get home. I will give you something to put under her chair." When the people had done so, the woman could no longer get up.
204272: One day a man from Embeek went to visit family in Sint-Paulus. When the man crossed the Mark, he saw a little dog lying asleep on the footbridge. The man stepped very carefully over the little dog. On his way back the man was surprised to find that the little dog was still lying in the same spot. When he gave the dog a kick, the animal grew bigger and bigger. The man ran home terrified, followed by the dog. The man bolted all the doors and many hours later saw that the dog was still walking around his house. In the end the animal did go away.
204293: A woman who went to pick peas in her garden saw a sorceress pass by, who said: "Do you think you'll make it home? You'll drop all your beans." The sorceress was proved right.
204353: In Pollare a big horse was sometimes seen at night. Then nobody dared to go outside. Through the window people saw sparks flying from the stones when that horse walked about there.
204373: A mother of twins was visited by a neighbour woman who rubbed the children's heads and said: "Your children will die." That evening one of the children was already dead. The priest came regularly to read prayers over the other child, but in the end the other child died too.
204424: In Edelare lived a woman suspected of being a witch. When a woman lay in childbed and was having many difficulties, her brother-in-law at one point pulled the door open. The witch was standing in front of it and the man said: "What are you doing here?" The witch claimed she had come to visit the woman in childbed.
204435: On a farm one day no butter could be made after a toad had been seen hopping around the butter churn. That toad was a witch who had bewitched the butter.
204454: A man from Onkerzele who did not go to church fell victim to some of his friends who wanted to play a trick on him. The friends came knocking on the doors of the unbeliever's house, so that his wife said: "We are bewitched! We will have to send for the parish priest to undo it!" The priest said to the man: "I will say a prayer, but you must do the same! If there is haunting at your house again, your wife must lead the prayer and you must respond." So the man and the woman began to pray, and in the end they were converted.
204480: A woman who was struggling with a plague of lice scrubbed and washed everything, but could not get rid of the lice. Someone said to the woman: "If the lice cannot be driven out by cleanliness, then they are lice that have been sent". A witch from the neighbourhood had caused lice or bedbugs in many houses. Those lice could only be got rid of by praying a paternoster before sunset for nine days. The woman followed the advice and was indeed freed of the lice.
204484:
If one saw a black dog in the street, it was believed to be the devil.
A man on his way heard a sound behind him. He looked back and saw a black dog. The man quickened his pace and a little later looked back again. This time the dog had already grown much bigger.
204488: On a farm near Marke-Kerkem stood an apple tree on which a little candle came to sit every evening. When the apple tree was cut down one day, it turned out to stand over a cellar in which leather money was hidden. When the money was touched, it turned to dust.
204498: Because a boy had put a paasnagel (Easter nail, a blessed nail from the Easter candle) under the door of the church of Everbeek, two witches could not leave the church on Sunday. Six months later the boy was completely emaciated and he died.
204529: When the hemp was being harvested in Hamme, a whole heap of fine apples was suddenly thrown into the field. No one knew where the apples had come from. The old people told the young ones not to eat the apples, because the evil hand had probably thrown them into the field. The young people did not take this advice seriously and ate the apples anyway. The next day everyone who had eaten the apples was ill. The dean of Hamme advised the people to lay a piece of the Easter candle on the thresholds of the houses of the sick. Whoever could not get over those thresholds was the guilty one. The next day a woman stood still before the door and cried that she could not get in. Everyone rushed at the woman. Only when she had undone the evil was she let go.
204568: A man coming home one night saw in front of him a figure without head or tail coming straight at him. The man immediately made the sign of the cross and began to pray. Because the ghost kept threatening him, the man promised to have a candle burned for a certain saint and quickly ran away. After that the man never again went home along that road.
204575: On a farm the horses were completely stiff after a witch had visited. An hour after the parish priest had come to undo the witchcraft, the horses behaved normally again.
204594: A boy was ridden by the mare several times at night. The boy was not dreaming, but felt as if he was being lifted by something under his mattress. Once, when the boy was lying on his stomach, he felt the mare crawling up from his heels. It seemed as if a hundred thousand kilos were lying on him. After the boy had said a prayer, he was freed from the mare. After that he always wore a scapular and was no longer troubled by the mare.
204603: On a farm in Sint-Cornelis-Horebeke the little children were all lying in their cradles when an old-fashioned dressed woman came in and gave one of the children something. An hour later the child lay dead in its cradle. Whenever that woman had stroked an animal in the stable over the head, the animal was later also found dead.
204648: In café de Zevenbergen there was dancing on Sundays and holidays. People even danced there during high mass. At midnight two devils with horse's feet came into the café. The devils danced everyone out of the door. That was a punishment.
204651: On the Kattenhul seven black cats always gathered in the evening. Passers-by who met such a cat always had an accident before they got home.
204654: On Tuesdays many beggars came to Wortegem. A farmer's wife saw a beggar woman from Ooike arrive and strike the water of the ditch with her clog. Because there was not much water left on the farm, the water from the ditch was used to give to the calves. The animals that had drunk from it, however, ran up the walls and died.
204672: In the Spanish hedge in the Kruiselingstraat in Kwaremont, people heard music.
204705: A handloom weaver from Kruishoutem sent his little daughter out one evening to buy a few bobbins of silk. On her way home the girl met a large dog, which pulled at her skirts. In desperation the girl threw a few bobbins at the dog, which gave her the chance to go home. When she got home, the girl saw her father sitting at the loom. She saw that he had the silk threads between his teeth and said: "Mother, it was father."
204712: A mother whose child began crying loudly every night at twelve o'clock had consulted the doctor in vain. Then the woman went to the friars, who said: "The child gets something from a woman every day. Tonight you will find something on the floor. You must throw it into the stove." The mother took her child to a day nursery every day. One evening she did indeed find a fish on the floor. She threw the fish into the stove, as the friar had said. The next day the mother met the woman who had bewitched her child. The mother said to her: "It's you who did that to me."
204737: One evening a man was visited by a friend who said that a certain Machiel had died. The cat sitting by the hearth stood up on its hind legs and cried: "Is Machiel dead?" Then the cat disappeared up the chimney.
204802: On a farm plagued by rats, a hunchback came to visit and asked: "Would you like to be rid of those rats?" When the people said yes, the man advised them to put earth with holy water in the attic. The man himself would go on a pilgrimage barefoot to Gaverland. Eight days later all the rats on that farm had disappeared.
204846: In Okegem lived a sorceress who could turn herself into a toad. If that toad had been struck or burnt, the sorceress would appear the next day with a wound.
204847: In a house that a certain woman often visited, the boys did not grow. The girls were not affected by this illness. After the children's father had been on a pilgrimage to Wallonia, the boys became healthy.
204897: A pigeon fancier who had lost all his pigeons found his neighbour woman's cat and killed the animal. Then the neighbour said to the man: "You caught my cat, but you won't play with your pigeons anymore!" The next Sunday the man let his pigeons fly anyway. When the birds came home, they fell dead on the roof tiles. Only after the man had given his neighbour another cat could he play with the pigeons again.
204917: A farmhand who lived on a farm had a strange experience one day when he was in the loft. Someone pulled off his leather shoes, although there was no one to be seen, and the farmhand heard a train running in the loft.
204937: A man who wanted to go to mass in Kwaremont left too early because his watch had stopped. It was not yet midnight. When the man came to the wood, he saw a creature there that looked like a streak of fire. The creature stuck its tongue out at the man. The man later died of fright.
204958: On a farm, the skin of a kledde (a werewolf-like creature) was found in the woodpile. When the skin had been thrown into the oven, the farmhand came running to save his skin. He had to be restrained until the skin had burnt. Afterwards the farmhand calmed down and was relieved.
204961: A family plagued by witchcraft went to the friars for advice. A friar said that a woman who often came to the family for coffee was the cause of all the evil. The priest gave the people a paasnagel (Easter nail, a blessed nail from the Easter candle) to put under their threshold. After that the woman no longer came to the house.
204964: A man from Wortegem had lost his way at midnight. A young lady kept walking along with the man. When the man stood still, the lady stood still too. If the man turned somewhere, the lady did as well. At a certain moment the man stood before a large embankment. When the man kicked the embankment, the obstacle had vanished and he could go on.
204996: People who were ridden by the mare had to suffer a great deal. To protect oneself against the mare, one had to put one's shoes upside down next to the bed.
204999: At nightfall in the Diepestraat in Sint-Goriks-Oudenhove, a woman heard a noise behind her. The woman looked round and saw a big werewolf. The woman quickly threw her apron on the ground, so that the werewolf had to unravel the cloth and she could run away. When the woman reached the door of her house, the werewolf was already standing behind her.
205005: When the sky turned red in the evening, the old people said it was because of the blood that had been shed in the war of '70. Some people even believed the red sunset was an omen of a new war.
205044: A man walking home drunk stopped to urinate against a lamppost. There the man suddenly saw a mewing cat approaching, which would not be chased away. When the man had kicked at the cat a few times, he was surrounded by dozens of cats, so that he could not go on and had to turn back. The man then took a detour to get home.
205053: A woman went to the Oudenberg with her neighbour. Because the weather was fine and the women were soon back from the chapel, they decided to go on to Moerbeke to visit a niece and nephew of the neighbour. The niece was not at home, but her husband stood there with a dismayed face and said: "My wife is always praying and reading books! I even found a wax doll here stuck full of pins. Every time my wife sticks a pin into it, she hurts the person she wants to bewitch. I don't dare throw it away or burn it, because then I might burn the bewitched child."
205075: Strange things happened on a farm. The ears of two pigs began to rot and one of the cows would not eat. The farmer went to the friars of Affligem. Afterwards he sprinkled everything with holy water and placed medals everywhere. After that intervention the misfortune was over.
205091: On a farm pigs always died after a certain woman had visited. So that woman was no longer let in. Once when the children were home alone, the woman got in again after all. Shortly afterwards a pig died.
205111: When it snowed, you were not to walk in the tracks of a black cat. Otherwise you were bewitched and could not move on. It could also happen that you died the next day.
205116: In the old days there were people who dressed up in a bearskin as kledde (a werewolf-like spook) or as the werewolf. These jokers jumped on passers-by's backs and made them carry them a little way.
205131: A man who was ridden by the mare nearly died. He had heard the mare coming.
205160: On a farm, the skin of a kledde (a werewolf-like creature) was found in a tree stump. On that farm no gates could be hung anywhere, because the next day the gates had been thrown into the field. One day the farmhand was sent to Gent so that his skin could be burnt while he was away. As soon as the skin caught fire, the farmhand was already standing by the oven to get his skin back. When the skin had burnt up, the farmhand was released.
205168: A woman who dealt in evil conjured a spider onto a child's belly while its parents were outside. Afterwards the parents did not know why their child fell ill. They took the child to the friars to have prayers read over it.
205176: When the people from the Kete went to mass on Sunday, they got lost, even though they had a lantern with them. The people had been ridden by the mare. Later it was said that the place was haunted.
205216: Witches dwelt in Raspaillebos between Waarbeke and Galmaarden. When people passed by there, their horses always stopped at that spot.
205226: A farm was haunted every night. At night people heard noises there as if butter were being churned in the cellar. One morning there was a very large wagon in a stable that normally could not get in through the door.
205303: In Nieuwenhove there was a Saint John's bell. When that bell rang during a thunderstorm, everyone came to it, because then one could not be struck by lightning. The bell sank in the Bosbroek.
205331: In a house in Iddergem the furniture could be heard creaking in the evening. The creaking was caused by the ghost of a dead person who was unhappy and was letting them know that prayers had to be said for him. After people had gone on pilgrimage to the friars of Aalst, the creaking was no longer heard.
205394: One morning on a farm all the little rabbits lay dead. The animals' legs were entwined with one another. The next day the tails of the two horses were braided. After the farmer's wife had been to Affligem, the witchcraft came to an end.
205419:
In Zarlardinge lived a woman who was ridden by the mare every night. At night a sorceress came and sat on her, making her cry loudly for help.
When other people came to her, the woman was freed.
205423: A woman who had promised a mass for her dead husband had forgotten the promise she had made. Moreover, the woman spent almost all her money on drink. One day the woman had put coal in the stove. Among it was an especially large lump of coal. During the night the large lump of coal was completely shattered. The next day the woman told her neighbours that she had seen her dead husband appear. The woman added: "I had promised a mass, but I couldn't fulfil that promise because I had no money left."
205425: Some people from the Nieuwhoek in Nokere walking home in the evening were circled by a large white cat that blocked their way. Because their child cried constantly after that incident, they went to the friars. The clergymen said the child was bewitched and read prayers over it. After that the child recovered.
205482: A woman who had special powers and who owned a few rabbits and a goat or a sheep went along the ditches in the morning to cut grass, which she then left to dry. One night hay was stolen from that woman. When she was spoken to about the theft, she said: "I'm not worried. The person who stole it will be glad to be able to bring it back." A few days later the woman saw that the hay had been brought back. She must surely have done the thief harm.
205509: In Mater lived a woman suspected of being a witch. The people of Mater who made gloves could no longer carry on, because the fingers of all their gloves had been cut off.
205553: Some children who were grazing the cows in the meadow saw a sorcerer pass by, who threw a mastel (a ring-shaped bread roll) on the ground. One of the cows ate the mastel. A short time later the animal died.
205592: In the old days 'loedies' (werewolves) went about, jumping on people and making them carry them to their house. To become a 'loedie' yourself, you had to stand at a crossroads of four or five roads at midnight.
205616: A man who had struck at a cat saw, a little later, some three or five hundred cats running around his feet.
205656: A man who was ridden by the mare was very restless. After he had drunk a shot of liquor, he felt fine again.
205660: A woman went to a farmer's wife to ask for milk. She got none, however, because it was the fair and the farmer's wife needed the milk herself to bake mattentaarten (curd tarts). The tarts looked especially delicious and not one was burnt. But when they were cut open, there turned out to be no curd in them!
205689: Along the Wolvenberg or the Volkegemberg, hollowed-out turnips with burning candles could sometimes be seen hanging in the trees. The people who saw this believed that a dead person had returned there.
205733: A woman who was out in Mater kicked at a cat sitting on the ground. The next moment there were more than a thousand cats. The woman knelt down and began to pray until all the cats had disappeared.
205744: On the farm De Kete in Wannegem there was a spot that was bewitched. Whatever animal was put there always died immediately.
205788: A man from Temse always saw black-and-white spotted rats running around his loft. His friends at the café advised him to call in the priest. The priest sent the man to the friars. One of the friars went with the man to his house. The man had to take his gun and shoot at the rats. But he could not hit a single rat, although he was a marksman.
205808: In the old days people believed that ladybirds brought luck.
205845: Near a foal running in the meadow, a leg was always seen jumping up. That was a witch who had changed herself into a leg.
205863: Toads had something to do with witchcraft. Some people who had toads in their house burnt the animals in the stove. The next day they saw a witch walking about whose face was completely burnt.
205881: A woman peddler often visited a farm where there were five children. When after a while the children fell ill and the farmer's wife noticed that something always went missing when the peddler had visited, she became suspicious. Her niece advised the mother to go and see a blind woman who lived in the town. The mother told her story to the blind woman, who sat praying a rosary in the dark. Although the mother had said nothing about the peddler, the blind woman said to her: "You must not let that peddler in anymore. But you will have no more trouble from her, because she will not come again." Indeed the peddler came no more and the children recovered.
205884: A little boy was covered in pimples that would not heal. The mother went to a friar, who predicted that on her way back she would meet the woman who had caused the evil. On the way the mother did indeed meet a woman, who said: "What a lovely child you have!" When the woman wanted to take hold of the child, the mother said: "Leave it alone." The child then quickly recovered.
205905: A house in Letterhoutem was haunted almost every night. One night there were hundreds of pigeons in it; another time it was swarming with cats. The house was eventually sold, but many people would not have wanted the house even if it were free.
205935: A wizard could send rats from one house to another. The rats had to cross a brook along a little plank.
205968: In Sint-Denijs-Boekel lived an ugly little woman who was said to be a witch. When people had hung their washing outside, that witch could tie knots in the laundry.
205977: A man going to Kruishoutem saw a beautiful procession in the sky near the 'Konijntjes' and heard splendid trumpet music. The man knelt on his bare knees watching until the procession had passed.
206040: On a farm in Vlierzele the animals were bewitched. When a rabbit was due to give birth, only toads were born. But it was never found out which witch was responsible for that misfortune.
206043: In Nederename lived two women suspected of being witches. Everyone was afraid of these women. Whenever a child was born somewhere, the woman would go to visit the new baby with a bunch of flowers. Afterwards people believed the child had been bewitched.
206056: A woman worked on a farm that was haunted. Every night the woman felt a heavy weight pressing on her body, so that she was almost strangled. After the woman had had the friars read prayers over her, she was no longer troubled by the ghost.
206076: A man was sent by his wife to the shop to fetch something. The man went outside and, not even fifty metres from his house, suddenly could no longer find his bearings. That man had been 'led off the yard' or ridden by the mare.
206077: A farm in Ouwegem had been struck by the evil hand. The friars came to the place, gave the people blessed biscuits and sprinkled the place with holy water. After that nothing strange happened on that farm again.
206079: A smith from Pamel had gone bankrupt. His house was sold to pay his creditors. When the smith lay awake at night, he saw a little woman pass by, who said: "Do what I want and follow me." The little woman took the smith to a big fire where a horned goat appeared. When the goat asked what the little woman had brought, she answered: "This smith is going to sell his soul for money." The smith had to sign with his own blood and then received a whole purse full of money and a heap of iron and coal.
206160: In the summer of 1900 a violent thunderstorm broke out. Afterwards large arcs resembling rainbows were seen in the sky, as well as a great light. People claimed this apparition foretold a bloody war. Some even said they had seen soldiers in the sky.
206167: Around Easter a mother had noticed that her little son had strikingly flushed cheeks. One morning the mother found that the child's cradle was full of black ants. The mother changed all the bedding, but still the cradle was full of ants again every morning. Because it was believed the child was bewitched, the parents went to Affligem. On the way they met a woman wearing old-fashioned clothes. She wore a headscarf and a neckerchief. When the people asked whether they were on the right road to Affligem, the woman answered: "Are you going to Affligem with that child? What are you going to do there?!" The woman had barely spoken those words when the child began crying incessantly. In Affligem the abbot laid his stole over the child and began to pray. Although no wind could blow in the room they were in, the stole flew away. The friar began to sweat and laid the stole on the child again. The abbot predicted that the people would meet someone. They were not to do that person any harm. The guilty one would come to undo the harm done within nine days. After the priest's intervention the people had no more problems with their child. One Wednesday night they woke up because there was loud knocking on the door. The parents opened it, but saw no one there.
206232: In the Groenstraat in Waasmunster a farmer had put his pig in a salting tub in the loft. Afterwards the people sat talking downstairs when suddenly a hoop sprang off the tub and rolled down. The hoop went through two rooms and then went back upstairs. When people went up to look after that strange event, there was nothing unusual to be seen on the tub.
206238: 'De platte Beurs' was haunted. At night the brother and sister who lived on that farm always heard noise and rattling in the loft. During the day nothing could be heard. No one dared to sleep in that loft.
206249: A skin lay in the ast (drying kiln). When the farmer threw the skin into the oven, a neighbour came running, crying.
206301: Every night a girl saw a little doll dancing on her bed. In the morning the doll had disappeared. The girl had probably been ridden by the mare (nightmare spirit). A witch also lived near the girl.
206304: A farm in Mespelare was badly haunted. At night lights were always seen there, but when people went to look, the lights had vanished.
206326: A man had a fine, healthy mule. One day the animal lay dead with its legs in the air. The man, however, believed witchcraft was involved and sent for a black friar from Gent. Because the friar took the trouble to come there and read prayers over everything, the man knew enough. After the friar's intervention all went well.
206357: During the First World War two girls went with their mother into the woods to gather dry wood. The three met a woman who claimed that she had been ridden by the mare.
206360: On a farm in Nieuwerkerken the animals were bewitched. No butter could be made there, even after churning a whole day. One afternoon a fine foal lay dead after it had been given water. Two calves dropped dead after they had been fed. It was believed the evil was caused by an old woman who lived nearby.
206382: A German shepherd who lived in Alsace had special powers. For example, he could make rats come to a heap of straw. Then he set the straw on fire, so that all the rats died.
206427: Strange things happened on a farm in Nokere. The horses got colic and were untied at night. The farmer's son and daughter fell ill. People looked everywhere, but everything seemed normal. When, to make matters worse, the farmer's daughter had died of her illness, the friars of Kruishoutem were sent for. When those friars came to read prayers over the farm, the sweat rolled down their faces. The farmer's son had to walk thirty kilometres on foot while reading from a missal. He was not allowed to talk to anyone on the way. After that he would be cured. And so it was.
206434: People who had a pearl (a white spot) on their eye believed they were bewitched. A girl had to go and tell a witch that a load of goods had arrived and that the witch could come and collect it. The witch was just bringing in the straw. She said: "There's a bit of straw on your head" and took it off. Then the girl went home and said to her mother: "I'm bewitched. She took a bit of straw from my hair and I'm sure there was no straw on my hair." When the girl got up the next day, she had a pearl on her eye and had to go to the friars of Gent. The girl's mother was convinced her daughter had been bewitched by that witch.
206451: A farmhand lying in his bed felt something fall on him that grabbed his wrists. The farmhand began to shout loudly, but no sound came from his throat. Only when someone came into the barn and spoke to the farmhand did the mare disappear.
206454: In a house where the child was always crying, people discovered a woman standing behind the house holding a wax doll, into which she was sticking pins to torment the child.
206478: People who had much misfortune in their stable and their house believed they were bewitched.
206485: In Meerbeke an old woman had died in a house fire. Her daughters went to live in a house a little further on. Every evening the daughters heard a ghost saying that they had to pray a great deal for their mother, or else they would soon die themselves. From then on the girls prayed a paternoster every evening.
206508: One Sunday in a café in Nukerke someone with goat's legs had danced. That was the devil. After that scene all the people had fled outside.
206514: In the old days, when people woke up at night, they often saw a dead person standing before them. After an Our Father had been prayed, the dead person vanished.
206516: A shepherd had seen one of his sheep root a crucifix out of the ground. The shepherd took it to the priest, who hung it in the church. The next day the crucifix was already lying again where it had been found. After that a chapel was built on that spot.
206534: A farmer from Herzele who was going to the field with his wheelbarrow, with his little son sitting in it, met a woman who said: "Hey, what a lovely child you have!" A little later the child let its head droop. It was suspected that the woman had bewitched the child. When that woman came to the farm later in the day to fetch water, the farmer grabbed her by the neck and pushed her over the edge of the well, saying: "If you don't undo what you have done, I'll let you fall." The frightened woman answered: "It will be done!" After that the child was indeed cured.
206536: A man whose friend had died saw a light like a candle moving around a tree. The man did not dare go closer, but a friend of his did. In the end a pot of money was found under the tree. Since then the light has not been seen. It was said that people who had hidden money somewhere had to come back every night to count it.
206614: A witch had been in the stable on a farm. After that something was regularly wrong with the cow. The people went on a pilgrimage to Affligem and had to throw a little holy water in the stable. After that the people there had no more problems.
206646: A woman was visited by a peddler selling rat poison. When the woman bought nothing, the peddler said: "But madam, don't you have any rats?", to which the woman replied: "Why no. And besides, we have cats that can catch the rats". The peddler then went on his way. The next morning, however, the barn and the stable were full of rats.
206654: A witch could be in two places at once. One day some people from Broeke went together to Ronse. When they passed the witch's house, they saw the witch standing there with her hands in the kneading trough. But she was not kneading dough; she stood stock-still as if she were dead. When the people came to the Bruul, they saw that same witch standing there. She was out with a clog full of glowing oven coals.
206677: A carter from Lede drove with some horses to Wallonia. On a certain hill, the man used to fetch two extra horses from a local farmer, because otherwise the cart could not get over the hill. Since the farmer was not at home that day, the man tried with his own horses alone. To his great astonishment he saw his horses pull the cart up without any effort. But when he saw beside the cart a horse three times the size of a normal horse, he cried: Jesus, Mary, Joseph, what is that? At that the devil's horse vanished and the man's horses could no longer pull the cart.
206709: In Edelare there were two families in which a child had died. The people attributed that misfortune to the magic power of a woman from the neighbourhood.
206787: Some sons worked on the railway together with their father. When the father fell ill, a priest was sent for, who said: "You must put some urine in a bottle. The culprit will come to ask forgiveness and also ask for the water to be poured out of the bottle."
209135: Several cases of haunting, caused by a sorcerer.
209163: Dream vision of a theft; dream vision preceding a death.
209164: Seeing an image of Christ before the mother's death.
209169: Ways in which a witch bewitches, and how the bewitchment is warded off.
209225: Attempt by a restless dead person to tempt someone into helping to take the key to a treasure from a lion's mouth.
209246: Man has learned magic from a book of spells; burning of the book of spells.
209248: Witchcraft by a witch causing horses at first to be unable to pull a wagon.
209249: Sorcerer makes a man lose his way and makes trees sway; sighting of a headless woman dressed in black.
209291: Threshing is heard while the workers are leaving; in the morning the pigs are out of their pens.
209296: A fireball that bursts apart; a fireball that bursts apart with a smell of sulphur.
209308: Dog leaps onto someone's back and has itself carried.
209314: A white lady's curse can be lifted if the key to a chest of gold treasure is taken from the mouth of a devil hound; a man who challenges the white lady to come is startled by a breaking branch and flees.
209315: Origin of a phantom dog with a rattling chain that frightens people at night; a smuggler in a dog's skin is unmasked.
209321: Burning the skin releases a man who can fly after putting on the skin.
209322: Bewitchment of horses stops after a friar has put a paasnagel (Easter nail, a blessed nail from the Easter candle) under the threshold of the doors.
209323: Toad that comes into a house with a sick child is wounded with a red-hot iron; the next day a neighbour has a burned arm.
209328: Fear of a phantom dog that rattles its chains.
209329: A fiery wagon with the devil on the box takes souls to purgatory.
209335: A ghost poses as a returned dead person, makes a farmer pray for the salvation of the dead person's soul, and meanwhile steals potatoes.
209337: Someone who can also work magic threatens a witch who has held him fast.
209338: Example of witchcraft by a farmer's daughters.
209340: In the evening a silent woman dressed in white walks along with people.
209341: Sighting of, and fear of, a white lady.
209342: The two shades nodding to each other turn out to be two bushes bent towards each other by the wind.
209377: For three nights at midnight, fishermen cannot haul in a heavy eel. The following night they succeed, but the eel is heavy and small, and floats away.
209378: At night in bad weather many horses walk along the roads.
209464: Witch and her husband and children in the shape of polecats.
209465: When a boy calls her names, a witch makes his trousers fall down, and the next time she also holds him fast.
209466: Sorcerer changes himself into a rooster.
209468: Cases of witchcraft and haunting, buying off a bewitchment by paying a doctor who can work magic, black cat in a box bed.
209469: Wizard's son makes people lose their way.
